At Tertium—[Note: [Col. 0214C] *Tertia*, or rather *Tertium*: a parish of the diocese of Senlis, where there is a very ancient chapel of Saint Geneviève, called “of Buxo” even before the year 1200.]—land and censuses, tithes, and field-shares.

At Baerne—[Note: [Col. 0214C] *Baernum*: Baerne, near Montépilloy, diocese of Senlis. It must have been merely a village in which there was a chapel, such as formerly existed on most estates of Saint Geneviève.]—land with tithes, field-shares, and jurisdictions.

At Borrane—[Note: [Col. 0214C] *Borrencum*: Borrane, diocese of Beauvais, three leagues from Senlis, near the abbey of Royaumont.]—beyond the water, lands and meadows, field-shares, rents, and chief rents.

One prebend in the Church of Blessed Mary at Paris.

At Paris, within and outside the city, houses, rents, and chief rents from many persons.

At Ivry—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Ivriacum* and *Vitriacum*: Ivry and Vitry, near Paris.]—and Vitry, lands, vineyards, rents, and chief rents.

At Villejuif [Col. 0213C]—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Villa Judaeorum*: Villejuif, near Paris; what the abbey held there was called the fief of Saint Geneviève.]—lands, tithes, and field-shares.

At the castle of Melun, on Mont Saint-Pierre, tithes of grain and wine; likewise, five solidi which the monks of Saint Faron pay you each year from the church [Col. 0214A] at Tri-le-Bardou.

At Corbeil, four solidi from the Church of Saint Exuperius.

Below Châteaufau, the mill of the village of Boussinville—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Bucelinivilla*: Boussinville.].

At Courpierre—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Curia Petrae*: Courpierre, near Gif.]—and Guigny—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Joviniacum*: Guigny, near Orly.]—lands, meadows, rents, and woods.

At Paris, one mill below the Petit-Pont.

Rents and tithes from a certain estate at Pontperrin—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Pons petrinus*: Pontperrin, near Paris by Villula, from which a particular territory took its name.].

At Tiloy—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Telletum*: Tiloy, near Château-Landon, diocese of Sens.]—by the castle of Landon, lands, chief rents, and rents.

At Saint-Non—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *S. Nonnus*: Saint-Non, diocese of Paris.]—lands, tithes, and field-shares.

At Soisy—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Sosiacum*: Soisy, near Corbeil, diocese of Paris.]—near Corbeil, lands and rents.

At Bois-le-Roi—[Note: [Col. 0214D] *Boscus regis*: Bois-le-Roi, or Balleroy, diocese of Sens.]—lands and revenues.

We also confirm for you, by apostolic authority, the liberty or authority granted to that church by our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, and the immunity granted to that place by the kings of the Franks and confirmed in their documents. No king or prince of the Franks holding the city of Paris may give that church to anyone as a benefice or alienate it from royal patronage by any kind of exchange. Thus may the canons of that church, continuing by God’s grace in canonical religious observance, rejoice both in royal patronage and in the protection of the apostolic see. Let your cloister be preserved in the liberty which it has hitherto possessed. [Col. 0214B]

We also forbid anyone, after making profession in that place, [Col. 0214C] to leave the cloister without the permission of his abbot; and no one may dare to retain one who has departed. We further decree that the church itself shall be subject to no archbishop or bishop, but only to the Roman pontiff. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination [Col. 0215A] of clerics to be promoted to holy orders from whichever bishop you prefer, provided that he is Catholic and enjoys the favor and communion of the apostolic see.

When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one shall be placed over it by any stratagem of deception or violence, except one whom the brothers, by common consent or the sounder part of the brothers, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine, shall judge to be elected. Since we desire to assist generously in the labors and expenses of your church, we decree that your elected abbot may go to whichever Catholic bishop he wishes to receive the grace of blessing; or, if he prefers, as is provided in your other privileges, he may freely go to the Roman pontiff to receive from him the gift of blessing. We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Walter, bishop of Albano. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. [Col. 0215C] I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, William, cardinal priest of Saint Peter in Chains. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Prison. I, Arditio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Cinthius, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Paris through the hand of Hermann, subdeacon and notary of the holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, in the fourth year of the pontificate [Col. 0215D] of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### CLI. Privilege for the Church of Gerberoy

(Paris, April 25.)

[PILLET, *History of Gerberoy*, Documents, p. 332.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Gerberoy, present and future, entering canonically, forever.

Whenever that which is known to accord with religion and integrity is requested of us, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and give an appropriate assent to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, [Col. 0216A] and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms: the church of Rotangy, with the great and small tithe and all its appurtenances; the churches of Haussé and Curchy; the church of Héricourt; the altar of Lhodosy; half the tithe of Collengnies; the tithe of Thieuloy; a third part of the court of Saint-Denis; and the churches of Wambez, La Chapelle, Sulles, Saint-Sanson, and Saint-Ouen. The jurisdiction which you possess in the precinct at Songeons, at Acy, and at the village called Ons-en-Bray, at Senantes, and at Vauroux; in the village of Bray and at Curchy; also the tithe of the revenues from toll, passage, and transit at Songeons and Ons; and the ironwork pit at Savignies.

Furthermore, the liberty granted to you canons and to your church by Guy, formerly bishop of Beauvais, of good memory, and confirmed by the text of his document, we confirm by apostolic authority, so that it may not be disturbed from its established condition by anyone’s rash attack or by the passage of time. [Col. 0216B]

By this present decree we also ordain that no one shall ever [Col. 0216C] hold a prebend in your church unless he is willing to serve it in person. Likewise, we forbid the chaplain acting in place of the lord who holds office for the time being to hold, together with that chaplaincy, a chapel or prebend of your church unless he has entirely ceased from the office of chaplain. We further add and forbid by apostolic authority that your prebends be divided; rather, they shall always remain entire.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole and intact, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. [Col. 0216D] We also forbid anyone ever to dare to impose new or undue exactions upon your church or its chaplains, or to burden your persons with unlawful commands and services, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. As a token of the protection received from the Roman Church, you shall pay one bezant each year to us and to our successors.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, should rashly attempt to contravene this page of our constitution, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour [Col. 0217A], and know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer, and be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Gualter, bishop of Albano. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy [Col. 0217B] Cross in Jerusalem. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, William, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. [Col. 0217C] I, Cinthius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Manfred, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Paris through the hand of Hermann, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of May [25 April], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLII. Privilege for the Church of Saint Peter at Douai. (Chartres, 29 April.)

[Miraeus, *Opera diplomatica*, III, 51.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HUGH, provost of the Church of Saint Peter at Douai, [Col. 0217D] and to his brethren, both present and future, who enter canonically: in perpetuity.

Just as no assent is to be granted to those who make unjust requests, so the petition of those seeking what is just ought not to be delayed. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Saint Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the same church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your [Col. 0218A] successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

From the gift of Robert, formerly bishop of Arras: the altar of Marcha-Gotranni, for the use of the canons serving God there, with all the rights of the bishop and his ministers reserved. From the gift of the same man: the altar of Saint Rictrude of Wasers, with its endowments, for the use of the same canons, free and unencumbered exactly as he granted it to you, with all revenues of the bishop and the customary dues of the archdeacon and his ministers reserved. When the priest of that place has died or has been reasonably removed, it shall be yours to provide another suitable priest and present him to the bishop of Arras, to whom he shall make his profession and promise obedience.

All the tithes [Col. 0218B] of your parish and all the offerings which Gerard, formerly bishop of Cambrai, granted for the use of the canons of your church while the bishoprics of Cambrai and Arras were still united, upon this condition: that no lay person shall ever govern your church or its property, but that it shall be administered solely by a provost who is a cleric and who is responsible for assigning prebends and arranging the other affairs of that church. We further will that the aforesaid church remain free and exempt from all provisioning obligations (*obsonia*) and every fiscal claim, as the same bishop decreed, reserving only, as in other abbeys, the jurisdiction of the bishop of Arras.

[Col. 0218C] From the gift of the aforementioned Robert, formerly bishop of Arras: the altars and churches of Saint Martin of Sin and Saint Remigius of Marca, with their endowments and appurtenances, for the use of the canons serving God there—every form of sale and exaction for disgraceful profit having been removed by the same bishop—to be possessed freely in perpetuity, as he reasonably granted them to you, with all cathedral revenues of the bishop and the customary dues of the archdeacon and his ministers reserved. When the priest of any aforesaid place has died or has been reasonably removed, you shall present another suitable priest to the bishop of Arras, to whom he shall make his profession and promise obedience; and thus he shall receive freely from the bishop’s hand the pastoral charge to be exercised among God’s people.

[Col. 0218D] Nevertheless, some among you shall make a point of attending the synod of Arras every year, unless they have been excused by the bishop’s favour.

The two chapels of Blessed Mary in the suburb of Douai, free and unencumbered, as your church is known hitherto to have possessed them lawfully.

With regard also to changing the prebends which have been lawfully established in your church from the goods of Provost Robert, Simon, and Gerard: the consent of any lay persons, contrary to the custom of that Church itself, shall by no means be admitted.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole and unimpaired, for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted [Col. 0219A], with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical justice of the diocesan bishop reserved.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, should rashly attempt to contravene this page of our constitution and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all [Col. 0219B] who preserve their rights for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Gualterius, bishop of Albano. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. [Col. 0219C] I, Albert, cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, William, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ado, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Boso, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Cinthius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. [Col. 0219D] I, Manfred, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Chartres through the hand of Hermann, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of May [29 April], in the eleventh indiction; in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLIII. Privilege for the Church of León. (Tours, 16 May.)

[Flórez, *España sagrada*, XXXV, 421.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother JOHN, bishop of León, and to his successors to be canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

Ecclesiastical authority has decreed that, in more serious affairs, recourse should be made to the Apostolic See as to the head and mother [Col. 0220A] of all. For she knows, through the depths of maternal charity, how to aid oppressed sons, and so to defend her own rights as also to take care that the fitting rights of others are preserved. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ John, bishop of León, we receive with due kindness your petitions and those of your Church, in order that we may preserve for the Church of León the right of freedom possessed from ancient times by long usage. For although it has flourished, illustrious and wealthy, among the other cities of Spain, it is nowhere recorded ever to have been subject to any metropolitan see. We therefore declare by the authority of this decree that this freedom of its own shall remain, in accordance with your petition, ratified, whole, and so secure that, if any deception has perhaps extracted from the occupations of the Apostolic See some enactment contrary to this [Col. 0220B] liberty, no prejudice against that liberty shall thereby be introduced.

For the benefit of liberty is fortified by every provision of the laws, so that it is exposed to no occasion of being overthrown. Therefore, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of good memory, Popes Paschal and Adrian, we decree by apostolic authority that you and your successors henceforth shall never be subject to any metropolitan, but only to the Roman pontiff; and that all who succeed you in that see shall be consecrated by the hands of the Roman pontiff as special suffragans of the Roman See. Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods that Church now possesses justly [Col. 0220C] and canonically, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with God’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors, and through you for that Church. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

Within the boundaries of Galicia: the archdeaconry containing the three castles, towers, Dancus, Cancellata, Valcarcer, and Navia; whatever right you possess in churches belonging to the monastery of Saint Facundus; whatever right the Church of León is known to possess in the Church of Saint Isidore and the churches belonging to it. Within the bishopric of Astorga: the village [Col. 0220D] called Canzanucos, with its churches. Within the bishopric of Palencia: the village called Bobada, the village called Abarca with its churches, and the churches of Capella. Within the bishopric of Oviedo: the village called Ovelgas with its church; the Church of Saint Martin of Fonte de Febro and the Church of Saint James; whatever right you possess in the Church of Saint Peter of Asloncia, the Church of Saint Michael of Escalada, and the church of the monastery of Vega; the monastery of Saint Claudius, founded upon the Church of León’s own hereditary estate; the castle of Coronio with all its appurtenances; the village called Villa Muzaref, with the *foderum* belonging to it.

Furthermore, those things which Alfonso, of illustrious memory, king of the Spains, and Berengaria his wife, with [Col. 0221A] their sons and his sister Sancha, offered or also acknowledged for the remission of their sins, from devotion to the Church of León, we, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Popes Eugene and Adrian, confirm by apostolic authority to you and your successors, and through you to that Church: namely, the tithes belonging to the bishopric of León in all villages contained within the bounds of that bishopric, which are known to pertain to the honour of Saint Pelagius and belonged to the dignity of the *infantazgo*; moreover, the villages in which these churches are founded—namely, the Church of Saint Michael of Escalada, Saint Peter of Aslonza, and the Church of Vega—excepting the monasteries in the city of León, namely the Church of Saint Saviour [Col. 0221B] outside the wall and the others within the wall, together with the village of Fresno in the valley of Uncina and the village of Saint Gervasius.

The rents or customary dues which the see of León has customarily received from the aforesaid churches shall be paid to that see by them in the accustomed manner. All these things are to be preserved for your future use, so that you ought lawfully to possess them henceforth, and may have your own agents in each village to receive the tithes.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be kept whole for the use and benefit in every way of you and of others for whose governance and support they were granted [Col. 0221C], with the authority of the Apostolic See in all things reserved. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly should rashly attempt to contravene this page of our constitution and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make amends by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who observe what is just for that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and, before [Col. 0221D] the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

“SHOW ME YOUR WAYS, O LORD.” (Place of the seal.)

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Gualterius, bishop of Albano. I, . . . , cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, . . . , cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. [Col. 0222A] I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa.

Given at Tours through the hand of Hermann, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of June [16 May], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLIV. Privilege for the Church of Saint John at Amiens. (Tours, 23 May.)

[Hugo, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, I, 694.]

[Col. 0222B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons EUSTACE, abbot of the Church of Saint John situated on the Selle, and to his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Those choosing the religious life ought to have apostolic protection at hand, lest an attack of any rashness should either turn them from their purpose or—God forbid!—weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Eugene of holy memory, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order which is known to have been established in that place according to God, the Rule of Blessed Augustine, and the institution of the Premonstratensian order shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now possesses justly and canonically [Col. 0222C], or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the benefactions of princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

[Col. 0222D] The altar of Marcel, with its tithe and appurtenances and endowed land; the free manor of Marcel, with the pastures of that territory; the tithe lawfully granted to you at Walbercurt; the altar of Saint Firmin; the altar of Saint Germanus; the field of Saint Germanus, with *terragium* and tithe; the manor of Bertricurt, in which your lay sisters dwell, with cemetery and the entire tithe, as has reasonably been granted to you; a fourth part of the territory of Long-Pré; half of Maresci; lordship over that same fourth part; the mill granted you by the lords of Pinchonio, and the manor belonging to that mill; the common use-right of Maresci; Hernencurtis; the course of the Selle descending from the aforesaid mill as far as the abbey and the brothers’ workshops; the pastures, [Col. 0223A] houses, and land of Ralph “who does not laugh,” with their appurtenances; the free manor of Ollaincurt, with its cultivated land and woodland use-rights; the whole tithe of Wattincurt, with its appurtenances and lands, which Girald of Petracloa, Gualterius, and their co-sharers gave you; the field of Uhuorum and the field of Saint Peter of Brihercurt; the field and enclosure of Saint Peter of Gaudiaco; a third part of the tithe of Hornast, with *terragium* and tithe; the tithe of Ultzabaiz; a sixth part of the tithe of Argovia, with two fields and the meadow situated there between the land and the stream; five fields of freehold land in the territory of Long-Pré, with *terragium* and tithe; the lands and tithes which you hold at Nointel; and six *modii* of wine to be paid to you annually; [Col. 0223B] the mill of Eures; the mill of Prato; the rent-paying mill granted by the chapter of Flaviacum; the manor of Septemvilla and the whole tithe of that territory, with pastures and woodland use-rights; a sixth part of all Septemvilla, which Jugelramnus Rufus gave you, together with a twelfth part of that territory granted to you by the Church of Aquicinum; the manor in Viconia called Valley of Houses, free from every exaction, with its pastures, woodland use-rights, and tithe; and the cultivation of eleven ploughlands in the same territory, with the whole tithe; the free manor called Guy’s Valley, with the lands which you possess in Viconia and in the territory of Mairia, together with lands, tithes, pastures, and woodland use-rights; the field of Stephen and the field of Maharavesne; a sixth part of the tithe of Saint Amand; the annual rents of lands and houses which you hold in diverse places; seventy-six *jugera* of land above the Somme, with *terragium*; [Col. 0223C] the free pastures of Argovia, with an eighth part of the marsh of Argovia, which Ralph of Haidincurt granted you; the free manor of Savières and the cultivation of its land, with pastures, woodland use-rights, and a third part of the tithe belonging to the altar together with another third part of that same tithe; the land granted you by Bernard of Baratangla in the territory of Baratangla; likewise the land given you by Arnulf Ferez and Ernold of Artois in the territory of Drihercurt; and also the land [Col. 0223D] and wood of Hernencurt, with *terragium* and tithe. Certainly, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; but that all things be preserved whole and unimpaired for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical justice of the diocesan bishop reserved. If [Col. 0224A] therefore in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly should rashly attempt to contravene this page of our constitution and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct his offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 0224B] I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given at Tours through the hand of Hermann, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends [Col. 0224C] of June [25 May], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLV. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims—Concerning the case pending between the Church of Saint Remigius and Dervensis, concerning a certain tithe. (Tours, 26 May.)

[Martène, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 691.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have recently learned from the complaint of the abbot and brethren of Saint Remigius that, although the case being litigated between them and the abbot of Dervensis concerning a certain [Col. 0224D] tithe of Franpas had formerly been debated at length in the presence of you and Samson, your predecessor, and appeal had often been made to our hearing concerning that case, the aforesaid abbot has been unwilling either to pursue the appeal or to render justice in any respect. Therefore, since by the office of apostolate entrusted to us we are debtors to all God’s faithful in the matter of their justice, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, within thirty days after you have been requested, you summon both parties before you and, after hearing and fully examining the arguments on both sides, decide the same case by means of justice, appeal set aside.

[Note: [Col. 0223D] Dervensis is an ancient and distinguished monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Châlons, founded by Saint Bertharius, and hitherto remains under the congregation of Saint-Viton, in French Montier-en-Der.]

[Col. 0225A] Furthermore, since, as we have learned from the complaint of the aforesaid abbot and brethren, the canons of Grand-Pré violently and unjustly carried off the body of the son of the count of that place, who, as they assert, had formerly been offered from his mother’s womb to the church of those brethren, we likewise command your discretion to admonish the aforesaid canons diligently and compel them strictly either to restore the removed body to the said brethren without any contradiction, or to reach with them a peaceful and amicable settlement concerning this matter, or to render them full justice in your presence.

Given at Tours, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June [26 May].

## CLVI. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Faith at Horsham. (Tours, 26 May.)

[*Monasticon Anglicanum*, I, 416.]

[Col. 0225B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERNARD, prior of the monastery of Saint Faith of Rosham, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Those choosing the religious life ought to have apostolic protection at hand, lest an attack of any rashness should either turn them from their purpose or—God forbid!—weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the protection of Blessed [Col. 0225C] Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that monastery now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

The village of Northam, with its people, lands, woods, pastures, and appurtenances, as Robert son of Walter and his sons gave it to you; and the hospital of the same village, which you hold from the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem, with wood and [Col. 0225D] all its appurtenances; that land of Kudda with all its appurtenances, which Sibyl, wife of the aforesaid Robert, gave you; the church of Horsford and the church of Bor. In London: the church of Saint Margaret, with all the lands which Robert son of Walter gave you as alms in that town; likewise the tithes of Abretuna, Sibetuna, Gulwerstunia, Colerbo, Relmigaham, Colostunia, Flemewrda, Wdetuna, Semera, Tikebzon, Thersham, Slortei, Cranesforda, Benges, Stramnigaham, Ludaham, Dalingaho, Stantuna, Sarlingaham, Sutburna, Adelingetuna, Ghor, Stilibi, Stocos, Hoa, Sothesham, and Wituella; the land of Odetuna; all the lands [Col. 0226A] and houses lawfully granted you as alms at Norwich and Great Yarmouth; the mill of Baldrusella; thirteen shillings at Kareseja and Buccheshala; the mill of Dalraforda; the land which Simon Pecchi gave you as alms; the land of Ralph of Berveswerda; the land which William of Chorzo gave you at Bischele; also the lands which William Bardulf gave you at Srecaham and Spicafurda; the land which Baldwin son of Guy gave you at Buchingaham; the land which Hugh of Duillers gave you at Kalaxaforda; the land of Nunterston which Richard son of Geoffrey gave you; the saltworks which William Strabo gave you at Kimnaham; the rent which Ralph son of Baldwin gave you; and the land of Rendringlat, which William of Bisnei gave you.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole and unimpaired for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical justice of the diocesan bishop reserved.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly should rashly attempt to contravene this page of our constitution and, having been warned a second [Col. 0226C] or third time, should fail to correct his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let him be subject, at the last judgment, to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. [Col. 0226D] I, Gualter, bishop of Albano. I, Ubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, William, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore.

Given at Tours, through the hand of Hermann, subdeacon and notary of the Holy [Col. 0227A] Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June [26 May], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLVII. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Bertin at Saint-Omer. (Tours, 26 May.)

[Collection of Cartularies, III, 333.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GOTHESCALC, abbot of Saint Bertin, and to his successors regularly appointed: in perpetuity.

“The order of justice and reason advises,” etc., as in the privilege of Pope Innocent written above, folio 240 verso and [Col. 0227B] following.

[Note: [Col. 0227] See volume CLXXIX of the *Patrologia*, under Innocent II, no. 398.]

Sealed with a circle around which is written: “SHOW ME YOUR WAYS, O LORD”; and in the middle of the said circle: “SAINT PETER. SAINT PAUL. POPE ALEXANDER III,” with the subscription that follows:

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia, etc.

Given at Tours, through the hand of Hermann, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June [26 May], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLVIII. He commands the abbess and nuns of Bourbourg not to receive for burial parishioners of the monastery of Saint Bertin at Saint-Omer. (Tours.)

[See Iperius, *Chronicle of Saint Bertin*, in Martène, *Thesaurus*, III, 654.]

[Col. 0227C]

## CLIX. Privilege for the Church of Saint Mary of Sniapes. (Tours, 26 May.)

[Rymer, *Foedera*, I, 23.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons W., prior, and the brethren of the Church of Saint Mary of Sniapes: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and that vows which do not depart from the path [Col. 0227D] of reason be fulfilled by effective action. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring with your just petitions in favourable assent, we confirm by apostolic authority to you, and through you to your Church, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the Church of Fressentum and the Church of Bedingefeld, with their appurtenances, and Brastanhae, which you now possess justly and canonically or may hereafter acquire by lawful means, with God’s favour. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or in any manner oppose it.

But should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation [Col. 0228A] of Almighty God and of His blessed Apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Tours, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June [26 May].

## CLX. To Dominic, abbot of the monastery of Saint Facundus at Sahagún: he grants “the power of binding and loosing in the town of Saint Facundus” and the use of the mitre. (Tours, 31 May.)

[Escalona, *History of Sahagún*, p. 541, on the testimony of Jaffé, *Regesta Romanorum Pontificum*, p. 692.]

## CLXI. To Hugh, Abbot of Saint-Germain-des-Prés at Paris—He decrees that the claim made by Maurice, bishop of Paris, in the Council of Tours against the immunity of the Abbey of Saint-Germain is not to be admitted and shall not prejudice its right or liberty. (Tours, 1 June.)

[D. Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 796.]

[Col. 0228B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HUGH, abbot of Saint-Germain at Paris: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When our venerable brother Maurice, bishop of Paris, and you were both present before us at the Council of Tours, the said bishop rose in the council and asserted that a certain right in your church reasonably belonged to him. But, considering how that church had from ancient times remained quietly and peacefully under the right and proprietorship of Blessed Peter, we were unwilling in any way to admit the bishop’s claim unless he showed that some one of our predecessors [Col. 0228C] had admitted it. Since he did not do so, and we do not think that he can do so, we decree by this present writing that the said bishop’s claim cannot in the future produce any interruption or any prejudice to the right and liberty of that church.

Given at Tours, on the Kalends of June [1 June].

## CLXII. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims—On behalf of R. of Corberio. (Tours, 3 June.)

[Martène, *Collectio*, II, 692.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Reims: [Col. 0228D] greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to our hearing that R. of Corberio, who for some time, in the habit of the brethren of the military Order of the Temple, served the heavenly King, resolved to transfer to the Cistercian brethren or another strict religious order, and firmly promised the same in our presence, is now somehow being drawn back from this intention and appears to be delaying that devout purpose. Therefore, by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood diligently to admonish the same R. and compel him to assume the habit of the aforesaid religious order, that he may worthily fulfil his vow. If he should perhaps scorn to do this before the next [Col. 0229A] feast of Saint John, you shall compel him by ecclesiastical censure.

Given at Tours, on the third day before the Nones of June [3 June].

## CLXIII. Privilege for the Monastery of Saint Salvius at Florence. (Tours, 5 June.)

[Lami, *Monumenta Ecclesiae Florentinae*, II, 1233.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Paul, abbot of the monastery of Saint Salvius, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Those who choose the religious life ought to enjoy apostolic protection, lest some assault of rashness either call them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously accede to your just requests; we take under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by lawful means through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors.

Following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Urban, Gregory, and Innocent, we decree that no archbishop, bishop, or other ecclesiastical or secular prelate—excepting the Vallombrosan congregation—may obtain any lordship over your church, as is known to have been established by those same predecessors of ours. Furthermore, just as the chapel of Saint Nicholas of Casa Arsa, belonging to your right, is known hitherto to have been exempt from every yoke of domination by bishop and parish priest, so we decree that it shall remain exempt hereafter as well. [Col. 0229B–C]

We likewise confirm to you the right which you have hitherto held in the hospital of Capraria. You may also receive into your monastery clerics and laymen fleeing the world, free and absolved, and retain them without any contradiction. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars, and ordinations of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to furnish these things freely and without improper exaction; otherwise, you may have recourse to whichever bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, may grant you what is requested.

We also grant that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that none may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; nevertheless, the canonical right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken shall be preserved. Moreover, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. [Col. 0229D–0230A]

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any exactions; rather, all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those for whom they were bestowed, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should attempt rashly to act against it, then, after a second and third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 0230A–B]

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Hubaldus, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed.  
I, Bernardus, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina, have subscribed.  
I, Gualterius, bishop of Albano, have subscribed.  
I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed.  
I, Henricus, cardinal-priest of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, have subscribed.  
I, Joannes, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed.  
I, Guillelmus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains, have subscribed.  
I, Hyacinthus, cardinal-deacon of Santa Maria in Cosmedin, have subscribed.  
I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed.  
I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of Saint Theodore, have subscribed.  
I, Boso, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed.  
I, Cinthius, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed.  
I, Petrus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa, have subscribed.  
I, Joannes, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in the Portico, have subscribed.  
I, Manfredus, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. [Col. 0230C–D]

Given at Tours, through the hand of Hermannus, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of June, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1163 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

“SHOW ME THY WAYS, O LORD.” (Place of the seal.)

## CLXIV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary at Sherborne. (Tours, 5 June.)

[Monastic. Anglic., I, 425.]

[Col. 0231A]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Clement, abbot of Blessed Mary of Sherborne, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Those who choose the religious life ought to enjoy apostolic protection, lest some assault of rashness either call them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously accede to your just requests; we take under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever goods and possessions that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the benefaction of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through God’s favor, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought it proper to specify the following by name:

Namely, the parish church of Saint Mary of Sherborne, which the same abbot holds as a prebend from Salisbury Church, with its chapels, lands, tithes, and appurtenances; lands, tenants, and rent-paying houses in the same town of Sherborne; Stapelbugg, with the church of that town, its chapels, lands, and all appurtenances; Weston with all its appurtenances; Horton, with the church of that town and the chapel of Onolton adjoining that church, together with lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; the chapel of the Holy Trinity at Watham, and rent-paying houses in that town, with lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Wymborne and rent-paying houses in that town; the portion of land and the chapel which you possess at Monerio of Kingeston; the church of Saint Mary Magdalene situated near Sherborne Castle, with the chapels of Saint Michael and Saint Probus and all its appurtenances; a mill in the town of Sherborne beside the chapel of Saint Andrew, and the fishpond adjoining that mill, together with tithes of all fishponds, both of eels and other fish, and the wine-tithe from the vineyard of the same town of Sherborne. [Col. 0231B–D]

The manor of Woborne, with the chapel of that town and its lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; Compton, and the other Compton, with chapels, tithes, and all appurtenances; the manor of Ehorneford, with chapel, lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; the manor of Bradford, with the church of that town and chapels, lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; Wyca and Loscumbe, with all appurtenances; Dalthestoke, with the church of that town and its chapels, lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; Corunduna and Rhistherstoke, with all appurtenances; Corescumbe and the church of that town, with chapels, lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; Lym, with the church of that town and chapels, lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; Seton, with the church of that town, chapels, lands, tithes, saltworks, and all appurtenances; Lytheleham, with the church of that town and its lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; Bromlega and Stiwtke, with all appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Cadweli, with chapels, lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; the church of Saint Ismael of Pennalt, with lands, tithes, and all appurtenances; and the church of Saint Eltwyc of Penbyay, with lands, tithes, and all appurtenances. [Col. 0232A–B]

Upon the death of yourself, now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be placed over it by any craft of intrigue or by violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the judgment of the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Saint Benedict. We decree also that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that none may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, saving, nevertheless, the right of the parish churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. [Col. 0232B–C]

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those for whom they were bestowed, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should attempt rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. [Col. 0232C–D]

Given at Tours, through the hand of Hermannus, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of June, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1163 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLXV. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—Exhortation to make provisions for the Roman curia. (Tours, 5 June.)

[MARTEN., Coll., II, 692.]

[Col. 0233A]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, Archbishop of Reims: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that your prudent discernment is unaware how our brother archbishops, bishops, and abbots dwelling around you have hitherto provided for us and our curia in necessary supplies. Therefore, because among the others we place particular hope and confidence in you, we command and earnestly admonish your brotherhood by apostolic letters to make diligent efforts to exhort your suffragan bishops and all abbots established throughout your province to make proper provisions for us and our brethren, so that we may receive them suitably and profitably from now until the first feast of Saint James; thus we shall rightly be bound to commend your devotion in the Lord. [Col. 0233A–B]

Given at Tours, on the Nones of June.

## CLXVI. To the same and his suffragans.—Exhortation to make provisions for the pope and his brethren. (Tours, 5 June.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 0233C]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren Henry, Archbishop of Reims, and his suffragan bishops, and to his beloved sons, all abbots and priors established throughout his archbishopric: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

The greater the confidence which we hold in all things concerning your sincerity and devotion, the more confidently do we invite you to matters which are expedient for us and our brethren. Accordingly, by apostolic letters we ask and admonish all of you to take care, with ready diligence, to attend to making proper provisions for us and for those same brethren of ours, and to endeavor profitably to send them to us by the coming feast of Saint James, so that we may be bound worthily to commend your devotion in the Lord. If any among you, beloved sons, abbots and priors, should perhaps neglect to do this, we shall, by the Lord’s authority, hold valid the sentence which the aforesaid archbishop shall canonically pronounce against you on this account. [Col. 0233C–D]

Given at Tours, on the Nones of June.

## CLXVII. Privilege for the church of Geneston. (Tours, 8 June.)

[MORICE, *Mém. pour servir à l’hist. de Bret.*, I, col. 649.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Clement, prior of the church of Geneston, and his brethren, present and future, to be canonically appointed: for perpetual remembrance.

A pious petition ought to be fulfilled with a favoring disposition, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the requested benefit may undoubtedly gain strength. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously accede to your just requests; we take under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, we decree that the canonical order which is established there according to God and the Rule of Saint Augustine, together with the institutions reasonably established in that church by our venerable brother Bernard, bishop of Nantes, with the consent of the canons of Saint Mary Magdalene, shall be preserved for all time. [Col. 0234A–B]

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess by gift or grant of that bishop and other faithful persons, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of pontiffs, benefactions of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through God’s favor, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought it proper to specify the following by name: Genestum, where your church is situated, with its appurtenances, by gift of Bernard, bishop of Nantes; the church of Montebert with its appurtenances; the church of Saint John of Boisel with its appurtenances, by gift of Mauritius Herveus and Willelmus Normandeli; whatever right you possess in the land called Petra-Stulta, by gift of Herveus Hoaut and his son Mauritius; half the houses at Landes of Pomeria, by gift of Rainaldus Matacrei; half a quarter of land in the *masura* and whatever right you possess, by gift of the same Rainaldus and Govenus of Paluel, in the heathlands extending from Petra-Lata to Genestosum; whatever right Paganus, son of Aliscia, possessed in the parish of Rezaio, by his gift; the place of Saint Lucian with its appurtenances, by gift of Matthias Herveus and Simon Judicaelis; and the land and vineyards which you possess in the parish of the port of Saint Peter, by gift of the cleric Rollandus and his daughter Landescia. [Col. 0234B–C]

Moreover, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the sustenance of your animals. We also grant that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that none may oppose the devotion of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; nevertheless, the canonical right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken shall be preserved. [Col. 0234D]

We decree, therefore, that no one may disturb the aforesaid church, take away, retain, or diminish its possessions, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those for whom they were bestowed, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should attempt rashly to act against it, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. [Col. 0235A]

Thus subscribed: I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, etc. [Col. 0235B]

Given at Tours, through the hand of Hermannus, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Ides of June, in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1163 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLXVIII. Concerning the priest Odo, harassed by the bishop of Paris. (Tours, 8 June.)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXI, 979.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother [Hugh], bishop of Soissons: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

From the complaint of the priest Odo, bearer of these letters, we have learned that, when our venerable brother the bishop of Paris (Maurice) accused him of a certain crime and deprived him of office and benefice, he harshly extended his hand, through himself and his officials, to Odo’s property. Since we wish to support him in his right, as he has repeatedly appealed to us, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to approach the said bishop, so that he may either restore everything taken from the aforesaid priest, or make a peaceful and amicable settlement with him concerning these matters, or render him complete justice in your presence. Accordingly, when you have been requested in this matter, summon both parties before you; after carefully hearing and considering the arguments on both sides, decide the case, without appeal, within twenty days after receipt of these letters, justice being administered. [Col. 0235C–D]

Given at Tours, on the fifth day before the Ides of June.

## CLXIX. To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—On the canonization of Saint Anselm. (Tours, 9 June.)

[WARTON, *Anglia sacra*, II, 177.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our venerable brother Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

Formerly, when you stood in our presence, you humbly and devoutly asked us to canonize that man of holy memory, Anselm, formerly Archbishop of Canterbury, whose life and venerable miracles you took care to present to us at the Council of Tours. But because many had gathered there who were urgently asking the same thing on behalf of other holy men, we judged that [what] you had requested should be deferred.

Now, however, having full confidence in your integrity and prudence in all matters, we entrust this business to your care and discernment. By apostolic letters we command you to summon before you our brother bishops, your suffragans, together with the abbots and other religious persons established in your province; and, when the life of the aforesaid holy man has been read before them all and the series of his miracles publicly set forth, to proceed, supported by our authority, concerning his canonization, with the counsel and assent of the assembled brethren, according to what you find determined in their counsel. Know that, by the Lord’s authority, we shall hold valid and firm whatever you and the said brethren decide should be established in this matter. [Col. 0236A–B]

Given at Tours, on the fifth day before the Ides of June.

## CLXX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Martin of Canigó. (Tours, 10 June.)

[AGUIRRE, *Concil. Hisp.*, III, 375.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Raimundus, abbot of the monastery of Saint Martin of Canigó, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made to us which is recognized as consonant with reason and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and afford appropriate support to the desires of those who ask. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we accede to your just requests; we take under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Saint Martin of Canigó, which indeed belongs by right and ownership to Saint Peter, following the example of our predecessor of happy memory, Pope Sergius, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been established in that monastery according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict shall be observed inviolate in times to come. [Col. 0236C]

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, benefactions of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through God’s favor, shall remain secure and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought it proper to specify the following by name: the place given to you by Count Guifredus of good memory, where the monastery itself is situated, with its tithes, first-fruits, and every liberty belonging to it; the village of Verneto, with its boundaries and appurtenances; the village of Odolo, with its boundaries and appurtenances; and whatever Count Guifredus or other faithful of Christ bestowed upon the aforesaid monastery in the village and parish of Marchexanes; the church of Saint Vincent of Elz, with its tithes, first-fruits, freeholds, and offerings. [Col. 0236D–0237A]

Estates, possessions, and freeholds in the parish of Saint Mary of Marcevol; in the parish of Saint Eulalia of Arbosols; in the parish of Saint Columba of Triliano; in the parish of Saint Stephen of Saorra; in the parish of Saint Eulalia of Foliano; in the parish of Saint Martin of Ascaro; in the parish of Saint James of Anyer; in the parish of Belloloco; in the parish of Saint Cosmas of Sagdaniano; and in the parish of Saint Marcellus of Flucano. The freeholds which you possess in Celrano, Aureliano, and Guissano, with all their appurtenances; the estates which you possess in the village of Eona and in the parish of Saint Stephen of Egued, in the parish of Saint Columba of Avidano, in the parish of Saint Saturninus of Targuesona, in the parish of Saint Vincent of Villa-Alta, in the parish of Edorres, in the parish of Saint Genesius of Ezerr, in the parish of Saint Leocadia of Darnacollecta, in the parish of Saint Julian of Estanar, and in the village of Bajanda; in the parish of Saint Martin of Ix, in the parish of Saint Vincent of Exaneda, in the parish of Saint Martin of Arao, and in the parish of Saint Stephen of Euvils. [Col. 0237A–B]

The church of Saint Faith of Taltorta, with all its appurtenances; whatever right you possess in the parish of Saint Peter of Alp, the parish of Saint Mary of Mosoll, the parish of Saint Lawrence of Adas, and the parish of Saint Saturninus of Faustiniano; the tithes, first-fruits, and rights which you possess in the church and parish of Saint Martin of Casafabra; freeholds and possessions in the parish of Saint Stephen of Illa; and, in the parish of Pontiliano, the church of Saint Romanus with all its appurtenances; estates, possessions, and freeholds in the parish of Saint Martin of Caneto, and in the village of Saint Lawrence, the village of Saint Felix, the parish of Corbera, and the parish of Saint Eulalia of Millars; and, further, whatever right you possess in the counties of Besalú, Cerdanya, Conflent, Roussillon. [Col. 0237B–C]

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, ordinations of monks or clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, the abbot’s blessing, and the other ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor of the Apostolic See, and is willing to furnish them freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, may grant what is requested. We also grant that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that none may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, saving the right of the mother church and of other churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. [Col. 0237D]

Upon the death of yourself, now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be placed over it by any craft of intrigue or by violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the judgment of the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Saint Benedict. Furthermore, as our aforesaid predecessor Pope Sergius is known to have established, so we likewise decree that the aforesaid monastery shall be subject to no one except the Roman pontiff alone. As a sign of this liberty received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay one *morabatin* to us and our successors each year. [Col. 0238A]

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations. Rather, all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those for whom they were bestowed, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should attempt rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to severe vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen. [Col. 0238B–C]

## CLXXI. Concerning the Count of Auvergne, whom he absolved because he considered this not unwelcome to the king. For he would never do anything that could displease him. (Tours, 10 June.)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXI, 1014.]

[Col. 0239A]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ Louis, illustrious King of the Franks: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

While we were still present at Paris, we recall that we firmly assured Your Highness that we would never knowingly wish to do anything that ought to prejudice the honor of royal majesty. Therefore, although we recently absolved the Count of Auvergne, when he was present before us, we nevertheless took such precaution in this matter that we believed we were properly consulting both our honor and yours, and also providing beneficially for the Church of Brioude.

For he did not deserve to be absolved by us until, having touched the sacred Gospels, he had sworn a bodily oath that he would firmly accept and observe our command both concerning the restoration of his daughter to her husband and concerning the redress of the injury inflicted upon the Church of Brioude. Therefore we immediately commanded him, under the binding force of that oath, to restore his daughter to the husband from whom he had taken her and to surrender all the goods of the Church of Brioude which had fallen either to him or to his men. [Col. 0239A–B]

Moreover, the aforesaid count declared that he had not himself principally attacked the said Church of Brioude, but had assisted his nephew; and we have not yet absolved that nephew, nor shall we absolve him or his accomplices hereafter until he has made full satisfaction. For, as we have said, we are firmly resolved and determined that in matters which we know to be serious to you, we shall by no means proceed without consulting you. If at any time through ignorance we should do anything contrary to this, we shall not hesitate, with appropriate discernment, to amend what we know displeases so great a prince. [Col. 0239B–C]

Given at Tours, on the fourth day before the Ides of June.

## CLXXII. To Peter, dean, and the chapter of Saint Anian of Orléans.—He confirms the decision issued by the abbot of Saint Benedict concerning the church of Saint Germanus, disputed between the bishop of Orléans and the canons of Saint Anian. (Tours, 10 June.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 798.]

[Col. 0239D]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Peter, dean, and the whole chapter of the church of Blessed Anian: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

We remember that we committed to A[raldus], abbot of Saint Benedict of good memory, the case between you and the bishop of Orléans (Manasses), concerning the dispossession of the church of Blessed Germanus—which you complained had been despoiled of its parishioners—and the presentation of the priest of that church; and we took care to set out by apostolic letters how he ought to proceed in that case.

But, as we have learned from the tenor of that abbot’s letters, he received your witnesses and took care to reinvest the aforesaid church of Saint Germanus with its parishioners, according to the form of our letters. We have also learned fully from the wording of his writing that he received witnesses concerning the free appointment of the priest in the same church, according to the command of the Apostolic See; and that, regarding both matters, he took care to authenticate what he did and the witnesses’ depositions by his own letters and seal.

We therefore hold valid what was done by the same abbot, confirm it by apostolic letters, and decree that what is contained in his authenticated document shall remain valid and unshaken for all time. [Col. 0240A]

Given at Tours, on the third day before the Ides of June.

Given at Tours, on the fourth day before the Ides of June.

## CLXXIII. To Stephen, bishop of Meaux.—Against Josolius of Rebais, who had arranged for sacred rites contrary to the bishop’s interdict. (Tours, 11 June.)

[LAUNOII, *Opera*, III, II, 408.]

[Col. 0240B]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Stephen, bishop of Meaux: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

When you and our beloved son B., abbot of Rebais, appeared together in our presence, we heard the case between you concerning the subjection and liberty of the monastery of Rebais and concerning the presentation of the chaplain of the church of Saint John. You maintained that the chaplain to be appointed in that church ought to be presented to you, so that he might receive from you the care of souls. [Col. 0240B–C]

The aforesaid abbot, replying that he had free disposal of the appointment of that chaplain, wholly denied that his presentation in any way pertained to you. And when various arguments had been advanced on both sides, we learned more fully from his own confession that the chaplain of that church had been presented by his predecessor to your predecessor and had received from him the care of souls. He further added that he himself had presented Josolius to you as chaplain to be appointed in that church. Therefore, since you delayed accepting him because you wished first to deliberate on the matter with your archdeacon, the abbot, as though exercising a liberty of his own, appointed him in that church on his own authority; and after you had reasonably pronounced against him a sentence of interdict and excommunication for this reason, he caused him there to celebrate the divine offices. We therefore, holding from his confession, as we have said, that you were in possession of that right of presentation, decree by the authority of the Apostolic See, with the common counsel of all our brethren, that the aforesaid chaplain, because he presumed to celebrate the divine offices contrary to your interdict, shall not in future presume to celebrate the divine offices either in the aforesaid church or in any other church of your bishopric, unless he may mercifully obtain this by your consent; without prejudice, however, to the right of his monastery, should it prove that it possesses against you any right both concerning the presentation of that chaplain itself and concerning its other liberties.

### CLXXIV. To Louis, king of the Franks.—He sends him the bishop of Meaux with instructions. He announces his intention of proceeding to Bourges.  
*(Tours, 11 June.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 1024.]

[Col. 0241A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, LOUIS, illustrious king of the Franks, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since we cannot always enjoy the presence of your Highness as we desire, so as to explain to you orally what we wish, it is necessary sometimes to arrange that the tenor of our will be conveyed to royal Majesty through one of our brethren, and that your answer upon it be awaited through a reliable messenger or by letter. At present, however, because we have been unable without difficulty to send away from us any of our brethren the cardinals, we have determined to communicate to you through our venerable brother the bishop of Meaux and our beloved son P., dean of Saint-Aignan of Orléans, certain matters which we desire you to hear attentively; and through that same dean we likewise seek the reply and counsel of your royal Serenity concerning them. Moreover, we wish Your Excellency to know that, unless some necessary cause compels us to alter our plan, we have resolved, God willing, shortly to proceed to Bourges and to remain there for some time. Therefore, by these apostolic letters, we ask, admonish, and exhort Your Magnificence in the Lord diligently to warn the people of that place that they should grant free access to all who wish to come there with what they need, and should render to us and our court due reverence and honour.

Given at Tours, the third Ides of June [11 June].

### CLXXV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Vite.  
*(Tours, 12 June.)*

[HUGO, *Annales Praemonstratenses*, II, Preface, p. 695.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons DOMINIC, abbot of the church of Blessed Mary of Vite, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life in Spain.

Since without the worship of true religion neither can the unity of charity endure nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it is fitting that we, insofar as divine grace has granted us power, establish in all churches a form of religion pleasing to God and preserve with exact diligence that which has been established.
