Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we take under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order known to have been established in your church according to the fear of God, the Rule of Blessed Augustine, and the institutions of the brethren of Prémontré, shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, by grants of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify among them the following by their proper names:

Namely, by the gift of Alfonso, king of the Spains of illustrious memory, and the grant of our venerable brother John, bishop of Osma: the place in which the abbey itself was founded, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Cubillas with its appurtenances; the grange called Aleoba of Brazacurta, with its appurtenances; the grange called Guma, with its appurtenances; the houses which you have at Bibilla, with their appurtenances; the house which you have at Cabanas, with its appurtenances; the monastery of Blessed Mary of Tortoles, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Julian of Ulmo, with its appurtenances; by the gift of Peter John, a house at Maderol; by the gift of Brother Dominic, a house at Ayllón near Saint Martin, with its appurtenances, and the grange at Talamonea called the King’s Tower (*Turris Regis*), with its appurtenances.

Furthermore, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you from your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the fodder of your animals. You may also receive into conversion free and unencumbered clerics or laymen fleeing the world, and retain them in your community. Providing with paternal concern for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone from daring, within the enclosure of your places or granges, to commit violence, robbery, or theft, or to seize a person; and if anyone rashly presumes to do this, let him be judged a sacrilegious person and punished by ecclesiastical penalty. We also grant that the burial-place of that site shall be free, so that no one may hinder the devotion and last wishes of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; saving nevertheless the rights of the mother church and the parish churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

[Col. 0242D] Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved unimpaired and entire for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Walter, bishop of Albano. I, Ubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Cinthius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in the Portico.

Given at Tours through the hand of Herman, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the second Ides of June [12 June], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### CLXXVI. He confirms the congregation of Piacenza, founded by the late Bishop Sigefrid, and the brethren’s right to elect an archpriest.  
*(Tours, 15 June.)*

[CAMPI, *Storia di Piacenza*, II, 359.]

[Col. 0243C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the archpriest of the congregation of Piacenza and all the chaplain-brethren of that congregation, both present and future, in perpetuity.

Considering the devotion and faith which you are known to have shown toward the most holy Roman Church and ourselves, especially in the time of schismatic persecution, we admit all the more willingly the devout petitions of your whole community because we recognize that greater advantages have thereby accrued to us and to the universal Church from the constancy of your sincerity. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just requests, we confirm by apostolic authority for you and your successors, and fortify by the protection of this present writing, the establishment of your congregation reasonably ordered by Sigefrid, formerly bishop of Piacenza, of blessed memory, and the beneficially instituted election of the archpriest of that congregation at the discretion of the brethren, as it is known to have been observed from the time of the aforesaid bishop until now. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Tours, the seventeenth day before the Kalends of July [15 June].

### CLXXVII. To [Pons], archbishop of Narbonne, [Artald], bishop of Elne, and [Pons], bishop of Carcassonne.—He rebukes them for harassing the monastery of Crassé with unjust exactions.  
*(Tours, 17 June.)*

[MARTENE, *Thesaurus anecdotorum*, I, 463.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren the archbishop of Narbonne and the bishops of Elne and Carcassonne, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us that, contrary to the tenor of the privileges of the Roman Church, you are burdening with unlawful exactions the churches belonging to the right of the monastery of Crassé. You also refuse to grant that monastery chrism, holy oil, and the other ecclesiastical sacraments without payment. Therefore, since this is dishonourable and alien to the episcopal office, by apostolic writings we command your brotherhoods that, if this is so, you shall no longer on any pretext unlawfully molest the churches of the aforesaid monastery of Crassé, nor presume to demand anything from that monastery for chrism or other ecclesiastical sacraments.

Given at Tours, the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July [17 June].

### CLXXVIII. He takes the monastery of Saints Facundus and Primitivus of Sahagún under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges.  
*(At Cormary, 19 June.)*

[ESCALONA, *Historia de Sahagún*, cited by JAFFÉ, *Regesta Romanorum pontificum*, 693.]

[Col. 0244C]

### CLXXIX. To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—Concerning the absolution of a certain man.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 24 June.)*

[MARTENE, *Collectio*, II, 667.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since the bearer of this letter was held excommunicate by your predecessor of blessed memory, as he asserts, without any reasonable cause, and since, if we remember rightly, we gave him letters of absolution when he then came into our presence; and since our beloved son O., cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, then legate of the Apostolic See, learned from our letters that he had been absolved, and, as we have learned from his report, commanded your aforesaid predecessor that he should in no way regard him as excommunicated, since he had been absolved by our authority: nevertheless, as the aforesaid D. has told us, you are attempting to return him to the same sentence. Therefore, because we have complete confidence in your discernment in all things, and because it is not fitting for your uprightness to oppose in any way what has been done by us, we ask, admonish, and command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to hold valid the same absolution granted by us, and always to take care to love him with paternal charity, so that God may not be offended in this matter and we may deservedly commend your devotion in the Lord.

Given at the monastery of Déols [Note: [Col. 0245D] The monastery of Déols, or Bourg-Dieu, was a notable monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Bourges, [Col. 0246D] not far from the town of Châtre, which in the preceding century passed to secular canons.], the eighth day before the Kalends of July [24 June].

### CLXXX. Privilege for the monastery of Gixal.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 25 June.)*

[FLÓREZ, *España sagrada*, XLV, 338.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERENGAR, abbot of the monastery of Gixal, and his brethren, both present and future, to be regularly appointed in perpetuity.

A devout request ought to be fulfilled by an effective result, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit requested may undoubtedly obtain force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we assent to your just requests; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Urban of happy memory, we receive under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the monastery of Guixal, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify these by the following proper names:

The church of Saint Mary of Fenals; the freehold called the village of Magno; the freehold of Catiano, or Peruls; the freehold of Locustaria, with the holding called Prat and all its appurtenances; the freeholds of Penedos and Spanedat; the freehold of Rodegario; the freehold of the valley of Aradi, together with the *fexa* which belonged to Countess Richelis; the freehold in the parish of Saint Martin of Romaniano; the donations which Bishop Arnaulf, Almoricus, Gaufred, Vitalis, and Bernard, son of the aforesaid Gaufred, bestowed upon our church, together with the vineyards which they held through Saint Felix; the tithes and first-fruits of the valley of Aradi and the village of Mordanici, and of the newly broken lands made in the freehold of Saint Felix from the day when Barcelona was captured until the present time; as, by the grant of Bishop Rogarius and the canons of the church of Girona, there were granted to you houses and possessions in Barcelona and its territory; the houses which you have in the city of Girona; the freeholds and possessions of Quartiano; the freeholds and possessions of Lofrid; the tithes and first-fruits in the village of Olivis and in the valley of Aradi; the tithes of all fish caught from Conarglum to Saint Leontius; the freehold of Fanals; eighteen holdings with their appurtenances; the freehold which belonged to Count Suniarius; another freehold at Colonico; the freehold which belonged to Bertrand Arnali; the freeholds of Vilar and Versus; the freehold within the same parish; the freeholds of the village of Romani, of the slippery valley of Torredella, of Palacio Trusels of Lofrid, of Buada, Fontanilies, Aguils, Pedrinians, Pubal, Val de Durqueres, Vals, and Palacio Ravani.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of deception or violence, except the person whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of them, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. Therefore, we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all things shall be preserved unimpaired and entire for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he corrects his presumption by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, subscribe. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore.

Given at the monastery of Déols, through the hand of Hermantius, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of July [25 June], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### CLXXXI. To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—Concerning O., a monk.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 3 July.)*

[MARTENE, *Collectio*, II, 668.]

[Col. 0247A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his brother HENRY, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The examples of the Lord and Saviour urge us to devote ourselves to works of mercy and to provide compassionately for those fallen through human frailty; and the office of charity requires it. Therefore, on behalf of O., bearer of this letter, who professed the monastic life in your monastery [Note: [Col. 0247] Is this Clairvaux, in which Henry had formerly professed the monastic life, or some monastery in his diocese?], but later departed from its cloister owing to his own instability, we ask and admonish your discernment that, for mercy’s sake and out of reverence for Saint Peter and ourselves, you receive him back into your monastery, without prejudice, however, to the discipline of the monastic order, and no longer allow him to wander outside the cloister into the jaws of the cunning enemy.

Given at the monastery of Déols, the fifth Nones of July [3 July].

### CLXXXII. To the same.—Concerning certain citizens of Arras.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 7 July.)*

[Ibidem.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Continually recognizing by the effect of deeds the fervour of your most sincere devotion toward the most holy Roman Church, and especially toward our person, we have the desire and will to embrace you, as our dearest brother and a principal member of the Church, with the arms of all affection, and to seek with still greater ardour your honour and advantage. Although we had fully intended to dismiss from our presence by every means G., J., R., a certain woman with them named R., and their other companions, citizens of Arras, who for a long time have followed us and our court, urgently offering proof concerning the defamation of their reputation, yet, because we must take the greatest care lest we acquit the guilty and condemn the innocent, and because we wish to defer to your brotherhood, we have thought fit to postpone the affair until we may more fully avail ourselves of the counsel and deliberation of you, your church, and our brother bishops of the kingdom of France. Meanwhile we send the said citizens back to their homes, on the condition that, when summoned by us, they must come into our presence and receive and firmly observe our judgment and that of the Church without any contradiction.

Therefore, we earnestly ask your brotherhood to investigate the matter through those persons to whom the life and conduct of these citizens are most fully known, and to take care to report it to us, so that, informed alike by your counsel and that of your church and of our other brother bishops, we may proceed usefully in this business, with the Lord as author. Since, moreover, we neither wish nor deem it fitting that the aforesaid citizens should suffer in the meantime any loss or danger in their persons or possessions, we command your brotherhood to notify your citizens that they must not presume to inflict upon their persons or goods any harm or injury.

Given at the monastery of Déols, on the Nones of July [7 July].

### CLXXXIII. He announces that the monks of Saint-Maximin have been dispersed among monasteries and others appointed in their place.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 11 July.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 1026.]

[Col. 0248B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, LOUIS, illustrious king of the Franks, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The care of apostolic administration compels us to provide for all holy places, and especially for those to which the excellence of your Highness urges us to attend. Moved by this consideration, we have dispersed among different monasteries the monks of Saint-Maximin, whose manner of life of excessive disgrace and the murder of their own abbot had brought them into ill repute; and, at your request, we have taken care, with the Lord’s aid, to appoint others there. We commend these men to Your Highness and earnestly ask that, out of reverence for Saint Peter and ourselves, you uphold, love, and honour them, foster, protect, and defend them in their rights; and that you strictly compel A., provost of Mecho, together with his mother and sister, either to restore to Henry, a monk of that monastery, the grain and many other things which he deposited with them, or to render full justice in your presence.

Given at the monastery of Déols, the fifth Ides of July [11 July].

### CLXXXIV. To Louis, king of the Franks.—He sends messengers with instructions concerning matters received from the emperor of Constantinople.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 14 July.)*

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 1005.]

ALEXANDER, etc., to his dearest son in Christ LOUIS, etc.

When we reflect and recall how, for the cause of God and love of justice, and also out of reverence for Saint Peter, prince of the apostles, you have embraced the cause of the Church as your own and, as a Catholic king and most Christian prince, have promoted it beyond the other princes of the world for its increase and exaltation, we are brought to this purpose and intention: that in any matter of that Church which is of some importance, we shall in no way proceed without the counsel and assistance of Your Serenity, when we are able to have them. For we believe—indeed, we hold as certain truth—that, no less than we ourselves or any of our brethren, you are solicitous and zealous, solely for the sake of the heavenly Creator, for the honour and advancement of the Church, and labour with earnest endeavour for its exaltation.

Accordingly, having recently received letters from the envoys of our dearest son, . . . ., illustrious emperor of Constantinople, who arrived at Saint-Gilles, we have thought fit to send them to Your Royal Serenity. They contain, indeed, that certain matters fit to be stated and directed toward advantage are, on his behalf, to be proposed only to us and to your Church. We send to Your Royal Highness our beloved sons P., chaplain, and Brother H., our almoner, most faithful and devoted to Your Excellency. Through them we set before Your Serenity certain things about the same matter which we have not thought fit to commit to writing, and upon which we await your counsel. We earnestly ask that, receiving them with royal kindness, you hear them graciously and disclose by your letters, through the same men, your counsel concerning what they shall propose to you. Also, at our request, send some persons from your side with our aforesaid sons to the said emperor’s envoys, so that they may provide them safe escort through your land as far as your and our presence.

[Col. 0249C] Given at the monastery of Déols, on the Ides of July [15 July].

### CLXXXV. Confirmation of the sworn peace between the church of Cluny, the count of Forez, and the barons of the land; and remission of one year of penance for those who keep that peace.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 18 July.)*

[*Bibliotheca Cluniacensis*, Appendix, p. 157.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the noble men HUGH of Belloloco and his sons; the count of Forez; the viscount of Mâcon, JOHN GROSSO; HUGH DE BERZ; HUGH DE SCALCEO; and all others who shall preserve the sworn peace of the church of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Both the advantage of the present life and an abundant increase of eternal blessedness come to you if you diligently cherish peace, and especially if you keep and preserve it inviolate with the holy churches. For just as it is shown to be impossible for anyone to please God without peace, so it cannot happen that the fruit of peace becomes worthless in those who take care to preserve it: rather, it brings them here most welcome benefits and obtains for them in the future the reward of eternal sweetness. Therefore, since in the deep inward affection of paternal charity we desire both blessings for you, we ask, admonish, and exhort your nobility in the Lord by apostolic letters, and enjoin this upon you for the remission of your sins: hold entirely firm and unchangeable what you have done concerning the peace of the church of Cluny, and devote yourselves to fostering and extending that peace. Labour earnestly and with the utmost diligence, so that through what you do for the good of peace you may, God willing, attain the joys of eternal rest.

Moreover, relying upon the mercy of God and the merits of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, we remit one year of that penance which you received humbly with contrite and compuncted heart, just as we do for those who seek Jerusalem, both to you and to other successors who keep continual peace with the aforesaid church of Cluny, its dependent churches, and ecclesiastical persons.

[Col. 0250B] Given at the monastery of Beroien. [read: Déols], the fifth day before the Kalends of August [28 July].

### CLXXXVI. To the Cluniacs.—Concerning the dean and clerics of Saint Maurice of Tours.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 20 July.)*

[MARTENE, *Collectio*, II, 669.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons [Note: [Col. 0249D] Stephen, who was substituted in the place of Hugh, deposed in 1161.] S., abbot, and the brethren of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved sons, the dean and canons [Note: [Col. 0249D] That is, of the cathedral church, which is dedicated to Saint Maurice and has hitherto acknowledged him as its patron, although it is commonly called after Saint Gatianus.] of Saint Maurice of Tours, have informed us that a dispute is pending between you and them concerning certain possessions situated at Tournon on the Marne. They ask that it be entrusted by us to our venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, to be heard and duly settled. But, providing with paternal concern for your peace and tranquillity, we counsel and command your whole community to strive more earnestly and labour with all diligence to reach a peaceful settlement with them.

If you cannot settle with them, then at the next feast of Saint Luke you shall appear before us, prepared to render and receive full justice; or you shall submit to the judgment of the aforesaid archbishop, accept without the impediment of appeal whatever he judges in the matter, and observe it. Whichever of these alternatives you prefer, notify the same canons in writing within twenty days after receipt of this letter, so that they also may instruct and prepare themselves usefully for its execution.

Given at the monastery of Déols, the thirteenth day before the Kalends of August [20 July].

### CLXXXVII. To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—Concerning the affair of the church of Châlons.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 22 July.)*

[Ibidem, col. 670.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From examination of your letters we have learned that both you and your church, together with the suffragans of your church, are applying yourselves and zealously striving for the advancement and exaltation of the church of Châlons. We ourselves also devote ourselves most earnestly to this, by reason of the duty of our office, and shall give suitable assistance at the proper time. We have nevertheless delayed proceeding thus far in the matter because we learned more fully that the will of our dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks, did not at all accord with your will in this affair. Therefore, we have thought fit to defer the matter until the next feast of Saint Luke, so that within that interval we may learn the king’s will concerning it and more conveniently consider what will serve the benefit and advancement of the said church.

Meanwhile it will be your task to incline the mind of that king toward this and soften it with gentle words. Yet we wish you confidently to trust and hope that, when that time has arrived, we shall take care to apply prompt diligence both to this matter and to the other concerns advantageous to your honour; and, with the Lord as author, we shall bring them, insofar as justice and reason permit, to a useful outcome with honour to you. Furthermore, because our beloved son the abbot [Note: [Col. 0251D] He appears to be Godfrey, abbot of Saint-Bertin, successor of Leonius, who was present at Tours when Alexander held a council there, according to John of Ypres, *Chronicle*, chap. 44.] of Saint-Bertin served us very honourably and devotedly, and his church is known to be greatly burdened, we ask your brotherhood to remit, at our intervention, one of the two procurations which we have learned were imposed upon him.

Given at the monastery of Déols, the eleventh day before the Kalends of August [22 July].

### CLXXXVIII. Having enumerated individually the estates of the church of Burgos, he confirms all of them and decrees that it is a special suffragan of the Apostolic See.  
*(At the monastery of Déols, 23 July.)*

[FLÓREZ, *España sagrada*, XXVI, 475.]

[Col. 0251C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, bishop of Burgos, and his successors canonically promoted.

Since, by the office of apostleship laid upon us by God, through which, by the Lord’s authorship, we preside over all Christ’s faithful, we ought to attend to the peace and tranquillity of each one, we must be especially solicitous for the repose of those endowed with pastoral dignity, promoted to the episcopal office, and known by special prerogative to belong to the jurisdiction of the Roman Church. For unless, by attending to their interests, we preserve their dignities and rights intact insofar as God permits us, and defend them by apostolic authority against the attacks of wicked men, those committed to their governance by the Lord’s disposition cannot truly be solicitous for their salvation.

Therefore, venerable brother in Christ Peter, bishop of Burgos, we graciously assent to your just requests. We confirm by apostolic authority for you and your successors the church over which, by God’s authorship, you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and reasonably possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors and, through you, to that church itself.

Furthermore, we decree that the things contained within the following boundaries—namely, from the settlements situated in the Pyrenean mountains until the Ocean Sea is reached, and throughout all Asturias as far as the River Deba, which descends from the aforesaid Pyrenean mountains; and as the waters run toward the southern region between Mutave and Rotundum as far as the Pierced Rock, [Col. 0252B] following there the river called Pisorga until it flows into the stream Aslanz—and likewise all other things belonging to the jurisdiction of your Church, both churches and other possessions, as you now justly and canonically possess them, shall remain established unimpaired for you and your successors in perpetual right. Among these we have thought it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

The church of St Peter of Berlangas; the church of St Mary of Castro Suriz, with all their appurtenances; the church of St Adrian in the village called Munio, with its appurtenances; the church of St Quiricus; the church of St Michael near Agosin, with all their appurtenances; the church of St Mary in Berbesica; the church of St Mary in Valleposita; the church of St Eulalia [Col. 0252C] of Muciefar; the church of St Euphemia of Cozuolos; the church of St Mary of Sasamon; the church of St Mary of Belforath, with all their appurtenances; the church of St Bartholomew; the church of St Faustus; the church of St Vincent of Buezo; the church of St Mary of Valde Moro; the church of St Emilian of Lara, with all their appurtenances; the church of St Genesius of Gama; the church of St Michael of Busto; the church of St Mary of Salas; the church of St Pelagius of Lucio; the church of St Martin of Cereso, with all their appurtenances; the church of St Michael of Fronducea; the church of St Lawrence; the church of St Stephen; the church of St James; the church of St Nicholas; the church of St Romanus; the church of St Giles; the church of St Michael; the church of St Peter; the church [Col. 0252D] of St Mary of Roccaboia; the church of St Agatha; and the church of St Saturninus. These eleven churches situated in the city of Burgos, with all their appurtenances; the church of St Christopher of Villa Didaco; the church of St Columba of Olmielos; the church of St Mary of Prato; the church of the Holy Cross of Ripa Hiberii, with their appurtenances; the church of St Leocadia of Egumia; the church of St George of Torranzo; the church of St Mary of Muslera; the church of St Mary of Latas, with their appurtenances; the church of St Martin of Davala; the church of St Torquatus of Old Castile; the church of St Martin of Porres; the church of St Michael of Toves; the church of St Michael [Col. 0253A] of Ponte Corvo; the church of St John of Cucullata; the church of St Mary of Rivio Cavie; the church of St Mametus of Barbadello, with all their appurtenances; and the church of St Vincent of Villa Gonzalua, with its appurtenances.

The right which you have in the monasteries of Oña, Cardeña, St Peter of Aslanz, and St Christopher of Evea, and in the other monasteries of the bishopric of Burgos which belong to your jurisdiction. By the gift of Sancho, of good memory, formerly illustrious king of the Spains: the village called Quintana Donnas; the villages of Mericii and Basconcillos; and the estate in Platano, by the gift of King Ildefonsus of pious memory; a tenth part of all revenues that he had at Burgos; the hospital house with all its estates; the village called [Col. 0253B] Arcos; the village of Isidore; the villages called Castellanos and Rave; the village of Otor; the village of Adiudam; and Ripiella; and in Rivo de Cavia another Ripiella with its *alfoz* [district], boundaries, and appurtenances; the estate in the village of Armentarius; another estate in Villanova; and the village of Orob with its boundaries. By the gift of the infanta Sancha: the village called Cardenola, and whatever she had at Burgos—houses, fields, vineyards, gardens, mills, and *colazos* [tenant-holders]. By the gift of García: the village called Paramo. By the gift of Peter Carriel: half of one village called Arraial.

Following the example of our predecessor Pope Paschal of holy memory, we also decree by apostolic authority that neither you nor your successors shall be subject to any metropolitan save the Roman Pontiff, and that all who succeed you in that see shall be consecrated by the hand of the Roman Pontiff as special suffragans of the Roman See.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations whatsoever; rather, all shall be preserved whole for the complete benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See being expressly reserved. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct [Col. 0253D] that presumption by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body of God and Blood of the Redeemer, our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject to severe vengeance at the Last Judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Hualterius, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. [Col. 0254A] I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Henry, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of St Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Albert, cardinal-priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, William, cardinal-priest of the title of St Peter in Chains, have subscribed. I, Oeldo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of St Theodore, have subscribed. I, Boso, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. [Col. 0254B] I, Cinthius, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of St Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal-deacon of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at the monastery of Dol, through the hand of Herman, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of August [23 July], in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1163 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CLXXXIX. To the Archbishop of Toledo.—That he is not to exercise the right of primacy in the province of Tarragona.  
*(At the monastery of Dol, 26 July.)*

[Mansi, *Councils*, XXI, 1060.]

[Col. 0254C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the Archbishop of Toledo: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that it has not escaped your prudence how the Church of Tarragona, after its archbishop was taken from its midst at the Lord’s calling, has lately been deprived of a pastor’s consolation. Since it ought at present rather to be fostered than in any respect disturbed, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that throughout the whole province of Tarragona you are in no way to intervene your authority either in ordinations in the churches or in conducting elections for vacant churches, nor are you there to attempt in any way to exercise any rights of primacy, until the case pending between your Church and that Church is brought before our hearing and, with the Lord’s help, is brought to a fitting conclusion.

Given at the monastery of Dol, seven days before the Kalends of August [26 July].

## CXC. To the Canons of Pamplona.—On electing a bishop within two months.  
*(At the monastery of Dol, 26 July.)*

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of Pamplona: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more serious the losses and dangers that are accustomed sometimes to arise for the most holy Churches from the lack of a pastor, the more diligently those who continually receive welcome benefits from them ought to exert themselves, with their whole affection, to provide them with a pastor’s consolation. Therefore, by repeated letters we command and enjoin your whole body that, within two months after receiving these letters, jointly agree upon some suitable, honourable, and learned person, and unanimously elect him as your pastor and bishop. After an archbishop has, with the Lord’s help, been appointed there, you are to take care humbly to present the person elected to the Church of Tarragona, as is customary, so that your Church may rejoice soon to receive the desired consolation of a pastor and, through his prudence, breathe again with most delightful refreshment, both spiritually and temporally.

Given as above.

## CXCI. Privilege for the Monastery of St Mary of La Charité.  
*(At the monastery of Dol, 26 July.)*

[Bernier, *History of Blois*, *Proofs*, p. 20.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Philip, abbot of the monastery of Blessed Mary of La Charité, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetual remembrance.

It is fitting that apostolic protection be present for those choosing the religious life, lest an attack of anyone’s rashness either recall them from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this document. First, we decree that the monastic order, known to be established in your monastery according to God, the Rule of St Benedict, and the institution of the Cistercian brethren, shall be preserved there in perpetuity.

Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or [Col. 0255D] princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with the Lord’s assistance, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

The site itself on which the abbey stands, with the adjoining wood; the grange of Puits Morel; the grange of Erembert; the grange of Mont-Calvi; the grange of Ottinville; the grange of Villeflor; the grange of Vivonès with the land of Roches; the grange of Mont-Maximin; the land of Herbiliac with meadows, vineyards, and all their appurtenances; the abbey of Gaverleia; the abbey of Tinterna; the abbey of Landesio; and the abbey of Begar. [Col. 0256A]

Certainly, from the produce of your labour which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the feed of your animals, no cleric or layperson whatsoever may presume to exact tithes from you. Moreover, providing with paternal care for your peace and tranquillity, we forbid by apostolic authority that within the enclosures of your sites or granges anyone dare commit violence, robbery, or theft; commit arson; or seize or kill a person. Whoever presumes to attempt this shall be judged a sacrilegious person.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all remain unimpaired [Col. 0256B] and entire, for the complete benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See. If anyone, therefore, etc.

[Note: [Col. 0255D] In the interest of brevity, we henceforth omit this formula, which occurs verbatim, or with slight alterations, in papal bulls. EDITORS OF THE *PATR.* [*Patrologia*]. [Col. 0256D]]

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Gualterius, bishop of Albano. I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Henry, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of St Anastasia. [Col. 0256C] I, Albert, cardinal-priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, William, cardinal-priest of the title of St Peter in Chains. I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of St Theodore. I, Boso, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Cinthius, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of St Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa. [Col. 0256D] I, Mainfred, cardinal-deacon of St George at the Golden Veil.

Given at the monastery of Dol, through the hand of Herman, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, seven days before the Kalends of August [26 July], in the second indiction, in the year 1163 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Alexander III.

## CXCII. To Louis, King of the Franks.—He sends the monk W. of Morimond with letters of Duke Welf.  
*(At the monastery of Dol, 28 July.)*

[Mansi, *Councils*, XXI, 1021.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son W., monk of Morimond, bearer of these letters, whom we formerly sent into the German kingdom on Church business, amid much labour and danger, has by God’s grace returned to us safe and unharmed. He has most faithfully brought back letters, both for us and for Your Excellency, from our beloved son, the nobleman Duke Welf. We now send him to the presence of Your Highness with those same letters, and ask, admonish, and exhort you in the Lord to receive both him and the letters with royal kindness, for reverence of blessed Peter and ourselves and out of regard for the aforesaid duke; and, having learned from his report in accordance with the tenor of those letters, to proceed as you judge expedient. [Col. 0257B]

Given at the monastery of Dol, five days before the Kalends of August [28 July].

## CXCIII. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—That he restrain the exactions of the Count of Registetus upon the Church of Laon.  
*(Bourges, 1 August.)*

[Martène, *Collections*, II, 672.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother H., Archbishop of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the complaint transmitted to us by the canons of the Church of Laon, we have learned that the noble Count of Registetus does not cease to harass that Church with exactions concerning its possessions situated in his territory. Since the office laid upon us compels us to ensure that churches are not unduly burdened in their affairs by any persons whatsoever, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to admonish the aforesaid count and, if necessary, strictly compel him in no way to impose unlawful exactions upon the lands of the aforesaid Church, and henceforth not to trouble it in such matters.

Moreover, a certain knight of the said count, as is reported, destroyed a mill belonging to the aforesaid Church and violently took its grain, as has been shown to us by the representation of those same canons. We likewise command your brotherhood that, if this is so, you endeavour diligently, both yourself and through the said count, to admonish and compel [Col. 0257D] that knight to make good the damage which he inflicted on the aforementioned Church by destroying the mill, to restore the grain taken away in its entirety, or to render full justice to the same canons. If he is perhaps unwilling to do either, bind him with the bond of excommunication.

Given at Bourges, on the Kalends of August [1 August].

## CXCIV. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Fleury.  
*(Bourges, 7 August.)*

[Mention of this privilege is found in Saussey, *Annals of Orléans*, 201.]

## CXCV. To Louis, King of the Franks.—He commends to him the monastery of Fleury.  
*(Bourges, 7 August.)*

[Mansi, *Councils*, XXI, 1006.]

[Col. 0258A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We received, with the goodwill of spirit that was due, our beloved son . . . , abbot of St Benedict on the Loire, when he came to us with letters from Your Magnificence. In consideration of your prayers—which we always wish to address with ready diligence, insofar as with God we can—and in view of his religious life and uprightness, we took care to honour him with particular affection and to grant his petitions effectively. [Col. 0258B]

As he returns home with the fullness of our love and favour, we earnestly commend him to Your Royal Serenity, admonishing, asking, and exhorting you in the Lord through apostolic letters that, for love of divine mercy, reverence for blessed Peter and ourselves, and in consideration of his religious life and probity, you may always regard, love, support, and honour the same abbot, his brethren, and the said monastery with merciful kindness; and that you may defend both them and the rights of that monastery from the attacks of evil persons by royal protection. Thus may you receive from Almighty God the reward of eternal blessedness, and may we be bound to offer abundant thanks to Your Royal Majesty.

[Col. 0258C] Given at Bourges, seven days before the Ides of August [7 August].

## CXCVI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—Concerning ecclesiastical coercion against Guy of Châtillon for Peter and Ric.  
*(Bourges, 8 August.)*

[Martène, *Collections*, II, 673.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, Archbishop of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since Guy of Châtillon accused Peter and Ric., bearers of these letters, of the crime of homicide, as we have learned from their account, and they appealed to our hearing at the most recent past feast of Pentecost, the said Guy neither came nor sent anyone to answer on his behalf. Although we had commanded your brotherhood by our letters diligently to admonish that Guy and strictly compel him either to allow them to remain in peace and without any molestation, or to appear before us, at the feast of St Peter, ready both to answer and to act, he neither came to us on the appointed day [Col. 0258D] nor has yet ceased from harassing them.

We therefore command your brotherhood by repeated letters strictly to restrain the same Guy henceforth from all persecution of them, and neither through yourself nor through others to allow any burden to be imposed upon them.

Given at Bourges, six days before the Ides of August [8 August].

## CXCVII. Concerning the envoy of the Emperor of Constantinople, who has a secret matter to disclose to the Pope and King when both are present.  
*(Bourges, 20 August.)*

[Mansi, *Councils*, XXI, 1013.]

[Col. 0259A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although from many other things concerning the most devoted sincerity which you have shown us we can and wish in many ways to commend Your Royal Excellency, we also deservedly commend the height of Your Royal Majesty in this: that lately, at our request, you sent your own envoy to provide security for the envoys of our dearest son in Christ, Manuel, illustrious Emperor of Constantinople. We offer abundant thanks for this to Your Magnificence.

Let Your Excellency know that, while one of those envoys is delayed at St Giles by an illness pressing upon him, the other is coming into our presence. But since, as you could learn from the letters formerly sent us by those same envoys, which we forwarded to you, he has a certain secret matter to lay before us and you alone, it is his wish, should this please Your Majesty, that we both be present in some place in order that we may hear that matter together from the aforesaid envoy. Your aforesaid envoy will explain his intention more fully to you. Although we should gladly wish to have your presence both for this and for other [Col. 0259C] affairs, it is for you to deliberate with your household and counsellors how you ought to proceed in this matter, and what is fitting for your honour and high estate in this business; you will proceed as you know to be expedient for your honour. Whatever you decide should be done in this affair, take care to notify both us and the said envoy swiftly by your letters.

Given at Bourges, thirteen days before the Kalends of September [20 August].

## CXCVIII. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—On behalf of Walter, deacon.  
*(Bourges, 23 August.)*

[Martène, *Collections*, II, 673.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0259D] brother Henry, Archbishop of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Walter, deacon and bearer of these letters, having come to the mercy of the Apostolic See, showed us in a tearful complaint that the canons of your Church had deprived him of the chaplaincy of Maceio without judgment or justice, and had granted it less than canonically to a certain priest. When he came to us at Anagni, he brought back our letters on this matter to S. [Note: [Col. 0259] Samson, your predecessor of good memory, who died in 1161 and was buried in the monastery of Igniacensis], in which, we believe, we had firmly commanded him either to cause that chaplaincy to be restored to the said deacon or to render full justice.

But since that predecessor has been taken from this world at the Lord’s call, Walter is compelled to renew his complaint in our presence because he has been deprived of his right. Moved by his need and repeated cries, and by the duty imposed upon us, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to admonish and strictly compel your aforesaid canons either peacefully and quietly to restore that chaplaincy to the said deacon, after removing the priest from it, or, with appeal set aside, to render him full justice in your presence. [Col. 0260A]

Given at Bourges, ten days before the Kalends of September [23 August].

## CXCIX. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—On behalf of a certain knight who, his sins requiring it, died in a tournament.  
*(Bourges, 25 August.)*

[Ibid., col. 674.]

[Col. 0260B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We received your letter with the goodwill due to it. In it we learned that, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother the Archbishop of Canterbury, you earnestly asked us to grant ecclesiastical burial to a certain knight who, through the exigency of his sins, died in a tournament. Although we wish, insofar as with God we can, to defer to both you and him in all things and more willingly to hear your requests, nevertheless, because we have often been earnestly asked the same thing by kings, princes, and barons of the land, and have granted no assent to requests of this kind, lest that wicked custom gain strength thereby, do not consider it burdensome or troublesome that we have left your request unanswered in this matter. [Col. 0260C]

Given at Bourges, ten days before the Kalends of September [23 August].

## CC. To Louis, King of the Franks.—He reports that one of the Emperor of Constantinople’s envoys wished “to lay that secret matter before himself and the king jointly.” He had decided that the envoy should first go to the king, “lest,” he says, “you should seem to meet him.”  
*(Bourges, 28 August.)*

[Mansi, *Councils*, XXI, 1007.]

[Col. 0260D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

As we recently informed Your Royal Highness through your servant and also by our letters, one of the envoys of our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious Emperor of Constantinople, who is now coming into these regions, wished to have both us and you present in order that he might lay before us jointly that secret matter which, he asserts, he received by command of that emperor. It was accordingly his wish to find you together with us at Bourges.

But we, considering what would be expedient for the honour of Your Highness, communicated our counsel to Your Royal Magnificence on this matter both through your envoy and in our letters. We represented that it would be more honourable if, before we came together, the aforesaid imperial envoy should come into the presence of Your Highness first, lest, if you should perhaps come to us on that occasion, you might seem in some manner to be meeting him. After he has come to you, if it is your counsel that we ought to confer on this matter together with you, we can meet together wherever seems good to you. Desiring, therefore, to defer to Your Majesty in all things insofar as with God we can, we wish the said envoy to come into the presence of Your Royal Serenity before he comes to us.

We therefore earnestly ask Your Excellency by apostolic letters to receive him honourably when he comes before you, treat him with your customary kindness, and consider and attend with the deliberation proper to you to the words which he lays before Your Majesty. But if it seems to you that anything should be communicated to us, you may notify us when it pleases you. [Col. 0261B]

Given at Bourges, eight days before the Kalends of September [25 August].

## CCI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—On behalf of the bishop-elect of the Church of Châlons.  
*(Bourges, 28 August.)*

[Martène, *Collections*, II, 674.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, Archbishop of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0261C] We have learned from the letters of your brotherhood that you came to an agreement with our dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks, your brother, that, if the case of the election held in the Church of Châlons is lawfully heard in our presence, it will not be in any way burdensome or troublesome to that same king.

[Note: [Col. 0261D] This election concerns Guy of Dampierre or Guy of Joinville, concerning whom Alberic writes in his Chronicle under the year 1163: “At Châlons, Guy of Dampierre, brother of Anseric, William, Andrew, and Milo—noble men—was elected bishop; but, by divine judgment, because he was unworthy, he died on the very day when he was to have been consecrated on the following day. Another Guy of Joinville, brother of Geoffrey and son of Roger, was elected, and he governed for twenty-eight years.” [Col. 0262D]]

Although elsewhere other information is suggested to us, we regard this as exceedingly welcome and acceptable. Since we have the firm purpose and will always to grant your just petitions, we have thought it right to reply to you as follows: when, on the appointed date, both parties appear before us on this matter, we shall most willingly proceed in that case, as far as justice permits us, to the honour of God, of the aforesaid king, and of yourself. Meanwhile, we have not thought it right to shorten the appointed time unless this should result from the consent of both parties. [Col. 0261D]

Given at Bourges, five days before the Kalends of September [28 August].

## CCII. To Louis, King of the Franks.—On reforming the monastery of St Maximin.  
*(Bourges, 1 September.)*

[Mansi, *Councils*, XXI, 1019.]

[Note: [Col. 0262D] Letter 183 above treats the same subject.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest [Col. 0262A] son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that Your Excellent Serenity has forgotten with what devout urgency of prayer you induced our mercy to punish with most fitting vengeance that monstrous crime which the monks of the Church of St Maximin, at the devil’s instigation, perpetrated against their abbot, and to see to it that the same church was beneficially provided with a suitable person. Accordingly, in response to the prayers of your royal piety and as a duty of our office, diligently punishing so great an offence as we judged expedient, we caused those implicated in such wickedness to be confined in various and different monasteries, and commanded that they be kept under secure guard.

Trusting at last in your royal goodness, we selected thoroughly suitable and religious men from an honourable [Col. 0262B] and religious house, and took care to establish them in the aforesaid church in order, with the Lord as author, to restore religious life there. We believe them so useful and suitable that, if royal piety deigns to foster and defend them from the attack of evil persons, they will enlarge that church in both spiritual and temporal prosperity and, with the Lord’s grant, advance it to greater things.

Therefore we ask, admonish, and exhort Your Royal Serenity in the Lord, and enjoin it upon you for the remission of your sins, that, for the sake of divine Providence, reverence for blessed Peter, and the salvation of your soul, you look with a more gracious eye upon the aforesaid church and the brethren established there for God’s service, and exert yourself vigorously to free the church from the troubles and injuries which those fugitive monks inflict upon it through their kinsmen and supporters. In particular, cause Her. of Cingy and Rob. Beriger, who assail those brethren with various burdens and vexations, to be forcefully apprehended and confined in those same places under stricter guard, so that henceforth they cannot devise anything, either personally or through their supporters, against that same church. We also ask Your Highness strictly to compel those of your burgesses to whom the possessions of the often-mentioned church have been pledged, to desist entirely from exacting usury and to credit the income received, or at least to be received, toward the principal after deducting expenses. For although, according to the ordinances [Col. 0262D] of the holy Fathers, every form of usury and excess gain is altogether forbidden to be exacted, those who pursue such profits less eagerly will nevertheless be punished more leniently.

Given at Bourges, on the Kalends of September [1 September].

## CCIII. To Hugh, Bishop of Soissons.—He commends his devotion and promises him every favour.  
*(Bourges, 2 September.)*

[Ibid., col. 980.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0263A] brother H. . . . . . Bishop of Soissons: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we sincerely love in the Lord all sons of the Church, and especially our brother bishops whom we know to be fervent in the Catholic faith and in devotion to the most holy Roman Church, and that we cherish them more abundantly in proportion as they are known to shine more richly with constancy of faith and the fragrance of a good reputation. Our beloved son P., dean of the church of Blessed Anianus, having come to us, has taken care, as he has often done before, to report to us again that you are fervent in the Catholic faith and adhere with sincere devotion to your mother, the most holy Roman Church. Since we remember having learned this long ago from practical experience itself, we consider it exceedingly welcome and acceptable. [Col. 0263B]

Accordingly, we love your brotherhood with sincere charity in the Lord, and desire to preserve and increase the dignity and honours granted you by the Lord. Moreover, you may know that we have equal concern and caution concerning the matters which our same son reported—namely, the concern which you are known to show in relation to our dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks. Nor, with the Lord willing, will anyone be able to induce us to diminish or remove the dignity or office granted to you. Rather, desiring to increase it, we shall gladly take care to give you counsel and aid in all matters in which we honourably can, so that the integrity of your devotion may have its merit and receive the reward promised [Col. 0263C] to great priests and cultivators of justice.

Given at Bourges, on the fourth Nones of September [2 September].

## CCIV. To Gilbert, Bishop of London.—He directs him to exhort Henry, King of the English, to promote the liberty of the Churches.  
*(Bourges, 4 September.)*

[Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II, 85.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother [G.], Bishop of London: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The greater the position which you are known to hold in the Church of God, the more are the eyes of many fixed upon you: those of some, indeed, in order to disparage you; but those of others in order to be instructed by your good actions. Therefore your prudence must conduct itself so cautiously and circumspectly in all things that everyone may find in you something to imitate and something by which the life of one’s neighbours may advance to greater things. For our dearest son Henry, illustrious king of the English, considering and observing your integrity, prudence, and religious devotion, earnestly and repeatedly asked us to have you exercise the episcopal office in that city which is, as it were, the head of the kingdom and where he customarily makes a more prolonged stay, and to remain there to give him spiritual and temporal counsel. It is therefore your concern to exhort more confidently to every good work him who has conceived such hope and confidence in you, and to strive to deter him from those things that bring danger upon his soul.

We therefore ask and admonish your brotherhood in the Lord that, by frequent exhortation, you set before him that he should consider more carefully and reflect upon the lofty and exalted station to which the providence of divine mercy has raised him; how by its grace it has subjected a kingdom to him; and how from day to day it causes him to abound in ever greater advances. Bringing all these things to heart and memory, let him keep God before his eyes in all his actions; abstaining from unlawful things, let him always advance toward better things; and let him strive to have God propitious to him, without whom he can neither hold an earthly kingdom nor obtain an everlasting one [Col. 0264B].

Moreover, in order to accomplish this more suitably, firmly assert and set before him that he ought to love the most holy Churches of God with a more sincere affection, uphold them, and apply himself and devote his attention to their liberty more diligently than he has been accustomed to do; Churches for whose sake the Lord Jesus Christ was seen upon earth and lived among men, enduring in his own body the passion of death. Likewise, endeavor to summon both archbishops and your other fellow bishops, so that together with you they may diligently induce that same king to do this. For although by many other works of piety he may please in the eyes of the Creator, this especially is the means by which his kingdom may happily be enlarged, and by which he himself will obtain from Almighty God no slight increase, both spiritually and temporally [Col. 0264C]. Strive to offer him such admonition both in season and out of season, and to induce him to this so diligently that we may perceive, from your warnings, that he corrects himself both in the relief of churches and in the other matters in which he is found blameworthy.

Furthermore, both we and all who use reason readily recognize how necessary and useful upright and religious persons are to the Church of God at this time, and how timely their life and preservation are.

We have heard, moreover, and learned from the truthful report of many, that you weaken and afflict your body beyond what is fitting and expedient, neither eating meat nor restoring your stomach by wine for the sake of health [Col. 0264D]. There is therefore reason to fear that, while necessities are withheld from the beast of burden, you may succumb through excessive weakness, and that the Church of God may suffer grave loss through your failure—God forbid!—though from your conduct and life it receives no small benefit.

We believe that you know how, in the Old Testament, the turtledove was not customarily killed in sacrifice, but its head is read to have been twisted back to the wings; signifying that a righteous man ought not to destroy his flesh by scantiness of food, but, by withholding superfluities from it, should cut away luxury and vices. For mortification of the flesh is useful to a small degree, but godliness is proved necessary for all things. We therefore admonish and earnestly exhort your brotherhood that henceforth you impose no such austerity upon your flesh [Col. 0265A], but, in accordance with the Apostle’s admonition, use a little and temperate wine (1 Tim. 5), and sometimes meat, whether when you have taken medicine or are burdened by bodily weakness; so that, with your body not weakened beyond what is fitting, you may adhere more vigorously to the service of the Creator and preserve yourself sound for the Church of God, to which you are exceedingly necessary.

Given at Bourges, on the second Nones of September [4 September].

## CCV. To the Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the son of the nobleman Frajapan. (Bourges, 5 September.)

[MARTÈNE, *Collectio*, II, 675.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of the people of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Having full confidence in the steadfastness of your sincerity and devotion, we confidently call upon your prudence concerning matters which we wish to be more zealously brought into effect. Let your discretion know that our beloved son, the son of the nobleman Frajapan, intends to come to us from the kingdom of Germany, where he resides with his parents. Therefore, concerning this matter, we have sent our letters to our beloved son the Bishop-elect of Verdun, admonishing him to have the young man conducted safely as far as the kingdom of France.

[Note: [Col. 0265D] This was Richard of Crisse, descended from the lords of Grand-Pré; after being archdeacon of Laon, he was elected Bishop of Verdun, and died on the expedition to Jerusalem in 1171.]

We did not name the man to him, wishing the matter to remain secret for the time being. Accordingly, we ask and admonish your uprightness [Col. 0265C] that, out of reverence for Saint Peter and for us, you transmit those letters to the same elect through some discreet man, and afterwards have that same son of ours, the nobleman, conducted honorably and safely to us. Meanwhile, let the matter remain secret with you.

Given at Bourges, on the Nones of September [5 September].

## CCVI. To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—Summoning the archbishop to a conference between pope and king. (Bourges, 10 September.)

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of the people of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0265D] We wish your brotherhood to know that we expect shortly to hold a conference with our dearest son Louis, the illustrious King of the Franks, your brother. Since we know that your presence will be exceedingly useful to us at that conference, we earnestly ask your discretion by apostolic letters that, upon receiving these letters, you immediately set out and hasten to the place where you learn that we are to hold the conference, so that we may have your counsel as we desire [Col. 0266A]. We do not, however, yet have a certain place at which we are to be present, whether we shall meet, with the Lord’s help, at Saint-Laurent or at Saint Benedict upon the Loire.

[Note: [Col. 0265D] A celebrated monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Orléans, commonly called Fleury, where the sacred relics of the holy father Benedict are kept; it still flourishes under the Congregation of Saint-Maur.]

Given at Bourges, on the fourth Ides of September [10 September].

## CCVII. To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—For the church of Saint John of Condas. (Bourges, 12 September.)

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us that Rainerius of Calvomont [Col. 0266B] presumes to despoil the monks of Saint John of Condas of their goods, and endeavors to seize those same goods contrary to justice. Therefore, since by the obligation of our office we ought with paternal kindness to attend to all God’s faithful who cry out for their justice, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if this is so, you compel the said Rainerius with every severity to restore what he has taken to the aforesaid brethren, and that he presume no further to trouble them concerning their right; otherwise, strike the said Rainerius with the deserved punishment of ecclesiastical severity until he desists from such presumption.

Given at Bourges, on the second Ides of September [12 September].

## CCVIII. To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—For the brethren of the church of Saint Remigius. (Bourges, 13 September.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 0266C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We entrust to your discretion for hearing and due final determination the case known to be in litigation between our beloved sons, the brethren of Saint Remigius, and G. of Joinville, concerning the dispute between them. We therefore command you by apostolic letters that you summon both parties before you and, after carefully hearing and examining the arguments on both sides [Col. 0266D], decide the case through the mediation of justice.

Given at Bourges, on the Ides of September [13 September].

## CCIX. To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—For the church of Saint Remigius. (Bourges, 13 September.)

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0267A] From the complaint sent to us by the abbot and brethren of Saint Remigius, we have learned that the advocate of Germigny presumes to take away and occupy contrary to justice the revenues of that village, which the brethren of the aforesaid monastery rightfully possess from the church of Saint Remaclus under an annual rent.

[Note: [Col. 0267] That is, from the monastery of Stavelot, which, we believe, recognizes Saint Remaclus as its patron and founder.]

Since, therefore, we ought with paternal solicitude to preserve the rights of churches whole and unimpaired, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if this is so, you carefully admonish and strictly compel the said advocate to restore what he has taken from them, and no longer presume to harass the aforesaid church concerning its right. But if the said advocate is confident of his right, let the matter be determined in your presence; otherwise, by the duty of your office constrain the same G. by ecclesiastical censure to carry this out [Col. 0267B].

Given at Bourges, on the Ides of September [13 September].

## CCX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Monte-Ramo. (Sens, 1 October.)

[YEPES, *Crónica general de la orden de San Benito*, VII, Appendix, p. 24.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SANCHO, abbot of Saint Mary of Monte-Ramo, and his successors, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

The office of the government entrusted to us invites us to assent to religious vows and to fulfill them by the performance of deeds; and the order of reason seems to require it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord [Col. 0267C], we graciously assent to your just requests, receive under the protection of Saint Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of the blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been established in that place according to God, the Rule of Blessed Benedict, and the Institute of the Cistercian brethren, shall be preserved there inviolate for all time. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now possess justly and canonically, or may in future acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings, the gifts of princes, the offerings of the faithful [Col. 0267D], or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among them we have thought fit to specify these by their proper names:

The place itself of Monte-Ramo, in which the abbey is situated, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Saint Cyprian of Penna, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Saint Adrian, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Saint Michael, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Saint Martha, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Pineyra, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Salcedo, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Pratis Humanis; the grange of Old Saint John [Col. 0268A], with all its appurtenances; the grange of Pratu-Goelis, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Pelagiones, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Cerdera, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Lanza, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Baronala, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Lancta Columba, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Saint John of Cota, situated in the land of Lemos, with all its appurtenances; the grange of Coba de Ruaço, with all its appurtenances.

Certainly, from the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals, let no one presume to demand tithes or first-fruits from you. Furthermore, by apostolic authority we forbid any of our brethren—clerics or laymen, that is—after making profession in that place, to depart from the cloister without permission of his abbot; and let no one dare receive or retain one who departs without documentary assurance from the community. Providing with paternal solicitude for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority that within the enclosure of your establishments or granges anyone dare commit violence, robbery, or theft, seize a man, or kill him [Col. 0268B].

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever, etc.

I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, confirm. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, confirm. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, confirm. I, William, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains. I, Bernard, Bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina, confirm. I, Walter, Bishop of Albano, confirm. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, confirm. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, confirm. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore [Col. 0268D], confirm. I, Rosso, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, confirm. I, Manfred, cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil, confirm. I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, confirm.

Given at Sens, through the hand of Herman, subdeacon and notary of the holy Roman Church, on the second Nones of October [6 October], in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1163, and in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CCXI. To Louis, King of the Franks.—That he urge the King of Sicily to fortify himself against his enemies and commend to him the Bishop of Tropea. (Sens, 12 October.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 1022.]

[Col. 0269A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ LOUIS, illustrious King of the Franks, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since the kingdom of Sicily pertains in a special manner to the right and property of Saint Peter, and we ought to be solicitous and zealous for its condition and preservation, we ask the diligence of your royal serenity prudently to disclose in your letters your counsel and intention to our dearest son in Christ William, illustrious King of Sicily [the printed *viduitatem* is evidently corrupt] [Col. 0269B]. Earnestly admonish and exhort him, since his enemies are preparing themselves and directing all their efforts toward entering his land and wearying him with repeated attacks, so to fortify himself and his land and to take such care for his own safety that the devices and snares of his enemies cannot harm him or inflict upon him any loss or damage.

Moreover, we earnestly commend to your royal serenity our venerable brother . . ., Bishop of Tropea, who desires to return to his bishopric in the land of that king. By apostolic letters we ask that, out of reverence for Saint Peter and for us, you receive him kindly [Col. 0269C], and commend him so affectionately to the aforesaid king in letters of recommendation that, through your recommendation, the same bishop may be held dearer and more acceptable; and that we may consequently be bound to render thanks to your highness.

Given at Sens, on the fourth Ides of October [12 October].
