The aforesaid cardinal, fearing that the election might be delayed or in any way impeded because of the difficulty of travel and the savagery of raging schismatics, confirmed it with the counsel of those bishops and other prudent men. Having afterwards learned the grounds and necessity of those making the election, we in turn took care to confirm it by apostolic authority.

Since, moreover, from the duty of our office and in consideration of your devotion, we sincerely wish to love both you and your church, and always with watchful concern preserve your rights and dignities, by this present document we decree that what has been done by us and by that cardinal can in future cause no prejudice to you or your church [Col. 0436C], nor may the brethren of Saint Benedict derive from it any example or occasion for malicious objection. Therefore we ask and admonish the prudence of your whole community that, considering the necessity and the evil character of the time, you bear this with all patience and humility; that you do not take it grievously or ill that the abbot’s death was not first reported to you, as is customary; and that you approve the election. For we have directed the same monks, before the elect is blessed as abbot, to send one of their brethren to Cluny with our letters and theirs, through whom they may inform you by what necessity they were induced not to report their abbot’s death, in accordance with the tenor of the aforesaid decree [Col. 0436D], and not to await your authority and consent in carrying out the election; asking you, on our behalf and theirs, to bear this with patience and equanimity in view of the necessity. They are also to state to you that they will by no means take this as a precedent, nor ever depart from the tenor of the decree, but will observe that decree perpetually.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of March [1 March].

CDXXVII. To the abbot of Saint-Remigius of Rheims.—On behalf of a deprived priest. (At the Lateran, 3 March.)

[MARTEN., *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 725.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved [Col. 0437A] son, the abbot of Saint-Remigius, greetings and apostolic blessing.

From the complaint submitted by the deprived priest, it has come to our ears that the abbot of Saint-Jean-des-Vignes—

> [Note: [Col. 0437D] Saint-Jean-des-Vignes, a distinguished monastery of the Order of Saint Augustine near Soissons, founded by Hugh, lord of Château-Thierry, and so called from the vineyards that formerly surrounded it.]

—has taken his church from him without judicial process and contrary to justice, and altogether refuses to restore it to him. Since we can neither may nor ought to fail that priest in his right, we command your brotherhood by apostolic writings diligently to admonish the aforesaid abbot on our behalf and, if necessary, strictly compel him either to restore his church in full to the said priest or to render adequate justice to him before you. But if he prefers to enter upon the case rather than restore the church [Col. 0437B], you, having summoned the parties before you at a suitable place and time, are to hear the case most diligently and decide it, with justice mediating and the obstacle of appeal removed.

Given at the Lateran, 5 Nones of March [3 March].

CDXXVIII. To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and his suffragans.—That they excommunicate the schismatic Drogo. (At the Lateran, 6 March.)

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers HENRY, Archbishop of Rheims, and his suffragans, greetings and apostolic [Col. 0437C] blessing.

We believe that you know, and in no way fail to know, how grievously and outrageously that schismatic Drogo, the violent and wicked usurper of the Church of Lyons, has sinned against the Church of God and continually laboured with all his might to harass it.

> [Note: [Col. 0437D] Drogo, formerly archdeacon of Lyons, was elected archbishop, six canons protesting and opposing his election, as may be seen in [Col. 0438D] the letter of the chapter of Lyons to King Louis in Chesne, vol. IV of the *History of France*.]

Therefore, holding the aforesaid Drogo and his principal supporters to be excommunicated and cut off from the body of Christ, which is the Church, we command your brotherhood by apostolic writings and under strict injunction to assemble together and publicly excommunicate them, with candles lighted, clergy and people gathered, and bells rung. Cause the same sentence of excommunication to be renewed throughout your dioceses every Sunday and on other principal [Col. 0437D] feast days. Also strive most earnestly to assist our venerable brother G., Archbishop of Lyons, and effectively provide him, by every means you can, counsel and aid.

> [Note: [Col. 0438D] Guichard, formerly abbot of Pontigny, was elected and ordained by the supreme pontiff at Montpellier in 1165.]

Work also to induce your parishioners to do the same, and impose it upon them for the remission of sins that they apply themselves to his assistance, so that he may find in you the consolation of fraternal charity. Whatever you do for him, we shall consider as specially rendered to ourselves, and must therefore return immense thanks to your sincerity [Col. 0438A].

Given at the Lateran, 2 Nones of March [6 March].

CDXXIX. To the same.—Concerning the absolution of certain excommunicated persons. (At the Lateran, 10 March.)

[Ibid., col. 727.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Rheims, greetings and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us that our brother, the Bishop of Châlons, subjected to excommunication Evan. Hengenbert, Hugh, Nicholas, Radulf, Roger, Segard, Adam, [Col. 0438B] Geoffrey, and Ogger Torelli, his parishioners, together with their households, although they had not been cited or called to account. Since we ought to be more ready to bless than to curse, we command your brotherhood by apostolic writings diligently to investigate the matter. If it is established to you that the aforesaid bishop excommunicated the said men in the manner described above, then, unless it is notorious that they sinned so grievously that by the very kind of offence they had incurred a sentence of excommunication, absolve them and their households by our authority and your own, with every appeal set aside, if the bishop refuses to do so without exacting money. First receive from [Col. 0438C] them an oath that they will submit to justice before our venerable brother the Bishop of Soissons together with the aforesaid Bishop of Châlons, should the latter have any claim of justice against them.

Given at the Lateran, 6 Ides of March [10 March].

CDXXX. To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Hugh the cleric. (At the Lateran, 13 March.)

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Rheims, greetings and apostolic blessing.

From the report formerly received from the clerk Hugh, bearer of the present letters, that his father and mother had pledged to Hescelin, clerk of Guisern, for six marks a share [Col. 0438D] of a certain mill which belonged to them—a share which, upon his death, his father, and likewise his mother, left to him—and that he alleged that the said Hescelin had already received his principal and more: we instructed our venerable brother M. [Note: [Col. 0438D] Milo.] bishop of Thérouanne, that, if it were established that the aforesaid clerk had received his principal out of the said share of the mill, after expenses had been deducted, he should carefully admonish him [Col. 0439A] and compel him with all strictness to surrender that same share to the said Hugh, without any exaction of money and with all recourse to appeal set aside, and to leave him to possess it peaceably and quietly. If he should perhaps refuse to do so, he was to deprive him without delay of every ecclesiastical office and benefice. But if Hescelin had not yet received his principal in full, then, after crediting toward the principal what he had already received and receiving what remained due, he was nevertheless to cause the aforesaid share to be assigned to the said Hugh, with the impediment of appeal removed.

But since, as the repeated complaint of the aforesaid Hugh shows, the above-mentioned bishop has in no way yet carried out our mandate, and since it is wholly unworthy for any layman, much less [Col. 0439B] a clerk, to devote effort or attention to profits of this kind, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if you learn that the said bishop has not proceeded in these matters, you shall not for any reason defer sufficiently carrying out within forty days after receiving these letters all the foregoing matters, as we directed him, with every excuse and appeal removed. Thus, if the aforesaid clerk Hescelin, having been lawfully cited, should refuse to come or to observe what you decree, or should perhaps attempt to withdraw himself from your jurisdiction through a secular court, you shall put the said Hugh into possession of the aforesaid share, all appeal set aside, and shall stoutly and steadfastly defend his possession against the molestations of the opposing party by both our authority and yours [Col. 0439C] alike.

Given at the Lateran, the third day before the Ides of March.

## CDXXXI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—On behalf of John the clerk, that he be invested with a prebend. (Lateran, March 14.)

[Ibid., col. 728.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since our brother G., bishop of Laon, granted one prebend to John, nephew of our beloved son the cantor of Douai, in the presence of our venerable brother the bishop of Ostia and [Col. 0439D] our beloved sons O., cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, and Manfred, cardinal-deacon of St George at the Golden Veil; and since, if we remember rightly, both we and you and the same bishop of Laon confirmed that grant by our letters, yet the aforesaid bishop of Laon has hitherto refused to invest the said John with the aforesaid prebend: we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters carefully to admonish that bishop of Laon and, if necessary, compel him not to delay investing the said John with the specified prebend, as we directed him in our letters, and to assign him a place both in chapter and in choir.

Given at the Lateran, the second day before the Ides of March.

## CDXXXII. To the same.—On behalf of the cantor of Douai, that he be restored. (Lateran, March 14.)

[Ibid., col. 729.]

[Col. 0440A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since your discretion knows that it is written, “to whom tribute is due, tribute; to whom honour, honour” (Romans 13), we are surprised that, as we are told, you have issued in the Church of Arras, contrary to the custom of that realm, an ordinance that in the choir of that church every man should take his place according to whether he had been instituted a canon there earlier or later, with no regard for any person’s learning, rank, [Col. 0440B] or age—matters which ought especially to be considered in these respects. But our beloved son, the cantor of Douai, whom, on account of his devotion, honourability, and integrity, we regard as a prudent and discreet man, very dear and welcome to us, declares that on this account his place has been changed and that his person has thereby been seriously injured.

Therefore we ask, admonish, and command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to have restored without delay to the aforesaid cantor the place which he is known hitherto to have held in the said church, on account of the devotion which he bears toward us and the Church, and out of regard for the affection which we have for his person; and to have him left henceforth in peace, so that he may remain ever [Col. 0440C] more devoted to you, and that you may do for us something wholly welcome and acceptable. Moreover, if you revoke this ordinance both as regards him and others, know that it will please us greatly. But whatever you do concerning others, we wish the place which the aforesaid cantor is known to have held until now to be restored to him. For we prefer to defer in this matter to your brotherhood, so that what has been done therein by you may be restored by your authority to its former state, rather than to employ our authority in this respect, although we could do so by right.

Given at the Lateran, the second day before the Ides of March.

## CDXXXIII. To the dean and chapter of Châlons.—That they are not to demand money for schools. (Lateran, March 16.)

[MARTEN, ibid., col. 730.]

[Col. 0440D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the dean and canons of the Church of Châlons, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to us that, when certain clerks in your bishopric wish to teach others and instruct them in literary learning, you prevent them by every means from doing so unless they are willing to give you money, and forbid them, under threat of excommunication, to do it. Since this is entirely contrary to reason and propriety, we command your whole body by apostolic letters that you permit all clerks who wish to lecture to others in your bishopric, and especially outside the city walls, [Col. 0441A] and to instruct them in the disciplines of the schools, to do so freely and without any contradiction; nor shall you henceforth presume to harass them on this account or to inflict any injury upon them under this pretext. If a further complaint of this kind concerning you is brought to us, know for certain that we shall by no means leave it unpunished.

Given at the Lateran, the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April.

## CDXXXIV. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—On admonishing ecclesiastical prelates to assist him; commendation of steadfast affection toward the Roman Church and exhortation to the same. (Lateran, March 17.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 0441B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has not escaped our memory, nor shall it ever slip away in the future, how sincerely and devoutly you have stood by us from the beginning of our elevation; how eagerly you have always sought to apply yourself to the welfare and advancement of the Church; and that you still persist in the same purpose and resolve and devote all due care and attention to our affairs and those of the Church. Of this we are not at all unaware, nor do we have any doubt about it. Holding this hope [Col. 0441C] and confidence, we confidently solicit your sincerity concerning our affairs and communicate them to your knowledge without any scruple of hesitation.

Let your discretion know that, through the grace of God, we have thus far remained in the City in sufficiently splendid circumstances, and at present, although the enemies of the Church continually devise many schemes against us, we remain there honourably, with the Lord’s aid. But because we are daily pressed by many and very heavy expenses and burdened by excessive obligations, we are compelled, at this moment of such need, to have recourse to you and the other sons of the Church and to request your assistance more urgently. Supported by your aid, we may be able courageously to resist the enemies of the Church and restore that Church to its former liberty. We see that this can be achieved in no more fitting way [Col. 0441D] than by preserving the City in fidelity to blessed Peter and to us, and by being able to remain there against the will of our enemies.

Therefore we ask, admonish, and exhort your brotherhood in the Lord by apostolic letters to endeavour swiftly and effectively to assist us for the remedy of your soul, and to stretch out a helping hand to your mother with filial devotion, so that the evidence of your most devoted sincerity may shine clearly hereafter in the eyes of the Church. Thus you will render us permanently obliged to you; your mother, namely the holy Church, will feel herself substantially relieved of her burdens and oppressions through you; you will be able to obtain a manifold reward from God and carry away praise and glory before men. [Col. 0442A] For this reason we have thought fit to send our beloved son Brother Rostra to you and to the other prelates of the churches. In accordance with your good pleasure, reply to him concerning this matter, and signify by your letters and through him what you have done.

Given at the Lateran, the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April.

## CDXXXV. To the same.—On behalf of the clerk Walter. (Lateran, April 18.)

[Ibid., col. 731.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Walter the deacon, coming before the clemency of the Apostolic See, carefully represented to us that the canons [Col. 0442B] of the church of Holy Cross granted him half of one prebend in that church, until they should be able freely to assign the said G. a full prebend. But now, as we have heard from his report, they wholly refuse to complete his prebend from the prebend which is vacant. Since it is unjust that a benefice established for the support of one person should be divided into several parts, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if this is so, you carefully admonish the aforesaid canons and strictly compel them not to delay completing the prebend of the said G.

Given at the Lateran, the fourteenth day before the Kalends of May.

## CDXXXVI. To the same.—On behalf of a certain G., that his inheritance be restored to him. (Lateran, April 19.)

[Ibid., col. 732.]

[Col. 0442C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

G., bearer of the present letters, has informed us that the knight Badar, Nicholas, and Adam are holding in occupied pledge his maternal inheritance, which they seized. He declares that he will pay them their principal if they refuse to surrender it to him. We therefore command your brotherhood by apostolic letters carefully to admonish and diligently summon the aforesaid creditors, that, once their principal has been received, they restore the aforesaid inheritance [Col. 0442D] intact to the said G.; or that they do not defer to render him full justice in this matter before your tribunal. If they are unwilling to do either, you shall compel them by ecclesiastical censure to perform one or the other.

Given at the Lateran, the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May.

## CDXXXVII. To the same.—Concerning the affair of the Bishop of Grenoble. (Lateran, April 29.)

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have learned from the report of certain persons that the noble Count of Toulouse, induced by the entreaties and promises [Col. 0443A] of Frederick, persecutor of God’s Church, has determined that he will compel all ecclesiastical persons dwelling in lands subject to him, including those from the realm of our dearest son in Christ Louis, illustrious King of the Franks, either to worship an idol or to leave their own homes and endure exile. Since this is wholly opposed to the honour of God, of the Church, of the aforesaid king, and of the entire realm entrusted to his governance, and is certainly known in every way to redound to the peril of his salvation, we ask, admonish, and exhort your brotherhood in the Lord by apostolic letters that, out of reverence for God’s Church—whose cause you have undertaken to defend in every respect as your own—and out of regard for blessed Peter and ourselves, you diligently admonish [Col. 0443B] the aforesaid king and induce him by every means, through letters and his messenger, to anticipate the said count before he attempts the crime of so great a sacrilege, and to endeavour to recall him wholly from the audacity of this presumption. You shall also carefully admonish and induce him by every means to restore as swiftly as possible to his own see our venerable brother, the Bishop of Grenoble [Note: [Col. 0443D] John, who had been raised from a Carthusian monk to the episcopal mitre of the Church of Grenoble.], whom he expelled. Thus may he gain from almighty God the reward of eternal recompense for this deed; may the Church of God remember it always; may we ourselves offer the king most abundant thanks for it; and may we be able to commend your brotherhood in many ways in the Lord for this matter.

Given at the Lateran, the third day before the Kalends of May.

## CDXXXVIII. To the same.—Concerning the election and consecration of the Bishop of Tournai. (Lateran, April 30.)

[Ibid., col. 733.]

[Col. 0443C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since from the beginning of our elevation we have known the ardour of your most sincere devotion by sure and manifest proofs—so that you received our brethren who came to the kingdom of France on our behalf with such affection that you always and everywhere conducted our affair and that of the Church with them as though it were your own—we cannot sufficiently wonder at your judgment if the reports brought to us regarding the affair of the Church of Tournai are true. For we have heard that, after an appeal and a special prohibition issued on our behalf, you consecrated as bishop the man whom the clerks of that church are said to have chosen; especially since we deferred hearing the case with the intention [Col. 0443D] of showing deference to our dearest son in Christ Louis, illustrious King of the Franks, and to you as our dearest brother, sparing the expenses and labours of both parties, and allowing the aforesaid clerks of Noyon to show us the documents on which they relied, which they did not have at hand. [Note: [Col. 0443D] From this passage one may infer that the canons of Noyon took the separation of the bishopric of Tournai from that of Noyon ill, and that after Anselm and Gerald, perhaps his successor Walter, they wished [Col. 0444D] to prevent the election of a new bishop and laboured to unite the bishopric of Tournai once more to that of Noyon, as formerly.]

For this reason we are more disturbed, since, in the matter in which we deferred to you, you did not, if what is alleged is true, take care to defer to us. Therefore we admonish and command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if the matter stands as it has been reported to us, you carefully consider what has been done, how greatly we have been injured in this, and how completely it runs counter to the sacred canons and ecclesiastical custom; and that you cause the person who is said to have been so unlawfully made bishop to cease entirely from episcopal office [Col. 0444B] until he and those who elected him come before us to obey our mandate on this matter [the text reads *quod*; read *et qui*]. But if this is not so, write to us as soon as possible, that you may thus remove all resentment and disturbance from our mind. If the matter is as stated, correct it quickly; and by letter and messenger inform us with all haste how you have corrected it, or, if it has not been corrected, so that we may be able to correct the transgression of so great a presumption as we know expedient. For, if it is true, we preferred that this be punished through you rather than by ourselves.

Given at the Lateran, the second day before the Kalends of May.

## CDXXXIX. To the same.—Concerning the case of the Church of Bragny. (Lateran, May 14.)

[Ibid., col. 735.]

[Col. 0444C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have committed for hearing and due final determination to our venerable brother, the Bishop of Laon, the case known to be pending between our beloved sons, the canons of St Peter of Bragny, and the prior of the monastery [Note: [Col. 0444D] A notable cell dependent on La Sauve-Majeure, near Registetum, in the diocese of Reims.] of Novy, concerning their church, which that prior is attempting to bring under his own jurisdiction. We therefore command your brotherhood by apostolic letters [Col. 0444D] that, when you are requested in this matter, you compel both parties with all strictness to appear before the said bishop and firmly to accept and observe his judgment.

Given at the Lateran, the second day before the Ides of May.

## CDXL. He commands the Pisan canons to avoid B., their former canon, an excommunicated defender of schism, but nevertheless to receive him if he returns to virtue. (Lateran, May 15.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 403.]

[Col. 0445A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the Pisan canons abiding in the unity of the Church, greeting and apostolic blessing.

His wicked and detestable deeds and his public conduct show how B., once your canon, has returned like a dog to his vomit, and according to his ability and limited powers has striven to persecute and harass us and the Church in every way, never ceasing to defend and foster the party of schism. Therefore we command you by apostolic letters [Col. 0445B] to have no association with him; to avoid him by every means as a schismatic, a rotten member, and one separated from the body of Christ, which is the Church; and to admonish and command by our authority all your fellow-canons and all Catholic men of your city to do the same.

But lest we seem to reject him, or anyone else wishing to return to the bosom of the Church, or to cast him into the snare of despair: if he is willing to correct his error, publicly to abjure schism, to profess obedience to us as his father and Roman pontiff, and to swear that he will abide by our command, then, once he has done this, you may without hesitation receive him as your brother and associate with him. But if any of you should associate with him, or presume to give him consent or support in such great wickedness, he must fear becoming a participant in that man’s condemnation and being punished together with him by the same penalty.

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of May.

## CDXLI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—On behalf of a certain Job., that what was taken from him be restored. (Lateran, May 26.)

[MARTEN, *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 736.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0445D] From the complaint of Job., bearer of the present letters, we have learned that Anch. of Waiseiac and Guiter of Ambonivilla violently took two cows from him. Manasses and Teob., moreover, with their companions, broke into the church of St Maurice with diabolical audacity and carried away from there the goods of the aforesaid Jo. which he had there. Since it is our concern to assist every person in the maintenance of his right, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters carefully to admonish the aforesaid wrongdoers and, if necessary, compel them under the strictness of anathema either to restore in full and without diminution all that they took from the aforesaid J., or to render him full justice in this matter before you without dilatory delay.

Given at the Lateran, the seventh day before the Kalends of June.

## CDXLII. To the same.—On behalf of a certain G., citizen of Reims. (Lateran, May 28.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 0446A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the statement transmitted to us by G., your citizen, we have learned that, when a dispute concerning a sum of money had arisen between him and Simon Deauratus and had been brought by appeal before our hearing, they reached an amicable agreement in our court and made this settlement between themselves: Simon was to pay the said G. twelve pounds. But afterwards, when they had returned home [Col. 0446B] and the aforesaid G. demanded from him the money agreed upon, he wholly refused to pay it. Therefore the said G. appealed the aforesaid Simon to our hearing, setting the octave of the Easter which has lately passed as the term for the appeal. When the said G.’s advocate was before us and had waited a long time after the day of appeal, the opposing party neither came nor sent to us any advocate on his behalf.

We therefore command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, when you are requested in this matter, summon both parties before you. If it is lawfully established to you that an amicable settlement or judgment intervened between them, compel both parties with all strictness, all appeal set aside, firmly to observe it. [Col. 0446C] But if you find that they did not reach a settlement or that no judgment was given between them, hear the case and decide it through justice, with appeal removed.

Given at the Lateran, the fifth day before the Kalends of June.

## CDXLIII. To the Bishop-elect of Cahors.—He commands him to render judgment concerning Peter Mancovela, priest.

[From Book VIII of the Register.—Mansi, *Concil.*, XXII, 432.]

## CDXLIV. He informs the Bishop of Norwich that he has released R., a clerk, from the vow of a journey to Jerusalem.

[Ibid.—From Book VIII of the Register.]

## YEAR 1167.

## CDXLV. To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the legation sent into England. (Lateran, January?)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXI, 882.]

[Col. 0446D]

You should know that the reason why we do not visit your person more often by our letters is that, through your messengers, we have more frequently taken care to communicate orally to your knowledge matters which we did not think fit to commit to writing. But now we wish it to come to your discretion’s notice that, earnestly desiring your peace with the heart’s most ardent affections, we have sent our beloved sons, William, cardinal-priest of the title of St Peter in Chains, and Odo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, [Col. 0447A] to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the English, to exercise a legation in his lands on this side of the sea; and especially to restore harmony and peace between you and that king, and, with the Lord’s cooperation, effect an amicable settlement.

Since we regard your peace and that of the Church as wholly one, and since we desire it all the more because we believe that it will bring greater benefit to the universal Church, we ask, admonish, counsel, and command your brotherhood by apostolic letters carefully to consider and reflect how dangerous the present state of affairs is and how greatly the Church entrusted to you needs your presence and counsel; and to incline your mind and will toward establishing peace and concord [Col. 0447B] between yourself and the said king, so far as this can be done without prejudice to your honour and that of the Church.

And if not everything in these matters turns out according to your wish, bear for the present what must be corrected, intending, with the Lord as author, to restore it in time to its former state. Nor should you in any manner be delayed from peace and the good of concord, or turn your mind and will away from these things, because of the message which, at your request, we communicated to our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious King of the Franks—provided that in the agreement you can preserve, as we have said, your own honour and that of the Church. For by proceeding gradually and with discretion you will later be able to remove many things which, if you pressed them now, [Col. 0447C] would seem to involve something serious.

You may place complete confidence in the aforesaid cardinals, and you need not have any doubt whatever about the said William, because we firmly and explicitly enjoined him to devote all his strength to securing your peace; and he has promised us so much that we have no doubt at all on that score.

Furthermore, we ask and admonish your brotherhood carefully to approach on our behalf our beloved son, the noble Count of Flanders, and urge him more insistently, in view of our need and that of the Church, to endeavour generously to assist us in some way. For we do not believe that he can make an alms more acceptable to God than [Col. 0447D] by striving now to afford us the help of worthy assistance for the defence of the Church’s liberty.

## CDXLVI. To Henry, King of England.—Of the same purport.

[Ibid., col. 883.]

Having gladly admitted the petitions of your magnificence, desiring to satisfy your will in all things, so far as we can with God and justice, and wishing to show deference to you and your honour, we have judged it fitting to send as legates into your lands on this side of the sea our beloved sons, William, cardinal-priest of the title of St Peter in Chains, and Odo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison—men indeed learned, [Col. 0448A] discerning and honourable alike, holding high rank in God’s Church, devoted to you and your kingdom, and among our other brethren especially dear and welcome to us—with full authority to hear and determine the cases which we set out to you in other letters, together with any others which they see ought to be handled. We have entrusted them with our functions to be exercised in every respect as fully as the Roman Church is accustomed to entrust them to those men, or other legates of the Apostolic See.

Therefore we ask, admonish, and exhort your serenity in the Lord by apostolic letters to receive them honourably and kindly, as such great men and legates of the Apostolic See, and treat them gently in the manner fitting royal [Col. 0448B] honour, so that the holy Roman Church may recognize your ancient devotion in her sons, and so that, with the Lord’s cooperation, no small benefit may result from this for your magnificence and for the whole land entrusted to your governance. Receive gravely the matters which they propose to your highness on our behalf, and assent to them with ready mind, so that the Lord and His Church may thereby be honoured as they deserve, and you yourself, together with the whole land entrusted to your governance, may obtain from this manifold fruit, reward from God, and praise and glory before men.

“Reveal this copy to no mortal except Master Gunter, because I gave my word on this matter to Master Walter as strictly as he wished.” [Note: [Col. 0447D] The words enclosed in brackets are not attributable to Alexander, the author, but were added by some other person who secretly copied the letter for the use of Thomas of Canterbury. JAFFÉ.]

## CDXLVII. To Louis VII, King of the Franks.—Concerning the legation entrusted through France to Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.

[Ibid.]

Among the other marks of your magnificence and devotion, this especially kindles our heart with great ardour: that you have honoured our venerable brother Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, a man religious, discerning, and honourable alike, and in every respect dear and welcome to us and to the whole Church of God, with so many and such great honours, and have deigned, with royal generosity, lavishly to bestow upon him such extensive and magnificent benefits of kindness. [Col. 0448D] For this indeed we offer your serenity as much and such thanks as we can, and commend your clemency with boundless praise in the Lord, regarding it as most weighty before God—since you did these things rather to God in his person—and as welcome to us as if you had bestowed them especially upon our own person.

And since we desire the peace of that archbishop with all the affections of our heart, we have judged it fitting to send our beloved sons William, cardinal-priest of the title of St Peter in Chains, and Odo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, to our dearest son in Christ Henry, illustrious King of the English, in order that, with the Lord’s cooperation, they may restore perfect harmony and peace between that king [Col. 0449A] and the aforesaid archbishop, to the honour of both alike; that they may hear and examine cases arising in the king’s overseas realm; and that they may there exercise the legation of the Apostolic See.

We therefore ask, admonish, and exhort your magnificence in the Lord by apostolic letters to intervene effectively and labour diligently with the aforesaid king and archbishop, out of reverence for God’s Church and honour for blessed Peter and ourselves, so that, to the honour of God and the Church and also to their own advantage and advancement, they may reach an amicable and peaceful settlement with one another; and that they may by every means incline their minds and wills to this, without prejudice [Col. 0449B] to the honour of the archbishop himself and of the Church. If peace and concord can be restored between them through the effort of the aforesaid cardinals and through your labour and assistance, the Church—which after God is especially sustained by your help—will receive no small advancement from it, and you will obtain from almighty God a special reward for this in the blessed recompense of the just.

But if—may God avert it—they cannot agree, provided it were acceptable to the royal will and to your good pleasure, it would please us greatly and be most welcome if, should it be possible without grave scandal to the persons of your realm, we bestowed upon the aforesaid archbishop a prerogative of special [Col. 0449C] honour above the rest and entrusted him with the exercise of our functions in those regions. We therefore beg your serenity with all the prayer we can offer that, if he cannot have peace without prejudice to his own honour and that of the Church—which we desire in every way—you endeavour with all speed to communicate your wishes to us on these matters. Meanwhile, keep this wholly secret.

## CDXLVIII. He takes the Venetian Church of St Saviour under his protection. (Lateran, January 5.)

[CORNELII, *Ecclesiae Venetae*, XIV, 97.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons VIVIAN, prior of the church of St Saviour situated at Rialto, and his brethren, present and future, who profess the canonical life, for ever.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may love religious persons and strive by every means to promote religion pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptably to God unless it proceeds from the root of charity and is preserved in the purity of religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of St Saviour, in which you are devoted to divine service, after the example of our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Innocent, Eugenius, and Anastasius; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 0450A]

Since you have vowed to observe the canonical order and to live according to the Rule of St Augustine, we willingly assent to your wishes and establish by apostolic authority that this order shall remain inviolate in that church for all time. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter obtain, with the Lord’s favour, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. We likewise confirm to you the portion of tithes from your parishioners which belongs to your church according to the sacred canons and the enactments of the holy Fathers. [Col. 0450B]

We further add and forbid that any prior be set over that church by any deceitful artifice or force, save one whom the brethren of that place collectively, or the sounder part of their counsel, canonically provide to be elected. We also grant that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while the right of the mother church is nevertheless preserved. You may also receive without anyone’s objection into conversion clerks or free and unencumbered laymen fleeing from the world.

But we prohibit anyone from presuming, after a brother has made profession in that [Col. 0450C] place, to leave the cloister rashly without his prior’s permission; and no one may dare retain a departing brother without a certificate in common letters.

Moreover, we confirm by apostolic authority the judgment which our venerable brother Henry, Patriarch of Grado, and our beloved son Ildebrand, priest-cardinal of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles and legate of the Apostolic See, reasonably rendered in the long-standing dispute between you and the lord plebanus of Saint Bartholomew concerning certain parochial houses—namely, the houses of the righteous Maurocenus of Grado, of the Greeks Leonard Fradelli and Dominic Aureus—which each party claimed to belong to his own right, as is known to be contained in their authentic instrument drawn up concerning this matter [Col. 0450D]. We decree that no one, without your consent, shall dare to give penance to your parishioners when sick, anoint them, or receive them for burial, save without prejudice to the right of your church in respect of its share of testamentary bequests.

Therefore we decree, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Walter, bishop of Albano. I, Ubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, of Pammachius. I, William, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Peter in Chains. [Col. 0451A] I, Boso, priest-cardinal of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, Theodinus, priest-cardinal of Saint Vitalis, of the title of Vestina. I, Galdinus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina and Archbishop of Milan. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Cinthius, deacon-cardinal of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of January, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1166, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## CDXLIX. He confirms the possessions of the monastery of Saint Savin of Tarbes.  
*(Lateran, 17 March.)*

*[Gallia Christiana, I, Instruments, 193.]*

[Col. 0451B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons DEUSDET, elect of Saint Savin, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Whenever that which is asked of us, etc., among which we have judged the following to be set out by their proper names: the castle in which that monastery is situated; the church of Saint John with the village of Bencus and its appurtenances; the church of Saint Martin of Arsissans, with all that the monastery possesses within its boundaries; the church of Saint Martin [Col. 0451C] of Cauterets with its baths, and whatever you possess in that valley or at Aestivis; the chapel of Saint Andrew of Solon; the village of Nestalas with its boundaries, and the chapel of Saint Peter of that village; the chapel of Saint Bartholomew of Adast; the chapel of Saint Martin of Balaignas; the church of Saint Mary of Castel; the church of Saint Saturninus of Orout, and whatever you possess within the bounds of that village; the chapel of Saint Cecilia of Uzol; the church of Saint Saturninus of Ugos; whatever you possess in the church of Saint Mary of Cera; whatever you possess in the village of Arreins, in estates, tithes, and peasant holdings; whatever you possess in the village of Aucun, in the village of Guaillaguos, in the village of Areisans, and in the village of Bun, in estates, tithes, [Col. 0451D] and peasant holdings; whatever you possess in the village of Arras and within the bounds of that village; whatever you possess at Villelongue and in the church of that village, in estates, tithes, and peasant holdings; the church of Saint Vincent of Beaviens with its appurtenances; the village of Souin with its appurtenances; the cattle-farm of Puisseda with its appurtenances; the cattle-farm of Sois with its appurtenances; whatever you possess in the village of Lurp, in estates and tithes; whatever you possess in the village of Curel and within its bounds, in the valley of Barèges; the cell of Saint Mary with its appurtenances; whatever you possess in the church of Saint Mary of Villars; the cattle-farms of Thiezam and Balaignam with their appurtenances; whatever you possess in the church of Geu; the houses which you possess in the city of Syracuse, with the ground belonging to them; [Col. 0452A] a garden with vineyards outside that city; the fields which you possess in the district of Curtida; and whatever the aforesaid monastery has, under a just title, peacefully and without disturbance possessed from forty years ago until now, and is presently known to possess peacefully—all these we likewise confirm to you by apostolic authority. Therefore we decree, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Walter, bishop of Albano. I, Uraldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Bozo, priest-cardinal of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. [Col. 0452B] I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, Teodhitus, priest-cardinal of the title of Vestina. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Mansfredus, deacon-cardinal at the Golden Veil. I, Hugh, deacon-cardinal of Saint Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa. I, Peter de Bonozo, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Aquiro, of Saint Mary the New.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Gerard, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year [Col. 0452C] of the Lord’s Incarnation 1167, in the eighth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III, with the seal of the said supreme pontiff.

## CDL. To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the absolution of Count Hugh if he restores what he took.  
*(Lateran, 22 April.)*

*[Letters of Saint Thomas, ed. Giles, II, 23.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother THOMAS, Archbishop of Canterbury, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

We wish it to come to the knowledge of your discretion that we have instructed our venerable brethren, the bishops of Winchester and Worcester, that, upon receiving adequate security from the noble Count Hugh that he will obey their command concerning the matters for which he has been excommunicated, they shall, all objection and appeal ceasing, absolve him from the sentence by which he is bound. Thereafter, by security accepted, they shall compel him to restore in full, within the following forty days, all that he took from the canons of Pantaenia or that is held by bishops as having been taken by him. But if the count does not make restitution in accordance with that command within the time prescribed for him, they shall, with all pretext and appeal removed, restore him to his former sentence of excommunication. If the aforesaid bishops neglect to carry this out, do not delay to return the said count, within thirty days after the aforesaid forty [Col. 0453A] days, to the former sentence. But if Hugh should wish to make satisfaction, you shall, when satisfaction has been made, cause him to be absolved either through another or by yourself. If, however, the same Hugh does not repent within a year after the sentence pronounced against him, you shall from that time place his whole land under interdict.

Given at the Lateran, on the tenth day before the Kalends of May.

## CDL *bis*. He confirms the immunities and privileges of the Church of Modena.  
*(Lateran, 4 May.)*

*[Tiraboschi, Memorie Modenesi, II, 93.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother . . . . bishop of Modena and his successors canonically appointed [Col. 0453B] for ever.

Just as no effect ought to be granted to those who request unjust things, so the petition of those who desire what is lawful ought not to be delayed. Therefore, assenting to your prayers, dearest brother in Christ, we establish by the authority of this present decree, for the perpetual peace and stability of the holy Church of Modena over which, by God’s authority, you preside, that all the boundaries of the bishopric of Modena shall henceforth be preserved wholly peaceful and intact for you and your successors. These boundaries are marked out by the following divisions: from those boundaries which divide the bishoprics of Lucca and Pistoia from that of Modena, as far as the river called Burana, and as far as the boundary [Col. 0453C] called Mutia; thence as far as the boundary which separates the bishopric of Bologna from your bishopric; and, on the other side, as far as the boundaries which distinguish the bishopric of Modena from that of Reggio.

We grant and confirm to you and your successors the consecration of churches lying within these boundaries, the promotion of clerics, tithes, and offerings, in accordance with the ordinances of the holy canons, just as you are known hitherto to have possessed them freely and peacefully; especially in the parish church of Saint Mary of Bodruntio, which is in the court of Sicci, and in its chapels; in all churches that are in the castle and court of Solaria and in the parish church of Roncaglia; in all churches of Ponte-Ducis; in the church of Camurana; in the churches [Col. 0453D] of the Court of Curtiola; in the church of Sclopano; in the church of Saint Peter in Siculo; and in the churches which are in the old castle and in its court; in all churches which are in the castle and court of Panciani of the abbey of Leonense; and in all churches which are in the parish church of Rubiani. Moreover, whatever goods and possessions you lawfully possess at present, or may hereafter, by God’s gift, justly and canonically acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We therefore decree that no bishop whatsoever shall have authority within the aforesaid boundaries, without your consent or that of your successors, to consecrate a church, make chrism, or ordain clerics—except the churches [Col. 0454A] and clerics of the castle and borough of Nonantola, as has been observed from ancient times. Nor may any person rashly disturb your church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with wanton vexations; rather, all shall be preserved intact for the use of you, of the clergy, and of the poor.

Indeed, concerning priests appointed in churches through parishes belonging to monasteries, we confirm the decree of our predecessors of holy memory, Popes Urban II and Calixtus II: abbots shall not install priests in the parochial churches which they hold without the counsel of bishops; rather, bishops, with the consent of abbots, shall entrust the pastoral care of the parish to a priest. Such priests shall render account to the bishop for the care of the people, while rendering to the abbot due subjection in temporal matters belonging to the monastery; and thus each person’s rights shall be preserved. If therefore in future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Bernard, bishop of the Church of Porto. I, Gualterius, bishop of Albano. I, C., Archbishop of Mainz and bishop of Sabina. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul. [Col. 0454C] I, Henry, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, William, priest-cardinal of Saint Peter in Chains. I, Boso, priest-cardinal of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, Theodinus, priest-cardinal of Saint Vitalis, of the title of Vestina. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Ardicio, deacon-cardinal of Saint Theodore. I, Cinthius, deacon-cardinal of Saint Adrian. [Col. 0454D] I, Manfred, deacon-cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Hugh, deacon-cardinal of Saint Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa. I, Vitellus, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Peter, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Aquiro. I, Jer., deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary the New.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Hermann, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, on the fourth day before the Nones of May, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1167, in the seventh year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

> **Note [Col. 0453]:** The chronological indications do not agree. Read: fifteenth indiction, eighth year of the pontificate.

## CDLI. To Cardinals William and Otto, legates.—He declares that no rights have been taken from Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.  
*(Lateran, 7 May.)*

*[Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II, 55.]*

[Col. 0455A]

After your departure serious reports have been brought to us: namely, that our beloved son John, Dean of Salisbury, has publicly asserted that, since we had exempted bishops and other ecclesiastical and secular persons of the kingdom of England from the jurisdiction and power of our venerable brother Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, we intended, in accordance with the pleasure and will of the King of England, to direct matters toward his disposition and condemnation alike; and that you ought to be sent especially for this purpose. We have also been told that [Col. 0455B] John Cumin showed Guy of Crema all the rescripts of our letters which he obtained from us and disclosed our secrets to him. Thus the archbishop himself is overwhelmed with shame and grief, while our dearest son in Christ, Louis, the illustrious King of France, and his princes have been considerably disturbed and violently stirred by rumours of this kind.

Although many have represented to us, and it appears in some measure credible, that the aforesaid John has laboured so faithfully for the honour and advancement of the aforesaid archbishop and his church, and solely for the liberty of the Church, that through his zeal and diligence, after returning home, he caused ecclesiastical men who were held in royal custody to be released from prison. Moreover, [Col. 0455C] John himself has informed us by letter that the king publicly said before many persons that he wished to preserve for the clerics of his land that liberty which they had enjoyed from the time of Henry, his grandfather.

Nevertheless, because this rumour has grown to such an extent that in those regions it causes our reputation to be impaired by hostile judgment, we admonish and command your discretion to take care at once to console the aforesaid archbishop by our letters. Remove every bitterness and suspicion from his mind; strive above all to reconcile him with the aforesaid king and to establish complete peace between them; and labour toward this with all the care and diligence you can muster. Thus you shall [Col. 0455D] preserve wholly intact and unimpaired for him and his church their ancient rights and liberties. Do not undertake anything important in his land, and on no account enter his kingdom, should you wish to do so, unless the archbishop is first completely reconciled with him; for on this account great reproach would be directed against both us and you, and the common voice of all would tear apart our honour by malicious disparagements.

As for John Cumin, if you find the matter to be as reported, administer strict justice, so that others may be deterred from like conduct. We further wish you to conduct yourselves in all your acts and undertakings circumspectly, maturely, and prudently, so that no occasion for detraction against us may arise, and that, through your zeal and conduct, the devotion of both kingdoms toward us and the Church may continually increase [Col. 0456A], and that everlasting praise and glory may thereby be secured for you.

Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of May.

## CDLII. To Raymond, Bishop of Brescia, and his successors, he affirms the right to sit at the Archbishop of Milan’s right hand in synods.  
*(Rome, at Saint Mary the New, 31 May.)*

*[Ughelli, Italia sacra, IV, 544.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RAYMOND, Bishop of Brescia, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

From the account sent to us by you, and long ago from the mouth of Oberto, of good memory, formerly Archbishop of Milan, we learned that whenever the suffragans of the Church of Milan were summoned, you ought to have the seat nearest the archbishop’s right hand. A question had, indeed, arisen between you and the Bishop of Vercelli on this matter, and we remember that we previously granted you letters of our confirmation. But, since we have subsequently heard that those letters were lost, we confirm by apostolic authority the aforesaid seat to your devotion and, through you, to your successors; and we fortify it by the protection of this present writing, decreeing that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way contravene it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul [Col. 0456C].

Given at Rome, at Saint Mary the New, on the day before the Kalends of June.

## CDLIII. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—Concerning the case of the abbot of Saint-Remi and the woman Si.  
*(Rome, at Saint Mary the New, 1 June.)*

*[Marten, Amplissima Collectio, II, 741.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

We entrust to your experience for hearing and due final determination the case known to be in litigation between our beloved son the Abbot of Saint-Remi and the woman Si. concerning a certain mill and the millstream belonging to that mill. Therefore we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, when requested concerning this, you summon both parties before you; and, after hearing and examining the reasons on either side, decide the case in accordance with justice [Col. 0456D].

Given at Rome, at Saint Mary the New, on the Kalends of June.

## CDLIV. To Galdinus, Archbishop of Milan.—That he revoke certain privileges granted by the late Archbishop Robald to the canons of Monza, to the injury of the convent of Cremella.  
*(Rome, at Saint Mary the New, 13 June.)*

*[Giulini, Memorie di Milano, VI, p. 535, Documents.]*

It has been represented to us and almost certainly shown [Col. 0457A] that your predecessor Robald, of good memory, formerly Archbishop of Milan, while still unaware of the customs and liberties of the church committed to you, made the following concession to the archpriest and canons of Monza: whenever the abbess of the monastery of Cremella is elected there, she is to be enthroned by the aforesaid archpriest; the nuns are to promise obedience to him; and the laymen are to swear fealty. Since we have heard that, by reason of this arrangement, utter desolation threatens the aforesaid monastery, and that the archpriest and canons are striving for its destruction, we revoke the aforesaid concession, if the facts are so, declare it void, and decree that it shall have no force henceforward. By the authority of these presents we command your brotherhood to announce that it is annulled by our authority and will retain no validity hereafter [Col. 0457B].

Given at Rome, at Saint Mary the New, on the Ides of June.

## CDLV. To Roger, Archbishop of York.—He commands that, if requested by Henry, King of England, he place the crown upon Henry, the king’s eldest son.  
*(Rome, at Saint Mary the New, 31 May.)*

*[Letters of Saint Thomas, ed. Giles, II, 45; Boehmer, Corpus juris canonici, II, appendix, 309.]*

The more it is known that greater aid and advantages have accrued to the Church of God, in this time of necessity, through our dearest son Henry, the illustrious King of England [Col. 0457C], and the more dearly we love him for the constancy of his devotion and keep him more beloved in our inmost heart, the more willingly and readily do we further what we know pertains to the honour, advancement, and exaltation of him and his family. Therefore, at his request, after consulting our brethren, we grant by the authority of blessed Peter and our own that our beloved son Henry, his first-born son, be crowned in England.

Since this pertains to your office, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, when requested concerning this by the same our son the king, you place upon his aforesaid son the crown by authority of the Apostolic See. We decree that what you do in this respect shall remain ratified and firm. You, however, shall render him due subjection and reverence, without prejudice in all things to his father’s command, and shall similarly admonish others to render it.

> **Note [Col. 0457D]:** Boehmer adds: “Given by the Roman Chancery at Saint Mary the New, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July.”

## CDLVI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—Concerning a certain woman, Hersendis.  
*(Rome, at Saint Mary the New, 27 June.)*

*[Marten, Amplissima Collectio, II, 741.]*

We cannot but wonder at the negligence and lukewarmness of the Bishop of Châlons [Col. 0458A]. Our beloved sons C. and M., deacon-cardinals of the Holy Roman Church, had formerly commanded him by our authority to compel O. Rufus to pay Hersendis one hundred solidi, which they had adjudged to that woman by our order. Yet he fulfilled neither their command nor ours, and did not excommunicate the aforesaid O. as had been enjoined upon him. Therefore we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if the said bishop has not carried out our command, you compel the aforesaid O., with all strictness, to pay the said woman in full the one hundred solidi, as adjudged by the cardinals. If he should presume to disobey your command, you shall, by our authority and notwithstanding any appeal, declare him excommunicated until he has fully carried it out, and cause him to be diligently avoided by all [Col. 0458B].

Furthermore, since the aforesaid woman makes many complaints against the priest Pag. and William the burgess, alleging that they have unreasonably inflicted many losses and injuries upon her, you shall likewise compel them, if necessary by ecclesiastical censure, either to make satisfaction to that woman as reason requires, or to render full justice in your presence.

> **Note [Col. 0458D]:** Cinthius of the title of Saint Adrian, and Matfredus of the title of Saint George in Velabro.

Given at Rome, at Saint Mary the New, on the fifth day before the Kalends of July.

## CDLXVII. To the same.—Concerning suspicion of forged letters against Milo.  
*(Rome, at Saint Mary the New, 28 June.)*

*[Ibid.]*

[Col. 0458C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

From the statement of the clerk Milo, bearer of these presents, we have learned that Eustace and Theob. declared to be false the letters which we formerly sent to your brotherhood concerning the affair of the woman Hersendis and her sons against them, and stubbornly asserted that they had not been drawn up in our chancery. But from the script of those letters and the confession of the person who drew them up, recognizing the manner and style of writing of the Roman Church, we declare to your diligence that they are genuine and entirely free from suspicion of forgery. We do not wish the aforesaid Milo, who obtained those letters from us, to be blackened on this account by any mark or stain of reproach. Yet we do not wish you to rely upon their tenor, especially in the part dealing with debtors [Col. 0458D].

Furthermore, by the authority of these presents we enjoin upon your diligence that, if you have excommunicated the aforesaid men, Eustace and Theob., as their offences required, you shall on no account absolve them unless they have made full satisfaction to the same woman concerning the matters for which they were excommunicated, as equity, reason, and the order of justice require. Rather, you shall cause that sentence to be inviolably observed until due satisfaction has been made [Col. 0459A]. On behalf of both us and you, strictly prohibit our brother, the Bishop of Châlons, from presuming to inflict any molestation or burden upon Milo because he frequents our curia; and should he presume to molest him on that account, protect and defend him with special care.

Given at Rome, at Saint Mary the New, on the fourth day before the Kalends of July.

## CDLXVIII. To the same.—Commendation and exhortation that he aid the pope, induce the king to do the same, and concerning the case of Master G., priest, for a prebend at Soissons.  
*(Rome, at Saint Mary the New, 1 July.)*

*[Ibid., col. 743.]*

[Col. 0459B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

When we earnestly recall the most sincere devotion and purity of faith which, from the beginning of this disturbance, you have shown as prudently as magnanimously toward our person and toward advancing the affairs of the Church, we are moved by desire and resolve to return a corresponding measure of affection to you as to a most dear brother, and to promote with ready mind and earnest care the honour and advancement of you and of the Church over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside.

Since we know that you share in our necessities and those of the Church [Col. 0459C], and are greatly troubled by adversities, let your brotherhood learn from this communication that the City, through the ignorance and inertia of its people and—as we believe—by divine judgment, has suffered a partial reverse at the hands of its enemies. By this, indeed, the condition of the Church could not but be burdened and suffer the inconvenience of adversity. Nevertheless, it has suffered much less damage than report alleges, as your discretion will learn fully and certainly from the account of our beloved sons J. and P., clerks of our brother the Archbishop of Tours, and of the beloved elect of Chartres.

> **Note [Cols. 0459D–0460D]:** This appears to be William called *ad Albas-manus*, born of Theobald and Matilda of Carinthia, of the lineage of the Counts Palatine of Champagne, who in 1164 succeeded Robert as Bishop-elect of Chartres; in 1168, before consecration, he was transferred to the see of Sens; and afterward, following Henry, to Reims.

Since we and the Roman Church have always found you a most diligent helper, [Col. 0459D] we ask, admonish, and earnestly exhort your prudence that, as you have well begun, you may labour steadfastly and courageously for the advancement and exaltation of the Church and strive unceasingly to advance its honour. Thus you may deserve to receive an eternal reward from almighty God; and both that Church and we, who, though unworthy, serve in it by God’s appointment, may at all times yearn with the devoted affections of our hearts for the increase in honour and exaltation of the Church entrusted to you.

[Col. 0460A] Given at Rome, at Saint Mary the New, on the Kalends of July.

## CDLIX. To William and Otto, legates of the Apostolic See.—That, for the good of the Church, the Kings of France and England be reconciled; and that in England they do nothing concerning the state of the realm and Church without the knowledge of Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.  
*(Benevento, 22 August.)*

*[Letters of Gilbert Foliot, II, 57.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to WILLIAM, priest-cardinal of Saint Peter in Chains, and OTTO, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison and legates of the Apostolic See, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

It is proper for our discretion to consider how great the losses and disadvantages that may arise for the whole Church of God—especially the Roman and Eastern Church—from the discord and dissension which, through the enemy of humankind, has occurred between our dearest sons in Christ, the illustrious Kings of France and England [Col. 0460B]; and to strive all the more diligently to extinguish them, the greater are the dangers which we fear may result, God forbid.

Therefore, by apostolic letters, we admonish, command, and direct your discretion to make every effort, through yourselves and through other religious and prudent men of both kingdoms, to restore peace and concord between them. Labour toward this with complete diligence and all your strength, taking every precaution that, at the request or in favour [Col. 0460C] of either one, you establish nothing by which the other ought to be offended or disturbed in any way.

Moreover, we strictly forbid either of you, or either one separately, to presume to enter the kingdom of England, or to transact matters concerning that kingdom, and especially to effect or ordain anything whatsoever concerning the consecrations of bishops, unless our venerable brother Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, is first fully reconciled to the aforesaid King of England. We trust and altogether hope that, through your zeal and efforts with the Lord’s assistance, this can be brought about. For, as we have learned from the letters of many prudent men, nothing has more disturbed or agitated the aforesaid King of France and all his land than the things which John, Dean of Salisbury, is said to have spread in those regions when returning from us [Col. 0460D].

Given at Benevento, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of September.

## CDLX. To the same.—That they compel those excommunicated by the Archbishop of Canterbury for invading the Church’s goods to render due satisfaction; and, should they refuse, excommunicate them again.  
*(Benevento, 2 August.)*

*[Ibid., p. 56.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, [Col. 0461A] to his beloved sons WILLIAM, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Peter in Chains, and OTTO, of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, cardinals and legates of the Apostolic See, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

It has been represented to us that certain persons whom our venerable brother Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, had subjected to excommunication presume to retain and lay hands upon the goods and possessions of his church and of its clerics. Since it is unworthy that they should be absolved from the bond by which they are bound while retaining those goods and possessions, we command your discretion by apostolic letters that, if, as we hear, they have already been absolved by someone, you firmly enjoin on them on our behalf and by force of oath to relinquish immediately the aforesaid [Col. 0461B] possessions and goods to the persons and churches to whose right they belong; nor may they presume, on any pretext, to retain them or hereafter to interfere with them. If they do not obey your command, restore them, all delay and appeal ceasing, to the former sentence of excommunication until full satisfaction has been made. If they have been absolved by you, you shall nevertheless do the same as we have said.

## CDLXI. To Albert, legate of the Apostolic See.—He forbids him to accept the archbishopric of Split offered to him.  
*(Benevento, 31 August.)*

*[Farlati, Illyricum sacrum, III, 188.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, [Col. 0461C] to his beloved son ALBERT, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina and legate of the Apostolic See, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

We have received the letter of your devotion with paternal kindness. Having understood its contents, we have sent, as you requested, quite careful and effective letters concerning the release of our beloved son Bon. of Siponto, our venerable brother Archbishop Lampridius, and the leading men of Zadar. Further, concerning your report that the clergy and people of Split wished to choose you as their shepherd, we disclose to you our will and mind: even if you wished it and the greater part of our brethren pressed for it, we would on no account consent [Col. 0461D], nor could we ever be induced to permit you to be absent from us, by whom you are so purely and sincerely loved and held so dear and acceptable.

Therefore, utterly banish such anxiety and apprehension from your mind, and prudently and diligently attend to the legation imposed upon you, so that the Roman Church may receive joyful advancement from your diligence and zeal, and you too may obtain a worthy reward from your labour and vigilance.

Given at Benevento, on the second day before the Kalends of September.

## CDLXII. He commands Henry, Abbot of Biburg, to accept the abbey of Saint Peter of Salzburg, offered to him by Archbishop Conrad and the monks.  
*(Benevento, 24 November.)*

*New Chronicle of the Monastery of Saint Peter, Salzburg, p. 241.*

## CDLXIII. He commands the monks of Biburg to release Abbot Henry to the monastery of Saint Peter of Salzburg.  
*(Benevento, 24 November.)*

*[Ibid.]*

[Col. 0462A]

## CDLXIV. Privilege for the Church of Ragusa.  
*(Benevento, 29 December.)*

*[Farlati, Illyricum sacrum, VI, 80.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother TRIBUNE, Archbishop of Ragusa, and to his successors canonically appointed, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0462B]

Being placed upon the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love our brother bishops with fraternal charity and, with the Lord’s help, to provide for their peace and tranquillity. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Tribunus, Archbishop of Ragusa, we graciously grant your just requests; and, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Innocent, Anastasius, and Adrian, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the Church of Ragusa, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document.

First, indeed, we decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods this church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings [Col. 0462C] or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other just means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired for ever. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: all parishes belonging to the jurisdiction of the Church entrusted to you, namely, the kingdom of Zachlumia, the kingdom of Servilia, and the kingdom of Tribunia; likewise the cities of Kotor, Risan, Gudu[a], Avarorum, Licionatense, Scutari, Drivast, and Polat, with their abbeys, churches, and parishes, etc.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, or to take away its possessions, or retain those taken away, etc., saving the authority of the Apostolic See. If therefore anyone, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 0462D] I, Bernard, etc.

Given at Benevento, through the hand of Gerard, notary of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of January, in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1167, and in the ninth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

CDLXV. He orders the bishops of Polat, Suacia, and Drivast to obey Tribunus, Archbishop of Ragusa. (Benevento, December 29.)

[Ibid., p. 81.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren the bishops of Polat, Suacia, and Drivast, and to the beloved sons, all clerics of the churches of Suacia, Scutari, and Polat, [Col. 0463A] greeting and apostolic blessing.

If you were willing to consider with humble mind and sincere devotion how great the power of obedience is, and to lay to heart how great a good proceeds from its observance, you ought to submit yourselves to your prelates in all humility and to take care to obey their wholesome counsels and commands with all the affection of your hearts. For obedience alone is the virtue that surpasses sacrifice in merit. Hence it is said: “To obey is better than to sacrifice, for to resist is as sin [lacuna], and not to acquiesce as the crime of idolatry” (1 Samuel 15). By disobedience the first man fell (Genesis 3); because of obedience the Son of God deserved to obtain the name which is above every name (Philippians 2).

We have set these things before you, beloved sons in the Lord, [Col. 0463B] because, as we have learned, Pope Adrian, our predecessor of good memory, commanded you through his letters to render due obedience and reverence to our venerable brother Tribunus, Archbishop of Ragusa, as father and ruler of your souls. But you, as has been reported to us, to bring this about—at which we are the more astonished and grieved, since you ought to be children of obedience—have stopped your ears; nor have you been willing to heed the command and admonition of the Roman pontiffs Anastasius and Adrian, of happy memory, who instructed you sufficiently and fatherly on this matter. Therefore, since for disobedience not only . . . . . a mere cleric ought to be punished by severe correction, [Col. 0463C] and since it pertains without doubt to the peril of your souls unless you more speedily . . . . ., we command and enjoin you by apostolic letters, in the virtue of obedience, that, as your predecessors are known to have done to his predecessors, you strive to render full obedience . . . . . to your metropolitan and humbly persist as good and devoted sons. But if perhaps you neglect this . . . . . our legate, whom we are sending to those regions, shall on this account canonically promulgate . . . . . against you . . . . . remain in force. And if even thus you do not come to your senses, you will have reason to fear the sentence . . . . . after the departure of the legate, the aforesaid archbishop, because of your disobedience and rebellion . . . . . we shall ensure is held firm.

CDLXVI. He commands the clerics of the bishoprics of Dulcigno and Antivari not to obey bishops excommunicated by Tribunus, Archbishop of Ragusa. (Benevento, December 29.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 0463D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, all clerics established throughout the bishoprics of Dulcigno and Antivari, greeting and apostolic blessing.

As has recently become known to us from the report of our venerable brother T., Archbishop of Ragusa, the bishops of Dulcigno and Antivari . . . . . have raised against him and his Church the horns of pride and the sting of arrogance; through the fault of disobedience they have sinned so grievously that, by the authority of the Roman Church [Col. 0464A] and his own, he has subjected them to excommunication.
