We remember that some time ago we commanded your discretion by other letters diligently to admonish and strictly compel the nobleman B., Count of Hainaut, who was said to have violently taken a certain fief from Amelius of Albiniac, to restore that fief promptly to him, together with the revenues already received, for peaceful and undisturbed possession; or to render him full justice concerning it under your examination. Since the aforesaid Amelius declares that he has still been unable to obtain his right, we command your brotherhood again by repeated letters diligently to admonish the said count, and not omit to compel him by ecclesiastical coercion, to restore the said fief to the aforementioned Amelius without delay and leave it to him in peace; or, within forty days after receipt of this letter, not delay to render him sufficient justice concerning it before you, appeal removed. We further admonish and command your prudence to be so diligent and zealous in carrying this out [Col. 0519D] that we may deservedly be bound to commend your solicitude in this respect, and Amelius, worn down by much hardship, may through you obtain his justice.

Given at Benevento, on the eighth Ides of December [6 December].

## DXXVI. To the same.—Likewise on behalf of Amelius concerning certain possessions. (Benevento, December 6.)

[Ibid., col. 767.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We remember that some time ago we entrusted to your experience the controversy known long to have been disputed between Amelius and John of Machelcurt concerning certain possessions. Since afterward, as we have heard, they reached an amicable agreement with one another, as our venerable brother A., Bishop of Arras, informed us by his letters, but the aforesaid John utterly refuses to abide by the agreement made, we again command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently and zealously to admonish that John to carry out promptly the agreement made between him and the said Amelius, as he promised upon the pledge given, and not delay to fulfill what was settled between them.

[Note: [Col. 0519] Andrew, who succeeded Godescalc, who resigned in 1164, and died in 1171.]

But if he neglects to comply with your admonition, restore him, every contradiction and appeal removed, to the former sentence, and cause it to be firmly observed throughout your province by all persons until suitable satisfaction has been made. [Col. 0520B]

Given at Benevento, on the eighth Ides of December [6 December].

## DXXVII. To the same and the Bishop of Laon.—That they compel Rainald of Roset to restore to Giles of Cimai his wife’s dower. (Benevento, December 8.)

[Ibid., col. 767.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, and the Bishop of Laon, greeting and apostolic blessing.

On his return from Jerusalem, Giles of Cimai laid before us a complaint that the nobleman Rainald of Roset, your parishioner, presumes violently to take from him his wife’s dower and to burden him with other unjust troubles and oppressions. Since it does not become the said Rainald to inflict upon anyone what he would not wish to have inflicted upon himself by others, and since we neither can nor ought to permit anyone to be defrauded of his right—since, by the duty of the supreme apostolate imposed upon us, we are bound to preserve each person’s right—we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to take care to admonish and urgently induce the said Rainald to restore to the aforesaid Giles, without molestation or diminution, his wife’s dower and the other things taken away; to repair the losses inflicted; and henceforth to cease harassing him. Or, within two months after receipt of this letter, he must not delay to render before you full justice in all these matters, every pretext and appeal removed. If, however, the aforesaid Rainald should perhaps refuse to comply with your admonitions and exhortations, compel him by ecclesiastical sentence, appeal set aside, to carry out one or the other of the alternatives stated above. [Col. 0520D]

Given at Benevento, on the sixth Ides of December [8 December].

## DXXVIII. To the same.—On behalf of Roland and Ebruin. (Benevento, December 10.)

[Ibid., col. 768.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0521A] brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The bearer of the present letter, Roland by name, complained to us that, when Ebruin appealed to our hearing because Roland refused to restore to him a house and vineyard which he asserted belonged to him by right of his wife, and a necklace which he had lent to that man’s wife on the day of their wedding, the said Ebruin came into our presence and, concealing the truth of the matter, represented to us that Roland owed him sixteen pounds; and he obtained from us letters to the bishop of Châlons committing that case to him. When the case was being heard in the presence of that bishop and the adverse party, as Roland states, wished to produce hired and false witnesses, [Col. 0521B] Roland appealed to our hearing. The bishop, however, disregarding the appeal, bound him with the bond of excommunication.

Since the truth of the matter is not established, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if the case was committed to the bishop without reservation of an appeal, you shall cause the sentence of excommunication pronounced against Roland to be maintained and observed. But if he gives adequate security in your hand that, concerning the matter for which he was excommunicated, he will submit to justice in your presence and obey your sentence without appeal, absolve him from excommunication; and afterwards, having summoned him and his adversary before you, hear the case both concerning that debt and concerning the other matters in dispute between them, and decide it through justice, with the impediment of appeal removed. But if it is established that the remedy of appeal was reserved in the case which we committed to the said bishop, and it is likewise established to you that the bishop excommunicated the aforesaid Roland after his appeal, declare that sentence void and cause him to be regarded as not excommunicated. Then hear carefully the complaint both of this man and of the other, and decide it without remedy of appeal, preserving the equity of the law.

Given at Benevento, on the fourth day before the Ides of December.

### DXXIX. To John, Bishop of Maguelone.—Grants various privileges.  
(Benevento, 11 December.)

[GARIEL, *Series episc. Magalon.*, I, 217.]

[Col. 0521D]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the bishop of Maguelone, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Wishing to preserve your right and dignity unimpaired, we establish by apostolic authority that, if anyone has a civil action against the provost, the chapter, or any canon of your church, it shall be referred to your judgment and heard and determined before you as their bishop and ordinary judge. But if a criminal question [Col. 0522A] arises, it shall be examined before you and the chapter and receive its due outcome. You shall also be permitted to correct and amend in chapter the misconduct of your canons according to the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We further decree that the provost of your church shall be compelled once or twice a year to render an account in chapter, in the presence of you and the brethren, of the administration entrusted to him; and that he shall have no power to alienate any immovable property to the detriment of the church without your consent and that of the sounder part of the chapter. If he has alienated, or hereafter alienates, anything from those possessions, you and your chapter shall have full liberty lawfully to recover it.

Given at Benevento, on the Ides of December, in the eighth year of our pontificate.  
[Note: [Col. 0521D] Another hand added the words “in the eighth year of our pontificate.”]

### DXXX. To the same.—Adds another privilege.  
(Benevento, 14 December.)

[Ibid., I, 216.]

[Col. 0522B]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother John, bishop of Maguelone, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We ought to be the more solicitous in preserving the rights of our brethren and fellow bishops, inasmuch as by reason of office and dignity they are known to be nearest to us. Therefore, since we are inclined toward the peace of all, and especially toward yours, we establish by apostolic authority that the church, together with the hospital, recently built by your authority in the forest of Gaultier, shall remain so wholly and absolutely under your disposition [Col. 0522C] that no one may withdraw that church and hospital from your jurisdiction, diminish your right, or transfer it to another’s governance, while the authority of the Apostolic See is, of course, preserved.

Given at Benevento, on the nineteenth day before the Kalends of January, in the eighth year of our pontificate.  
[Note: [Col. 0522D] See the note above.]

### DXXXI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—That the monastery of Saint-Denis be commended to him.  
(Benevento, 16 December.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 769.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, [Col. 0522D] greeting and apostolic blessing.

The obligation of the pontifical office and the order of reason require us to take diligent care for the condition of those churches which are known to belong especially to the right and property of the most holy Roman Church and to our own governance. Therefore, since the monastery of Saint-Denis pertains especially to the provision and protection of the Apostolic See and ourselves, we earnestly request and exhort your brotherhood, for the sake of that monastery, to strive, in contemplation of things above and out of reverence for blessed Peter and for us, to love, support, and foster alike the abbot and brethren there devoted to divine service. And when [Col. 0523A] they have recourse to you for the needs of that monastery, gladly and kindly afford them the assistance of your defense and patronage, so that you may thereby appear more pleasing to us and may deserve henceforth to enjoy more abundantly and at all times the favor of the Apostolic See.

Given at Benevento, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of January.

### DXXXII. To the same.—For John, priest, concerning the church of Poegni.  
(Benevento, 19 December.)

[Ibid.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When Uldred, priest, formerly informed us and grievously complained that he had been unjustly and unlawfully deprived of the church of Saint Mary, which he asserted that he had held by right, we committed the case to your experience for decision. When he and John, priest and bearer of the present letter, appeared before you and made many assertions against one another, and the same Uldred produced two witnesses concerning the case, the aforesaid John appealed to our hearing against those witnesses as insufficiently qualified. Although each side pursued the appeal, the said Uldred, getting ahead of John, obtained from us, if we remember correctly, letters addressed to you in which it was stated that, if he could convict the aforesaid John of perjury, as he alleged to us, [Col. 0523C] you were to impose fitting penance upon John, admit the said witnesses notwithstanding the appeal, and bring the matter to its proper conclusion.

But when John, pursuing his appeal against the said Uldred, encountered him on his departure not very far from us, neither Uldred nor the persons with whom he was travelling, as John asserted, could ever induce him to return to our presence. The said John therefore came and presented to us letters of our beloved sons B., dean, and the chapter of Châlons. Those letters expressly stated that John the priest, upon their presentation, as is customary, received the aforesaid church of Saint Mary from B., of good memory, formerly bishop of Châlons, without anyone objecting, [Note: [Col. 0523D] Boso, bishop, who ceased to live in the year 1161.] and administered it quietly and peacefully for more than thirteen years. They further asserted that they had neither received nor presented the said Uldred to that bishop, but that he had obtained our letters to you by false representation. Moreover, our beloved son G., archdeacon of Châlons, likewise bore witness in his letters for the said John, he being the person to whom, after the bishop, the grant of the same church is said to belong.

Since it would be wholly unworthy and altogether contrary to reason that their testimony should, in canonical regard, generate any prejudice against the assertion of the other party, we command your brotherhood in repeated [Col. 0524A] letters that, if the aforesaid chapter is willing lawfully to affirm what it suggested to us in its letters, you shall, with every delay and appeal removed, impose silence upon the said Uldred concerning this case and wholly free the aforesaid John from his attack. The letters which Uldred himself obtained from us concerning this matter are not to occasion John any prejudice or loss. And because the above-mentioned Uldred is John’s adversary, do not permit him to prosecute John the priest in criminal matters, unless, by raising an exception against him, he should allege a crime against him.

Given at Benevento, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of January.

### DXXXIII. To Gerard, Archbishop of Split.—That he order property taken from a certain man to be restored.  
(Benevento, 23 December.)

[FAREATI, *Illyricum sacrum*, III, 190.]

[Col. 0524B]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother G[erard], archbishop of Split, legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the report transmitted by our beloved son, the nobleman Bonumir of Siponto, it has come to our ears that the men of Sevenico did not hesitate violently and secretly to take away the property of his son Goffrid. Since we ought to assist the said B. in the preservation of his rights, both from the obligation of our office and in consideration of the devotion which [Col. 0524C] he bears especially toward us, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to admonish earnestly and compel strictly the men of that city who committed this crime, so that they may restore without delay to the son of the aforesaid B. the things which they took from him secretly or by force. If they perhaps refuse to do this within a suitable term fixed for them by you, do not delay to bind them with the bond of excommunication until they make fitting satisfaction.

Given at Benevento, on the tenth day before the Kalends of January.

### DXXXIV. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—That he cause an alms taken from the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem by the duke of Louvain to be restored.  
(Benevento, 23 December.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 771.]

[Col. 0524D]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have heard the complaint communicated to us by the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem: the noble duke of Louvain has presumed to take from them a certain alms in the village called Benten and has hitherto refused to restore it. Since we ought to restrain noble and powerful men more severely with the sword of ecclesiastical rigor from oppressing others, and especially Christ’s poor, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters [Col. 0525A] earnestly to exhort and urgently admonish the said duke, in person or through your letters or messengers, to restore the aforesaid alms to the said brethren, laying aside every pretext and excuse, and to leave them in peace; or, in person or through a sufficient representative, to render them full justice concerning it before you without appeal and without delay.

If he neglects to comply with your admonition, subject the land which he is known to possess in your province to an interdict; and, if he does not amend even then, bind his person with the bond of excommunication and command that he be avoided throughout your province by all as an excommunicate.

Given at Benevento, on the tenth day before the Kalends of January.

### DXXXV. To all ecclesiastics established in the land of Duke Welf.  
(Benevento, 26 December.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, VI, 488.]

[Col. 0525B]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, all ecclesiastics established in the land of our beloved son, the noble Duke Welf, which lies in the diocese of Augsburg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have learned both from common report and fully from the transmitted account of the aforesaid duke that, because of your love for the Catholic faith, you have endured and continually endure many straits, tribulations, and troubles from the aforesaid bishop of Augsburg. Therefore, weighing with careful [Col. 0525C] consideration the ardor of your devotion and faith, and wishing to respond worthily to you as beloved sons in accordance with your deserts, at the request and intercession of the said duke we grant you, by the customary clemency of the Apostolic See, that, so long as you remain in Catholic unity and the aforesaid bishop of Augsburg holds the church of Augsburg, you may receive ordinations, consecrations of churches, and the other ecclesiastical sacraments from whatever Catholic bishop you choose, notwithstanding any contradiction or appeal.

It will therefore be for you, in return for the favor granted to you, henceforth to be more devoted to the most holy Roman Church and to show yourselves more steadfast and ardent in devotion and service toward it.

[Col. 0525D] Given at Benevento, on the seventh day before the Kalends of January.

## YEAR 1168–1169

### DXXXVI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For Amelius of Albiniac.  
(Benevento, 28 February.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 786.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the report of Amelius of Albiniac it has come to our ears that, when a controversy concerning certain possessions was being litigated in your presence by our command between him and John of Malecicurt, you carefully heard and examined the arguments on both sides and pronounced judgment for the said Amelius against John, adjudging that the aforesaid possessions should be restored to Amelius. Since the said John neglected to obey the judgment, you bound him with the bond of excommunication. Therefore, because the authority of law decrees that a matter adjudged must stand, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if this is so and the sentence was not suspended by appeal, you shall for no reason absolve the said John, or permit him to be absolved by another, until he has made suitable satisfaction to the said Amelius; but if he does not amend even then, subject his land to interdict.

[Col. 0526B] Given at Benevento, on the second day before the Kalends of March.

### DXXXVII. To the same.—For Peter, formerly a Jew.  
(Benevento, 7 March.)

[Ibid.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Peter, formerly a Jew but now a Christian, came to us and represented in a humble petition that the abbess of Saint Peter of Reims, who received him from the sacred font, with the consent of the whole chapter assigned him one portion of the provisions of her refectory; and that, although he had long received it peacefully, you took it away from him. Since those who abandon Judaism [Col. 0526C] and are converted to our law are to be treated humanely and kindly, because they readily fall into despair, we exhort and command your brotherhood to cause the aforesaid provision to be restored to Peter and to let him retain it in peace. Or, if—as we believe—you withdrew the benefice from him for a just cause, provide for him in another equivalent benefice, so that through an unexpected withdrawal of human assistance he may not be compelled to abandon our law and return to his own, like a dog to its vomit.

Given at Benevento, on the Nones of March.

### DXXXVIII. To Gerald, Bishop of Toulouse, etc.—Releases Toulouse from interdict, at the request of King Louis VII.  
(Benevento, 12 March.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 860.]

[Col. 0526D]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Gerald, bishop, and to his beloved sons the consuls and the whole clergy and people of Toulouse, greeting and apostolic blessing.

As we earnestly consider the integrity of faith and devotion which you steadfastly maintain toward the most holy Roman Church and toward our person, and likewise carefully consider the favor and fullness of affection which our dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks, shows especially toward you and your city, [Col. 0527A] we wish, as for devoted sons of the Church, in regard for the said king and in consideration of your sincerity, to honor you with a singular privilege of love and favor and to bind you to us in a closer affection.

Accordingly, moved by this consideration, we graciously relax, at the request of the said king, the sentence of interdict which we caused to be imposed upon your whole city for the wrongdoing of the count of Toulouse. We likewise grant that, in the absence of that count, divine offices may be freely celebrated in the churches of your city and its suburbs. In return, we exhort and command you, on account of this and the other marks of our favor, to take care to be more devoted to us and henceforth to remain more ardent and steadfast in the service of blessed Peter and ourselves.

[Col. 0527B] Given at Benevento, on the fourth day before the Ides of March.

### DXXXIX. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For Hugh, a servant.  
(Benevento, 12 March.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 788.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us that, when a certain dispute was to be heard before our venerable brother, the bishop of Laon, between a knight and Hugh, a servant, and Hugh refused either to satisfy the knight or to submit to justice before the bishop, he incurred a sentence of excommunication. Afterwards, when he had taken up the cross of the Lord and was intending to set out for Jerusalem, he came, as we have heard, into our presence and, having sworn that he would abide by our command concerning the matters for which he was excommunicated, obtained absolution. Having then, as he says, obtained our letters concerning this, he sent them to those parts through a messenger of his, but that messenger is said to have lost them while travelling, during the time when Hugh was delayed on the journey to Jerusalem.

Since the truth of these matters is wholly unknown to us, because we are human and cannot remember everything, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters carefully to investigate the course of events. If the said [Col. 0527D] Hugh can lawfully prove through persons who were with him before us that he was absolved by us, regard him as absolved and cause him to be regarded as absolved by others, provided that he is willing to submit before you to the equity of the law concerning the aforesaid case. Then hear the case and decide it through justice, without appeal. But if he cannot give you full assurance concerning his absolution, receive from him an oath that he will submit to justice under your examination concerning the matters for which he was excommunicated, absolve him from the sentence by which he is bound without a ban (*bannus*), and then endeavor to bring the case which arose between him and the knight to a conclusion without remedy of appeal.

Given at Benevento, on the fourth day before the Ides of March.

### DXL. To the same.—For Drogo, canon of Ham.  
(Benevento, 14 March.)

[Ibid., col. 791.]

[Col. 0528A]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received with kindly affection the letters of your devotion and sincerity, which you sent us on behalf of our beloved son Drogo, canon of Ham, and have caused them to be read carefully. But concerning the matter about which you asked us, we reply nothing else to your prudence except that we remember having already previously answered our brother B., of good memory, formerly bishop of Noyon, concerning it, if his messengers wished to carry our letters to him.

Although we have very often seen regular clerics raised to ecclesiastical prelacies, we have never read or ever heard that anyone who was a regular canon had been made secular. Therefore, if we have not acceded to your requests in this matter, you ought not to take it heavily or grievously, nor be disturbed by it, since it is written that “no one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God” (Luke IX); and Lot’s wife, who looked back, is read to have been turned into salt, to season it, [Col. 0528C] (Genesis XIX). You should rather exhort the aforesaid Drogo more carefully and induce him altogether to return quickly to his cloister, and there humbly strive to serve the Lord according to his profession. For it is no less grievous to us than to you that we cannot, with a clear conscience, grant your requests in this matter as we should wish.

Given at Benevento, on the second day before the Ides of March.

### DXLI. To the same.—For G., priest.  
(Benevento, 14 March.)

[Ibid.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0528D] G., a priest and bearer of the present letter, complained to us that W. of Carten owes him seventy-five solidi, which he refuses to pay. Therefore, since a dispute was being litigated between them concerning this and concerning certain damages which the said G. alleges were inflicted upon him by the aforesaid W., G. appealed to our hearing. We therefore command your brotherhood by apostolic letters carefully to admonish and strictly compel the said W. either to pay the aforesaid G. without any delay the specified sum in full, and make complete satisfaction for the damages inflicted, or without delay to render him full justice concerning the matter under your examination, without appeal.

Given at Benevento, on the second day before the Ides of March.

### DXLII. To the same.—For John, canon of Laon.  
(Benevento, 15 March.)

[Ibid., col. 792.]

[Col. 0529A]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Nothing is more fitting to episcopal honor than to love right and equity and to aid those burdened by injury in the maintenance of their rights. Moved by this consideration, and fully trusting in your prudence, we ask and exhort your discretion by apostolic letters that you shall by no means permit John, cleric and canon of the church of Laon, to be disinherited contrary to justice by his adversaries, or [Col. 0529B] his property to be occupied by them through violence; rather, by our intervention and for the love of justice, support him in his right and preserve that right for him by your protection.

Given at Benevento, on the Ides of March.

### DXLIII. To the same.—For Ha., priest.  
(Benevento, 17 March.)

[Ibid.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Ha., a priest and bearer of the present letter, came to us and declared in his confession that, since he had long ago sinned through a lapse of the flesh, your predecessor S. deprived him of his office and benefice. But, moved by mercy, you restored to him his priestly office, as he states, while hitherto refusing to grant him any indulgence concerning the benefice, although he has no other benefice from which he can obtain the means of life.

Since mercy should be shown to him rather in regard to a benefice than an office, especially since many persons may lawfully receive a benefice without, nevertheless, having the administration of the priestly office, we ask and exhort your brotherhood by apostolic letters to endeavor, for the love of God, reverence for blessed Peter and ourselves, and the obligation of your office, [Col. 0529D] to provide the said Ha. with some benefice other than the church which he formerly held, from which he may suitably obtain the necessities of life and faithfully serve the Lord in his order. We in turn shall hold your solicitude in this matter very highly commended and shall regard this as welcome and acceptable.

Given at Benevento, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April.

### DXLIV. He commands the bishop of Thérouanne and the abbot of Saint-Quentin of Mont to hear the case between the abbots of Humolaria and Ribemont, the abbess of Monasteriolum, and the knight of Brenoth.  
(Benevento, 17 March.)

[Ibid., 793.]

[Col. 0530A]

Alexander, to the bishop of Thérouanne [Note: [Col. 0529D] Thérouanne, or Tervana, was a distinguished episcopal city on the river Lys, under the metropolitan see of Reims; after the city was destroyed by Charles V, its see was transferred to Boulogne.] and the abbot of Saint-Quentin [Note: [Col. 0529D] Saint-Quentin of Mont, near Péronne, was a monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict under the Congregation of Saint Maur.] of Mont.

Since a case concerning a certain wood had long been litigated between our beloved sons R., abbot of Saint Nicholas [Note: [Col. 0529D] Saint Nicholas of Ribemont, or Ribodimont, [Col. 0530D] was a monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Laon.] of Ribemont, P., abbot of Humolaria, [Note: [Col. 0530D] Humolaria was first a convent of virgins and afterwards a monastery of monks of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Noyon, not far from Saint-Quentin.] the abbess of Monasteriolum, [Note: [Col. 0530D] Monasteriolum was a convent of Cistercian virgins at the foot of Mount Laon.] and G., knight of Brenoth, it was finally brought to our hearing by appeal.

At length, when both the prior of Saint Nicholas and the representatives [Col. 0530B] of the adverse party appeared before us, each asserted that the aforesaid wood belonged to his own right. The same prior steadfastly maintained that the case had been decided by a settlement, through the intervention of our beloved son Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. The other party alleged that the settlement had not been made with the consent of the aforesaid churches and knight. It further added that the settlement had been repudiated and that afterwards the aforesaid abbot of Saint Nicholas held the said wood at rent, although the prior who appeared for him wholly denied this.

Because they were unable fully to inform us either about the matters alleged on both sides or about the merits of the case, we defer our decision of the dispute and commit it to your experience for hearing and proper conclusion without appeal. We therefore command your discretion by apostolic letters, once you have met together and summoned the parties before you, to endeavor to settle the matter peacefully and amicably between them. If this cannot be done, carefully hear and examine the arguments on both sides and decide the case by justice, without appeal.

But if the abbot of Saint Nicholas should rely upon the settlement said to have been made through the said cardinal, or upon an arbitral award pronounced by that cardinal after the parties referred the matter to him, we do not wish it to generate any prejudice against the right of the other party unless it is reasonably established [Col. 0530D] that it was pronounced upon the common submission of the parties. If, however, the settlement was made with the approval and consent of those three chapters and of the same knight, or if the arbitral award was pronounced upon the common submission of the parties, or even if the settlement was afterward ratified by the parties, we wish the settlement or arbitral award to stand. But if both of you cannot be present in this matter, one of you shall nonetheless carry out the business as set forth above.

[Col. 0531A] Given at Benevento, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April.

### DXLV. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For the abbot of Saint-Martin of Laon.  
(Benevento, 20 March.)

[Ibid., col. 795.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

A report recently sent to us on behalf of our beloved sons, the abbot and brethren of Saint-Martin [Note: [Col. 0531D] The church of Saint Martin, formerly in the suburb of Laon and now within the city walls, passed first from secular clerics to regulars, and finally, in 1124, chiefly through the action of Bishop Bartholomew, to the Premonstratensians.] has reached us [Col. 0531B] that E., priest of Mont Bunold, and Hu. of Warch unjustly demand tithes from them, and that G. of Chamelsi grievously and unjustly harasses them over certain pastures. We wish those men to appear before our venerable brethren, the bishops of Amiens and Noyon, so that these disputes may receive their due conclusion under their judgment.

We therefore command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to compel those men, with all strictness, to appear when summoned by the bishops and to submit to their judgment; and to exercise the authority of the pontifical office in restraining their malice in such a way that the said brethren may rejoice, through your diligence, in the preservation of their rights, and that your brotherhood may find commendation for having secured peace for religious brethren.

Given at Benevento, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of April.

### DXLVI. To the same.—For William, dean of Soissons.  
(Benevento, 22 March.)

[Ibid.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son William, dean of Soissons, earnestly represented to us—and certain letters of Pope Adrian, our predecessor of good memory, made the same matter more fully known to us—that, when our brother Hugh, bishop of the church of Soissons, had been called and elected to that church, our aforesaid predecessor, considering the revenues of the said deanery to be slender, granted to the said dean the prebend which the bishop-elect had held and invested him with it. He further provided that this prebend should henceforth belong to the office of dean.

He therefore commanded both the said bishop-elect and the chapter of the church of Soissons to treat that grant as ratified, neither to act against it nor presume ever to disturb it. Since the aforesaid bishop, as we have heard, did not at all comply with this but ventured to transfer the prebend contrary to it, we commanded him in our letters to assign, to the said dean, without any contradiction or appeal, the prebend which he holds in his own hands and which had belonged to Theobald of Vieux-Marché, and to permit him to hold it in peace, so that it should henceforth belong to the office of dean in accordance with the ordinance of our aforesaid predecessor. If the bishop should perhaps scorn to execute our command in this matter, do not fail carefully to execute it yourself, with every delay and appeal removed.

Given at Benevento, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of April.

### DXLVII. He informs Hugh, bishop of Soissons, of the preceding letter.

[Ibid., 796.]

[Col. 0532B]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the bishop of Soissons, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the report of our beloved son William, dean of your church, and from the tenor of certain letters of Pope Adrian, our predecessor of good memory, we have learned that, when you were elected and called to the said church, he granted to that dean the prebend which you held in it and invested him with it, adding that from that time the prebend should belong to [Col. 0532C] the office of dean.

Since, therefore, as we have heard, you have in no way permitted the aforesaid dean to possess the specified prebend in accordance with the ordinance and command of our predecessor and your benefactor, but have not hesitated to confer it upon another at your own pleasure—although it would not become you so soon to act against the ordinances of the Roman Church, from which you had immediately received so great a benefit—we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that you assign without delay to the said dean, laying aside every pretext and appeal, the prebend which you are known to hold in your own hands and which T. of Vieux-Marché held, and permit him to possess it in peace. Thus that prebend, as the aforementioned predecessor established, shall henceforth belong to the office of dean.

If you delay in fulfilling this, know that we have commanded our venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, fully to execute the matters stated above, with every delay and appeal removed.

### DXLVIII. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For Albert, priest.  
(Benevento, 22 March.)

[Ibid., 797.]

Alexander, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0533A] brother Henry, archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The bearer of the present letter, Albert the priest, returning to us not without hardship, showed us by a suppliant complaint that the priest of Basauchis and the castellan, together with her son Nicholas, rashly imprisoned his mother when she was seeking her revenues and had recourse to you on that account, and detained her for a long time; so that on that occasion she lost her revenues. Since we neither wish nor ought for any reason to permit those who visit the most holy Roman Church to suffer loss or damage to their property, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to admonish urgently and compel strictly both the priest and the castellan and her son that they make satisfaction to the said priest for the injuries inflicted and compensate the losses sustained; or, under your examination, afford him full justice in the matter, with appeal set aside. But if they refuse to obey your admonition, strike them with ecclesiastical censure. Moreover, compel those who received the said priest’s revenues either to restore them to him or to render justice before you, with every appeal set aside.

Given at Benevento, the eleventh day before the Kalends of April [22 March].

## DXLIX. He confirms to Albert the priest the church of St Remigius of Augeio and the chapel of Cersolio.  
*(Benevento, 22 March.)*

*[Ibid., col. 798.]*

[Col. 0533C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to ALBERT the priest, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant our assent to the just desires of petitioners, and that wishes which do not depart from the path of reason be fulfilled with their proper effect. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, concurring gladly with your just requests, we confirm by apostolic authority to your devotion the church of St Remigius of Augeio, with the chapel of Cersolio belonging to it and its other appurtenances, canonically granted to you; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or to oppose it in any way. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Benevento, XI Kalends of April [22 March].

## DL. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For B., a priest.  
*(Benevento, 23 March.)*

*[Ibid., col. 799.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

B., a priest, has complained to us that, having lent twenty pounds of Provins currency to the abbot and convent of Prémontré in their necessities, and having repeatedly demanded them from them, they refuse to repay him.

> [Note: [Col. 0533D] Prémontré, a famous monastery of the Premonstratensian Order in the diocese of Soissons, passed from secular canons to regular canons of that order in the year 1130. The burial-place of the lords of Prémontré may be seen there.]

Since it is unjust and contrary to honesty not to repay borrowed money, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to admonish the said abbot and brethren, within thirty days after receipt of these letters, and strictly compel them to pay the aforementioned priest the stated sum in full. But if they choose rather to enter into litigation than to repay him, summon the parties before you, hear the case diligently, and decide it through justice, with the impediment of appeal removed.

Given at Benevento, the tenth day before the Kalends of April [23 March].

## DLI. To the same.—For the church of St John of Soissons.  
*(Benevento, 23 March.)*

*[Ibid.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to our hearing that G. and his retainers presume to take away a certain wood belonging to the church of St John de Vineis, [Col. 0534C] and do not cease to harass it on this account. Since, as far as lies in us, we ought to protect and preserve intact the rights of churches, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to compel the said G. and his retainers wholly to cease molesting the aforementioned church, with appeal set aside. If they do not otherwise comply with you, bind them by the bond of excommunication until they make fitting satisfaction, unless they are willing entirely to desist from their harassment or to litigate judicially before you with the aforesaid church concerning the matters in dispute.

Given at Benevento, the tenth day before the Kalends of April [23 March].

## DLII. To the same.—For Her., that what was taken from him may be restored.  
*(Benevento, 28 March.)*

*[Ibid., col. 800.]*

[Col. 0534D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The bearer of the present letter, named Her., complains gravely of the canons of Mont, because they have unjustly taken from him one house, one vineyard, one garden, and one *oscha*—which he maintains belongs to him by hereditary right. Since it is not fitting for ecclesiastical men unlawfully to occupy another’s rights, when they ought to furnish others with an example of virtue and uprightness, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters continually to admonish and strictly compel the said canons to restore without delay or pretext to the said Her. the aforesaid house, vineyard, garden, and *oscha*, and to leave them to him freely and peacefully. But should they wish to litigate with him concerning this, summon the parties before you; after hearing and considering the arguments on both sides, diligently endeavour to determine the case by means of justice, without recourse to appeal.

Given at Benevento, the fifth day before the Kalends of April [28 March].

## DLIII. To the same.—For the dean and canons of the Church of Soissons.  
*(Benevento, 31 March.)*

*[Ibid.]*

[Col. 0535B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although we ought to give more earnest attention to all persons in their rights, we must especially attend to those known to visit the Apostolic See concerning their own affairs and those of others. We do not believe that your prudent discretion is unaware how our beloved sons, the dean and canons of Soissons, came to the Apostolic See concerning the case pending between them and their bishop, our brother, and brought with them certain chaplains of the same bishopric.

> [Note: [Col. 0535] He was Hugh de Champfleury, chancellor of Louis VII, formerly a canon of Paris and made bishop.]

Therefore, wishing to preserve their rights in full and unimpaired, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if the aforesaid bishop should wish to burden any of the suspects, witnesses, or other supporters of the dean and canons because they came into our presence, because they stood with the said dean and his brethren in their case, or for any other reason, you shall compel him wholly to desist from such presumption, with every pretext and appeal set aside. If he has decreed anything against them on this ground, do not delay, with recourse to appeal removed, to revoke it as void. Protect and defend the said dean and canons, and all who assist them in their affair, so that they may not be unduly burdened by the aforesaid bishop or suffer any prejudice to their right.

Given at Benevento, the second day before the Kalends of April [31 March].

## DLIV. To the same.—For R., precentor of Soissons.  
*(Benevento, 31 March.)*

*[Ibid., col. 801.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When our beloved son R., precentor of the church of Soissons, was before us, we learned from his account that his two predecessors possessed the altar of Bosserre throughout their lives while they were precentors. The venerable brother, the Bishop of Soissons, is said to have granted it to someone when the precentorship was vacant; the said precentor asserts that this has gravely derogated from his right and dignity. Since it is unworthy that he, whom we do not believe inferior in merit to his predecessors, should without reasonable cause be deprived of the benefices which they held by reason of the office entrusted to them, we have instructed the said bishop in our letters that, if it is established that his immediate predecessors held it peacefully for the preceding forty years and that he himself was deprived of it against his will, he is to place him in possession of it, with every pretext and appeal set aside, and permit him to possess it in peace, nor presume thereafter to molest him concerning it.

But if our command in this matter has not been carried out within twenty days after receipt of our letters, we enjoin your discretion by authority of the present letter that, if you find this to be so, you shall within another twenty days restore the aforesaid altar to the said precentor, with every pretext and appeal set aside, and ensure that he possesses it peacefully; so that the bishop may henceforth be unable to bring any complaint against him concerning it.

Given at Benevento, the second day before the Kalends of April [31 March].

## DLV. To the same.—For Ralph de Cuphies, against Josbert de Mont and Peter de Nantolio.  
*(Benevento, 31 March.)*

*[Ibid., col. 802.]*

[Col. 0536C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the complaint transmitted by Ralph de Cuphies: Josbert de Mont unjustly possesses a certain house which belonged to his father, and Peter de Nantolio holds in pledge a certain piece of his land, from which he is said to have received his principal and much more besides. Since we must so preserve each person’s rights that we by no means deny justice to others, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to exhort the said J. and compel him with all strictness either to restore the aforesaid house to the said R., setting aside every objection, or not to fail to give him full justice concerning it in your presence.

Further, if the aforesaid P., from the land which he holds in pledge, has received his principal and an equal sum after deduction of expenses, admonish him carefully, and compel him by ecclesiastical coercion with appeal set aside, to restore it to the said R. without demanding any money.

Given at Benevento, II Kalends of April [31 March].

## DLVI. To the abbess and sisters of Bruburc.—How he imposes silence upon the priest Manasses concerning their chaplaincy.  
*(Benevento, 31 March.)*

*[Ibid.]*

[Col. 0537A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved daughters in Christ, the abbess and sisters of the monastery of Bruburc, greeting and apostolic blessing.

> [Note: [Col. 0537D] Broburg or Borburg, a distinguished Benedictine monastery of noble virgins, formerly in the diocese of Thérouanne and now in that of Saint-Omer, founded about the year 1039 by Clementia, Countess of Flanders.]

When our beloved son Master Matthew, your representative, and the priest Manasses were present before us in the case long known to be pending between you and the said Manasses concerning your chaplaincy, we carefully heard the letters of the judges to whom we had committed that case and fully understood the arguments on both sides. By apostolic authority, we imposed perpetual silence concerning it upon the said Manasses, and wholly absolved you from his claim in the matter; so that henceforth you are in no way bound to answer him concerning the aforesaid chaplaincy on account of an appeal or any other cause.

Given at Benevento, II Kalends of April [31 March].

## DLVII. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—That he compel the Premonstratensians to restore to A. de Vilers his land.  
*(Benevento, 31 March.)*

*[Ibid., col. 805.]*

[Col. 0537C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the complaint transmitted to us by the nobleman A. de Vilers, we have learned that our beloved sons, the Premonstratensian abbot and brethren, entered without his consent upon a certain land which he alleges belongs to his fief, and unjustly hold it in occupation. Since, just as we are bound to preserve the rights of religious men, so we ought not fail other Christians in their justice, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to admonish the said abbot and brethren and, if necessary, strictly compel them to restore without delay the aforesaid land to the said A. and leave it to him in peace; or to afford him sufficient justice in the matter under your examination.

Given at Benevento, II Kalends of April [31 March].

## DLVIII. To the same.—For a canon of Laon.  
*(Benevento, 3 April.)*

*[Ibid.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0538A] It is judged equitable and reasonable that those who sustain expense and labour for their church should receive the reward of worthy recompense and the fruit of hoped-for consolation. Our beloved son P., canon of Laon, has represented to us in a detailed account that, at the request of certain of his fellow canons, he travelled to our presence at his own expense on business of his church. Since it is neither fitting nor consistent with reason that he should sustain labour and expense without any recompense, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to admonish and strictly compel the said canons to reimburse the said P., without appeal or objection, for the necessary expenses which he incurred in coming to us at their direction.

Given at Benevento, the third day before the Nones of April [3 April].

## DLIX. He decrees that persons henceforth made canons in the Church of Chartres who are not resident canons shall receive only forty shillings annually.  
*(Benevento, 4 April.)*

*[PETIT, Theodorus’ Penitential, II, 429.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, . . . . . dean and canons of Chartres, greeting and apostolic blessing.

As it is written, “he who proclaims the Gospel should live by the Gospel,” and “he who serves at the altar should share in what comes from the altar” [1 Corinthians 9], so it may manifestly be inferred from the same words that one who does not serve at the altar ought not to share in its benefits. Therefore, unwilling that your church—which is not customarily reckoned among the lesser churches of the kingdom of the Franks—should be deprived of its due services, we have decreed by apostolic authority that those who are henceforth to be made canons in your church and are not resident there shall receive only forty shillings in each year. Nor may they demand or receive more from you or from the aforesaid church, provided that they wish to remain continually in the services of that church, as resident canons do.

Given at Benevento, the day before the Nones of April [4 April].

## DLX. He permits the canons of Split to restore a certain canon to his former position, though he had been deprived of his own church because, owing to a headache, he had once not read in church.  
*(Benevento, 5 April.)*

*[FARLATI, Illyricum sacrum, III, 191.]*

[Col. 0538D]

## DLXI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For the clerics of the church of Brague.  
*(Benevento, 5 April.)*

*[MARTEN., Ampl. Collect., II, 806.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Let it be known to your brotherhood that the canons of Brague recently informed us that Gauses of Mauceriensis and the monks of Novicis do not fear irreverently to withhold the revenues of March, which the canons allege that their church possessed peacefully for one hundred years. Since it is our concern to preserve everyone’s rights whole and inviolate, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters urgently to admonish and strictly compel the said Gauses and monks either to leave the stated revenues freely and peacefully to the aforesaid canons, compensate the losses sustained, or, under your examination, without delay afford them full justice in the matter, with appeal set aside.

Given at Benevento, on the Nones of April [5 April].

## DLXII. To the abbot of St Remigius of Reims.—For the clerk Waland.  
*(Benevento, 7 April.)*

*[Ibid., 807.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved brother, the abbot of St Remigius of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The care of the government entrusted to us invites and exhorts us to give more earnest attention to clerics who are known to have been received into the bosom of the most holy Roman Church, and to provide them more suitably with the assistance of our protection. Since our beloved son Waland, our clerk, has adhered to us with unbroken and most steadfast devotion, and is endowed with such learning and integrity of character that we ought deservedly to love him and embrace him with sincere charity, we earnestly commend him to your charity. We ask and strongly admonish you, for reverence for blessed Peter and for us, and in consideration of Waland himself—who, if he lives, can confer very many advantages and benefits upon you and your church—to provide liberally and honourably for the said Waland in the schools at Paris, and to arrange that the benefice be conveniently assigned to him during two suitable seasons of the year. Thus we may owe more abundant thanks to your generosity and hear your petitions more willingly and effectively.

Whatever you do at our intervention, we shall regard as done particularly for us. We wish, however, that you should make this known to us by your letters.

Given at Benevento, VII Ides of April [7 April].

## DLXIII. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For the abbess of Bruburc.  
*(Benevento, 11 April.)*

*[Ibid.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

M., a priest, came to the clemency of the Apostolic See and set forth before our tribunal a complaint against the abbess of the Church of Bruburc: she had removed him, without canonical cause, from the chaplaincy of that church, to which she herself had appointed him. But since we know that in nunneries priests ought to be appointed who are mature and advanced in years, and who, by age or conduct, give no ground for suspicion concerning themselves, we did not consider him entitled to be heard in his complaint on the ground of youth.

Nevertheless, because he asserted that another, younger man had been appointed in his place, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to investigate the truth of the matter. If you find this to be true, remove that man from the office and benefice of the chaplaincy, and correct the abbess by canonical discipline because she desires to have young chaplains. Correct her frivolity in such a way that she endeavours to amend for the better, rather than for the worse, what was done with insufficient caution; and so that other abbesses who hear of it may exercise greater caution in appointing chaplains.

Given at Benevento, the third day before the Ides of April [11 April].

## DLXIV. To the same.—That he compel the dean of St Lawrence of Roseto to reside.  
*(Benevento, 12 April.)*

*[Ibid., col. 808.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us that, although the dean of St Lawrence of Roseto ought to maintain continual residence there and continually attend to the services of that church, he presumes to live elsewhere and wholly neglects the service of the church entrusted to him. Since it is not fitting that he who holds the greater dignity in it should thus absent himself from its service, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to admonish and strictly compel the said dean either to reside continually in the aforesaid church according to its custom or wholly to relinquish the said deanery.

Given at Benevento, III Ides of April [11 April].

## DLXV. To Peter, abbot, and the monks of Vallis-Laurea.  
*(Benevento, 12 April.)*

*[MANSI, Councils, XXI, 1063.]*

[Col. 0540D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons PETER, abbot, and the brethren of Vallis-Laurea, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From letters of our beloved son, the Abbot of Cîteaux, and from the report of your envoy, we have learned that, when the confined and unsuitable nature of your site compelled you to move to another place, our venerable brother, the Bishop of Barcelona, at the end of his episcopate granted you, out of love of God, a certain estate, where you were to pitch your tents. When you began to do this, our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Tarragona, opposed his authority, maintaining that the same place belonged to his diocese. Since his opposition prevents you from carrying out your purpose and compels you to suffer many hardships in your present location, we instruct both of them in our letters to put an end to this controversy by agreement or judgment by the feast of the Assumption, so that you may no longer, through this obstacle, be deprived of the benefit of the grant made to you.

If, therefore, the matter has not been settled by that date, then by our authority you shall have leave to inhabit the place without prejudice to either party.

Given at Benevento, II Ides of April [12 April].

## DLXVI. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For Walter, a clerk.  
*(Benevento, 12 April.)*

*[MARTEN., Ampl. Collect., II, 808.]*

[Col. 0541B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the tenor of certain letters of yours, we have learned that, when a dispute concerning certain possessions and an alms was being heard before you, by our commission, between the Abbot of St Peter of Châlons and Walter, a clerk and bearer of the present letter, you imposed no due conclusion upon it, but instead referred it to our examination. Since we do not know on what ground you did this, we command your brotherhood again by these letters that, when requested concerning the matter, you summon both parties before you and, after diligently hearing and considering the arguments on either side, decide the case by means of justice, with recourse to appeal removed.

But if you should refuse to impose its due conclusion upon the case within thirty days after receipt of these letters, notify the venerable brother, the Bishop of Amiens, as soon as possible, so that he may determine the case according to our command to him.

Given at Benevento, II Ides of April [12 April].

## DLXVII. To the same.—For G., a clerk, and for Hu., a burgess, and M., his wife.  
*(Benevento, 23 April.)*

*[Ibid., col. 809.]*

[Col. 0541D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

G., a clerk and bearer of the present letter, lodged before us a complaint that Hu., a burgess, and M., his wife, presume to take from the said G. a certain house which belongs to him by hereditary right. Since we ought to assist all persons in their right, and especially the poor, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to admonish and strictly compel the said Hu. and his wife either to restore the aforementioned house without delay to the said G. or, within forty days after receipt of these letters, not delay to afford him full justice in the matter under your examination.

Given at Benevento, the ninth day before the Kalends of May [23 April].

## DLXVIII. To the same.—Concerning the case of G., canon of Seclin, and Walter.  
*(Benevento, 29 April.)*

*[Ibid.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We commit to your discretion for hearing and due determination the case known to be pending between G., a canon of the church of Seclin, and Master Walter, concerning a certain prebend.

> [Note: [Col. 0541D] Seclin, a town in Belgium in Mélantois, where the body of St Piat rests.]

Accordingly, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, when requested concerning the matter, you summon both parties before you and, after diligently hearing and considering the arguments on both sides, decide that case by means of justice. We further command your affection to hear and determine by a due conclusion the case pending between our beloved son Gunter and the canons of Seclin concerning sixty shillings.

Given at Benevento, the third day before the Kalends of May [29 April].

## DLXIX. He commands the Bishops of Amiens and Meaux to investigate and determine the case concerning the chancellorship of Noyon, pending between Henry, son of Count Robert, and Bald.  
*(Benevento, 30 April.)*

*[Ibid., col. 810.]*

[Col. 0542C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers, the Bishops of Amiens and Meaux, greeting and apostolic blessing.

A report has been transmitted to us on behalf of Henry, son of our beloved son the nobleman Count Robert, brother of our dearest son in Christ, Louis, the illustrious King of the Franks. It states that the chancellorship of the church of Noyon had been granted to the said Henry by our venerable brother, the Bishop of Noyon, but that the same bishop is afterward said to have granted it to Bald., a canon of that church.

> [Note: [Col. 0542D] From whom the illustrious family of Dreux derived its origin.]

Since B. maintained that the same chancellorship had been canonically granted to him, while the count’s son sought confirmation of it from us, we considered that we should assent to neither of them. Therefore, placing fuller confidence in your prudence and integrity, we commit the case to your experience for hearing and due determination. Accordingly, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, when requested concerning it, you meet together, summon before you both Henry’s representative and Bald., and, after diligently hearing and considering the arguments on both sides, decide the case by a due conclusion.

Given at Benevento, II Kalends of May [30 April].

## DLXX. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—For Garin de Blanciis, whose wife was murdered.  
*(Benevento, 11 May.)*

*[Ibid.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that the horrible and enormous crime committed in your city by certain persons touched by an evil spirit has already come to your brotherhood’s notice. For while Garin Blanc had come to Apulia for trade, certain persons entered his house at night, killed his wife and son, secretly carried off the property of himself and his wife, and with diabolical boldness burned the house by fire. Since so monstrous and cruel a crime must be punished more strictly, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, if you can discover those who committed the aforesaid crime, you shall admonish them by your authority and strictly compel them to restore all that was taken to the said Garin, make reparation for the damage caused, and make so full satisfaction to God for so great an offence that they may deserve to obtain pardon for this crime and that others, hearing of it, may fear to commit similar deeds.

Further, command generally under excommunication that whoever has taken any of his property from that house, or has held any of the wife’s property under a title of deposit or debt, restore it to him without any objection. Bind under the strictness of anathema those who know the evildoers, compelling them to reveal them to you and to the Church—unless the person be a priest to whom that sin has been disclosed in confession.

Given at Benevento, V Ides of May [11 May].

## DLXXI. To the chapter of Holy Trinity, Canterbury.—That they receive as prior whomever Archbishop Thomas appoints over them.  
*(Benevento, 16 May.)*

*[Letters of St Thomas, ed. GILES, II, 37.]*

[Col. 0543D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the whole chapter of Holy Trinity, Canterbury, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since your church is known chiefly to belong to the ordering and disposition of our venerable brother Thomas, your archbishop, such that you have not customarily had any prior except one assigned to you by the archbishop, we command and enjoin upon your community by apostolic letters, under the authority of obedience, that you receive, setting aside every pretext and appeal, the man whom the said archbishop wishes to appoint as prior for you according to the ancient custom of your church. You are not to presume either to elect another there or to receive anyone at another person’s suggestion or appointment.

Given at Benevento, XVII Kalends of June [16 May].

## DLXXII. To Henry, Archbishop of Reims.—That he compel the canons of Arras to return the head of St James.  
*(Benevento, 26 May.)*

*[MARTEN., Ampl. Collect., II, 811.]*

ALEXANDER, to HENRY, Archbishop of Reims, etc.

It has come to our hearing that the nobleman Philip, Count of Flanders, violently carried off the head of Blessed James from the church of St Vaast and is said to have placed it in the church of Arras. Since we do not wish the aforesaid church of St Vaast, which acknowledges no bishop except the Roman pontiff, to be deprived of its relics, any more than of its other goods, without reasonable cause, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters urgently to admonish and strictly compel the provost and canons of the aforesaid church of Arras to restore, with every pretext and appeal set aside, the aforesaid head together with the other relics to the above-mentioned church of St Vaast.

But if, in accordance with your admonition, they should refuse to return the said head with the relics, subject the aforesaid church of Arras to interdict, with delay and appeal removed; and prohibit the celebration of divine offices in any other church to which the said relics may be conveyed, for as long as they remain there.

Given at Benevento, the seventh day before the Kalends of June [26 May].

## DLXXIII. He commands O., Abbot of Ourscamp, and F., Dean of Reims, not to separate Alermus of Beauvais from his wife unless his brother B. is separated from his own wife.

*[Ibid., col. 812.]*

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons O., Abbot of Ourscamp, and F., Dean of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

> [Note: [Col. 0543D] Odo. Ourscamp is a distinguished monastery of the Cistercian Order in the diocese of Noyon, of the Clairvaux filiation, founded in 1129.]

Know that it has been brought to our hearing that a certain man named B. is said to have contracted a lawful marriage in the city of Beauvais, and to have lived with his wife in complete tranquillity for about ten years. But when Alermus, the brother of the aforesaid B., had joined in marriage to himself the cousin of his brother’s wife, certain young men, as is represented to us, to whom the inheritance of that bride appears to belong in the nearest degree, while their fathers and elders remain silent, are attempting to impede the marriage of the younger brother Alermus, yet by every means keeping silent concerning the marriage of the eldest brother, which is in every respect very similar to the younger brother’s marriage. Since, however, a fairly evident suspicion seems to arise that the young men, while their elders remain silent, are attacking and trying to dissolve only the marriage of the younger brother—especially since, if they were moved by zeal for charity, they ought first to have pressed for dissolution of the eldest brother’s marriage, if, as is said, it rests upon a like basis—we command your discretion by apostolic letters to investigate the truth of the matter more carefully. Unless other such persons appear who wish, and can lawfully, challenge that marriage, you are in no way to admit the aforesaid young men to accuse the marriage, since, while their elders are silent, they seem to raise the dispute not out of love for justice but rather through the heat of avarice and the rancour of hatred. Instead, cause the marriage itself to remain in its present state, unless perhaps common report in the locality holds that there is some kinship between them. Moreover, if other serious and mature persons appear whose testimony is to be credited, hear the case and, with the impediment of appeal removed, bring it to a canonical conclusion, earnestly warning and exhorting those persons that, as reason appears to require, they should first challenge and accuse the marriage of the eldest brother, and then that of the younger. But if common report in the locality does not maintain that any kinship exists between them, and no other persons of the kind described appear who wish or are able lawfully to challenge the same marriage, by our authority cause Alermus and his wife to remain together without any dispute.

Furthermore, if the brothers’ wives are so related by blood, and the brothers themselves are so related to one another, that there is absolutely nothing in one marriage which is not also in the other, hear no one unless they wish to challenge both marriages; for they appear to do this not from love of justice but from hatred, not from good zeal, since it is more tolerable to be joined contrary to human enactments than to separate what God has joined.

Given at Benevento, the third day before the Kalends of June [30 May].

DLXXIV. To Chajalisio, count of Pharos. He commands Chajalisio, count, and the other nobles of the island of Pharos, under penalty of excommunication, to treat Bishop Martin with due honour. (Benevento, 1 June.)

[FARLATI, *Illyricum sacrum*, IV, 242.]

[Col. 0545D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, CHAJALISIO, most valiant count, and all the nobles of the island of Pharos, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Know that it has been reported to us that, at the prompting of the devil, you entertain an improper indignation against our brother Martin, your bishop and shepherd. For you say that he whom you honoured in his youth is now, when weighed down by old age, unsuitable and unworthy in your eyes; and you wish, at your own discretion, to choose a better man, although the Lord long ago appointed him shepherd of your Church. But since this is not lawful, we command you by apostolic letters that both you and the rulers of the other islands hold him in reverence until his death, more than ever before.

Moreover, if anyone, on account of this madness, is found to have defrauded him of tithes or first-fruits, and, moved by penitence, has not made amends and has not rendered him the reverence due to him, then, as far as lies in our power, by apostolic authority we bind that person with the bond of excommunication.

Given at Benevento, on the Kalends of June [1 June].

DLXXV. To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—That satisfaction be made to L., a crusader, for one of his men who was killed. (Benevento, 2 June.)

[MARTEN., *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 813.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the report of the nobleman Lod. de Buren it has been made known to us that Angult. de Aiteio, after that same L. had taken up the Lord’s cross in preparation for departure to Jerusalem, killed one of his men, as he asserts, inflamed by diabolical fury. Since so grave and detestable an offence ought not to be left uninvestigated, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters strictly to compel the aforesaid Aug. either to make worthy satisfaction to the same L. for so great an offence, or to render full justice. If the aforesaid A. is known to have taken anything from the goods of the said L., compel him with all strictness by our authority to restore it to him or to render sufficient justice.

Given at Benevento, on the fourth day before the Nones of June [2 June].

DLXXVI. To the same.—On behalf of Aprilis de Manso. (Benevento, 3 June.)

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the report of the nobleman Aprilis de Manso it has become known to us that Henry de Magnoprato, after the same A. had taken up the Lord’s cross in preparation for departure to Jerusalem, is said unjustly to have seized his peasants and many things belonging to him, and presumptuously to be holding them by force. Although, by reason of the office of supreme pontiff entrusted to us by God, we are bound to preserve the rights of all persons whole and inviolate, yet we ought to protect more earnestly the rights of those who, leaving their possessions behind, desire through much toil to go and worship where the Lord’s feet stood.

We therefore command your brotherhood by apostolic letters carefully to admonish the aforesaid Henry and earnestly endeavour to exhort him to restore and leave in peace, without any pretext or excuse, those things which he took from the said A. after he had been marked with the sign of the cross. If, within forty days after receipt of these letters and of your admonition, he refuses to carry this out, do not fail to place all his land under interdict. If even then he does not come to his senses, do not delay binding his person with a sentence of excommunication.

Given at Benevento, on the third day before the Nones of June [3 June].

DLXXVII. To the same.—On behalf of Geoffrey, clerk of Amiens. (Benevento, 3 June.)

[Ibid., col. 814.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Geoffrey, a poor clerk, appearing in our presence, showed us in a humble petition that, when his father had pledged as security, by hereditary right, one half of a certain house which he possessed within the cloister of the church of Amiens, and lacked the means to redeem it, he proposed to Geoffrey that, if he redeemed the half, he would give it to him. Geoffrey, complying with his father’s wish, sold a piece of land and redeemed with his own money the half of the aforesaid house.

Afterwards, however, that same father, compelled by necessity, borrowed money from Geoffrey, a canon; in repayment he pledged to the latter the aforesaid half of the house, while the same Geoffrey was absent and unaware. The other part of the same house, which had been given to his mother as dower, he pledged to a certain clerk named Engelarius. Since Geoffrey represents that he has thereby been wrongfully burdened, we entrust that case to your experience to hear and determine by due judgment. Therefore, when you are requested concerning this matter, summon both parties before you and decide the case through the administration of justice, taking careful care that the aforesaid clerks may not, through power or wealth, be able to trample upon the justice due to a poor clerk and a widow.

Given at Benevento, on the third day before the Nones of June [3 June].

DLXXVIII. To the same.—On behalf of Berengar, clerk. (Benevento, 4 June.)

[Ibid., col. 815.]

[Col. 0547D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of the people of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

On behalf of the canons of Saint Symphorian at Rheims it has been made known to us that, although they granted the church of Wistri to Berengar, a clerk of good reputation, as we have learned, the abbot of that church is unjustly trying to obstruct the grant of the chapter.

[Note: [Col. 0547] From this passage you may infer that the collegiate body of canons of Saint Symphorian at Rheims was formerly either a regular or a secular abbey.]

We therefore command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to inquire into the truth of this matter; and if it becomes clear to you that the grant of the aforesaid church belongs by right to the chapter and not to the abbot, and if the church itself was canonically granted to the said Berengar, cause him to hold it freely and compel the abbot, with every appeal set aside, to cease harassing him.

Given at Benevento, on the second day before the Nones of June [4 June].

DLXXIX. He informs the canons of Pisa that the priests V. and M., who had abandoned “Malincasa” (that is, Benincasa), have been absolved from excommunication, but that communion has not been restored to Villanus. (Benevento, 12 June.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 403.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of Pisa, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From letters of our beloved sons, the abbot of Saint Michael and Hen. . . . , a Camaldolese monk, we have learned that V. and M., priests, compelled by threats and wicked persuasions, rendered reverence and obedience to the intruder Malincasa. Afterwards, moved by penitence and humbly acknowledging their guilt, in the presence of that same abbot they freely and voluntarily swore that they would obey our commands.
