MCC. To the Bishop of Soissons.—That A., who had left the monastery after the journey to Jerusalem, be received back into it. (Anagni, 25 April.)

[Ibid., col. 997.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother . . . . . . Bishop of Soissons, greeting and apostolic blessing.

A report was recently made known to us by A., bearer of the present letters, returning from Jerusalem [Col. 1043C]: that, terrified by fear of his abbot W., he irregularly abandoned the monastery of Dorbac, in which he asserts that he had received the monastic habit. Afterwards, having obtained permission from his abbot, as is said, he sought, out of devotion, the land which the Lord visited bodily; and, while returning by way of us, he implored the aid of the Apostolic See. Therefore by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood diligently and urgently to admonish the abbot of the aforesaid monastery, that, discipline being observed according to the Rule of St Benedict and the custom of the order of that monastery, he receive the said A. into his monastery and treat him with paternal charity.

Given at Anagni, 7 Kalends of May [25 April].

MCCI. Privilege for the Church of St Mary of Corbeil. (Anagni, 26 April.)

[DOUBLET, *History of the Church of Saint-Denis*, p. 509.]

[Col. 1043D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the prior and brothers of Saint Mary of Corbeil, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since your church is known to belong to the jurisdiction of blessed Denis, it is incumbent upon the office of our solicitude to preserve the rights of that church whole and unimpaired, and to fortify it by apostolic protection so that it may not be troubled by any improper molestations. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just requests, we confirm to you and to your church by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of the present writing, the whole prebend [Col. 1044A] in the church of St Exuperius, and the entire half of the tithe of Chancolia and half of the proceeds of that tithe, just as you reasonably possess them. We decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to harass you or your church with improper molestations concerning your goods or possessions, or to violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it in any manner. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 6 Kalends of May [26 April].

MCCII. To the dean and chapter of Blessed Martin of Tours.—Concerning the granting of *modiationes* to the highest bidder within a fixed term. (Anagni, 29 April.)

[*Defence of Saint Martin of Tours*, 22.]

[Col. 1044B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the dean, treasurer, and chapter of Blessed Martin of Tours, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more specially your church is known to pertain to our care, the more carefully we wish to provide for its security, so that, with the Lord’s assistance, it may continually attain a better condition, since we have endeavoured to bestow watchful care and diligence upon it. Therefore, beloved [Col. 1044C] sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just requests, we decree by apostolic authority that, when those known to hold *modiationes* from you die or in any way forfeit those *modiationes*, the same *modiationes* shall be granted within forty days to the person or persons offering the most, provided there is certain hope that they can pay what they offer. But if any *modiatio* should become vacant about the feast of St John the Baptist, since the harvest season then approaches, we decree by apostolic authority that that *modiatio* shall be granted within ten days after becoming vacant to someone, or to several persons, offering the most and possessing the means to pay what they offer.

[Col. 1044D] Given at Anagni, 3 Kalends of May [29 April].

MCCIII. He confirms an exchange made by the canons of St Anianus of Orléans with A[dela], Queen of the Franks. (Anagni, 4 May.)

[*Antiquities of the Church of Saint-Aignan of Orléans*, p. 85.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to PETER, dean, and the chapter of the Church of St Anianus of Orléans, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since it belongs to our solicitude and office to remove causes of disputes, we are bound by the ministry of governance entrusted to us to provide that what has been done amicably may not turn into a ground of contention. It has come to us that between you and our dearest daughter in Christ, A[dela], illustrious Queen of the Franks, concerning the estate of Caleio, which belonged to the property of your church, an exchange of the following kind took place by the free and spontaneous consent of both parties: you retained the churches of that estate and the revenues, both in money and grain, which you had from Cisiniac; and, receiving from the queen Artenao, Altrochio, and Exart with their appurtenances, you relinquished to her the aforesaid estate free and unencumbered. Therefore, wishing to provide for the future peace and tranquillity of your church, we hold ratified and firm the aforesaid exchange, just as it was made by the free and spontaneous consent of the parties and is known to be contained in the authentic instruments of our dearest son in Christ L., illustrious King of the Franks [Col. 1045B], and of the aforesaid queen; and we confirm it by apostolic authority.

Moreover, lest on the occasion of this exchange any molestation or burden should in future be imposed concerning the churches of the aforesaid estate of Calcio which you are known to have reserved for yourselves, we likewise judge worthy of confirmation to you and your successors those churches and the revenues which you possess in them, as is contained in the authentic writing of our venerable brother Will., Archbishop of Sens and legate of the Apostolic See; and also the grain and money from Cisiniac which you retained for yourselves. By apostolic authority we forbid anyone to dare to inflict molestation or burden upon you and your church concerning those churches, their revenues, or their administration, whereby you might be prevented from possessing the aforesaid churches and the revenues from Cisiniac which you are known to have reserved for yourselves. [Col. 1045C]

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it in any manner.

But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 4 Nones of May [4 May], in the sixteenth year of our pontificate.

MCCIV. He forbids laymen to interfere in the elections of Camaldolese abbots or priors. (Anagni, 20 May.)

[MITTARELLI, *Camaldolese Annals*, IV, Appendix 1.]

[Col. 1045D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons GREGORY and all the Camaldolese brothers, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those things which are known to oppose canonical sanctions and to be wholly alien from the decrees of councils must be more earnestly avoided as pernicious corruptions and uprooted from the midst of the Church with great solicitude, so that the authority of the canons may be observed and the assembly of God’s servants may more freely devote itself to good works and remain more steadfastly in the service of its Creator. For when the presumption of laymen shamelessly intruded itself into the election and promotion of clerics and strove to dispose of sacred things according to the judgment of its own will, decrees of the supreme pontiffs and holy Fathers were promulgated [Col. 1046A], and statutes of various councils issued, that lay persons, however powerful or eminent, should on no account rashly take part in the election or promotion of clerics, or presumptuously dispose of ecclesiastical affairs. For Pope St Adrian II says: “Let no lay prince or powerful man insert himself into an election or promotion,” etc.

Yet we have heard that certain laymen, under colour of patronage, do not fear to intrude themselves into the elections of abbots of your order contrary to the ordinances of the holy Fathers, and do not allow you to conduct canonical elections in your monasteries. Therefore, adhering to the footsteps of our predecessors the Roman pontiffs and following the institutions of the holy Fathers, by the authority of blessed Peter and our own we decree and strictly forbid that any lay person, on account of patronage or for any other reason, shall in any way interfere in the elections of your abbots or priors. We have determined that all laymen are to be deprived of a voice in the election of your prelates, and by apostolic authority we grant you the authority to conduct canonical and free elections according to the freedom of your congregation. In order that this page of our constitution may be inviolably observed in future times, we confirm it by the authority of the Apostolic See and fortify it by the protection of the present writing. We decree that no person whatsoever may violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it in any manner. But if anyone should presume to attempt this [Col. 1046C], let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 13 Kalends of June [20 May].

MCCV. To the canons of St Quentin, he grants that the Bishop of Noyon “shall not dare to bring more than thirty mounts to their church.” (Anagni, 30 May.)

[COLLIETTE, *Memoirs of Vermandois*, II, 339.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the dean and canons of St Quentin, greeting and apostolic blessing.

By the Lord’s providence, although unworthy, we are placed in such a position and office that we must labor with pastoral care for the well-being of all churches and provide for their security insofar as the Lord grants us the means. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just requests, since the Bishop of Noyon is said, on the day of the solemnity of your church when he is bound to visit it annually, to burden your church so greatly by bringing with him a numerous multitude of men and horses that his visitation results in serious loss to that Church, we strictly prohibit and in every way forbid by apostolic authority that the Bishop of Noyon for the time being shall dare to bring more than thirty-five men and thirty mounts to that same church [Col. 1047A]; nor shall they inflict any trouble upon the canons, so as to prevent them from being content with what you deem fit to assign them honourably and sufficiently for so many men and so many mounts. You may also appoint your own servants for assigning this procuration in such manner, according to the ancient custom of your church.

Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to violate this page of our constitution or oppose it in any manner. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 3 Kalends of June [30 May].

MCCVI. He confirms a certain statute made by the chapter of St Quentin. (Anagni, 11 June.)

[Ibid., p. 350.]

[Col. 1047B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the dean and canons of St Quentin, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those measures established by reasonable and circumspect provision ought to gain due force; and, lest they may in future be torn from their stability by anyone’s presumption, they should be fortified with apostolic protection. It has been reported to us that it was long ago established in your church and confirmed by the safeguard of your writing that, if any canon of that church did not maintain residence there, unless he resided elsewhere by permission of the chapter, he ought not to receive the full fruits of his prebend, except for one canon only who was the count’s chaplain. Yet certain fixed and determinate portions were, according to that same institution, to be held by those who had to be absent from the service of that church. The provision is as follows: if he were a cleric not promoted to a stall, he should receive annually six measures of grain, besides certain other fixed and determinate items; if a subdeacon, ten; if a deacon, thirteen; if a priest, sixteen. Therefore, lest what has been established from consideration of propriety might in future be violated by rash audacity, we hold the aforesaid constitution ratified and firm, just as it was made by you and confirmed by your writing; confirming it by apostolic authority [Col. 1047D], and by this present page strictly prohibiting that it be lawful for any canon of your church—except only the canon who is the count’s chaplain—to seek anything beyond what is established in that constitution, unless he is resident in it or has withdrawn to reside elsewhere by leave of the chapter from the number of residents; nor may anyone dare to assign anything to one who seeks it.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it in any manner. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 3 Ides of June [11 June].

MCCVII. He commands all bishops that “in places where Premonstratensian brothers or sisters live, they shall introduce no secular clerics.” (Anagni, 15 June.—See LE PAIGE, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, p. 639, or FÉJER, *Codex diplomaticus Hungariae ecclesiasticus et civilis*, Buda, 1829, octavo, vol. II, p. 187.)

[Col. 1048A]

MCCVIII. To the Archbishop of Tarragona, legate of the Apostolic See.—He decrees that the Churches of Tortosa and Lleida, recently freed from Moorish servitude, shall be subject to Tarragona as their metropolitan. (Anagni, 16 June.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 1071.]

[Col. 1048B] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother, the Archbishop of Tarragona, legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The authority of the dignity entrusted to us induces and exhorts us to extend the fullness of our favour to our brothers and fellow bishops, and further to provide the aid of apostolic favour and protection for those things which they lawfully possess, so that they may be bound to show themselves more fervent in devotion toward blessed Peter and toward us, in proportion as they know themselves to be cherished by a more ample prerogative. Therefore, benignly assenting to your requests, we confirm by apostolic authority to your devotion, and fortify by the protection of the present writing, that honour which Raymond, formerly Count of Barcelona, granted you in Lleida and Tortosa when they were taken, just as you are known peacefully to possess it [Col. 1048C]. We decree that no person whatsoever may violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it in any manner. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 16 Kalends of July [16 June].

MCCIX. To V., prior, and the canons of the Church of St Fridianus of Lucca. (Anagni, 17 June.)

[BALUZE, *Miscellanies*, ed. Mansi, IV, 596.]

[Col. 1048D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons V., prior, and the canons of St Fridianus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The sincerity of your religious life and faith especially exhorts and moves us to attend by pastoral provision to your welfare and advancement, and utterly to annul those things known to have been obtained to the prejudice of your liberty and right. Therefore, wishing also to provide with paternal solicitude for the tranquillity of your Church, by the authority of the present letters we decree that, if the canons of Lucca have obtained from us by false suggestion anything known to derogate from the privileges granted you by the Apostolic See, such unjustly obtained matters [Col. 1049A] can create no prejudice to you.

Given at Anagni, 15 Kalends of July [17 June].

MCCX. To the prior and brothers of the monastery of St Savinus.—That they be obedient to the abbot and surrender their private property to him. (Anagni, 29 June.)

[MARTÈNE, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, I, 457.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the prior and brothers of St Savinus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We do not believe that you are in any way ignorant of the degree of humility and devotion in which you ought to be obedient to our beloved son, your abbot, since you would appear to wear the habit of religion in vain if you did not endeavor to imitate the works of religion with the willing affections of your heart. But, as we have learned, certain of you raise the heel of pride against the aforesaid abbot; and those who seem to have renounced secular desires and left their own possessions dare, contrary to the profession of their order and to the teaching of their master, to retain private property. Since we neither wish nor ought to leave such offences unpunished, by apostolic letters we command your whole body, and in commanding enjoin upon you, that you devoutly and . . . . show obedience and reverence to the aforesaid abbot, and, when required by him, surrender your private property into his hands. You must take care promptly to show yourselves such in matters known to concern the keeping of the cloister and the observance of religious life and of the order, that the report of good reputation may commendably edify your neighbours and that you may deservedly be praised [Col. 1049C] for humility and the virtue of obedience and happily merit the grace of the Most High. Otherwise, the sentence which the aforesaid abbot canonically pronounces against you as contumacious and rebellious on this account we shall, with the Lord’s authority, hold ratified and firm.

Given at Anagni, 3 Kalends of July [29 June].

MCCXI. To the Bishop of Ausona and his chapter.—He admonishes them to restore to the monastery of Ripoll the church of Granoylers, which they were unjustly holding. (Anagni, 30 June.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 1062.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother bishop and beloved sons, the chapter of Ausona, [Col. 1049D] greeting and apostolic blessing.

You should know that a complaint from the abbot and brothers of the monastery of Ripoll has reached our ears: although the church of Granoylers belongs to them, you are holding it contrary to justice. Therefore, since we neither wish nor ought to fail the said monastery in its right, by apostolic letters we command your discretion, and in commanding enjoin upon you, that you restore the aforesaid Church to the said abbot and brothers for peaceful possession without difficulty; or else do not delay to render them full justice concerning it before our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Tarragona, accepting and inviolably observing whatever he shall decide in the matter.

Given at Anagni, 2 Kalends of July [30 June].

MCCXII. To the dean, treasurer, and chapter of the Church of Blessed Martin of Tours.—He grants that they may lawfully reclaim churches held from their fiefs and possessions pertaining to their own property. (Anagni, 4 July.)

[*Defence of Saint-Martin of Tours*, 27.]

[Col. 1050A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the dean, treasurer, and chapter of the Church of Blessed Martin of Tours, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more specially your church is known to belong to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter and ourselves, and to look more directly to the provision [Col. 1050B] and protection of the most holy Roman Church, the more earnestly we attend to its welfare and advancement and desire with our whole heart to labor for those things which concern its honour and increase. Therefore, following more diligently the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, just as it is known that their privileges granted you the right lawfully to reclaim churches held from your fiefs and possessions pertaining to your property, so we likewise grant this to you by apostolic authority: if knights or others wish to convey to you the right which they possess in churches and possessions held from your fiefs, you may have it freely and without any contradiction, so that, relying upon our authority in this matter, you may not rashly be troubled or impeded by anyone.

Given at Anagni, 4 Nones of July [4 July].

MCCXIII. To the clerics and laypeople of Bagnacavallo.—That they return to obedience to the canons of Faenza. (Anagni, 6 July.)

[SAVIOLI, *Bolognese Annals*, II, II, 37.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the clerics and laypeople of Bagnacavallo, greeting and apostolic blessing.

You should know that something has reached our hearing which, if true, greatly astonishes and disturbs us: although you are bound in every way and in all things to answer to the Church of Faenza as members to their head [Col. 1050D], and to show it due obedience and reverence, without consulting the canons of that church you caused a cross to be set up in a certain place by the Bishops of Bologna and Reggio, who have no right in your castle or church, as a sign that an oratory was to be built there. When the aforesaid canons came to that place and humbly and devoutly asked you to permit the cross, which had been placed there without their consent, to be removed, you not only did not comply with their requests, but even set up in the aforesaid place another cross larger than the first, to their injury and contempt. You said that you would not allow the cross to be removed from that place by them, nor would you remove it; and that they might come for the reconciliation of your church if they wished; otherwise, without consulting them, you would have your church reconciled by one of the surrounding bishops. You also assailed them with many other reproaches and insults. [Col. 1051A]

Therefore, because these acts, if true, ought to be punished with severe vengeance, by apostolic letters we command your discretion, and in commanding have commanded you, that you humbly show to the Church of Faenza, as to your spiritual mother, and to those same canons, the obedience and reverence due; and that you make such satisfaction to them for the injuries inflicted that no indignation on account of them may remain in their minds. And if you began that oratory without the consent of the Church of Faenza, do not hereafter construct anything there under the name of an oratory without the permission of that Church, nor presume to celebrate divine offices in that place. But if you presume to act otherwise and do not make due satisfaction to those canons, the sentence which they reasonably pronounce against you on that account we shall, with the Lord’s authority, hold ratified and cause to be inviolably observed. [Col. 1051B]

Given at Anagni, 2 Nones of July [6 July].

MCCXIV. To the Bishop of Vic.—He orders the Church of St Stephen, violently seized and held, to be restored to the monks of Ripoll within forty days. (Anagni, 22 July.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 1062.]

[Col. 1051C] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother, Bishop of Vic, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever prelates of churches do anything in which they seem to exceed the due bounds of their office, or unjustly seize what belongs by right to others, it is incumbent upon the office of our solicitude to restrain them from such presumption by the authority granted us and to preserve each person’s rights. Indeed, from the complaint transmitted to us by our beloved sons, the abbot and brothers of the church of Ripoll, we have learned that you unjustly took from them the Church of St Stephen, which belongs to their right, and hold it by violent occupation. Therefore by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood, and in commanding enjoin upon you, that within forty days after receiving these letters, all contradiction and appeal ceasing, you restore the aforesaid church to the said abbot and brothers; or, in the presence of our venerable brothers the Bishops of Huesca and Barcelona, with recourse to appeal removed, render full justice.

Given at Anagni, 11 Kalends of August [22 July].

MCCXV. To the Bishops of Huesca and Barcelona.—He orders them to admonish and induce the Bishop of Vic to restore the Church of St Stephen, which he had violently seized. (Anagni, 22 July.)

[Ibid., col. 1063.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable [Col. 1052A] brothers, the Bishops of Huesca and Barcelona, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the complaint transmitted to us by our beloved sons, the abbot and brothers of the Church of Ripoll, we have learned that our venerable brother, the Bishop of Vic, unjustly took from them the Church of St Stephen, which belongs to their right, and holds it by violent occupation. Therefore by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood, and in commanding enjoin upon you, that you admonish and induce the aforesaid bishop, and, if necessary, more strictly compel him, with recourse to appeal removed, to restore the aforesaid Church to the said abbot and brothers within forty days after receiving these letters, all contradiction and appeal ceasing; or, in your presence and with appeal removed, to render full justice. [Col. 1052B]

Given at Anagni, 11 Kalends of August [22 July].

MCCXVI. To the Pisan clergy.—That they induce the people to pay tithes to the canons. (Anagni, 6 August.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, III, 404.]

ALEXANDER, etc., to the beloved sons, the whole clergy of Pisa, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting and wholly consonant with reason that children should always regard their mother with filial reverence and devotion and should be solicitous and zealous for her advancement, so that they may bind her to themselves with a more abundant affection insofar as they are proved to bear a more sincere disposition and exhibit a steadier faith toward her. Therefore by apostolic letters we command your whole body, and in commanding enjoin upon you, that with all urgency you admonish the people committed to you and firmly and strictly command them to pay to your beloved sons, the archpriest and canons of the Church of Pisa, without trouble and difficulty, the tithes in accordance with what is contained in their privileges; otherwise they may fear that, if they deny the tithes, they will be reduced to a tenth and thereby incur divine indignation. [Col. 1052C]

Given at Anagni, 8 Ides of August [6 August].

MCCXVII. He grants to the abbot and brothers of the Premonstratensian order “that they may impose penance upon servants who live from their table, and administer the Lord’s body to them at the appointed times.”

[Anagni, 21 August.—See LE PAIGE, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, p. 630.]

[Col. 1052D]

MCCXVIII. He confirms the chapel of St John to the monastery of St German of the Meadows at Paris. (Anagni, 30 August.)

[BOUILLART, *History of Saint-Germain-des-Prés*, pr. 42.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons Hugh, abbot, and the brothers of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From letters of our beloved sons Elias, Abbot of St John of Neuf-Moutier, and the Abbot of St Severinus of the castle of Nanton, it has been plainly made known to us [Col. 1053A] that, when they had undertaken by our command to bring to due conclusion the cause being litigated between you and the abbot of St Savinus concerning the newly constructed chapel of St John, in the place called Château-Neuf near the castle of Airald, they summoned the parties and, having more fully heard and considered the arguments on both sides, adjudged the aforesaid chapel to you and your monastery by definitive sentence. Therefore, since it is fitting for us to approve matters lawfully decided and to strengthen them by the force of apostolic authority, holding the aforesaid sentence ratified and firm, we confirm to you and your monastery by apostolic authority that same chapel, just as it was lawfully adjudged to you, and fortify it by the protection of the present writing. We decree that [Col. 1053B] no person whatsoever may violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it in any manner. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 3 Kalends of September [30 August].

MCCXIX. He writes as follows to the Archbishop of Milan: “The nobleman P. informed us that he refused the castle of Ferruce [otherwise, Verruca] to F[riderick], called emperor, when he was once returning from Rome; as a result, four castles were destroyed, more than two thousand houses were destroyed, and many people were killed.” He commands him to impose penance upon P. (*Decretals of Gregory*, book V, title 38, chapter 3.)

[Col. 1053C]

YEAR 1166–1176.

MCCXX. He commands Henry, Patriarch of Grado, and Theodinus, cardinal priest of St Vitalis, to judge between C. and L[eonard], elected Bishops of Torcello.

(Ibid., book II, title 28, chapter 23.)

YEAR 1170–1176.

MCCXXI. He replies to Ildebrand, cardinal priest of the Twelve Apostles and legate of the Apostolic See, that he should “have the bishop-elect, who has recently returned to the unity of the Church after abjuring schism, consecrated by the Catholic suffragan bishops of the Church of Aquileia.” ?(Ibid., book I, title 6, chapter 5.)

[Col. 1053D]

YEAR 1173–1176.

MCCXXII. To Simon, Abbot of St Albans.—He answers his questions. (Anagni, 8 April.)

[Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. GILES, II, 104.]

ALEXANDER Pope III, to SIMON, Abbot of St Albans, concerning certain questions.

Consulted concerning the individual cases, we are compelled by the office of our service to reply, so that if any question or doubt arises in anyone’s mind, it may be resolved by the Roman Church, which, by the Lord’s disposition, has merited to hold primacy among the others. We have indeed been asked whether, when someone who maintains that he has been deprived of a church or any possession without judgment and reasonable cause obtains from us letters to a judge, ordering that the possession be restored to him within a fixed time if it is established to the judge that he was thus dispossessed, the possession ought to be restored to him when the person holding the church or possession claimed by him had departed, before any mention was made of those letters, for the sake of study, pilgrimage, or some similar cause, and cannot appear before the judge within the prescribed time.

To your inquiry on this point we reply as follows: he cannot and ought not to obtain restoration, even if he is prepared to prove before the delegated judge, by suitable witnesses, both his possession and his ejectment, unless the possessor has absented himself through contumacy. But if the judge postpones the term until the return of the possessor, his jurisdiction expires, because a judge may not in any way extend a term fixed by the delegator without the consent of both parties.

Furthermore, if a cleric has been instituted in a church by the ordinary judge at the presentation of someone believed to be patron of that church, and afterward another person prevails in court concerning the right of patronage, the cleric who was instituted ought not for this reason to be removed from that church, provided that, at the time of his presentation, the person who presented him possessed the right of patronage over the church. But if at that time he did not possess the right of patronage, but was only thought to be patron while in fact he was not, and had no possession of the patronage, then, according to the custom of England, he may be removed from the same church.

Donations or grants of churches made to private persons while those who possess the churches themselves are alive are to have no force; but if they are made to religious houses, they are to be held valid—provided, however, that the persons already possessing the said churches are not deprived of them during their lifetime without their consent.

Given at Anagni, on the sixth day before the Ides of April.

MCCXXIII. To Theobald, bishop of Piacenza.—That he restore to the monks of Saint Sabinus “the tithe of the enclosed estate situated beside Saint Ambrose.” (Anagni, April 8.)

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, II, 360.]

[Col. 1054D] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother T[HEOBALD], bishop of Piacenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the representations of our beloved sons the abbot and brethren of Saint Sabinus, you should know that it has come to our hearing that, whereas Arduin, of good memory, formerly bishop of Piacenza, and his other predecessors, had, out of regard for divine love, bestowed upon their monastery the tithe of an enclosed estate situated beside Saint Ambrose, as is known to be contained in a public instrument, your predecessor Hugh, of good memory, who afterward became bishop of Tusculum, eventually withdrew from them at his pleasure the aforesaid tithe, and in the castle [lacuna] withheld from them annually one *vegeta* of wine.

Moreover, since it is to your honour, praise, and salvation if you take care to observe the reasonable enactments of your predecessors and to correct whatever any of them may have done unlawfully, we earnestly admonish and command your brotherhood not to imitate the violence of the aforesaid Hugh in this matter. Rather, out of reverence for blessed Peter and for us, restore without awaiting judgment or contradiction the aforesaid tithe to the said abbot and his brethren, and leave them in peace, as the above-mentioned Arduin, your predecessor, is known likewise to have bestowed it upon them, and as is contained in the public instrument. Cause also the aforesaid monastery to be supplied annually with the said full *vegeta* of wine, according to the custom of the aforesaid Arduin and his predecessors, so that the brethren may continually intercede before the Most High for your salvation with the devout affections of their hearts, and we may in consequence commend your charity and prudence with worthy praises in the Lord.

Given at Anagni, on the sixth day before the Ides of April.

MCCXXIV. He commands the archbishop of Vienne and his suffragans to restrain those molesting the Carthusians in their boundaries or pastures, and to prevent other religious from building near them. (Anagni, April 11.)

[*Privileges of the Carthusian Order, and the multiple confirmation thereof*, fol. 1b, Basel, 1510, folio.]

[Col. 1055C] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers the archbishop of Vienne, legate of the Apostolic See, and his suffragans, in whose dioceses the houses or pastures of the Carthusian brethren are situated: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Your prudent discretion is not unaware with how great a desire and love the aforesaid brethren devote themselves to divine service; renouncing carnal desires and despising the delights of earthly things, they have chosen to live soberly, justly, and piously in this world, and have resolved to devote themselves unceasingly to heavenly contemplation. Accordingly, it is fitting, proper, and consonant with reason that they be supported in their holy and pious purpose by the efforts of bishops and by necessary and suitable assistance.

By apostolic writings we command your brotherhood, under precept, that if any of your parishioners presume to molest or disturb the aforesaid brethren concerning boundary-markers or pastures which they reasonably possess, you are to administer against them strict and full justice, without appeal, unless, having been warned, they desist. On our behalf, you are also to prohibit most strictly the construction near their houses of any other religious house by which those religious might reasonably be impeded or disturbed, or which might even occasion scandal.

Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Ides of April.

MCCXXV. To Peter, archbishop of Salona.—He praises his fidelity and consoles him amid afflictions. He denies that he will make any decree concerning the Church of Zadar to the archbishop’s injury. (Anagni, May 5.)

[FARLATI, *Illyricum Sacrum*, III, 186.]

[Col. 1056A] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother P[ETER], archbishop of Salona: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received with so much the more kindly charity your letter and our beloved son J., the sacristan who bore it, whom you sent to the Apostolic See, because we know that you adhere with greater firmness to your special mother, the most holy Roman Church, and to ourselves. Her devoted and faithful sons, although they are sometimes troubled by the persecutions of perverse men and may for a time appear to be oppressed, are nevertheless not utterly deprived of temporal assistance; rather, in her they always find fitting and secure aid.

That constancy of devotion and affection of sincere purity which we clearly know you to possess toward that same your mother, the Roman Church—and concerning which your past acts do not permit us to doubt—we consider most pleasing and welcome; and we extol it with a greater reward of praise, in proportion as we perceive it to proceed from a more sincere token of charity. Therefore we and the Roman Church love with the pure abundance of charity both your ecclesiastical person and the city entrusted to your governance, and embrace them with the arms of inward affection. We have a fervent purpose and will, in whatever ways may be possible with God and justice, gladly to consider your honour and exaltation and, by the Lord’s assistance, to provide for them according to the ardour of so great an affection.

As for those troubles and oppressions inflicted upon you without reasonable cause, we are distressed over them as though they were our own, and we pour forth prayers to the Lord that, according to the multitude of His mercies, He may soon deliver you from the persecutions threatening you and bring you to a tranquil harbour. We hope that the Lord will not restrain His mercy in anger, but will with this temptation provide an outcome, so that you may be able to endure it [1 Cor. 10]; and that, besides the rod of correction, He will add the staff of consolation, so that you may say with the Prophet: “According to the multitude of my sorrows, your consolations, O Lord, have made my soul glad” [Ps. 93].

Since the Lord commands the power of the sea and calms its movement in the twinkling of an eye, lift the eyes of your mind to heaven, whence help shall come to you. Consider also how the almighty Lord cast down the glory of the proud by the hand of a boy casting a small stone, and granted the children of Israel victory over a multitude of enemies through one woman. Place your hope in Him who knows how to grant a prosperous outcome to His faithful amid impending distress, and to bring consolation after tears and weeping.

[Col. 1057A] Therefore, holding full confidence in His aid, put on the spirit of fortitude; prudently and manfully resist your enemies; and remain immovably steadfast in devotion to blessed Peter and to us. But if [lacuna] whatever ought to pertain to the advantage and honour of the holy Roman Church and to your own honour is most pleasing and welcome to us. For, by God’s assistance, we have decreed, and shall decree, nothing new concerning the Church of Zadar apart from justice and the honour of the Church of Split.

Further, we earnestly commend to your brotherhood our beloved son L., our chaplain, asking that, out of reverence for blessed Peter and at our request, you hold him dear, and henceforth still dearer. Know also that we and the brethren around us are, by God’s grace, sound and well; and we hope that the Church of God will shortly enjoy tranquil peace.

Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Nones of May.

MCCXXVI. To the bishop and consuls of Bologna.—That they desist from injuries against the Church of Nonantola. (Anagni, May 23.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *History of Nonantola*, II, 277.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the bishop and to his beloved sons the consuls of Bologna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since the Church of Nonantola belongs directly, without intermediary, to the right of blessed Peter and to ours, it was fitting that you should refrain in every way from molesting and burdening it, and should preserve its possessions and rights whole and unharmed with proportionately greater zeal, since it is known to be subject in a special manner to our care. Thus your devotion toward us and the Church would appear more fervent and constant, since we would recognize that you applied due diligence and concern to the conduct of those who belong to our jurisdiction.

But you, brother bishop, as the abbot of the aforesaid church has informed us in his letters, grievously harass that church and its people contrary to the duty of your office; nor do you fear violently to plunder their goods and take away their possessions. Although we had sent you letters ordering you to appear before our son Ildebrand, cardinal-priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles and legate of the Apostolic See, together with the said abbot and brethren, concerning the matter of Palade, you not only refused to receive our letters, but, as though on the occasion of those letters, presumed to harass the people of Palade more severely.

You also, sons, consuls, have bound by oath all the people whom the aforesaid Church is known to possess in your diocese, so that they might thereafter render it no further service. But since it is not proper for you to burden the aforesaid church in this way, and since we can endure this for no reason—we who are bound to extend the protection of apostolic guardianship to the individual Churches of God, and especially to those which belong more particularly to our jurisdiction—we admonish and command your discretion by apostolic writings wholly to desist from the unjust molestations and burdens imposed upon the aforesaid abbot, brethren, and their church; to release without delay the oath which you unlawfully compelled the people of that church to take; and finally, when summoned by the aforesaid cardinal on this matter, to appear before him and firmly accept and observe whatever he determines between you by agreement or judgment.

For we have instructed that cardinal to compose amicably between you, or determine by judicial procedure, the matters proposed by either side, so that no further evils may be committed by either party. And if the abbot and his brethren have committed any offence against you, let him cause it to be corrected and remedied in such a way that you ought not only to refrain from burdening them, but henceforth to extend to them your favour and affection more fully and effectively.

Given at Anagni, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June.

MCCXXVII. He confirms the peace concluded between Hugh, bishop of Terracina, and Peter de Roberto. (Anagni, August 26.)

[CONTATORE, *On the History of Terracina*, 399.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HUGH, bishop of Terracina: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When you and our beloved son Peter de Roberto stood before us concerning the dispute between you and him over half of Saxone, you settled the matter with him, through the mediation of our venerable brother B., bishop of Porto, and our beloved son P., cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, in order to avoid scandal. At the request of our beloved sons, the noblemen O., C., and P. Frajop., and L. de Supin., you granted him the said half of Saxone to hold during his lifetime, on the condition that after his death it should return freely and absolutely to your church, without any custom or law standing in the way and without any dispute; and that you and your successors should be free to enter into possession of Saxone without contradiction.

(Much is missing, having been eaten away by mice.) [lacuna] He more clearly acknowledged that it belonged to your right and to that of the church entrusted to you, and, before us and our brethren, the witnesses, and those who had been summoned on either side, he forever submitted every lawsuit and public dispute to judgment; and he is to cause, together with his sons, a charter of renunciation and a public instrument to be drawn up for you and your successors.

That this settlement may be observed inviolably for all time, we confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it with the protection of this present writing. We decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, on the seventh day before the Kalends of September.

MCCXXVII *bis*. To the chapter of Saint Peter at Wessinsbrunn.—That they do not receive again the expelled schismatic abbot. (Anagni, September 30.)

[LEUTNER, *History of the Monastery of Wessofont*, 211.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the chapter of Saint Peter at Wessinsbrunn: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Your monks Henry and Charles have reported to us that, after your former abbot had been expelled by you for his offences, he subsequently released you altogether from your obedience of his own free will. But the bishop of Augsburg, who is a schismatic, is making every effort to restore to him the administration of the monastery. Therefore, since that abbot fosters schismatic perversity, we neither wish nor ought to permit his return to the monastery, especially through a schismatic.

By apostolic writings we command you under precept that, if the said abbot is a schismatic and has released you from obedience to him, you must in no way presume henceforth to receive him as abbot.

Given at Anagni, on the second day before the Kalends of October.

MCCXXVII *ter*. To the same.—That they receive the brethren Henry and Charles. (Anagni, September 30.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1059C] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the chapter of Saint Peter at Wessinsbrunn: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the report of your brethren Henry and Charles, and from the letters of our beloved son, the noble Duke Welf, it has become manifest to us that those brethren did not hesitate to adhere to the man who held the place of abbot among you, although that abbot is a schismatic and fosters schismatic perversity. But because, as we have learned from their confession and the letters of the aforesaid duke, the said monks have withdrawn from him and returned to our devotion and to Catholic unity, we have received with paternal charity their apparently ready conversion to us; we have caused them to be absolved according to the custom of the Church, and now send them back, absolved and with favour, to your church.

We therefore command and enjoin your discretion that you receive the aforesaid monks as absolved and cause them to be regarded as absolved. For it is fitting and proper that the faithful of God should be received as absolved when the Apostolic See judges them absolved.

Given at Anagni, on the second day before the Kalends of October.

ANNO 1174–1176.

[Col. 1060A]

MCCXXVIII. At the request of Abbot Rodulf and the monks of Cluny, he forbids abbots, without the consent of the chapter, to alienate the treasure, offices of honour, dependent houses, or possessions of the Church of Cluny. (Anagni, January 16.)

[*Library of Cluny*, 1431.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RODULF, abbot, and the brethren of the monastery of Cluny: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more closely we love you and your Church—which is known, as regards the jurisdiction of blessed Peter and our own care, to belong specially and directly to us—on account of the religious life, devotion, and faith in which, by the Lord’s gift, you are known to excel, the more we desire to assist you in your needs, preserve your rights with more earnest care and solicitude, and grant you, where expedient, the favour of our grace and the protection of our guardianship.

Through our beloved son I., one of your monks, you, son abbot, have devoutly and humbly requested us strictly to prohibit you and any of your successors, without the common consent of the chapter, from disposing of or alienating the treasure of your Church, its honours, possessions, and dependent houses which it presently holds or may hereafter, by God’s assistance, justly acquire.

Therefore, desiring earnestly to attend to your welfare and advancement, and willing, by God’s assistance, that your monastery should remain in perpetual peace and tranquillity, so that, free there from secular tumults, you may devote yourselves more quietly to the service of almighty God, we prohibit by apostolic authority, under threat of anathema, that you or any of your successors may in any way dispose of or alienate, without the common consent of the chapter or of its sounder part, the treasure which your said Church now possesses or may recover or lawfully acquire by God’s help; or its honours, possessions, or dependent houses; or pledge them to outsiders under any title whatsoever.

Given at Anagni, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of February.

MCCXXIX. To Rodulf and the brethren of Cluny, he declares that the church of Saint John was built by them. (Anagni, January 17.—*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 72.)

MCCXXX. He confirms the goods of the convent of Gudhem, given by King Canute and his brother. (Anagni, January 19.)

[LILJEGREN, *Swedish Diplomatic Collection*, I, 97.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the nuns at Gudhem: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners and bring to effect the vows which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, concurring favourably with your just requests, we confirm by apostolic authority to you and to your monastery whatever you reasonably possess in the aforesaid estate through the gift of King Canute, his brother, or any other of their predecessors, and strengthen it with the protection of this present writing.

We decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1061B] Given at Anagni, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of February.

ANNO 1175–1176.

MCCXXXI. To Peter, cardinal of Saint Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—He complains that the bishop of Paris, contrary to the pope’s command and an appeal that had been made, conferred an archdeaconry. (Anagni, November 6.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 964.]

If it became known to our dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks, how seriously the insolence and rashness of the bishop of Paris—who, contrary to our command and to the appeal lodged with us by you concerning this matter, did not fear, to our grave contempt and injury, to confer the archdeaconry of his church at his own pleasure—has detracted from the institutions of the holy Fathers and the dignity of the Roman Church, he would, as we believe, patiently endure that so great and grave a presumption be punished with due severity. Nor would he be disturbed, as he is said to have been, because we did not judge that so dreadful and detestable a deed should be approved.

But lest the royal majesty remain unaware how grievously the authority of the holy Fathers and the dignity of the Apostolic See, which chiefly rests upon appeals, have been injured in this affair, we will and command your discretion to approach the aforesaid king and explain to him fully, wisely, and carefully how grievously the censure of the sacred canons and the authority of the Roman Church have been impaired by the fact that the said bishop presumed, after the appeal which you are known to have lodged with us at our command, to grant the aforesaid archdeaconry; and how from this a perverse and unjust example will pass to posterity. For whatever is undertaken by anyone contrary to an appeal cannot be left uncorrected without injury to canonical enactment and derogation from justice.

By diligently setting forth these matters and others, strive carefully to call the aforesaid king back from his purpose and policy in this matter. But if he cannot be recalled from it, declare to him on our behalf that, in regard for his most welcome devotion, we bear with equanimity the act of that bishop—however grave and offensive to us, and contrary to the institution of the holy Fathers—and that we have determined to remit this offence to the bishop and to the nephew of our beloved son Walter, the king’s chamberlain. On the occasion of this offence, we shall inflict upon neither of them any burden or molestation; we remit any sentence which has been pronounced against them for this reason, and we relinquish against them the prosecution of any appeal which they are known to have lodged.

Nevertheless, lest we or our beloved son Gratian, our subdeacon, appear to endure such disgrace and shame, persuade the aforesaid king to provide in this matter for our honour and that of the said G. in such a way that we may receive fitting consolation and deservedly commend the royal care in the Lord.

Given at Anagni, on the eighth day before the Ides of November.

ANNO 1176.

MCCXXXII. He takes the convent of Saint Justina of Lucca under protection and confirms its rule, possessions, and rights. (Anagni, January 13.)

[MURATORI, *Italian Antiquities*, V, 567.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, Cecilia, abbess of Saint Justina of Lucca, and the sisters, present and future, professing the monastic life, forever.

[Col. 1062C] The Apostolic See ought to grant protection to prudent virgins who, under the habit of religion, with lamps kindled by works of holiness, continually prepare themselves to go out to meet the Bridegroom. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it with the privilege of this present writing.

First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in that monastery according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolably for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions, etc., among which we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The possessions and property which the same monastery has within or outside the city of Lucca: namely, leasehold lands and holdings at Flexo and within its boundaries; at Vico Solari and within its boundaries; at Marlia and within its boundaries; at Lammari; at Tassignano; at Capannore; at Paganico; at Antraccole and within their boundaries; at Vico Moriano; at Arepentina; in the parish of Turre and within its boundaries; in the parish of the monastery of Sigerad; in the parish of Saint Stephen and within its boundaries; in the parish of Saint Micharius and within its boundaries; at Caprili and within its boundaries; at Avane and within its boundaries, which the people of Avane have held and hold from that Church; in the parish of Computo and within its boundaries; at Calcinaria; at Valivo; at Gallicano; at Alverni; at Ponte Colphi; at Filicajo; at Saxorosso; and at Castro Falfi.

Furthermore, you may receive into conversion free and unencumbered men and women who, being their own masters, wish to give themselves to your monastery, and retain them in your monastery without any contradiction. We also decree that no person may dare to pronounce a sentence of interdict against you or your monastery without manifest and reasonable cause. Upon the death of you, the present abbess of that place, or of any of your successors, no one is to be placed over the monastery by any artifice of deception or violence, except the woman whom the sisters by common consent, or the sounder part of the sisters, shall have determined ought to be elected in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict.

When there is a general interdict upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, without ringing bells, excluding those under interdict and excommunicated persons, and in a low voice. We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, John, cardinal-priest of Saints Paul and Pammachius. I, etc.

Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the holy Roman Church, on the nineteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1175, and in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCXXXIII. To Peter, cardinal of Saint Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—That he exhort the king of the Franks, princes, and others to take the cross. (Anagni, January 29.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 970.]

We have learned from the letters of our dearest son in Christ, Manuel, illustrious emperor of Constantinople, that he entered the land of the Turks with a strong hand, destroyed cities and castles with sword and fire, and, in the midst of the territory of the sultan of Iconium, built a large and populous city in which he stationed Latins and Greeks to guard it. Through this city, by God’s grace, he holds sway over a great region of the Turks—to such an extent that, by the Lord’s action, he has made safe for all Christians, both Latins and Greeks, the road for visiting the Lord’s Sepulchre.

Since the emperor declares that he holds a firm vow and purpose not to cease in any way from attacking that accursed people until, by God’s help, he has completed against them what he began, we, desiring at his request to advance his pious purpose, have sent apostolic letters of exhortation to the kings and princes of the world and to other faithful persons, urging them, from the motive of pious devotion, faithfully and diligently to labour to confound that people and exalt the name of the Christian faith.

We therefore earnestly admonish and command your discretion to strive, by diligent warnings and exhortations, to induce the king, the princes, counts, barons, and other faithful of the kingdom of the Franks to the same undertaking, so that your persuasion may be made clear in the execution of the work and we may worthily commend your prudence and diligence in the Lord.

Given at Anagni, on the fourth day before the Kalends of February.

MCCXXXIV. To the clerics of the Church of Alessandria.—Concerning the new bishop granted to them, or transferred from elsewhere. (Anagni, January 30.)

[Ibid., col. 911.]

The novelty and necessity of the case caused us, in the presence of the envoy of the Church of Milan and without any preceding election, to provide you and your church, by our authority, with a bishop-elect. Therefore, lest any prejudice arise from this for you or your successors, we have judged it necessary to make provision for you by apostolic authority.

Accordingly, beloved sons in the Lord, by this present writing we decree that this shall not prejudice you in the future, so as to prevent you and your successors, upon the death of the present bishop-elect or any of his successors, from freely electing your bishops, just as the canons of cathedral churches subject to the Church of Milan are known to have such freedom. Let it therefore be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our constitution or in any way oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Kalends of February.

MCCXXXV. He confirms the settlement made by William, archbishop of Reims and legate of the Apostolic See, between the brethren of Saint Peter and the chaplains of the churches of Saint John, Saint Nicholas, and Saint James at Ghent.

(Anagni, March 4.—See Miraeus, *Diplomatic Works*, vol. III, p. 70.)

MCCXXXVI. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Camaldoli. (Anagni, March 17.)

[*Annals of Camaldoli*, IV, 52.]

[Col. 1064D] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons … the prior of Camaldoli and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to labour for the welfare of churches and, with the Lord’s salutary assistance, to provide for their peace and tranquillity. For it is deemed fitting and honourable that we, who by the Lord’s disposition have been appointed to their governance, should protect them from the malice of wicked men and fortify them with the patronage of blessed Peter and the Apostolic See.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your requests. Following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Paschal, Eugenius, Anastasius, and Adrian, we command and enact by the authority of this present decree that no person whatsoever—cleric, monk, or layperson, of whatever order or dignity, now or in future—may in any way separate from its subjection and unity those communities and places which have adopted the discipline and order of the hermitage or cenobium of Camaldoli and which today remain under its government. For the preservation of unity, these places and communities have seemed worthy to be recorded under their individual names:

In the diocese of Arezzo: the monastery of Saint Saviour of the Berardingi; Saint Peter at Rota; Saint [Col. 1065B] Mary at Agnano; Saint Quirinus at Rosa; the hermitage of Fleri; the monastery of Saint Virianus; Saint Bartholomew at Anglare; near Bagno, the monastery of Saint Mary at Trivio; at Galiota, the monastery of Saint Mary on the Island; in the diocese of Montefeltro, the monastery of Monte Ercole; in the diocese of Forlimpopoli, the hospice of Almeric; in the diocese of Pesaro, the monastery of Saint Decentius and the hermitage of Fajolo; in the diocese of Bologna, the monastery of Saint Michael the Archangel near the castle of Britti, and Saint Felix; in the diocese of Florence, the monastery of Saint Peter at Laco and Saint Saviour near the city; in the diocese of Fiesole, the monastery of Saint Mary at Poplena and the church of Saint Margaret; in the diocese of Volterra, the monastery of Saint Peter at Fontiano, [Col. 1065C] Saint Mary at Policiano, Saint Peter at Cerreto, and Saint Justus near the city; in the diocese of Pisa, the monastery of Saint Mary of Morrena, the monastery of Saint Stephen at Cinctoria, and Saint Sabinus at Montione; in that city itself, the monasteries of Saint Michael, Saint Frigidianus, and Saint Zeno; in the diocese of Lucca, the monastery of Saint Saviour at Cantiniano and Saint Peter at Puteoli.

Likewise in Sardinia, in the archdiocese of Torres: the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Saccaria; the church of Saint Eugenia at Samanar; the church of Saint Michael and Saint Lawrence at Vanari; the church of Saint Mary and Saint John at Altasar; the church of Saint Mary at Contra; the church of Saint John and Saint Simeon at Salvenaro; the church [Col. 1065D] of Saint Nicholas of Trulla; the church of Saint Peter at Scano; the church of Saint Paul at Contrognano; and the church of Saint Peter at Olim.

Likewise in Tuscany, in the diocese of Chiusi: the hermitage of Vivo on Mount Amiata, together with all the appurtenances of the places stated above; moreover, the estate of Majona, which you purchased from Henry the provost and the other canons, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Montione, which you purchased from the abbot of Saint Flora, as is contained in your charters, and which was adjudged to you through the administration of justice by Pope Anastasius of blessed memory and confirmed by the judgement of his written instrument. Furthermore, by apostolic authority we confirm to you and your community the monastery of Urano, saving the right of the Church of Ravenna.

We therefore decree and, by authority of the apostolic see, ordain that all the aforesaid monasteries, with everything belonging to them, [Col. 1066A] shall remain forever as one body under one head—namely, under the prior of the Camaldolese hermitage—and shall persevere in the observance of its discipline, under that prior, that is, whom the abbots or priors of that congregation and the hermits shall, by God’s grace, regularly elect. Moreover, we decree that the congregation itself shall forever be fostered under the protection of the apostolic see in such a way that no bishop may excommunicate any of these monasteries, or place it under an interdict from divine offices, without the prior’s consent or the permission of the apostolic see. The brethren themselves, however, may receive the sacraments of consecration or ordination from whichever Catholic bishop they prefer.

[Col. 1066B] Given at Anagni, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1175 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCXXXVII. He asserts for Ubaldo, archbishop of Pisa, the primacy of Sardinia. (Fragment.) (Anagni, 11 April.—UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 408.)

MCCXXXVIII. To the monks of Saint George of Lucca.—That they are to surrender the church which they had acquired with money. (Anagni, 11 April.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 1080.]

[Col. 1066C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the provost and monks of Saint George of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to our ears that, although you had bought for forty pounds, contrary to the statutes and decrees of the holy Fathers, the church of Saint Matthew of Fossa Natali, and had held it for a long time through violence and the favour of the consuls of the city of Lucca, you, son provost, at the admonition of the canons of the Church of Lucca, had simply renounced it in chapter, or through the priest residing there; nevertheless, the bishop-elect of Lucca later entrusted that church to the said priest, to be governed and administered under your obedience, [Col. 1066D] and in this matter did not maintain the gravity and prudence which were fitting.

Therefore, since it is unsafe for you—and indeed wholly perilous—to retain any longer a church which you acquired through money, and since it would be fitting for you to do penance for such an acquisition and worthily be reconciled to God through works of suitable satisfaction, because such a contract is unjust and smacks of the wickedness of simony, we admonish, command, and enjoin your whole community that, as you love your salvation and reputation, you utterly abandon the aforesaid church and do not henceforth concern yourselves with it or its goods. For this could without doubt result in grave loss and injury, and indeed danger, to your order and religious life. [Col. 1067A] We too would be compelled to punish sharply the vice of simony.

Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Ides of April.

MCCXXXIX. Privilege for the monastery of Vallombrosa. (Anagni, 20 April.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 221.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JAMES, abbot of Vallombrosa, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

A desire which is recognized as pertaining to the purpose of religious life and the salvation of souls ought, with the Lord as its author, to be fulfilled without delay. Since, therefore, your purpose, the simplicity of your religious life—divine mercy preceding and following it—has diffused the fragrance of good repute both near at hand and far away, [Col. 1067B] we, wishing with the Lord’s assent to add advancement to your advancement, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Paschal and Adrian, Roman pontiffs, receive your monastery, dedicated in reverence of blessed Mary ever Virgin, into the possession, guardianship, and protection of the Roman Church and the apostolic see. Strengthening it by the privilege of apostolic authority, we decree that it shall remain free from the yoke of all persons.

First, indeed, we ordain that the monastic order which is known to have been established there according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods, etc., among which we have judged the following to be expressly named: the monastery of Saint Salvius; the monastery of the Most Holy Trinity of Florence; the monastery of Strumene; the monastery of Osolla; the monastery of Saint James of Castello; the monastery of Passignano; those of Saint Michael of Siena and of Alpiano; the monastery of Coltibuono; that of Monte Pisis; the monastery of Monte Scalario; that of Nerano; the monastery of Fivilo; the monastery of Cappiano; Saint Paul of Pisa; Saint Michael of Plajano; Saint Michael of Salvenero in Sardinia; the monastery of Saint Angelus of Pistoia; the monastery of Paviano; the monastery of Saint Mary of Prato; the monastery of Vaiano; [Col. 1067D] the monastery of Opleto; the monastery of Monte Plano; the monastery of the spring of Thaon; the monastery of Musceto; the monastery of Monte Armato; the monastery of Saint Cecilia; Saint Reparata; the monastery of Trecento; the monastery of Crispino; the monastery of Razolo; the monastery of Bujo Caesaris; the monastery of Coneo; the monastery of Turri; the monastery of Caprilia; the monastery of Saint Mark of Piacenza; the monastery of Saint Benedict of Herba Amata; the monastery of Saint Prosper of Reggio; the monastery of Cavanna; the monastery of Saint Mercurialis of Forlì; the monastery of Novara; the monastery of Vercelli; the monastery of Genoa; the monastery of Saint Paul of Tortona; the monastery of Brescia; the monastery of Verona; the monastery of Saint Carpophorus; [Col. 1068A] the monastery of Asti; and the monastery of Saint Angelus of Guniperti.

You may receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics from whichever bishop you prefer, provided that he is Catholic and enjoys the favour and communion of the Roman Church; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested. We further decree that no bishop may pronounce against you a sentence of excommunication or interdict; and, since you have been received as special sons of the apostolic see, you are not rashly to submit to the judgement of any other person. Nor may anyone remove or transfer any monastery of your religious order from the stability of its place without the common consent of the abbot and community.

We establish, moreover, that the monastery situated in Vallombrosa shall be regarded as the head of all the aforesaid monasteries. When, by divine appointment, the end of life comes to your shepherd, the person to succeed him, since he must preside both over you and over all the others, shall be elected by the consent and judgement of all who preside over the other monasteries. If perchance one of those abbots is, by God’s ordering, elected to this general government, he shall transfer principally to your chief monastery; and thereafter, by his judgement, all the other monasteries united to you shall be ordered, as is known to have been done in the days of John, your first abbot of venerable memory. [Col. 1068C]

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away or diminish its goods or possessions, or harass it with reckless vexations; but that all things, etc., shall be preserved for its benefit, saving the authority of the apostolic see. If anyone, therefore, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Ubaldo, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. I, William, cardinal priest of Saint Peter in Chains, have subscribed. I, Boso, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. [Col. 1068D] I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark, have subscribed. I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of Saint Vitalis, of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace near the temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Raynerius, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Anagni through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, [Col. 1069A] and in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCXL. He confirms the goods, rights, and privileges of the monastery of Saint Mary of Florence. (Anagni, 30 April.)

[MARGARINI, *Bullar. Casin.*, 20.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERNARD, abbot of Saint Mary of Florence, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Although the care of all Churches has been entrusted to us, unworthy though we are, and we are bound to exercise general solicitude for all, we ought to give more attentive assistance to those known to belong specially to the right of blessed Peter. [Col. 1069B] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive your monastery, known specially to belong to the right and possession of the Roman Church, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by God’s grace, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged the following to be expressly named:

The place in which the monastery itself is situated, [Col. 1069C] with its appurtenances; the castle of Signa; a third part of the castle of Grumulo, with their churches and appurtenances; the estate of Greve, with the church of Saint Martin and its other possessions; the church of Saint Bartholomew, with the estate and land of Berizo and his wife Aza of Radda; moreover, their land at Petroio or wherever it may be, with all its appurtenances; the castle of Radda, with its estate, churches, and everything belonging to it; a third part of the castle of Tignano, with its churches and appurtenances; the church of Saint Nicholas in the field of Clarentis, with its estate and all the churches belonging to it; the estate of Cacierini, with its possessions; the castle of Bibbiano, with its estate and all the churches belonging to it; [Col. 1069D] the church of Saint Martin at Confluente, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Martin within the city, beside the aforesaid monastery, with houses, lands, and all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Martin at Mensola, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Monte Domini, with everything belonging to it; the estate of Mandria, with its appurtenances; the land of John, son of Teudus, with houses and other possessions, as Mary and her son Donatus gave them to the monastery; the houses and lands of John, son of Boia; the church of Saint Proculus, with the lands and houses around it; and the castle of Vicli, with its estate, churches, and all its appurtenances.

Furthermore, whatever you lawfully possess from the gift of Boniface, brother of Benedict, formerly your abbot, [Col. 1070A] and all tithes from Viclo, as you are known to possess them canonically by the grant of our venerable brother, the bishop of Florence, and the tithe from your allod, from the estate, from Casalia, Fusci, and Rochetta, as you are known canonically to possess that tithe through the grant of Guido, formerly bishop of Volterra—all these we confirm to you and your monastery by apostolic authority. Likewise, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the free appointment of persons in your churches, as your predecessors and you yourselves are known to have enjoyed it without interruption for forty years.

Moreover, we forbid any bishop or his official to dare burden your churches or their clerics with unlawful exactions or molestations, or to presume, without a mandate from the Roman pontiff or a legate sent from his side, to impose a sentence of excommunication upon them, or of interdict upon you or your monastery. [Col. 1070B] No one shall presume to demand from you or your monastery tithes or first-fruits from your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the produce of your animals.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordination of your monks or clerics who are to be promoted to holy orders, from the bishop of Florence, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the apostolic see, and is willing to provide these things freely and without abuse. Otherwise, you may approach whichever bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant you what you request. We also grant that the burial-place of that site shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and final wishes of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; the rights of those churches, however, from which the bodies of the dead are taken shall remain intact.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain things taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations.
