Rather, all things shall be preserved unimpaired and whole for the use and benefit [Col. 1070D] of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, shall rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not make amends through suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honour; let that person know that he or she stands guilty before divine judgement for the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let that person be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgement.

But let all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may both receive here the fruit [Col. 1071A] of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

The sign of Pope Alexander III:

“Show me thy ways, O Lord.” Saint Peter; Saint Paul.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernard, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, William, cardinal priest of Saint Peter [Col. 1071B] in Chains. I, Boso, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of Saint Vitalis, of the title of Vestina. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace near the temple of Agrippa. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Raynerius, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

[Col. 1071C] Given at Anagni, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of May, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCXLI. He sends Roger, archbishop of York, a copy of the letters of William, king of Scotland, who, after making peace with the king of England, asks him that the Church of Scotland be subjected to the Church of York. (Anagni, 13 May.)

[WILKINS, *Concilia Magnae Britanniae*, I, 481.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ROGER, archbishop of York, legate of the apostolic see, and to his beloved sons the dean [Col. 1071D] and canons of York: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Wishing, with provident care, to make provision and secure advantage in this matter for the welfare of your Church, we have caused the tenor of the letters of our dearest son in Christ, William, illustrious king of Scotland, to be written word for word, with nothing added or removed, and have deemed it fitting to send it to you under our seal, so that you may keep it in perpetual remembrance. The tenor of these letters is as follows:

> “To the most reverend lord and father Alexander, by God’s grace supreme pontiff: William, by the same grace king of Scotland, greeting and devoted reverence.
>
> Let Your Holiness know that, concerning the subjection of the Church [Col. 1072A] of Scotland, which the Church of York claims for itself by ancient right, I have, by diligently investigating the truth both through authentic writings which I have examined and through the report and testimony of ancient, authoritative, and truthful men, discovered that from ancient times it belongs by right to the Church of York, and that it lost possession of it through the hostility and power of the kings who were my predecessors.
>
> But now, since by God’s grace perpetual peace has been restored between my lord, the king of England, and myself, I humbly request that, with every objection and appeal set aside, you command that the aforesaid subjection and possession be restored and reinstated by your authority to my lord the king and his realm, and to the Church of York. Nor can it be omitted, without the greatest harm to me and detriment to my land, that this be done, since in the peace thus restored it was so agreed between my lord the king and me, and I have confirmed this same matter by oath. For I know that it would result in the gravest peril to our souls if what we know for certain ought to belong were not carried into effect.
>
> May Your Holiness ever flourish.”

Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Ides of May.

MCCXLII. To Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Chrysogonus, and Hugh, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, legates.—That the daughter of the king of France is either to be married by the son of the king of England or restored to her father. (Anagni, 21 May.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 965.]

[Col. 1072C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, priest of Saint Chrysogonus, and HUGH, deacon of Saint Angelo, legates of the apostolic see: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since the daughter of our dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the Franks—whom Henry, illustrious king of England, had long ago received to be joined in marriage to his son Richard, duke of Aquitaine—is said to have reached marriageable age, the same king of France seems grievously to complain of us because, as he asserts, while we tolerate it, his daughter is neither restored to him nor married to the aforesaid duke, as she ought to be.

Therefore, since the same king of the Franks insists upon one of these alternatives, and since we do not wish, as we ought not, to fail him in this matter—for it is unworthy, improper, and absurd that the king’s daughter should be held in such a manner any longer—we command and enjoin your discretion by apostolic letters that you labour, jointly and severally, with earnest warnings and exhortations, in our name and yours, to induce the aforesaid king of England to have the said daughter of the king married in splendid fashion by the aforesaid duke within two months, as is fitting for both kings, or not to delay restoring her to the king aforesaid. If he does neither of these things in response to your summons within the prescribed time, then, with appeal excluded, [Col. 1073A] by our authority forbid the celebration throughout the whole province of Canterbury of every divine office except baptism for infants and the rites of penance for the dying, until he performs one of these alternatives. If he still does not come to his senses, subject the whole county of Poitou to a like sentence. If one of you is unwilling or unable to take part in carrying these matters out, the other shall nevertheless execute them.

Given at Anagni, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June.

MCCXLIII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint John in Venere. (Anagni, 16 June.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, VI, 709.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ODERISIUS, abbot of the monastery of Saint John [Col. 1073B] in Venere, and all the brethren, present and future, to be regularly installed: in perpetuity.

“The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God,” admonishes us to enter the path of uprightness, since the strength of the Lord is straight in the simple way. Therefore a hearing is not to be denied to petitioners, because it belongs to our office to provide for the peace of God’s servants, so that, free from secular tumults, they may be able with simple hearts to walk steadfastly in the way of the Lord.

Accordingly, lawful son in Christ, Abbot Oderisius, moved by the just prayers of you and your brethren, in honour of Saint Mary, Mother of God and Virgin, and of Saint John the Baptist, the Lord’s holy Forerunner, we fortify by the authority of this privilege the monastery dedicated to his name, in which you unanimously serve almighty God, to be cherished forever in the bosom of the apostolic see, God granting it. Following, indeed, the form of the privileges granted to your monastery by our holy predecessors—namely Leo, Victor, Nicholas, and Urban—we confirm for your perpetual possession and that of your successors all that Count Transmund, son of Duke and Marquess Transmund, is known to have offered to your monastery in the counties of Chieti, Penne, Abruzzo, Fermo, and Termoli, [Col. 1073C] and also the rest which has come into your right and lordship through the offerings of other faithful persons, namely:

[Col. 1073D] In the county of Chieti: these cells—Saint John at Malotraverso; Saint Zechariah; Saint Benedict; Saint Romanus; Saint Severinus; Saint Mary at the chapel beside Ortona; Saints Paul and Peter, with the borough which lies beside it; likewise, the church of Saint George; Saint Philip of the Palace; Saint Angelus, with a third part of the port of Ortona; Saint Mary beside the stream called Fricius in the estate of Ateana; the Holy Martyrs Leontianus and Domitianus, with a thousand modii of adjoining land in the estate of Agrama; Saint Calarus; and the Holy Virgins Aurea and Petronilla; Saint Ambrose; Saint Martin; Saint Stephen, on the hill at Bessi; Holy Cross, with twelve *marnatae* of men; Saint Angelus within the Seven Towns, opposite Saint Nicholas.

Likewise: the cell of Saint John at Rocca, with its town; Saint Thomas, with its town; Saint Fermanus; [Col. 1074A] Saint Eusanus, with its castle; Saint Apollinaris, with its castle; Saint Nicholas, with its castle; Saint Mary Inca, with its castle; Saint Mary in the Crypt of Trinea; Saint Angelus at Pesclo; Saint Angelus at Ortecle, with its town; Saint Mark; Saint Quiricus; Saint Lucy at Argelli; Saint Pantaleon; Holy Cross at Alento, with the town of Mucela; Saint Ansuinus; Saint John in Retro; Saint Paul at Pescara, with its town; Saint Lawrence at Pescara, with a fourth part across the same river and a fourth part of its port; Saint Nicholas, with the town of Sangro; Saint Cantiana in the castle of Palledo; Saint Martin of the sons of Teudald; Saint Peter at Batinario, with its *fara*; Saint Agatha; Saint Pancras; Saint Justus of Casole; Saint Peter at Lauro; Saint Peter of Linari, with the castle of Resse; Saint Peter at Parlasi; Saint Mary in the Valley; Saint [Col. 1074B] Mary in Eramo; Saint Vitus at Portule.

The towns, moreover: Fossa Caeca; Castellum Muratum; Rocca dei Schiavi; Giruli; Laternum; Montes Octaviani; Guastura; Meruli; Porcile; Milianico; Castellum Vetus; Balerianum; the *fara* of Benedict, son of Hubert; the *fara* of the sons of Bederoch; Monte San Silvestro; Petrarium; Senella; Castellinum; Castrum Aymonis; Turricella; Monte Colle Marsino; Ilice; Rivo Giusto; Macla; Scorriosa; Casale di San Benedetto; Moro Rivo; and Petri Peschi.

In the county of Penne: the cell of Saint Mary at Anfrisano; Saint Mary at Ponzano, with the castle of Casavetere; Saint Michael at Boccarieto, with its *fara*, and the *fara* of Saratico; Saint Michael at Fine, with its *fara* and hill; Saint Peter at Campo Rotondo; Saint Mary at Loquiano, with its hill; Saint Mary at [Col. 1074C] Rivo Sonuli; Saint John at Aqua Viva, with its hamlet; Saint Peter; Saint John at Ponticulum; Saint Anthony; Saint Mary at Rigulo; Saint Saviour at Casa Nigra; Saint Margaret at Legoniano; Saint Io at Carpeneto; Saint Angelus at Rivo Turbido; Saint Mary in the Valley; Saint Nicholas at Plomba; Saint Lawrence near Gomarium; Saint John at Casa Comusta; the castle by the sea; Speltore; the pass of Consenga; Monte Silvario; the town of Saint Angelus; Ilice of Holy Cross; Casa Lariti; Ilice Trallionium; Pizanum; Scurranum; Monte Valterii; Monticula; Spatula Rupta; Arseta; Bifenum; Antianum; Ranchi; Silva; Mitialianum; Casulae Murus; Alto Castello beyond Monte Peditarum; and Saint John of the sons of Tribunus.

[Col. 1074D] In the county of Abruzzo: the cell of Saint John at Gomano, with its castle; Cerro Bifurco; Saint Donatus at Salinello, with the castle of Palma; Saint Stephen at Mura; and the church of Saint Angelus; Monte Pagano; Grassiano; Ripa of the sons of Azo; Poggio Mulorum Morelli; the whole estate of Pedoniano; the whole estate of Bucelliano; and a third part of the estate of Semproniano.

In the county of Fermo: the cell of Saint Nicholas, with the castle of Paterno; Monterone; half the estate of Supplica; the whole estate of Acquaviva; Monte Bolario; the castle of Rodactariscus; the castle of Colinari; and the church of Saint Passicus. In the county, the whole estate of Palveniano; in the county of Camerino, the land with its cultivators. In the estate of Cesepalumbo, half the estate [Col. 1075A] of Visiliano and a fourth part of the estate of Albano. In the county: the cell of Saint Martin; Saint Mary at Contro, with the church of Saint Januarius; Saint Victorinus; a sixth part of Saint Lawrence; Saint Saviour at Lisina; the cell of Saint Michael at Ferraria; the cell of Saint Nicholas; and, in the city, the church of Saint Mary at Vinea Talliatata. In the principality of Benevento: the church of Saint Mary; Saint John at Barsica; the cell of Saint Anastasius; and in the city, the whole inheritance of Leo Pinninus. In Dalmatia, at Belgrade: the cell of Saint Thomas; likewise the merchants’ toll, and the price, tithes, and offerings of the dead, from all things without objection or dispute, or by whatever title you hold them.

Furthermore, by the charter of this present decree we establish by apostolic authority that whatever your monastery now justly possesses in cells, [Col. 1075B] churches, towns, villages, woods, pastures, rivers, ports, shores, fisheries, whether of sea or rivers, mills, watercourses, male and female slaves, and any movable or immovable things, or may hereafter justly acquire with God’s help, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. You shall receive chrism, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of other clerics to be promoted to holy orders from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer.

Within the boundaries of the whole abbey no bishop, unless invited by you, may hold a synod or compel clerics, so that you may understand that this care belongs to your charge only by virtue of the delegated office granted you by us. Upon the death of you, the abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be placed over it by any artifice or violence except the person whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall elect according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. The person elected shall go to the Roman pontiff to be consecrated.

You, lawful sons in Christ, ought in all things to respond by worthy works to the grace conferred upon you by these constitutions and to the great benefits of the apostolic see. Do not abuse this liberty as an occasion for the flesh and a cloak for malice; rather, in proportion as you are freer from secular tumults, endeavour all the more to please the Lord with all the powers of mind and soul. We decree, [Col. 1075D] therefore, etc.

Given at Anagni, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCXLIV. He confirms for Gunteram, bishop-elect of Siena, the church on Monte Bonizi. (Anagni, 22 June.)

[UGHELI, *Italia sacra*, III, 547.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUNTERAM, bishop-elect of Siena, and to his successors canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1076A] We are bound by a common and special obligation to yield to your petitions and grant them suitable effect, so that we, who are bound to hear all persons in their just requests, may seem more favourable to you in proportion as we love you and the Church committed to you with more abundant charity. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, assenting willingly to your just petitions, we grant and confirm to you and your successors, with the common counsel of our brethren, the church on Monte Bonizi, built by Raynerius, your predecessor of blessed memory, on the estate which Count Guido of blessed memory formerly granted to blessed Peter and to our predecessor Pope Adrian of pious memory, by the authority and grant of that predecessor of ours. We give you free power, as that same predecessor is known to have given it, [Col. 1076B] to consecrate the same church without any opposition, to appoint clerics there according to your own judgement, and freely to ordain them.

This is notwithstanding the revocation which our aforesaid predecessor is known to have made in this matter, led by a slight and groundless error, on the consideration that the place lies in the diocese of Florence; since his privilege contains that the aforesaid estate had been granted by the said count, and that the same predecessor assigned it to your predecessor for the construction of a church there, subject to an annual rent of one Byzantine coin. We establish, as our aforesaid predecessor is known to have established, that whoever from your diocese goes to that place shall owe obedience to you and your successors alone in all spiritual matters, and that you shall retain over them in every respect the same authority which you had before. Finally, as a token of this our grant and confirmation, you shall pay one Byzantine coin each year to us and our successors.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may infringe this charter of our grant and confirmation or in any way act against it. If anyone, therefore, in the future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, Bernardus, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. [Col. 1076D] I, John, cardinal priest of the Holy Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, William, cardinal priest of the title of St Peter in Chains. I, Boso, cardinal priest of St Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, John, cardinal priest of St Mark. I, Theodosius, cardinal priest of St Vitalis in Vestina. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St Susanna. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of St Adrian. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of St Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico.

Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on 22 June, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1077A], in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCXLV. Privilege for the monastery of Boscaudun. (Anagni, 4 July.)

[Gallia Christiana III, Instruments, 186.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUIGO, abbot of the monastery of Boscaudun, and his brothers professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

. . . Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to the divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever [Col. 1077B] goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, by the Lord’s gift, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their own terms:

The place called Boscaudun, with its appurtenances, where the monastery itself was founded; the abbey of Pratis; and the abbey of Lura, which you have built, with its possessions; Lavera with its possessions; the house of St Maurice with its appurtenances; the vineyards of Romolono, Capdavaco, and Moillarou; the grange of Pailheyrol, with everything that you possess in that territory; [Col. 1077C] the grange of Villario Roberti, and whatever you hold and possess there. Moreover, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you upon your newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the produce of your animals. Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ubaldus, bishop of Ostia, etc.

Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on 4 July, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCXLVI. Privilege for the Church of Aquileia. (Anagni, 7 July.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 69.]

[Col. 1077D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons VALDERICUS, provost, and the canons of the Church of Aquileia, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

Whenever that which is sought from us, etc., we decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the same Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s assistance, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their own terms.

[Col. 1078A] The estate of Melereto with all its boundaries and appurtenances, namely the Slav village which is likewise called Meleretum, Palmata, Ronch, and Ronchetas, with fields, vineyards, meadows, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands, woods, and hunting rights, as far as the wood of St Lawrence, and as far as the village called Claviam, and as far as the village called Antonianum, and as far as Feletas, and as far as Becinis, and as far as the village of St Stephen, and as far as Risa, and as far as the village called Perseriano. Likewise, the estates of Casteone and Mursano, with their boundaries and appurtenances, from the village of St Andrew as far as the village called Ganarium, and as far as the wood, with all their revenues, vineyards, fields, meadows, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands, marshes and woods with hunting rights, [Col. 1078B] waters and watercourses, mills and fisheries; also the estate of Mariano, the estate of Carlinis, the estate of St George, and the estate of Mutiana, with all their revenues, together with all their boundaries and appurtenances, fields, vineyards, meadows, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters, watercourses, and mills; islands from the sea and from the river called Carnium as far as the water called Aruvinius, with marshes and fisheries, woods and hunting rights; the baptismal churches of the patriarchate of Aquileia with the chapels belonging to them, as you peacefully possess them.

In the market of Aquileia, thirty stalls; and in the port of Piri, twenty. Fifty holdings in Ossella, with churches and tithes; the estate of Farra with the adjacent [Col. 1078C] villages, namely Petolan, Drasam, Sebredam, Villa Nova, Gradisca, and Bruma, with all their appurtenances from the mountain called Cars as far as the Hungarian Road, and as far as the village called Algo, with churches and all its appurtenances—meadows, woods, pastures, cultivated and uncultivated lands, hunting rights and fisheries, and every imperial jurisdiction—as Emperor Otto of good memory conveyed them to the Church and canons of Aquileia. Also in Carni(a), the estate of Penicles, the estate of Nogarias, the estate of Felas on Mount St Peter, the mountain of Tenca, four holdings in the village of Avale, the estate of Battalia, three holdings at Ingiam, nine holdings at Pinzan, fifteen holdings at Gruans, and a certain mountain near Avenzon.

[Col. 1078D] Furthermore, just as Burkardus, advocate of the Church of Aquileia, and afterwards Henry, renounced into the hand of Patriarch Valericus, for themselves and their successors, their claim to the advocacy over all the goods belonging to the Church of Aquileia, with all districts, usages, and appurtenances, so we too confirm this by apostolic authority.

Therefore we decree, etc., saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the patriarch of Aquileia. If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church.

I, Ubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, John, cardinal priest of the Holy Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. [Col. 1079A] I, Albertus, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St Peter in Chains. I, Peter, cardinal priest of St Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St Mark. I, Theodorus, cardinal priest of St Vitalis, of the title of Vestina. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St Susanna. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of St Adrian. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of St Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico.

Rainerius, deacon of St George at the Golden Veil.

[Col. 1079B] Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of July [7 July], in the ninth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCXLVII. He grants to the sisters of St Mary’s Parthenon at Soissons that “until the number of nuns is reduced to eighty, they must admit no one as a sister except at the point of death, nor exceed that number once they have been reduced to it.” (Anagni, 21 July.)

[D. GERMAIN, *History of Notre-Dame de Soissons*, 442.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the abbess and sisters [Col. 1079C] of St Mary of Soissons: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since, as we have learned, there is so great a multitude of nuns in your monastery that they can scarcely be supported in any fashion from its resources, it has been determined, upon the counsel of prudent and religious men and with the assent of our dearest son in Christ Louis, illustrious king of the Franks, that until the number of nuns is reduced to eighty, you must admit no one as your sister except when death is imminent, nor, after you have been reduced to that number, exceed it. Therefore, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we hold the aforesaid constitution valid and firm; we confirm it by apostolic authority [Col. 1079D] and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our constitution or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 21 July.

### MCCXLVIII. He commends Robert, bishop of Exeter, Roger, bishop of Worcester, and Clarembald, abbot of Faversham, because they deposed Clarembald, abbot of St Augustine’s, Canterbury. (Anagni?—See the Chronicle of W. Thorn, in TWYSDEN, *Histories of English Writers*, II, 1818.)

### MCCXLIX. He exhorts the monks of St Augustine’s, Canterbury, after Clarembald’s deposition, to choose another abbot for themselves. (Ibid.)

[Col. 1080A]

. . . Therefore, holding his removal valid and firm and confirming it by apostolic authority, we command and direct your discretion by apostolic letters to take care to agree harmoniously, without any division or scandal, upon a suitable and honourable person worthy of so great an office, and to elect him as your abbot and master, so that through his care and diligence the same monastery may, with the Lord’s help, advance in spiritual observances and [Col. 1080B] increase in temporal prosperity, etc.

### MCCL. He annuls whatever Clarembald did with the goods of the church of St Augustine without the chapter’s consent. (Ibid.)

The concern of our office, etc. And below: Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, granting favourable assent to your just petitions and discharging the duty of our office, whatever Clarembald, once your elect—indeed, the destroyer of your church—is known to have done, to the detriment of that church, with its goods and possessions without the counsel and assent of the whole chapter, we annul by apostolic authority and decree to be wholly without force, etc.

### MCCLI. To Guigo, prior of the Charterhouse, and his brothers.—He approves their institute. (Anagni, 2 September.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 1056.]

[Col. 1080C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUIGO, prior of the Charterhouse, and his brothers, present and future, in perpetuity: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since through God’s grace you earn much glory by your merits and, choosing the solitary life, devote yourselves more closely to divine contemplation, the good fragrance of your religious life moves us to believe that, by a common and special obligation, we ought to attend to your peace and preserve your rights most diligently.

[Col. 1080D] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves you and the other houses of your order, together with all goods, pastures, and possessions which you now justly and canonically possess or may hereafter acquire by lawful means, through the Lord’s assistance; we strengthen you by the privilege of this present writing; and by apostolic authority we confirm for you and your houses the boundaries which you have reasonably established.

Moreover, by apostolic authority we strictly forbid, under threat of anathema, anyone to dare within your boundaries or those of your houses to seize a person, commit theft or robbery, [Col. 1081A] or perpetrate homicide, or in any way molest persons coming to or returning from your houses, so that, out of reverence for God and your places, within these boundaries not only you and your brothers, but also others, may have full peace and quiet. We further decree that no religious person may establish any building or acquire possessions within half a league of the boundaries of the possessions which you hold.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb you concerning your possessions or pastures, inflict trouble or burden upon you concerning them, retain them after taking them away, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; [Col. 1081B] but that all things shall be preserved unimpaired and whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, John, cardinal priest of the Holy Saints John and Paul. I, Albertus, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, Ruerus, cardinal priest of St Peter in Chains. I, Boso, cardinal priest of St Pudentiana. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St Mark. I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of the title of St Vitalis. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St Susanna. [Col. 1081C] I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of St Adrian. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of St Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico.

Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on 2 September, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the seventeenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCLII. To the cardinals sent as legates into Lombardy.—What hope he has hitherto given the envoys of Emperor Frederick, who were to negotiate peace with the Church. He orders them to strengthen the Lombards in their league, etc.

[PEZ, *Treasury of Anecdotes*, VI, 397.]

[Col. 1081D]

To H. [HILDEBRAND], cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles, and A. [ARDICIO], cardinal deacon of St Theodore, legates of the Apostolic See.

Concerning the proposed peace, of which discussion had been raised in Lombardy and elsewhere, we received the envoys of F., the said emperor: namely, the archbishop of Magdeburg, C., the chancellor; the bishop-elect of Worms; and A., the said emperor’s protonotary. They repeatedly and steadfastly affirmed that the emperor’s mind and will were most ardently inclined to peace. When they strongly urged us to work for the conclusion of peace between the Church and the emperor, and could not obtain [Col. 1082A] from us that we should establish peace fully and permanently without the Lombards, the king of Sicily, or the emperor of Constantinople, we finally determined—lest we seem to flee from the peace which we desire with all our heart, or to furnish grounds for accusation—to approach the regions of Lombardy at the most urgent request of those envoys, so that we might negotiate peace more safely and freely. We have also agreed that we should inform the king of Sicily by our letters that he should without delay send his envoys to take part in the peace negotiations.

Therefore we admonish, direct, and command your prudence to take care to urge and advise the rectors and consuls of the Lombard League to inform us without delay at what place we may arrive more safely [Col. 1082B] and negotiate peace more freely and honourably; and meanwhile, so that you may suffer no obstacle, to consolidate and strengthen their association and unity. You yourselves are to investigate their wills and dispositions fully, and with all speed report to our concern whatever you find among them and what counsel may arise from it; and you are to devote yourselves to strengthening and preserving the aforesaid unity.

### MCCLIII. He confirms the judgment pronounced by the bishop of Brescia in the dispute between the bishops of Piacenza and Parma concerning the church of the Castle of Speculum and the church of St Christina, which are adjudged to Piacenza. (Anagni, 8 November.)

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, III, 364.]

[Col. 1082C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother T[HEOBALD], bishop of Piacenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the letters of our venerable brother, the bishop of Brescia, we have learned that, after receiving our mandate concerning the church situated in the Castle of Speculum and the church of St Christina, concerning which a controversy was pending between you and our venerable brother the bishop of Parma, he heard the case committed to him, with appeal set aside. Having heard the arguments and allegations of both parties, and taking counsel with prudent men, as we clearly perceive from the written judgment drawn up by the public notary’s hand, [Col. 1082D] he adjudged both churches to you and, relying upon apostolic authority, absolved you from the claim brought against you by the aforesaid bishop of Parma concerning the aforementioned church of Speculum. Therefore we . . . [that which] is known to have been reasonably done by our mandate and authority should be strengthened in force: holding valid and firm the judgment of the aforesaid bishop of Brescia, as it was reasonably rendered by him and is contained in his authentic instrument, we confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation [Col. 1083A] of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, 8 November.

### MCCLIV. He receives the monastery of St German of the Meadows under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Anagni, 15 November.)

[BOUILLART, *History of Saint-Germain-des-Prés*, Preface, p. 44.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot of St German at Paris, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See, over which, though unworthy, we preside, admonishes us that we ought to bear general concern for the condition of all churches [Col. 1083B] and keep particular watch over the protection of those which belong especially to the right of blessed Peter and pertain to our jurisdiction and guardianship without an intermediary. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, following the example of our predecessors of pious memory, the Roman pontiffs, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves your monastery, which is known to adhere especially to the Roman Church, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of popes, [Col. 1083C] the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s assistance, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their own terms:

In the diocese of Sens: the church of Emant; the church of Mont Machou; the church of Matricolis; the church of St German near Musterolum; the church of St Peter of the Old Matrials; and the church of Balneolis. In the diocese of Paris: the church of Old St German within the city; the church of Villeneuve; the church of Crona; the church of Valenton; the church of Theodosia; the church of Pirodium; the church of Antoniacum; the church of Verrariae; the church of Avremville; and the church of Suresnes. [Col. 1083D] In the diocese of Chartres: the church of St Martin of Drocis; the church of St Mary Magdalene of Mont Calvulo; the church of Domnus Martinus; the church of Laoniarium; the church of Neeffleta; and the churches of Septulia. In the diocese of Rouen: the church of St Leodegarius; the church of Vilers; and the church of Longuessa. In the diocese of Soissons: the church of Novigentum. In the diocese of Meaux: the church of Colli; the church of Blessed Mary of Ramainvillare; the church of Monteri; and the church of Abeli. In the diocese of Autun: the church of Gilli; the church of Vilerbichet; and the church of Marri. In the diocese of Bourges: the church of Britiniacum; the church of Neuveville; and the church of Lemauso. In the diocese of Poitiers: the church of Naintriacum; [Col. 1084A] the church of St John of the market of the Castle of Eraud.

We confirm to you and your monastery by apostolic authority the aforesaid churches with everything belonging to them, as you canonically possess them. By this present written decree, we establish that in these churches you shall have, without any opposition, the right of presentation of priests, as your predecessors and you yourselves are known from ancient times to have had it. But if priests instituted in your churches upon your presentation refuse to render to you what is temporal, you shall have free authority by apostolic authority to withdraw from them the temporalities which they hold from you.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, [Col. 1084B] take away its possessions, retain them after taking them away, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved unimpaired and whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, John, cardinal priest of the Holy Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Albertus, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, William, cardinal priest of the title of St [Col. 1084C] Peter in Chains. I, Boso, cardinal priest of St Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of St Vitalis, of the title of Vestina. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St Susanna. I, James, cardinal deacon of the title of St Mary in Cosmedin. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of St Adrian. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of St Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico. [Col. 1084D] I, Raynerius, cardinal deacon of St George at the True Golden Veil.

Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on 15 November, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 [1176] of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCLV. He receives the church of St Lawrence of Florence under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Anagni, 28 November.)

[LAMI, *Monuments of the Florentine Church*, III, 1780.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERNARD, prior of St Lawrence in the city of Florence, and his brothers, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

A petition proceeding from pious will ought to receive effectual fulfilment, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the requested benefit may assuredly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s assistance, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. [Col. 1085B] Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their own terms:

The parish belonging to your church, as you have hitherto peacefully held it; the hospital situated beside the same church of St Lawrence, with all its appurtenances; the *citinas* of St Lawrence situated nearby [term uncertain]; the church of St Mark with all its appurtenances; the church of St Bartholomew situated at Faltignano with all its appurtenances, and all possessions which you hold in that same estate; and the church of St Andrew at Percussine. Whatever has also been granted to you by our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, and confirmed to your church by their privileges, we likewise ratify. [Col. 1085C] We further grant that the cemetery of that place shall be free, so that no one may in any way hinder the devotion and final wishes of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken remain reserved.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, etc., saving the canonical right of the bishop of Florence. If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal priest of the Holy Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Albertus, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed. [Col. 1085D] I, Guilbertus, cardinal priest of the title of St Peter in Chains, have subscribed. I, Boso, cardinal priest of St Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of St Vitalis, of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of St Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. [Col. 1086A] I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Raynerius, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on 28 November, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCLVI. To the rectors of the March.—Concerning peace with Emperor Frederick, which is never to be confirmed unless they too are consulted. (Anagni? about November.)

[PEZ, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, VI, I, 388.]

[Col. 1086B] A., servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the rectors of the March: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have learned from the letters which your devotion sent us how the emperor does not hesitate to pretend that peace between us and himself has been concluded. But whatever he may say, and whatever others may say, we wish you to hold this as certain: peace between us and the same emperor has not been confirmed by oath or written instrument, although peace has long been negotiated between us and him. Although the archbishop of Magdeburg [Note: [Col. 1085D] Wichmannus], Chancellor O. [Note: [Col. 1085D] Christian, archbishop of Mainz], the bishop-elect of Worms [Note: [Col. 1086D] Conrad], and the emperor’s protonotary, sent to us by that emperor to restore peace, [Col. 1086C] strongly urged us that we should restore peace to the Church, they nevertheless could never induce us to be willing to accept peace for the Church without [peace] with you and that of the king of Sicily and the other helpers of the Church. Therefore, in order that they may negotiate more conveniently concerning peace for us and for you, we have resolved, however much the labour may be contrary to our age, to travel in person into your regions, accompanied by the envoys of that king. You therefore must act courageously, be strengthened in the Lord, and persist in your pious purpose, until peace brings your association to completion—an association which must be strengthened more earnestly in that same purpose—being equally certain and secure that peace has not been confirmed and, God being its author, will not be confirmed without you.

### MCCLVII. He receives the house of St Julian of Pereyo under protection and confirms all its goods. (Benevento, 29 December.)

[HENRIQUEZ, *Rules, Constitutions, and Privileges of the Cistercian Order*, II, 506.]

[Col. 1086D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GOMETIUS, prior of St Julian of Pereyo, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made to us which is known to accord with religion and honour, it is altogether fitting that we grant it willingly and provide suitable [Col. 1087A] support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously inclined to your just supplications, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid house of St Julian, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing . . . . . Furthermore, whatever possessions and whatever goods the same house of St Julian now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s assistance, we decree shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their own terms:

The place itself where the said church is situated, with its appurtenances, lands, vineyards, woods, meadows, [Col. 1087B] pastures, waters, and mills. Moreover, no one shall presume to extort from you tithes or first-fruits from your newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the produce of your animals. You may receive into conversion clerics or laymen released from worldly obligations who flee from this world, and retain them without any opposition. Furthermore, we prohibit anyone, after having made profession in that place, from departing without the prior’s permission; nor may anyone dare to retain a person who comes to him without the common testimony of letters, unless that person wishes to transfer to a stricter life. Furthermore, we grant to all Christ’s faithful, except the excommunicated or those under interdict, freedom to choose burial in that place, and forbid anyone [Col. 1087C] to oppose them; nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the deceased are taken remain reserved. And whenever it happens that you or any of your successors dies, no one shall be installed by stealth, trickery, or force; rather, let the person be installed whom the brothers, by common consent or by the decision of the greater and sounder part, shall elect in the fear of God.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid house, etc., saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If anyone therefore, etc.

Given at Benevento by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on 29 December, in the tenth indiction, in the year [Col. 1087D] 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCLVIII. He directs Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See, to protect the Parisian monastery of St Maglorius, which King Louis of the Franks has commended to him. (Benevento, 30 December.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 968.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, cardinal priest of the title of St Chrysogonus, legate of the Apostolic See: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our dearest son in Christ, Louis, illustrious [Col. 1088A] king of the Franks, has earnestly and carefully asked us on behalf of the Parisian monastery of St Maglorius. Therefore, beyond our common obligation, we wish the rights of that monastery to be kept unimpaired and whole, and we urge you thereto with earnest exhortations. Hence we attentively admonish and command your discretion that, while you are in that land, you shall diligently protect and defend, so far as lies within your power, the rights of the aforesaid monastery by the authority of the legation which you exercise; and you shall labour to foster the aforesaid monastery in its rights in such a manner that, through your foresight and diligence, it may rejoice in the integrity of its rights and that we may deservedly commend your discretion and prudence on that account.

Given at Benevento, 30 December.

### MCCLIX. He grants a bull to the monastery of Laetiense “concerning altars and the Church’s complete freedom.”

[Col. 1088B]

Given at Benevento by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on 31 December, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

(REIFFENBERG, *Monuments Serving the History of the Provinces of Namur, Hainaut, etc.*, Brussels, 1844, vol. VII, p. 657.)

### MCCLX. He receives the monastery of St Ghislain under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Benevento, 31 December.)

[REIFFENBERG, ibid., VIII, 385.]

[Col. 1088C] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son LAMBERT, abbot of St Ghislain, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized as consonant with religion and propriety, it befits us gladly to grant it and to afford suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree first of all that the monastic order, known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, shall be inviolably observed there for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the bounty of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other just means, with the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is built, with all its appurtenances; the altar of Hersella; the altar of Homberghes; the altar of Rascenghem; the chapel of Herieriponte; the mill of Roacheries; the altar of Lovengies; the altar of Doulchies and the chapel of Squiri; the altar of Hunchignies, [Col. 1089A] with its appurtenances; the estate of Alemannis with all the tithe of that estate and of the land belonging to it; and the tithes of newly cleared lands and of the increase of animals. Let no one presume to exact tithes from you. In the parish churches which you hold, moreover, you may choose clerics and present them to the bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall entrust them with the care of souls. They shall answer to the bishop concerning the care of the people, but to you concerning temporal matters. We also grant that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. You may also receive clerics or laymen who flee from the world and are free to enter religious life, and retain them in your monastery without any opposition.

Furthermore, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in your monastery, from leaving that monastery without the permission of his abbot; and no one shall dare retain one who departs without letters of authorization from your community. Moreover, we decree by the present ordinance that the liberties, immunities, and ancient reasonable customs of your monastery shall remain whole and unimpaired. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any artifice of intrigue or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, [Col. 1089C] or the sounder part of the brethren, shall determine is to be elected according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

Therefore, we decree that it shall be lawful for absolutely no person to disturb rashly the aforesaid monastery, or take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Boso, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, [Col. 1089D] title of Pastor. I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of Saint Vitalis, title of Vestina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, William, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Manfred, bishop of Palestrina. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

[Col. 1090A] Given at Benevento, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of January [31 December], in the tenth indiction, in the year 1176 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCLXI. He orders that the archbishops of York and Canterbury be regarded as of the same rank and standing, provided that the one ordained first is held to be first. (Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. GILES, II, 75.)

Desiring, by the Lord’s authority, that the ancient dignity of the Church of York should be preserved intact, and following in the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, we forbid by apostolic authority that henceforth either the archbishop of Canterbury shall demand a profession of obedience from [Col. 1090B] the archbishop of York, or the archbishop of York render one to Canterbury; nor, what has been altogether forbidden by blessed Gregory, shall York in any way be subject to Canterbury’s jurisdiction. Rather, in accordance with the constitution of that same Father, this distinction of honour shall be perpetually maintained between them: he who was ordained first shall be held to be first.

If, indeed, the archbishop of Canterbury withholds from the elect of York the hand of consecration, which, according to the custom of their churches established for them by Honorius of the Apostolic See, they ought to receive from him, then the archbishop of York may be consecrated by his suffragans or by the Roman pontiff, in accordance with the common custom, the decree of our aforesaid Father Gregory, and the command of our lord Pope Paschal of holy memory.

CIRCA THE YEAR 1176.

[Col. 1090C]

MCCLXII. He directs the bishop of Exeter [or: Worcester] to forbid Geoffrey, bishop-elect of Lincoln, “since his election has not been confirmed, to grant an archdeaconry or prebend to anyone.” (MANSI, *Councils*, XXII, 1176.)

BETWEEN THE YEARS 1159–1177.

MCCLXIII. To the rectors of Lombardy.—That they should restrain the people of Modena from oppressing the monastery of Nonantola. (Anagni, 20 December.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *History of the August Abbey of Nonantola*, II, 275.]

[Col. 1090D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the rectors of Lombardy, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more sincerely we love you, the more gladly we invite your prudence to perform those acts through which you may obtain temporal praise and favour and undoubtedly gain the favour of the highest King. Among the other duties incumbent upon you, this is recognized as pre-eminent: that with all the powers of mind and body you should love the churches of God, and by every means endeavour to turn their wrongdoers back from their course of rashness. We have learned from our beloved sons, the abbot and brethren of the Church of Nonantola—which, as we believe you know, belongs immediately, without intermediary, to the jurisdiction of the Roman Church and to ours—that the citizens of Modena, grievously harassing them and their church, compel their men to swear allegiance to themselves and presume thus to extort money from them. They do not fear to violate their promise confirmed by oath, which they made to Eugenius, Pope of holy memory, our father and predecessor, when formerly he had extended his hands [lacuna] against them [lacuna] the city for a similar deed. Therefore, asking, warning, and earnestly exhorting your discretion by apostolic letters, we direct that you diligently and promptly restrain the consuls [Col. 1091B] and people of the aforesaid city from molesting and burdening the aforesaid church and its men. Carefully admonish them wholly to release from the obligation of those oaths the persons from whom they forcibly extorted the oaths contrary to the honour of God and of ourselves. Labour also to bring it about that by this means the sincerity of your devotion toward us and the Roman Church may shine forth more fully, and that we may be bound always to show you, as special sons of the Church, the fullness of our affection and favour with cheerful countenance and glad mind.

Given at Anagni, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of January [20 December].

MCCLXIV. At the request of A., bishop of Lodi, he confirms the sentence pronounced by Aribert, formerly cardinal priest of Saint Anastasia, by which the office of vicedominus of the Church of Lodi had been removed from Lanfranc of Trissino, knight of Lodi. (Anagni, 30 December.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 669.]

[Col. 1091C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother A., bishop of Lodi, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have plainly learned from a certain written record that, when A., your predecessor, had unreasonably granted the office of vicedominus of your church to Lanfranc of Trissino, knight of Lodi, and had confirmed the grant by an instrument, Aribert, of good memory, cardinal priest of the title of [Col. 1091D] Saint Anastasia and then legate of the Apostolic See, annulled the aforesaid grant on the counsel of O., formerly archbishop of Milan, Gregory, bishop of Bergamo, W., bishop of Novara, and V., bishop of Vercelli, in the presence of O., formerly bishop of Cremona, and many others. He ordered that the instrument made concerning it be returned to your aforesaid predecessor and cancelled, so that it could not thereafter be produced to the detriment of his church. Therefore, holding valid what was done by the said cardinal, we confirm by apostolic authority his sentence, as it was reasonably pronounced and is contained in the public instrument then drawn up; and we fortify it with the protection of this present writing, decreeing that it shall be lawful for absolutely no person to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way oppose it. If anyone, etc.

Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Kalends of January [30 December].

MCCLXV. He writes to John, bishop of Caserta, concerning the dissolution of marriages of certain persons related in the third degree. (THEINER, *Critical Investigations*, 431.)

Concerning what we have learned from your letter—that the son of Adalard, the bearer of the present letter, and the son of his sister are related to the daughters of Stantion, sister of the late same A., whom that same S. had begotten not by his own sister but by another woman whom he married after her—we make known to your prudence by these letters that, if this is so, you must not permit them to remain together; rather, they are to be separated from one another. For their unions may be called cohabitations rather than marriages, since such persons related by affinity even in the third degree ought not remain together.

BETWEEN THE YEARS 1167–1177.

MCCLXVI. To the regular canons of Saint Satyri. [Note: [Col. 1091D] It is an abbey of the Order of Saint Augustine, established not far from Sacro Caesare in the diocese of Bourges.]—He exhorts them diligently to observe regular discipline, and forbids them to eat meat even outside the monastery. (Benevento.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 994.]

[Col. 1092C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the chapter of Saint Satyri, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those who, abandoning vanities and worldly allurements, have vowed to serve the Lord in a stricter way of life must keep continual watch with the utmost care and diligence, and apply themselves to ensuring that the habit of religion which they have assumed accords with their morals and life, and that their purpose remains firm and immovable, lest they appear to have founded themselves upon sand rather than upon the Lord’s solid rock. Therefore we warn, command, and enjoin your charity that, rendering wholehearted obedience and reverence devoutly and humbly to our beloved son your abbot, you should fervently and unanimously devote yourselves to the cultivation of religion and honourable conduct and to the observance of canonical order, as you did formerly under Radulf, [Col. 1092D] your abbot of good memory.

[Note: [Col. 1091D] He appears to have died in 1164, for in that year he had John as his successor, as is clear from a bull of Alexander III reported in the new *Gallia Christiana*.]

You must by no means attempt to violate the approved customs which were instituted and observed in your monastery during the days of that abbot by wholesome and reasonable provision, especially abstinence from eating flesh outside the cloister as well as within it. But if any of you rashly attempts to act against those same ordinances, we decree that until [Col. 1093A] he has made suitable satisfaction, he shall be subject to the same sentence which the aforesaid abbot is said reasonably to have established against their transgressors; and that in chapter none of you shall, in order to evade discipline, break out in an appeal. If anyone should think an appeal necessary for such a reason, we judge that appeal to be of no force, so that he may nevertheless be subjected to regular discipline according to the ordinances of the order.

Given at Benevento.

BETWEEN THE YEARS 1173–1177.

MCCLXVII. To the bishops of Paris and Senlis.—They are to have the wood called Sagitta, taken from the Cluniacs by Hu., cupbearer to the king of France, restored to them. (Anagni, 22 December.)

[BOUQUET, *Collection*, XV, 938.]

[Col. 1093B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren [MAURICE], bishop of Paris, and [HENRY], bishop of Senlis, and to his beloved son [PETER], abbot of Saint-Remi of Reims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved sons, the abbot and brethren of Cluny, have informed us through their messenger that Hu., cupbearer of our dearest son in Christ L[ouis], most illustrious king of the French, has presumed unjustly to take from them a wood called Sagitta, and wholly refuses to restore it. Since we are bound to maintain and preserve the rights of the aforesaid brethren all the more diligently because their monastery is known to belong in a special manner to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter and ourselves, we command your discretion by apostolic letters that you earnestly admonish the aforesaid Hu. and labour with all diligence to induce him either freely and without opposition to restore the aforesaid wood with all that has been taken to the said abbot and brethren, and thereafter leave them in peace and quiet, or to render them full justice in the judgment of your discretion. If within twenty days after receiving these letters he is unwilling to do either, publicly declare him excommunicated, without appeal; and forbid the celebration throughout all his land of every divine office except baptism of infants [Col. 1093D] and penances for the dying. Do not relax the sentence of excommunication or interdict without suitable satisfaction.

Given at Anagni, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of January [22 December].

MCCLXVIII. To R., bishop of Saint Andrews, and to the other bishops of Scotland.—He confirms their privileges. (Anagni, 24 December.)

[WILKINS, *Councils of Great Britain*, I, 461.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren R., bishop of Saint Andrews, and the other bishops established throughout Scotland, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The care of the government entrusted to us admonishes us, and the duty of the pontifical office requires, to love our brethren and fellow bishops with more abundant charity, preserve their condition whole and secure, and provide with more attentive zeal and care lest their rights or dignities be diminished or disturbed by anyone’s rashness. For they cannot be diligent concerning the cause entrusted to them if the protection or favour of apostolic provision is lacking to them. Taking this into consideration, and induced and moved by the regard due to your devotion, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the ancient liberties and reasonable customs which you are known hitherto to have possessed, both in consecrating bishops and in other matters. If anyone presumes to act against those liberties or customs, you shall be compelled to answer before no one except in our presence or in that of a legate *a latere* sent by the Roman pontiff. [Col. 1094B] Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for absolutely no person to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, on the ninth day before the Kalends of January [24 December].

IN THE YEAR 1177.

MCCLXIX. Privilege for the Scottish monastery of Saint James at Regensburg. (Foggia, January.)

[RIED, *Diplomatic Codex of Regensburg*, I, 247.]

[Col. 1094C] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GREGORY, abbot of the monastery of Saint James, situated in the suburb of Regensburg, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by an effective result, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth laudably and the requested benefit may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Calixtus, and of our father and predecessor Eugenius and Adrian, Roman pontiffs, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree first that the monastic order known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be inviolably observed for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by just means, with the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. We also decree that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated, while preserving nevertheless the right of those [Col. 1095A] churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for absolutely no person to disturb rashly the aforesaid monastery, or take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, all things shall be kept whole and unimpaired for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the bishop of Regensburg. As a token of this protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay one Byzantine coin yearly to us and our successors. If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1095B] I, William, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Manfred, bishop of Palestrina. I, Albert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of Saint Vitalis, title of Vestina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given at Foggia, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon [Col. 1095C] and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of February [1 February], in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Alexander III.

[Note: [Col. 1095D] Before “Kalends of February” a numerical date appears to have fallen out. JAFFÉ.]

Lead seal: ALEXANDER, POPE III.

MCCLXX. To Martin, abbot of Saint-Vaast.—He receives the monastery of Saint-Vaast under his protection, grants it various privileges, but especially permits the abbot the use of the dalmatic. (Siponto, 26 January.)

[MARTÈNE, *Amplified Collection*, I, 901.]

[Col. 1095D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MARTIN, abbot of Saint-Vaast, and his brethren, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized as consonant with religion and propriety, it befits us gladly to grant it and to afford suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery, which is known to belong especially to our jurisdiction. We decree first that the monastic order which is known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict [Col. 1096A] shall be inviolably observed there for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the bounty of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

Indeed, from your newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, and from the increase of your animals, or from what is contained in the proper territory of your villages of Moylens, Ernaumaynil, and Tatiscam, let no one presume to exact anything from you. We therefore prohibit anyone holding lands or possessions from your monastery from presuming, without your permission or consent, to confer them on other churches or monasteries in life or at death, or alienate them from the monastery itself. Moreover, in the churches which you hold, according to the decree of our predecessor Pope Urban II of good memory, you shall choose priests and present them to the bishops in whose parishes your churches are situated. If those bishops cannot canonically reject them, the priests shall receive from them the care of souls and answer to them concerning the care of the people; but they shall render you due subjection in temporal affairs.

Furthermore, since we ought to adorn with a singular prerogative of honour and dignity and fortify with the privilege of our favour those persons and places whom we know to be devoted to blessed Peter and ourselves and certainly to belong, without intermediary, to the jurisdiction of the most holy Roman Church, considering more attentively the fervour of most sincere devotion and faith which you and your monastery constantly and laudably show in a special manner toward that same most holy Roman Church and toward our person, and considering also how that monastery belongs immediately and properly, without intermediary, to the right and disposition of the Apostolic See, we grant to you, son abbot, and through you to your successors, from the customary clemency and kindness of the same Apostolic See, the use of the tunic and dalmatic during the solemnities of Mass on the principal feasts. Thus, the more you are adorned by the bounty [Col. 1096D] of our gift and favour, the more ready you ought to be found in honouring and serving the aforesaid holy Roman Church. Moreover, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the altar of Streis, as you reasonably possess it through the grant of the bishop of Thérouanne. Therefore we decree, etc.

Given at Siponto, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of February [26 January], in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCLXXI. He receives the Church of Saint Mary at Pulsano under protection and confirms its goods and possessions. (Vesta, 9 February.)

[MITARELLI, *Camaldolese Annals*, IV, Appendix, 64.]

[Col. 1097A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to ANTHONY, prior of Saint Mary at Pulsano, and his brethren, present and future, professing the monastic life, in perpetuity.

Whenever that which is requested of us . . . we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the monastery of blessed Mary, to whose divine service you are devoted. First, decreeing that the monastic order known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict [Col. 1097B] shall be inviolably observed there for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions, etc., among which we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

Namely, the monastery of Saint James near Foggia with its appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Nicholas in the territory of the same castle with its appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Stephen situated at Matinanta, with its appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Saviour in the territory of Piacenza, with its appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Peter of Vallisbona, with its appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Peter of Cellaria, situated in the territory of the castle of Calvello, with its appurtenances; the monastery of Saint Bartholomew of Carbonaria, with its appurtenances; the church [Col. 1097C] of Saint Andrew on Monte Sant’Angelo, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Pancras outside the Trastevere gate; the church of Saint Mary Immaculate of Fabroro outside Florence; the church of Saint Mary outside the city of Lucca, in the place called Guamo; the church of Saint Michael outside the city of Pisa, in the place called Orticaria; the church of Saint Michael in Meleta; the church of Saint Mary at the foot of Monte Sant’Angelo; the church of Saint John; the church of Saint Paul of Civitate; the church of Saint John of Pleuti outside the castle of Foggia; the church of the nuns of Saint Cecilia; the church of Saint Mary of Fusti Ficti and the church of Saint John of Barani; and the church of Saint Peter of the New Crypt [Col. 1097D] at Scitella; the lands which you hold in the territory of Pleuti; the lands which you hold in the territory of the city of Trani; the lands with olive groves which you hold in the territory of Giovinazzo; and the saltworks which you hold at Siponto.

Chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or basilicas, and ordinations of monks to be promoted to holy orders or of clerics, shall be received from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, is in the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to furnish them to you freely and without any wickedness. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. The abbots of your dependencies, or your ministers, shall always look to you as to their head; and we will that correction of them for their offences, when necessary, be exercised through the abbot of Pulsano and his successors.
