We also decree that the monastic order or eremitical life established in that place through God’s grace shall be inviolably observed there for all time, and that only religious persons may be permitted to dwell in your dependencies or residences. We further add that, according to your vow and permission, you should be content with the labour of your hands, or of your animals, their increase, and the alms of the faithful, and should seek no other things upon the land. Indeed, from the fruits of your labour which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals, let no one presume to exact tithes from you. [Col. 1098B]

Therefore we decree, etc., saving the authority of the Apostolic See. As a token of this liberty received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay two Byzantine coins each year to us and our successors. If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

Given at Vesta, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of February [9 February], in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCLXXII. At the request of Stephen, bishop of Monopoli, he receives the Church of Monopoli under protection and confirms its goods. (Vesta? 10 February.)

[This privilege is of the same tenor as the bull granted by Eugenius III to Michael, bishop of the same church, on 19 December 1150; see *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXX, no. 411.—The subscriptions to Alexander III’s diploma are these:]

[Col. 1098C]

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Manfred, bishop of Palestrina. I, Boso, cardinal priest of the Church of Saint Pudentiana, title of Pastor. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa.

Given . . . through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of February [10 February], in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Alexander [Col. 1098D] III.

MCCLXXIII. He directs William, archbishop of Reims and legate of the Apostolic See, “after calling together the masters of the schools of Paris and Reims and of the other surrounding cities, to forbid anyone to dare say that Christ is not something insofar as he is human; for,” he says, “as he is true God, so he is true human being, subsisting from a rational soul and human flesh.” (Vesta, 18 February.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 1081.]

MCCLXXIV. He receives Marmoutier under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Vesta, 28 February.)

[Institut des Provinces de France, Paris 1845, 2nd Series, I, LXXXIV.]

[Col. 1099A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, abbot of Marmoutier, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

By the Lord’s providence, though unworthy, we have been placed in such a position and office that we ought to extend the gaze of our concern over the whole body of the Church and, with pastoral solicitude, provide for the peace of all churches. Therefore, beloved [Col. 1099B] sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, your monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service. First, decreeing that the monastic order known to have been established in that monastery according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be inviolably observed there for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the bounty of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The parish church of Saint Mary situated in the castle of Mayenne, withdrawn from lay hands and, with the consent of Robert the cleric who held it, reasonably conferred upon your monastery by Hildebert, formerly bishop of Le Mans, of good memory, together with what the same cleric possessed in the church of Parigniac; likewise, by the donation of the same bishop, the following churches, as you lawfully possess them: namely, the church of Saint Wingaloeus of Château-Lédo; the church of Saint Saviour of the same castle; the church of Saint James in the same castle; the church of Manzeniac; the church of Jupileis; the church of Saint Cecilia; the church of Lavernet; the offerings [Col. 1099D] and tithes of your men of Fulgeria; the church of Saint Nicholas of Sablolio; the church of Saint Maclovius; two churches of Saint Martin in the aforesaid castle; the church of Boheria; the church of Boareto; the church of Pratellis; the church of Saint Martin of Gradis; the church of Saint Lupus; the church of Balaio; the church of Archasseiac; the church of Bunione; the church of Villiers of Charlemagne; the church of Huxedo with the chapels belonging to it, namely those of Oriniac and Saint-Sulpice; the church of Lupiniac; the church of Saint Martin of Laval; the church of Saint Berthevin; the church of Loiron; the church of Curvavetula; the church of Hahuelledo; the church of Villa Tremensis; [Col. 1100A] the chapel of the castle of Mayenne; the church of Saint Mary in the same castle; the church of Saint Martin in the same castle; the church of Comeriis; the church of Saint Albinus of Meleriac; the chapel of Laciac; the chapel of Manciliac; the church of Saint Hippolytus of Vivonio, with the remaining churches or chapels belonging to it; namely, the church of Saint Mary of Château-Bellimont; the church of Saint Andrew of the same castle; the church of Saint Nicholas of Chalineio; and the church of Saint Lawrence of Rivo Profundo; the church of Saint Martin of Mareschiac; the church of Saint Mary of Murchiac; the church of Saint Albinus of Vineis; the church of Saint Christopher; the church of Roulariis; the church of Saint Mary of Torceio; the church of Saint George; the church [Col. 1100B] of the Holy Trinity of Saint-Céneri; the church of Saint Céneri; the church of Saint Martin of Lavardin; and the chapel of Saint Peter in the same castle.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for absolutely no person to disturb rashly the aforesaid monastery, or take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or burden it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the bishop of Le Mans in the above-mentioned churches. If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 1100C] I, Manfred, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Boso, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustachius beside the Temple of Agrippa, have subscribed.

Dated at Velte [Vestae], through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, the second day before the Kalends of March, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Pope Alexander [Col. 1100D].

MCCLXXV. To the brethren of the Carthusian house of Seitz, whom he exhorts to live holily and according to the rule of their order. (Venice, Rialto, March 31.)

[PEZ, *Treasury of Anecdotes* (*Thesaurus Anecdotorum*), VI, I, 400.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and brethren of the Carthusians dwelling in the Valley of St. John, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since, by divine grace inspiring you, you have wholly renounced the world and its pomps, and have chosen to serve as soldiers for the Lord alone in the garb of strict religion, it befits you to reject worldly riches and allurements, and patiently to endure tribulations, straits, and poverty, [Col. 1101A] so that you may deserve to become sharers with those to whom it was said: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for they shall possess the earth.” [Note: [Col. 1101] Vulgate: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth” (Matt. V, 3, 4).] Therefore, by these apostolic letters, we earnestly admonish your discretion and exhort you in the Lord that, continually observing, as is fitting, the religion and uprightness of your order and the keeping of your cloister, you may strive with greater diligence to devote yourselves to works of charity, so that thereby you may worthily please your Creator and, with the Lord’s help, merit the rewards of eternal recompense. For we have earnestly requested in our letters our beloved son, the nobleman Otakar, Margrave of Styria, that he may more generously love, support, and honour you, and provide you counsel and [Col. 1101B] suitable assistance in constructing your houses.

Given at Venice, Rialto, the second day before the Kalends of April.

MCCLXXVI. Privilege for the Church of Parenzo. (Venice, Rialto, April 5.)

[UGHELLI, *Sacred Italy* (*Italia Sacra*), V, 404.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother PETER, bishop of Parenzo, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever that is requested of us . . . Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, bishop, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves [Col. 1101C] the Church over which, by God’s authorisation, you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document, decreeing that whatever possessions . . . Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The monastery of St. Michael of Subterra; the monastery of St. Barbara; the monastery of St. Michael of Pisino; the monastery of St. Petronilla at Duobus Castella; the monastery of St. Michael of the Valley; the church of St. Mary of the Tower with its chapels; the church of Nigrignano with its chapels; the church of St. Mary of the Field with its chapels; the church of Rosario with its chapels; the church of Montona with its chapels; the church of Zumesco with its chapels; the church of Hebor with its chapels; the church of Valta with its chapels; the church of Vermo with [Col. 1101D] its chapels; the church of Greater and Lesser Pisino with its chapels; the church of Arecio; the church of Visinat; the church of Antiniana; the church of Curicitico with its churches; the church of St. Lawrence with its churches; the church of Duobus Castella with its churches; the church of St. Vincent with its chapels; the church of Zimino with its chapels; the church of Valle with its chapels; the church of Medilano; the canonry of Rubino with its chapels; the church of Ursario with its chapels; the castle of Ursaria with all its appurtenances; the castle of Castellione with all its appurtenances; the church of [Col. 1102A] St. Justus with all its land. Therefore we decree, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal priest of St. Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, Manfred, bishop of Palestrina. I, Cynthius, deacon of St. Adrian. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of St. Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of St. Angelo. I, Raynerius, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Venice, Rialto, through the hand of Bardo, judge and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of April, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Alexander [Col. 1102B] Pope III.

MCCLXXVII. He confirms the goods, possessions, and privileges of the monastery of Saint-Bénigne of Dijon. (Ferrara, April 27.)

[PÉRARD, *Recueil de pièces servant à l’histoire de Bourgogne*, p. 248.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JOHN, abbot of the monastery of Saint-Bénigne of Dijon, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever that is requested of us which is known to accord with religion and uprightness, it becomes us willingly [Col. 1102C] to grant it and to afford suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Saint-Bénigne, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been established in the same monastery according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The site itself upon which the aforesaid monastery is built, with all its appurtenances. In the diocese of Langres: the cell of St. Amator, with the church of St. Ferreolus and its precincts, as well as the churches and other things belonging to it; the cell of Grancheio; the place of Clement’s meadow, called Mores, in which the lay brothers dwell. We command—and confirm by apostolic authority—that these lay brothers shall remain perpetually subject to the Church of Dijon and shall not, through anyone’s faction, remove themselves from subjection to you or to the Church of Dijon; [Col. 1103A] one half of the coinage, so that without the abbot’s permission it shall neither be diminished, increased, nor transferred elsewhere; your share of the toll. Decreeing that henceforth no person whatsoever may harass the said monastery on this account, or inflict upon it any trouble or diminution: the village of Dianetum with its appurtenances; the village of Castenedum; likewise Casnetum and Spaniacum, Marcenniacum, Norgias, Waregas, Sariacum and its tithe; Longovicum, Asiriacum, Plumberias, Prunedum, Escheiriacum, Flaceiacum, Magnum Montem, Viverias, and Salciacum in the wood, with their tithes.

In the diocese of Toul: the cell of Bertiniaca curtis; the cell of Solini Mons, with churches, villages, lands, and all things belonging to them. In the diocese of Autun: the cell of Belna with its churches and the community of Prato Pergeolo with all its appurtenances; the cell of Sarmatiaca; the cell of Curtis Bertaldi; the cell with all things belonging to the same. In the archdiocese of Besançon: the cell of St. Marcellus; the cell of Anfonisvilla; the cell of Sacrofagis; the cell of Logia Nova; the church of Torpa. Near Salins: the cells of St. Peter and St. Michael; the chapel of St. Mary Magdalene, and all things belonging to it. In the diocese of Chalon: the cell of St. Mary; the cell of Palluel, with all things belonging to them. In the diocese of Valence: the cell of St. Genesius of Mont Madrian with its [Col. 1103C] appurtenances; the church of Vulpilierii, and of Comas, and of Glum. In the diocese of Die: the church of Boventia. In the diocese of Bayeux: the cell of St. Vigor with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Sens: the cell of St. Bénigne at Vulnon, with all its appurtenances; the cell of Eskino with all its appurtenances; the cell of Ruz with the things belonging to it; the chapel of Hes, with the tithes and lands granted there. In the diocese of Geneva: the church of Villare with all its appurtenances. In the diocese of Lausanne: the cell of St. Mary Magdalene of Berlay, with the churches and lands granted there; the church of St. Philibert and St. John the Baptist; the church of Longevico; the church [Col. 1103D] of Sarceio; the church of Atiriaco; the church of Penaio; the church of St. John. Near Ladon: the church of Vivariis; the church of Villare; the church of Plumbariis; the church of Prunedo; the church of Missiniaco; the church of Spaniaco; the church of Castnedo; the church of Marcenniaco; the church of Norges; the church of Varesiis; the church of Eschiriaco; the church of St. Apollinaris; the church of Orgialo.

Moreover, concerning your newly cleared lands (*novalia*), which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense and with your own beasts of burden, or concerning the increase of your animals, let no one whatsoever presume to exact tithes from you. We also grant that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, [Col. 1104A] unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken are preserved. In the parish churches which you hold, you may choose clerics and present them to the bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall commit the care of souls to them, so that they shall answer to the bishop for the people and to you for temporal matters. Moreover, you may receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, provided they are free and absolved, and retain them in your monastery without any opposition. We further forbid that any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, may lawfully leave it without the permission of your abbot, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one may dare retain one who departs without letters of release from your community. Furthermore, we decree that the liberties, immunities, and ancient reasonable customs of your monastery shall remain entire and unimpaired by this present decree.

Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of intrigue or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall judge ought to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, [Col. 1104C] or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired for those for whose governance and support they were granted, to be of benefit to them in every respect, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If anyone therefore in future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Hildebrand, cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Susanna, have subscribed. I, Boso, cardinal priest of St. Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. [Col. 1104D] I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of St. Vitalis, of the title of Vestina, have subscribed. I, Peter de Bono, cardinal priest of the title of St. Susanna, have subscribed. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Walter, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, William, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Manfred, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, James, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Arditio, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian, have subscribed. I, Hugh, cardinal deacon of St. Angelo, have subscribed.

[Col. 1105A] Given at Ferrara, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCLXXVIII. He receives the Premonstratensian Church under protection and confirms its privileges. (Ferrara, April 27.)

[LE PAIGE, *Library of the Premonstratensian Order* (*Bibliotheca ordinis Praemonstratensis*), 632.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot of Prémontré, and the other abbots and canons of the Premonstratensian Order, present and future, professing the religious life, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1105B] Set, though unworthy, by the Lord’s providence upon the watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are obliged to be concerned for the condition of every individual and sincerely bound to embrace those things which pertain to the increase of religion and the adornment of virtues, so that the peace of religious persons may be secure from every disturbance and preserved unharmed from the yoke of worldly oppression when fortified by apostolic protection. Considering, therefore, how your religious life and order, resplendent with the great glory of merits and fragrant with the grace of holiness, have extended their branches from sea to sea, we have judged that the order itself and all houses of the same order should be cherished by the safeguard of apostolic protection and fortified by the present privilege.

[Col. 1105C] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, more graciously assenting to your just petitions, we strengthen by apostolic authority and fortify by the protection of this present document all the ordinances and arrangements which you have reasonably made by common consent, or by that of the greater and sounder part, as are set forth below. Namely: that the canonical order which is known to have been established at Prémontré, in white habit, according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine and the ordinances of Norbert of revered memory, former founder of the Premonstratensian Order, and of his successors, shall be observed inviolate for all time in every church of the same order; and that the same observances and the same books pertaining to the divine office shall be uniformly maintained by [Col. 1105D] all churches of the same order. No church or person of your order may seek any privilege contrary to the common institutions of the order, or in any way presume to retain one that has been obtained.

Moreover, none of the churches shall impose upon the church which begot it any exaction whatsoever of earthly advantage; rather, the father abbot alone shall have care for the advancement both of the abbot-son and of the brethren of that house, and shall have authority, according to the order, to correct what he knows requires correction there; and they shall humbly render him filial reverence as to a father. But the abbot of the Church of Prémontré, which is known to be the mother of the others, shall hold the dignity and office of father not only in those churches which it established, but also in all the other churches of the same order, [Col. 1106A] and due observance shall be rendered to him by all, both abbots and brethren.

Furthermore, all abbots of your order shall, every year, setting aside every excuse, assemble at the general chapter of Prémontré, except only those whom bodily illness has hindered from the labour of travel; nevertheless, they must send a suitable messenger through whom the necessity and reason for their delay may be made known to the chapter. Those who dwell in more distant regions and cannot attend the chapter every year without grave difficulty shall assemble within the period assigned to them by that chapter. In that chapter, with the abbot of Prémontré presiding and the others sitting with him and cooperating in the Spirit of God, careful discussion shall be held concerning matters that pertain to the edification [Col. 1106B] of souls, instruction in morals, formation in virtues, and the advancement of regular discipline. Concerning all questions and complaints, spiritual as well as temporal, proposed in this chapter, that shall be held and inviolably observed which the abbot of Prémontré, together with those who appear to possess sounder counsel and greater fitness, shall justly and prudently decide.

If, indeed, any abbot of your order is found to be disgraced and unfit, or a transgressor against his order, and, having first been admonished by his father abbot or by his messengers, neglects to correct and amend his offence, or perhaps refuses to resign if he is to be removed, he shall be deposed by authority of the general chapter; and, once deposed, he shall without delay return to the house from which he came, or to another house of the same order which he chooses, there to remain firmly in obedience to its abbot as do the other brethren of that house. The same may also be done at another time, if necessary, when the chapter cannot be awaited without scandal or danger, by the abbot of Prémontré, the father abbot, and such other abbots as he summons. If the deposed person should obstinately attempt to resist the sentence passed upon him, both he and his principal supporters in such obstinacy who belong to your order shall be restrained by ecclesiastical censure by the abbot of Prémontré and the other abbots until they make satisfaction.

But whenever one of your churches [Col. 1106D] is deprived of its own abbot, it shall remain under the authority and direction of the father abbot; and, with his counsel, the person to be elected shall be elected by the brethren. The elected person, however, shall not, as though freed from the power of the father abbot or of his order, make profession to the archbishop or bishop in such a way as to transgress the constitutions of his order on that occasion, nor shall he become in any respect a transgressor against it. If one of you, canonically elected abbot and presented once and again to the diocesan bishop by the abbots of your order, cannot obtain his blessing from him, then, lest the church to which he has been called should be imperilled through lack of guidance, he shall exercise the office and place of abbot therein, both in providing for external matters and correcting internal ones, until he obtains the blessing, whether by the intervention of your general chapter or [Col. 1107A] by the command of the Roman pontiff or metropolitan.

Moreover, if any of your churches is deprived of a pastor’s consolation and disagreement or division arises among the brethren concerning the appointment of an abbot, and they cannot readily be recalled to concord or unity, the father abbot, with the counsel of his fellow abbots, shall provide them with a suitable person; and they shall receive him as abbot without opposition. If they refuse to receive him, they shall be subject to the sentence which the father abbot, with the counsel of his fellow abbots and with due deliberation, judges should be pronounced against them. If any churches of canons from another order enter your order, they shall without objection be subject to that church of your order in which they are known to have assumed [Col. 1107B] your order.

No ecclesiastical person may demand a palfrey or anything else for the blessing of your abbots; nor may any of your abbots presume to give it even if it is demanded, since both the person demanding and the person giving incur the mark and danger of simoniacal depravity.

Further, because the Church of Prémontré is the first mother of all churches of the whole order and has no father over it, it has been established, for the safeguarding and preservation of the order, that an annual visitation shall be made there by the first three abbots—namely, of Laon, Floreffe, and Cuissy—and, at their recommendation, anything requiring correction in that house shall be corrected. If the abbot proves slack in correcting matters and the brethren, though frequently admonished, remain incorrigible, the matter shall be referred [Col. 1107C] to the general chapter; it shall be remedied according to the counsel of the general chapter as seems best, and the chapter’s sentence in this matter shall be observed without any reconsideration. Whenever the Church of Prémontré is without an abbot, its care shall belong to the aforesaid three abbots; and, with their counsel, the canons of that church shall elect a suitable person as abbot, summoning likewise to their counsel four other abbots belonging to the same church whom those canons shall judge ought to be summoned.

Likewise, every mother church of your order may, with the counsel of the abbot of Prémontré, take for itself as abbot whichever abbot it wishes from among the abbots of churches known to have proceeded from it, provided he is suitable. But none of your churches may choose as its pastor a person from another order; nor may anyone of your order be appointed abbot of a monastery of another order except by authority of the Roman Church. No one may receive or retain your canons or lay brothers without permission from their abbots. If any temporal dispute arises between churches of your order, recourse shall not be had outside the order to an ecclesiastical or secular tribunal; rather, through the mediation of the abbot of Prémontré and others whom he summons, it shall either be settled charitably between them or, after the arguments on both sides have been heard, the controversy shall be determined by a just judgment.

[Col. 1108A] Since every provision which you have ordained for the advancement of religion and the salvation of souls could not be attached to this present abridgment, we strengthen by apostolic authority, together with the matters written above, your customs which you have regularly established among yourselves for the sake of religion, and which hereafter, with the Lord as author, you shall establish; and we decree that they shall be observed inviolate for all time by you, your successors, and all who profess the order. Moreover, for the greater reverence of your order and the observance of regular discipline, we grant you, sons, full authority, with justice and reason as guide, to bind and loose the abbots subject to you, after penance and satisfaction have preceded; reserving to the metropolitan or Roman pontiff the greater and more difficult manifest crimes.

Furthermore, because, removed from the clamour and tumult of secular persons, you love peace and quiet, we decree that your granges, like the precincts of churches, shall be free from the assault and violence of evil persons; forbidding anyone to dare there to seize, despoil, beat, or kill, or to commit theft or robbery. In order to avoid the frequent coming of secular persons, it shall be lawful for you, without prejudice to the right of the diocesan bishops, to build oratories on your granges and, when necessary, to celebrate the divine offices therein for yourselves and your household. We further forbid anyone to dare summon the brethren of your order before secular courts; but if anyone believes that he has a legal claim against them, he shall have the opportunity of pursuing it under examination [Col. 1108C] by an ecclesiastical court. Furthermore, just as you have possessed, since the time of our predecessor of pious memory Innocent, by his privilege, so we also establish by the authority of this present document that no ecclesiastical or secular person may presume to exact tithes from you on newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved unimpaired and whole for those for whose governance and support they were granted, to be of benefit to them in every respect, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See. [Col. 1108D] If anyone therefore in future, etc.

Given at Ferrara, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Roman Church, the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCLXXIX. To Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus, legate of the Apostolic See.—He states that he has not yet made peace with Emperor Frederick; he orders him to urge the king of the French to observe the agreements made with King Henry of England. (Ferrara, April 30.)

[MANSI, *Councils* (*Concilia*), XXI, 966.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus, [Col. 1109A] legate of the Apostolic See, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We were astonished by what you reported to us: that it was being publicly proclaimed throughout the whole kingdom of France that we had made peace with Emperor Frederick, and that as a result our most beloved son in Christ, Louis, illustrious king of the French, had been greatly surprised, because he had received no confirmation of it from us. We wondered how that powerful man had spread such reports throughout the world, declaring in his letters that we had gone at his summons and concluded peace, whereas, although terms have been put forward on both sides and there is hope that peace should be restored, we nevertheless have no certainty that peace will be concluded. For we should already have informed the king himself, who has rendered so much to the Church and has fully committed both himself and his kingdom to us and to our brethren. We wish you carefully to explain this to the aforesaid king, as a lover and defender of the Church, and more earnestly to impress upon him that we shall at once take care to inform him more fully if peace is restored by a gift from above.

Moreover, although we have sent letters to our most beloved son in Christ, Henry, illustrious king of the English, admonishing, counselling, and exhorting him to restore his daughter without delay to the aforesaid king, or to have her betrothed to his son, nevertheless the aforesaid king of England asserts that he is ready to complete the marriage if the king of France is willing to keep the agreements which he made with him. We therefore earnestly admonish and exhort your prudence [Col. 1109C] to admonish, earnestly exhort, and induce the same king of France with every diligence to fulfil and observe for the aforesaid king of England those demands, if they are honourable; for he bound himself to them in such a manner that it would disgrace him if he did not fulfil them. But if perhaps he cannot be induced to do this, strive with all insistence to admonish the king of England and labour by every means to induce him speedily to carry out one of the two things which we have mentioned; for it ought sufficiently to satisfy him that he restores the girl to the king, since the latter does not observe the stipulated demands. But if, within forty days after your admonition, he fulfils neither of these things which have been said, pronounce a sentence of interdict upon his kingdom and land, all excuse and appeal being set aside. [Col. 1109D] And command, on our behalf, our venerable brethren the archbishops of Canterbury and Bordeaux and the bishop of Poitiers to observe the same sentence, all excuse and appeal being set aside, and to cause it to be inviolably observed. We wish, however, that you keep this matter secret until you receive a definite reply concerning it from the king of England; and carefully lay the same point before the king of France on our behalf, because it is neither fitting nor expedient that our command should be made public before the king’s reply.

Given at Ferrara, the second day before the Kalends of May.

MCCLXXX. Privilege for the Church of Verona. (Ferrara, May 1.)

[UGHELLI, *Sacred Italy* (*Italia Sacra*), V, 1014.]

[Col. 1110A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RIPRAND, archpriest of the Church of Verona, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to labour for the condition of the churches and, with the Lord’s help, beneficially provide for their peace and welfare. For it is recognised as worthy and expedient that we who, by the Lord’s disposition, have been chosen for their governance should protect them from the wickedness of evil men and fortify them by the protection of Blessed Peter and of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and, following the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Calixtus and Innocent, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves [Col. 1110B] the aforesaid Church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these [Col. 1110C] we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

Namely, the churches of St. George, St. John the Baptist, St. Clement, St. Cecilia, St. Faustinus, St. Firmus in Capella, and St. Paul in Burgo; the church of St. John the Baptist in Valle; the monastery of St. Michael in Campanea; St. John the Baptist in Quintiano; the church of St. Peter in Carnario; St. Paul of Pruno; and All Saints of Novariis; St. Mary of Turano; St. Cassian; and All Saints of Martiana; St. Pancras; St. George in Salsis; St. Michael of Carmasino; St. Faustinus of Monte Draconis; St. Prosdocimus with its tithe; St. Ambrose of Casalialto; the village of Quinti, and the place called Vila, and Lusia with their churches and tithes; and we likewise confirm to you your castles and villages, namely Cerreta, Erbetum, Fagnanum, Ponteposserum, Pradellae with its chapel, half of Englare, Biunde, Porcille, Tresolanum, Gretiana, Martiana, Pulianum, and half of Romagnanum, Pruno, Calmasinum, in the county of Trento Bergusium, Buado, Bulbeno, Badabiones with its chapel; also the wood called Collegaria with its fisheries, and the third part of the grove called Badaugnano; and the palace with the gate of St. Zeno; likewise, one half of the offering made to the monastery of St. Zeno on each feast of that confessor, from dawn until the third hour; also the tithe of the city, the gate of St. Zeno, and the borough. We grant your lawful customs confirmed to you by our predecessors, and command that they be kept unimpaired by apostolic authority; [Col. 1111A] likewise, that none of you may presume, without the common consent of all or of the sounder part of the council, to give the goods, revenues, or possessions of your Church to any person. Whatever has been improperly given away or destroyed shall freely return to your right and lordship. No layman may presume to exact or receive tithes from your own labours or revenues. Therefore we decree, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Walter, bishop of Albano. I, Conrad, archbishop of Mainz and bishop of Sabina. I, W., bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Manfred, bishop of Palestrina. [Col. 1111B] I, Hildebrand, cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Theodinus, cardinal priest of St. Vitalis, of the title of Vestina. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Arditio, cardinal deacon of St. Theodore. I, Cynthius, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian.

Given at Ferrara, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of May, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCLXXXI. To the archpriest and canons of the parish church of St. Michael of Nonantola.—That the number of twelve canons is not to be increased. (Ferrara, May 5.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *Storia della badia di Nonantola*, II, 302.]

[Col. 1111C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the archpriest and canons of the parish church of St. Michael of Nonantola, greeting and apostolic blessing.

In matters which you justly request, you ought readily to obtain our favour, lest we seem to refuse just petitions which it is fitting for us graciously and effectively to grant. Therefore, since, giving careful attention to the number of canons in your church, you have, as you assert, determined after due deliberation [Col. 1111D] that your church should be content with the number of twelve canons, so that neither you nor your successors should be compelled on any grounds to admit anyone as a canon beyond that number unless the possessions of the same church have been so increased that they can support more canons, we, yielding to your petitions, hold and confirm the constitution thus made by you, as we have said; and we confirm it by apostolic authority and fortify it by the protection of this present document. Let no one, therefore, etc.

Given at Ferrara, the third day before the Nones of May. [Note: [Col. 1111D] In the year 1177, while peace was being negotiated with Frederick Barbarossa, Alexander III was at Ferrara for some time at the beginning of May (see Muratori, [Col. 1112D] *Annals of Italy*); this demonstrates that this brief, dated and issued from that city, must be assigned to that year.]

MCCLXXXII. To Albert, archpriest, and the canons of the Church of Bologna.—He confirms their privileges. (Ferrara, May 6.)

[SAVIOLI, *Annals of Bologna*, II, II, 69.]

[Col. 1112A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT, archpriest, and the canons of the Church of Bologna, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Considering the devotion which you show toward us and the Roman Church, we willingly desire to grant your just petitions and, with a favourable outcome, to fulfil your pious wishes. Therefore, since, as you state, with the consent of your bishop and by the authority of our beloved son J., cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles, [Col. 1112B] then legate of the Apostolic See, with the counsel of the consuls and other wise men of the land, it has been established that you must always have a syndic from your own body, we hold your enactment in this matter ratified and firm, confirm it by apostolic authority, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. Moreover, by this present document we establish that, whenever it should happen that your bishop makes a levy in his bishopric, he must use your counsel in demanding and collecting it. We also confirm by apostolic authority the three parts of the tithes from mills, whether any have newly been made or may hereafter be made—excepting mills belonging to religious houses—if these have been granted to you. [Col. 1112C] We decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation and enactment or in any way to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Ferrara, on the second day before the Nones of May [6 May].

MCCLXXXIII. The monastery of St Mary of Vangadizza is taken under protection, and its goods and rights are confirmed. (Ferrara, 7 May.)

[BIANCOLINI, *Historical Notices of the Churches of Verona*, vol. IV, Appendix, p. 69.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ISAAC, abbot of the monastery of St Mary [Col. 1112D] of Vangadizza, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

The authority of the Apostolic See, over which by God’s will we preside, exhorts us to labour for the well-being of churches and to establish with more earnest care those provisions made for their peace. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we fortify with the privilege of the Apostolic See the aforesaid monastery of St Mary the Virgin of Vangadizza, in which you are devoted to the service of God. It is known to have been built by Hugh, formerly marquis, of revered memory, [Col. 1113A] and to have been endowed with liberty by our predecessors of holy memory, the Roman pontiffs Sylvester, Calixtus, and Innocent. As belonging by a special prerogative to the right of Blessed Peter and of the Holy Roman Church, we protect it; decreeing that whatever possessions, etc., among which we have judged the following to be specified by their proper names:

The estate of the abbey, in which the monastery is situated, with the parish church of St John; Vangadizza, with the church of St Michael; the village called Salvaterra, with the church of St Antoninus; Cavazzana, with the church of St Lawrence; the church of St Andrew of Ramo de Palo, with its appurtenances. Within the city of Verona, the church of the Holy Saviour with all [Col. 1113B] its appurtenances; likewise whatever possessions you have at Illasi and Bardolino and in any places whatsoever in the diocese of Verona. In the diocese of Vicenza, the land of Albaretto; in the diocese of Padua, the church of St Peter situated on Monte Silicano, with all its appurtenances; the estate of the valley of Almerico, with the church of St Andrew; at Este, the church of St Firmus and the church of St Peter with their appurtenances; at Palso, the church of St Michael, possessions in the court or estate of the village, and in other places of the same diocese. In the diocese of Adria, Venezia with the church of St Martin; Broxeto with the church of St Zeno; at Contina, the church of St Sixtus; at Gorgnano, the church of St Bartholomew; in the village of Comeda, the church of St Peter; [Col. 1113C] and whatever possessions you have in that same diocese or county; possessions in the diocese of Ferrara and in the diocese of Bologna; the church of Saints Simon and Jude of Urbizzani with its appurtenances.

Therefore let it be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted. Finally, wishing that the statutes of our aforesaid predecessors be observed without any opposition, we decree that the monastery itself, placed under the protection of the Roman pontiffs alone, shall remain wholly free from the authority of other bishops and exempt from every synodal exaction, together with all the churches which it is known now to possess [Col. 1113D] or may hereafter justly acquire. Accordingly, son abbot, you and all your successors may peacefully possess all your churches with their cemeteries, baptisteries, chapters, and synods, and administer them through your own priests, notwithstanding the opposition of any bishop. We likewise establish in perpetuity that promotions of your clerics, consecrations of churches, and the confirmations of children dwelling in your villages shall be performed by such Catholic bishops as you may invite, out of reverence for the Apostolic See and without any taint of venality.

[Col. 1114A] Moreover, by the authority of this privilege, permission is granted to priests appointed at any time in the parish churches of the monastery to impose penances on the people committed to them for public as well as secret crimes. Questions arising concerning marriages, and also more difficult matters, shall likewise fall within their care, so that they may be determined according to the ordinances of the holy Fathers, by reference to you, son abbot, and your successors. [lacuna] Furthermore, let it be your care each year to receive the most holy chrism through your delegates from whichever Catholic bishop you wish, and, once received, to distribute it according to custom among the baptismal churches, as you are known hitherto to have done in all these matters.

Indeed, in consideration of piety, we grant that you shall possess in full the tithes of the abbey estate, together with those of Vangadizza, Salvaterra, and Cavazzana, [Col. 1114B] and also of Ramo de Palo and of the territories of Broxeto, Saguedo, and Venezia. But in other places, you shall claim by our authority the tithes of estates cultivated at your own expense and of your revenues, just as you have held them without disturbance for the preceding forty years and have been accustomed to do.

When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of intrusion or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, elect in accordance with the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, from their own community or another community of religious; should no suitable person be found there—which God forbid. The person elected, however, shall approach the Roman pontiff to be consecrated. If therefore in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

Given at Ferrara, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of May [7 May], in the tenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1177, in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCLXXXIV. To Guido, provost, and the chapter of the Church of Modena.—Concerning the number of fourteen canons, neither to be increased nor diminished. (Ferrara, 9 May.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *Historical Memoirs of Modena*, III, 69.]

[Col. 1114D] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUIDO, provost, and the chapter of the Church of Modena, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The fervent and sincere devotion which you show toward us and the Roman Church urges and exhorts us to grant you readily our favour in those matters which you justly request, especially since you ask from us things which concern the peace and prosperity of your Church. For we have learned from the tenor of your letters that, after considering the resources of the same Church and taking careful counsel, you have enacted that the same church should have neither more nor fewer than fourteen canons, unless its resources should, by the Lord’s bounty, increase so greatly [Col. 1115A] that it could fittingly maintain more. We therefore, assenting to your petitions, hold the aforesaid enactment made by you, as stated, ratified and firm; confirming it by apostolic authority, we strengthen it with the protection of this present writing. We decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Ferrara, on the seventh day before the Ides of May [9 May].

MCCLXXXV. He praises and confirms the devotion of Provost Balderam and the canons of St Mary of Magdeburg toward the Roman Church. (Venice, Rialto, 14 May.)

[HUGO, *Annals of the Premonstratensian Order*, II, 122.]

[Col. 1115B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BALDERAM, provost, and the canons of the church of St Mary at Magdeburg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We commend and pursue with fitting praise the integrity of devotion and faith which, as we have learned, you have constantly shown and continue continually to show toward our mother, the most holy Roman Church, and toward our person. We purpose and desire sincerely to love you and your church, and, when opportunity arises, to consider more earnestly in the Lord the welfare and advancement of your church. We further admonish and earnestly exhort all of you that you may persevere laudably to the end in so worthy and praiseworthy a purpose, and devote yourselves in every way to the increase of your undertaken religious life and to blessed perseverance, so that thereby you may attain eternal glory.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the second day before the Ides of May [14 May].

MCCLXXXVI. To Hugh, abbot, and the brethren of St-Germain-des-Prés, Paris.—He grants that they need not pay procurations to the archbishop of Sens except for at most forty mounts and forty-four persons. (Venice, Rialto, 23 May.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Collection*, XV, 956.]

[Col. 1115D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot, and the brethren of St German at Paris, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more clearly we have experienced, son abbot, the fervour of your devotion in many matters, and the more specially your monastery belongs to our jurisdiction and protection, the more willingly we desire to safeguard its immunity and provide more diligently for its welfare. Therefore, because the archbishop of Sens receives procuration from certain churches which you possess in his diocese, and is said to visit those churches with such a number of persons and mounts that his visitation is exceedingly burdensome to them, we, desiring diligently to provide in this respect for the burdens of the aforesaid churches, have judged it proper to grant you by apostolic authority [Col. 1116A] that, if the aforesaid archbishop or his successors demand procuration from your churches where they ought to receive it for more than forty mounts at most and forty-four persons, those churches or you cannot for any reason be compelled to pay it to them or to provide anything on the pretext of procuration. Let it therefore be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our enactment or in any way to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1116B] Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June [23 May].

MCCLXXXVII. He informs Duke Welf that he has taken the church of Steingaden under protection against the bishop of Augsburg. (Venice, Rialto, 26 May.)

[Monumenta Boica, VI, 490.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the nobleman Duke WELF, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since we know that you diligently promote the honour and advancement of the most holy Roman Church and burn with much devotion toward our person, we desire also to honour you as a special and devoted son of the Church, whom [Col. 1116C] we love with sincere charity in the Lord. We willingly accept your prayers and petitions, insofar as we can do so without prejudice to our honour, and bring them usefully to fulfilment. Therefore we take under the protection of Blessed Peter and our own the church in which the body of your son is buried, and which our venerable brother the bishop of Freising consecrated at your request. By apostolic authority we decree that it shall not be lawful for the bishop of Augsburg or another to raise a question concerning the aforesaid consecration, impose new and unlawful customs upon the aforesaid church, or burden it or the churchmen who serve the Lord there with unwarranted harassment. Indeed, if Almighty God grants that the Church may enjoy the desired peace [Col. 1116D] and that peace between the Church and the emperor may, as we believe, be restored, we shall firmly command the bishop of Augsburg not, either personally or through others, to inflict annoyance or burden, on account of the orders received, upon churchmen dwelling in your land who received orders from Catholic bishops; and to cease entirely from unjust harassment of them and of their churches.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June [26 May].

MCCLXXXVIII. To those visiting the church of St Mary of Charity at Venice, he grants an indulgence of twenty days. (Venice, Rialto, 29 May.)

[MURATORI, *Italian Antiquities*, V, 763.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1117A] sons and brethren of St Mary of Charity, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When, led by the Lord, we had come to Venice for the benefit of the universal Church, whose care and governance we bear, although unworthy, and at your request had been invoked, we dedicated your church on the Nones of April [5 April], as the duty of our office required, by the grace of the Holy Spirit. To all who, with contrite heart and devoutly and humbly, visit that church on the anniversary of its dedication, or during the three days before or the three days after it, we have judged that twenty days of the penance imposed upon them should be remitted, trusting in the mercy of Jesus Christ and the merits of the blessed Peter and Paul. Therefore, lest the indulgence which we have yearly granted to visitors to your church should hereafter slip from human memory, [Col. 1117B] we confirm by apostolic authority the remission which we have made and have judged it proper to commit it to writing for the perpetual remembrance of future generations.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the fourth day before the Kalends of June [29 May].

MCCLXXXIX. To the provost and chapter of Modena.—He enacts that benefices are not to be granted to canons residing elsewhere. (Venice, Rialto, 30 May.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *Historical Memoirs of Modena*, III, 70.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the provost and canons of Modena, greeting [Col. 1117C] and apostolic blessing.

Since we desire to love and honour you and your Church with a special prerogative of charity, we have judged it necessary to give more careful thought to your condition, so that the sincerity of your devotion and faith, which you have hitherto shown unceasingly to us and the Roman Church, may always be able, with the Lord’s help, to increase. Therefore, since, as we have learned from your report, you have enacted for the benefit and advantage of your church that henceforth no prebend shall be conferred in that church upon any canon residing elsewhere, unless he is perhaps in the schools, we hold this enactment, made with the consent of your bishop and of yourselves, ratified and firm; we confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. [Col. 1117D] We also establish that no one may receive your parishioners for burial unless the right of your church in respect of the testamentary portion is preserved. We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation and enactment or in any way to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the third day before the Kalends of June [30 May].

MCCXC. To the same.—He forbids churches to be built within the parishes of Modena without the authorization of the bishop and chapter of Modena. (Venice, Rialto, 30 May.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1118A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the provost and canons of Modena, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We are bound to give more earnest support to ecclesiastical persons, especially to those who, steadfastly remaining in the unity of the Church, are especially faithful and devoted to Blessed Peter and to us; and to consider their welfare and advancement with so much greater care as we love them with more sincere charity and desire that their rights be preserved with more attentive concern. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your petitions, we establish by apostolic authority that no one may, within the parishes of your church or of your other churches, build a church or oratory without the consent of your bishop and yourselves, saving the privileges of the Roman Church.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the third day before the Kalends of June [30 May].

MCCXCI. He confirms the judgment rendered by the bishops of Equilio and Torcello: that the monks of St Nicholas are to receive Vitalis, bishop of Castello [Venice], on the day of the Lord’s Ascension “for the procession and for the provision of a meal.” (Venice, Rialto, 31 May.)

[UGHELLI, *Sacred Italy*, V, 1245.]

[Col. 1118C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother V., bishop of Castello, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Things established by judicial decision ought to remain in their force and be strengthened by apostolic authority, lest they may be disturbed by anyone’s malice or presumption. We have learned that, when our venerable brethren the bishops of Equilio and Torcello had undertaken, by our command and without [Col. 1118D] appeal, to determine the case pending between you and the abbot and monks of St Nicholas concerning your reception by that abbot and brethren on the day of the Lord’s Ascension—at the principal Mass, for a procession, and for the provision of a meal for you and yours—they finally rendered a definitive judgment in your favour concerning that reception, procession, and meal, after hearing the arguments, fully understanding them, and sufficiently ascertaining the truth of the matter through the confession of the abbot and monks of the same monastery. We hold this judgment ratified and firm, confirm it by apostolic authority, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way oppose it; but if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of June [22 May].

MCCXCII. To the abbot and brethren of St-Ouen.—He upholds their right in the church of St Leufroy of La Croix. (Venice, Rialto, 1 June.)

[POMMERAIE, *History of Saint-Ouen of Rouen*, I, 447.]

[Col. 1119A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and brethren of St Ouen, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and that wishes which do not depart from the path of reason be brought to effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, joining your just petitions with welcome assent, we confirm for you by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the right and dignity which you are known reasonably to possess in the church of St Leufroy of La Croix, as is contained in the authentic [Col. 1119B] document of our venerable brother Rotrou, formerly bishop of Évreux and now archbishop of Rouen. We decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the Kalends of June [1 June].

MCCXCIII. He writes to the men of Steingaden that, moved by Duke Welf’s prayers, he has taken their church under protection. (Venice, Rialto, 10 June.)

[Monumenta Boica, VI, 491.]

[Col. 1119C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and brethren of St John the Baptist of Steingaden, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son, the nobleman Duke Welf, informed us that our venerable brother the bishop of Freising, at the request of the aforesaid duke and of yourselves, consecrated your church, which was built on his estate, where his son is buried, and in which he himself has chosen to be buried. Although that church lies on the boundary between the dioceses of Augsburg and Freising, the same bishop found in the privilege of his church that the aforesaid church belongs to [Col. 1119D] your jurisdiction. Therefore, lest the bishop of Augsburg, on the ground of that consecration, harass you or that church with unwarranted oppression, we hold the same consecration ratified and firm, forbidding the bishop of Augsburg to presume, on the pretext of the aforesaid consecration, to inflict annoyance or burden upon you or your church.

Moreover, prompted by the duty of our office, moved by the prayers of the same duke, and recalling nonetheless how the said duke has devotedly adhered to us from the beginning of our elevation and has steadfastly remained faithful in devotion to us and the Church, we take your church, with all the goods which it now lawfully possesses [Col. 1120A] or may hereafter, by just means and with the Lord’s assistance, acquire, under the protection of Blessed Peter and our own, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We establish that it shall not be lawful for the bishop of Augsburg or another to raise a question against you or your church concerning the aforesaid consecration, impose new and unlawful customs, or otherwise unjustly burden you or that church. We therefore decree, etc.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the fourth day before the Ides of June [10 June].

MCCXCIV. To the provosts of Salzburg and Gurk.—Concerning the prevented arrival of Cardinal Henry. That it is false that he intended the deposition of Adalbert, archbishop of Salzburg, etc. (Venice, Rialto? 12 June.)

[PEZ, *Treasury of Anecdotes*, VI, I, 389.]

[Col. 1120B]

A., bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the provosts of Salzburg and Gurk, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since you repeatedly recount the oppressions and anxieties with which your Church is afflicted, we sympathize and grieve with you in heartfelt concern; and if we had not found, by your own word and the counsel of your brethren or your conscience, [Note: [Col. 1119D] “A dark and perhaps corrupt passage.”] that we could offer you counsel and help amid such great labours and pressures, we would have offered it with our whole desire. For we are established in such desire and purpose that, as our office requires, we wish gladly to devote ourselves to that Church, which we see so firmly and steadfastly grounded in devotion to St Peter [Col. 1120C] and to us that it could not be torn from the strength of its constancy either by the blast of winds or by storms of tempests; and we wish to apply prompt diligence to those things which concern its advancement and preservation. For we should appear forgetful of all humanity and reason if we were unmindful of such devotion and allowed oblivion to pass over the troubles and persecutions which it is known to have endured with immovable firmness for love of justice.

Furthermore, although you informed us that our beloved son H[ildebrand], cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles and legate of the Apostolic See, would find full security, enabling him to approach the aforesaid Church safely and securely, he reported something very different to us: when he had reached Treviso and waited there for several days, neither you nor others came to meet him to provide safe passage to his destination; and the rulers of the March, doubting and fearing that without them we might conclude peace with F., called emperor, forbade the same cardinal to proceed farther.

Moreover, the envoys of our venerable brother A[dalbert], archbishop of Salzburg, stated firmly before us and our brethren that you had in no way delivered to him our letters, by which we had ordered him to come at the cardinal’s [Col. 1121A] summons; but that throughout Bavaria, Bologna, Bohemia, Germany, and Hungary you had publicly caused it to be proclaimed that we intended entirely to depose and eject the aforesaid archbishop. In this matter we have certainly been aggrieved and greatly disturbed; our honour has been seriously impaired and our reputation torn to pieces among many persons who perhaps either did not know our intention or eagerly sought material and occasion for reviling and insulting us. They further alleged that the archbishop could by no means have had a safe-conduct, and that the prelates could not safely approach that Church; rather, one of them, who considered himself protected by a more powerful patron, had been robbed on his return and treated very dishonourably and improperly. [Col. 1121B]

They further reported that he had refused to receive the letters which his father, the king of Bohemia, obtained from the aforesaid emperor, and had wholly recoiled from carrying out their tenor, wishing to remain steadfast in the Catholic faith and in devotion to the Church and to us. His father, it is said, did not obtain the said letters with the intention of making him depart from Catholic unity, but in order to discover the emperor’s mind and learn his will more expressly, whereby it would be [understood] that the emperor sought and desired not merely to arrange the Church of Salzburg, but to make it alien from obedience and devotion to the Roman Church. Indeed, when we put to one of the envoys of the aforesaid archbishop, who [Col. 1121C] was still present, the allegation that the archbishop had entrusted the church’s ornaments to a certain female sorcerer and enchantress, he wholly denied it and declared it utterly false.

And because we perceive that your writings are varied and contradictory—for you write against him under one seal on behalf of the whole chapter and the prelates of the archbishopric of Salzburg, while the archbishop’s envoys have produced the writings of many persons, and almost of the same prelates, under their individual seals, urgently requesting our authority—we cannot and ought not deny him our hearing or commit his case to other judges, since he has chosen our tribunal and asks to be judged before us alone, if any persons wish to [proceed against] him. [Col. 1121D] Nor ought you to withdraw from him the obedience and reverence due to him, but render them with devout mind and humble spirit.

Given … on the second day before the Ides of June [12 June].

MCCXCV. To Adalbert, archbishop of Salzburg.—That the rumour reporting that his disposition toward him had turned hostile is false. He is, however, to come to him in Lombardy, where he will hear a just judgment. [Venice, Rialto? June.]

[Ibid., col. 395.]

A., by the grace of God bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved brother A., archbishop of Salzburg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

H., your faithful servant and intimate, informed us that it had been firmly asserted to your fraternity [Col. 1122A] that we bore such indignation against you as to appear altogether to intend and labour for your deposition. On hearing this, we were astonished and troubled, and do not know whence such a suspicion concerning us could have arisen in you, since we love you as a venerable brother and embrace you in the arms of sincere charity. Yet, since, though unworthy, we are placed by the Lord in an office and position in which we ought to provide for each person what is just and right and not harden apostolic ears against those seeking justice, you ought neither to find it strange nor to have less confidence in our favour because we summoned you into our presence, wishing to ascertain and see whether the reports made known to our ears concerning you are true. Therefore come confidently and safely, setting all doubt aside, into Lombardy to [our] presence, because we shall gladly see your person, hear you kindly, endeavour, insofar as the Lord grants us, to preserve your right, and render a just judgment in your case.

MCCXCVI. He grants Robert, abbot of the church of St Quirinus at Tegernsee, the use of the mitre. (Venice, Rialto, 14 May.)

[Monumenta Boica, VI, 185.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son R[OBERT], abbot of the Church of St Quirinus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1122C] We ought gladly to assent to the vows and desires of religious persons and readily to support them in their just petitions, so that their houses, fortified by apostolic protection, may not be shaken by anyone’s disturbances. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, giving more careful consideration to the sincerity of devotion and faith which we have learned that you show toward Blessed Peter and ourselves, we take under the protection of Blessed Peter and our own the church over which, by God’s will, you are known to preside, together with all that it now lawfully possesses or may hereafter, through God’s provision, acquire by just means; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. Moreover, wishing to adorn you with a special privilege of our love and favour, [Col. 1122D] by the customary clemency and kindness of the Apostolic See we grant you the use of the mitre on the principal feasts during the solemnities of Mass and in the processions of your church, and also in councils of bishops, so that by this you may be bound always to remain more devoted to Blessed Peter and to us.

We therefore decree, etc.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of July [14 June].

MCCXCVII. He confirms the city of Lodi Nuova, endowed with the possessions of the old town. (Venice, Rialto, 15 June.)

[UGHELLI, *Sacred Italy*, IX, 672.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1123A] sons the consuls and people of Lodi, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since your city has been transferred from the place where it was formerly built to another place, you have asked that the condition of your city be fortified and confirmed by the authority of the Apostolic See, lest anything that you previously possessed could be withheld or taken away from you on the occasion of this transfer. We therefore graciously assent to your petitions; and, considering the devotion which you show toward us and the Roman Church, we hold the condition of your new city, with all your goods and possessions and with all the territory which belonged within or outside the old city, valid and firm, and confirm it by apostolic authority. By this present document [Col. 1123B] we establish that you may, without opposition, receive and retain free persons from Crema or other places who transfer themselves to you, as it is known recently to have been reasonably established between you and the rulers of Lombardy.

Given at Venice, in Rialto, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of July, 1177 [15 June].

MCCXCVIII. Privilege for the monastery of St Mary of Porto Nuovo. (Venice, Rialto, 28 June.)

[UGHELLI, *Sacred Italy*, I, 331.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RUSTICUS, abbot of the monastery of St Mary of Porto Nuovo, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life.

[Col. 1123C] Whenever something is requested of us which is known to accord with religion and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and give suitable support to the desires of those concerned.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; we take under the protection of Blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it with the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order which, according to the Lord and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, is known to have been instituted in that place shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions … among which we have judged the following [Col. 1123D] to be specified by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with its port, wood, and all its appurtenances; the church of St. Severinus; the church of St. Lawrence; the church of St. Blaise in the castle of Poggio, with its parishioners; the church of St. John; the church of St. Gervasius, with all its appurtenances; the vineyards and fields around the estate of Poggio which you hold in your own possession; the fields of Corsiciano; the church of St. Marcellinus; the church of St. Angel or Archangel, with all its appurtenances. Whatever you possess in the estate of Varano, both in lands and vineyards; the church of St. John; the church of St. Damian; the field of Tripontium; the church of St. Mary of Umbriano, with its parishioners and with the estate of Castello; and the possessions which you have in the estates of Umbriano, [Col. 1124A] Caprofici, Consortii, and Buranacii; the church of St. Peter in the castle of Camurano, with its parishioners; the field of Plage; the vineyard of Plano; the great vineyard beside the rampart of Camurano; and the other possessions which you have in the estate of Camurano. The church of St. Senius, with all its appurtenances near Lotentia; the church of St. Terentianus; the church of St. George; the possessions which you have in the estate of Offania; the possessions which you have in the estate of Puliniano and in the landholding of Aspia; and, in the city of Ancona, the church of St. Nicholas.

Moreover, no one shall presume to exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, nor on the produce of your animals. We likewise decree that the burial-place of that same site shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion [Col. 1124B] and last wishes of those who resolve to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated or under interdict; the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken nevertheless being preserved. Furthermore, you may receive into your religious conversion clerics or laymen, free and unencumbered, fleeing from the world, and retain them in your monastery without anyone’s opposition. We further prohibit anyone, after making profession in that place, from leaving the cloister, moved by any frivolous impulse, without the permission of his abbot; and no one shall dare retain one who leaves without letters of authorization from the community, unless he wishes to transfer to a stricter life. When a general interdict is imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, [Col. 1124C] excluding the excommunicated and those under interdict, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice.

Furthermore, by this decree we ordain that the liberties, immunities, and ancient reasonable customs of your church shall remain whole and inviolate. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any trickery of usurpation or by force, save one whom the brothers by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers, shall have provided to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of St. Benedict. We therefore decree, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubaldus, bishop of Ostia. [Col. 1124D] I, Gualterius, bishop of Albano. I, Chunradus, archbishop of Mainz; bishop of Sabina. I, Guigliemus, bishop of Porto. I, Manfredus, bishop of Palestrina. I, Adebrandus, priest-cardinal of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Anastasia.
