three solidi and nine denarii of rent which you have at Vullierens [Note: [Col. 1152D] Vullierens.], and other money-rents which you have in various [Col. 1151C] places; and the land and vineyards of Luins.

Moreover, wishing with paternal care to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we forbid by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosure of your places or granges to commit violence, theft, robbery, or arson; or to seize or kill persons. We also decree that the burial place of that same house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final will of those who wish to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, without prejudice, however, to the rights of those churches from which the bodies are taken. When a general interdict has been imposed on the land, you may celebrate the divine offices in low voice, with the doors closed, excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, and bells not rung. No one may presume to demand tithes from you on your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the fodder of your animals. [Col. 1151D]

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all shall be kept intact and whole, to benefit in every way the purposes for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future, etc.

Given at Venice in Rialto, through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of October, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the nineteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MCCCXXIV. Privilege for the church of Ferrara. (Venice in Rialto.)

[UGHELLI, *Sacred Italy*, II, 538.]

[Col. 1152B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WIDO, archpriest and provost, and all the canons of the Church of Ferrara, present and future, to be canonically instituted: in perpetuity.

The petition of pious desire, etc. He enumerates their possessions: namely, the estate called Quartisana; the property opposite the Po; the place Cucula; the head of Reda; the estate called Baniolum; the property Burduragum; the estate called Quartiatica; the sheep-farm; and the estate called Fossa Nova; the chapel of Saint Mark situated there; Pilearitia, called Mortitium; the church of Saint Michael with its appurtenances; [Col. 1152C] the chapel of Saint Stephen with its appurtenances; in the borough of Ferrara, the chapel of Saint James in the city of Ferrara; the chapels of Saint Peter and Saint Saviour, situated in the castle of Ferrara itself, with all their appurtenances; the chapel of Saint Mary Magdalene and Saint Vitus, which is in the market of Ferrara; the chapel of Saint Leonard; the whole Corrigium Stadii; half of Greater and Lesser Lendenaria; the Cocolaria mud-flat fishery; Zemedelle; a holding situated at Caput Sandali; the holding of the port of Vetraria; the holding of Gamolaga; half the property of Bucentula; the property of Bagnoli; the communal marshes; half the property of Gallinarium; half the property of Purpuraria; the port of Caput Redae; likewise the land which belonged to Ajacha, situated in the [Col. 1152D] estate called Zuccula; one holding in the property called Duce.

Further, half of the entire proceeds of the parish church of Saint George in the bishopric of Ferrara; half of all movable and immovable things left to that church for the souls of the departed; the entire tithe of the estate called Cocomarium; and everything else which canonically and justly belongs to it in lands, vineyards, meadows, cultivated and uncultivated fields, waters and fisheries, hunting rights and mills, male and female serfs; and twelve men of that place, who shall carry you by boat wherever your need may be, without any payment.

In addition, we decree and forbid by apostolic authority that no one may, against your will, subject the clerics of the chapels belonging exclusively to your jurisdiction to interdict or excommunication, or oppress them by any other undue molestation. Rather, you shall have free disposition, ordering, and correction of the chapels and their clerics without any contradiction, as you had until the time of your present bishop. Furthermore, by this present page we decree that no one, contrary to your will, may within the city or the suburbs of your city baptize, anoint, according to the arrangement once made by Azo, cardinal of the Roman Church and then legate of the Apostolic See, with the counsel and assent of Land., formerly bishop, and observed until now; nor may anyone presume to impose public penances. [Col. 1153B] No one may presume to remove from you or forcibly withhold the fourth part of the tithes which are known by right to belong to you in your parish.

Likewise, by apostolic authority we forbid anyone to dare, before absolution, to admit to divine offices or burial any of your parishioners whom you have canonically subjected to excommunication or interdict by authority of your bishop. We further grant you that, if your bishop, when humbly requested, is unwilling within thirty days to restrain by ecclesiastical sentence invaders, disturbers, or possessors of your property—unless a manifest and reasonable cause prevents him—you may, by our authority, according to the quality and gravity of the offence, pronounce upon them a sentence of excommunication or interdict. We hold ratified and firm the arrangement concerning the testaments of the deceased which the aforesaid cardinal is known to have reasonably made with the counsel and assent of the aforesaid bishop, and which our venerable brother Am., your bishop, approved; and we decree that it shall remain unshaken for all time. [Col. 1153D]

We also decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid body of canons, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall remain intact, to benefit in every way the uses of you and of the others for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the bishop of Ferrara. If, therefore, etc.

Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, Gualterius, bishop of Sabina.

[Col. 1154A] Given at Venice, the third day before the Kalends of . . . in the year 1179 of the Lord’s Incarnation . . . through the hand of . . . holding office for . . . Lord Pope Alexander III, in the year . . . indiction . . . [Note: [Col. 1153D] The date formula is corrupt.]

MCCCXXV. He thanks Master Hugh Eteriano for having sent him, through Master Cacciaredus, a book composed “for God and for devotion to the Church.” He admonishes him “to urge the emperor of Constantinople more diligently to show devotion and reverence toward the Roman Church and toward its unity.” (Troyes, November 16.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 909.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Master HUGH: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Recognizing the great labour which you endured [Col. 1154B] in composing the book which you sent us through our beloved son Master Cacciaredus [Note: [Col. 1153D] For Hugh’s letter dedicating to Alexander III his book *On the Heresies [Col. 1154D] Which the Greeks Cast upon the Latins*, see *Patrology*, vol. CCII, col. 227.], and considering also the fruit which we hope will come from it for the Church of God, we received the book with grateful and joyful hand. For this we return most abundant thanks to your devoted diligence and generosity. We desire and intend henceforth to love more fervently, to hold much dearer, and to embrace more sincerely you whom until now we held dear through reports from our people returning from the regions of Constantinople.

We ask and carefully admonish your prudence that, just as you composed the aforesaid book for God and for devotion to the Church, so you should also more diligently urge, induce by admonitions and exhortation, our dearest son in Christ, the illustrious and glorious emperor of Constantinople, to show devotion and reverence toward the most holy Roman Church and toward its unity, so that, as it ought to be, there may be one fold and one shepherd. [Col. 1154C]

Given at Troyes, on the Ides of November.

WITHIN THE YEARS 1160–1178.

MCCCXXVI. He grants the lepers of Abbeville exemption from tithes and confirms the land of Cantastra, granted by the count of Ponthieu. (Anagni, January 17.)

[R. P. Ignace-Joseph de JESUS-MARIA, *Ecclesiastical History of Abbeville*, p. 387.]

[Col. 1154D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the lepers of Abbeville: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The continual sufferings which you endure move us and earnestly lead us to afford you the support of the Apostolic See, so that you who are grievously afflicted by the just judgment of God’s heavenly visitation may feel, in your necessities, the aid of fitting consolation. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, mercifully assenting to your just requests, from the clemency of the Apostolic See we grant you that no one may presume to demand tithes from you on your gardens, which you cause to be cultivated for your own use, or on fodder for your animals. [Col. 1155A]

We also confirm to your devotion by apostolic authority, and fortify by the protection of this present writing, the house and a certain land of Cantastra which the count of Ponthieu—here named as a benefactor—with the assent and will of his brother Guy, justly granted you in perpetual alms. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our grant and confirmation or in any way oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1155B]

Given at Anagni, the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February.

MCCCXXVII. He forbids the parish priests, chaplains, and other clerics of the district surrounding the monastery of Puteoli “in any way to prevent any of their parishioners from freely being able to take the monastic habit at the monastery or to be buried there.” (Anagni, January 20.—See MITTARELLI, *Camaldolese Annals*, IV, Appendix, p. 103.)

MCCCXXVIII. To Rainald, bishop of Jesi.—He grants certain privileges. (Anagni, January 23.)

[BALDASSINI, *Historical Memoirs of Jesi*, Appendix, p. III.]

[Col. 1155C] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother R[AINALD], bishop of Jesi: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It was set forth before us on your behalf that our messenger, the beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of Saint Anastasius of the diocese of Fermo in the March of Ancona, carefully warned the citizens of Jesi, by our authority, to take care to return, within a fixed peremptory period assigned to them for that purpose, to the devotion of the Church from which they had rashly withdrawn; and that, if they failed to do so, he placed the city of Jesi under ecclesiastical interdict and deprived it of episcopal dignity. You therefore humbly petitioned us mercifully to provide that, through the fault of the aforesaid citizens, no prejudice may arise to your position by occasion of such deprivation; and that you, abandoning the city because of that interdict and the rebellion of the aforesaid citizens, may not suffer want of necessities. [Col. 1155D]

We therefore, inclining to your petitions, grant you by the authority of this present document that, if the said citizens do not return within a fixed period to devotion to the Church, you may reside in some suitable place in the diocese of Jesi and receive there, in full, the revenues of the bishopric by our special grace—not as bishop of Jesi—as you did previously, notwithstanding any apostolic letters obtained or yet to be obtained, unless in such petitions express and full mention is made of the present grant. Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted to infringe this page of our concession, etc. [Col. 1156A]

Given at Anagni, the tenth day before the Kalends of February, in the fifth year of our pontificate.

MCCCXXIX. Privilege for the church of Saint Margaret of Elenfordesmer. (Anagni, January 27.)

[RYMER, *Treaties, Conventions*, I, 43.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GERELM., prior, and the brethren of Saint Margaret of Elenfordesmer: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It becomes us graciously to admit and to bring to useful completion the prayers and petitions of the sons of the Church which accord with reason and do not depart from ecclesiastical propriety. [Col. 1156B] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, more generously assenting to your just requests, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves your church, in which you are devoted to divine service, . . . [lacuna]

Furthermore, we confirm to you and to the same church by apostolic authority, and fortify by the protection of this present writing, the place itself in which your church is situated and the possessions which the nobleman Ralph of Chedeleswurd legitimately granted to your church in perpetual alms through pious generosity, as you reasonably possess them. No one may presume to demand tithes from you on your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the fodder of your animals. [Col. 1156C]

Moreover, by apostolic authority we forbid the bishop of Salisbury, in whose diocese your church is situated, or his archdeacons or officials, to impose upon you or your church new and undue customs, or unjustly burden you or your church.

We decree therefore, etc.

Given at Anagni, the sixth day before the Kalends of February.

MCCCXXX. He confirms to Robert of Chedeleswurd four hides of land in Chedeleswurd granted to him by the monks of Abingdon. (Anagni, January 28.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1156D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ROBERT of Chedeleswurd, clerk: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and that prayers which do not depart from the path of reason be brought to completion with effective fulfilment. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, concurring in your just petitions with gracious assent, we confirm to your devotion by apostolic authority, and fortify by the protection of this present writing, the four hides of land at Chedeleswurd reasonably granted to you by the monks of Abingdon, as is contained in the authentic document made concerning them and as you lawfully possess them.

We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way oppose it, etc. [Col. 1157A]

Given at Anagni, the fifth day before the Kalends of February.

IN THE YEARS 1174–1178.

MCCCXXXI. He commands the bishop of Terracina to induce the people of Terracina to restore the possessions of the church of Saint Stephen of Montanis which they had bought. (Anagni, February 25.)

[TOSTI, *History of Monte Cassino*, II, 205.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother . . . , bishop of Terracina: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1157B] Our beloved son, the abbot of Monte Cassino, informed us that certain inhabitants of Terracina, contrary to the prohibition of Raynald, his predecessor of blessed memory, did not hesitate to buy from the provosts of the church of Saint Stephen of Montanis, which belongs to the monastery of Monte Cassino, certain possessions of that church, and that they hold them thus occupied. Since, therefore, we can neither nor ought to pass over with closed eyes the loss of the aforesaid monastery, whose rights we are especially bound to preserve, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters, after diligent inquiry into the truth of this matter, carefully to admonish and diligently induce those inhabitants of Terracina whom you ascertain bought from the provosts of the aforesaid church, contrary to the prohibition of the aforesaid Abbot Raynald, possessions of that church, or otherwise acquired them against justice without the knowledge of the abbots of the aforesaid monastery, to restore those possessions to the same church without delay or appeal and leave them in peace. [Col. 1157C] Yet what they gave in acquiring those possessions, insofar as it has passed to the use of the said church, ought to be restored to them.

But if they will not comply with your admonition, bind them by our authority with the bond of excommunication, and have them avoided as excommunicated persons until they make worthy satisfaction.

Given at Anagni, the fifth day before the Kalends of March.

WITHIN THE YEARS 1176–1178.

[Col. 1157D]

MCCCXXXII. To Master Girard Puella.—Concerning school revenues. (Anagni, February 7.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 963.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1158A] son Master G.: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Considering your learning and knowledge, and how you are endowed with harmony of character and uprightness, and reflecting likewise upon this, we are bound by a common and special duty to attend to your advancement and progress and to show you much kindness. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, since under your teaching many, by God’s grace, advance in literary learning, we grant you by apostolic authority that for up to four years, if you direct schools, your revenues which you have in England shall be paid to you freely and without any diminution while you are teaching, notwithstanding any contradiction or appeal. Thus no one may lawfully diminish or withhold anything from those revenues, or inflict undue molestation or burden upon your affairs on that account; nor shall you be compelled within that period to leave the schools, unless such necessity arises in a church in which you hold a personal benefice or major benefice that you ought rightly to offer it your presence and protection. [Col. 1158B]

Given at Anagni, the seventh day before the Ides of February.

MCCCXXXIII. He grants Peter, abbot, and the chapter of Monte Cassino “that nothing shall at any time be demanded for passage-toll or market-toll upon goods which they buy, or have bought, at Benevento for the use of the monastery.” (Anagni, February 23.)

[TOSTI, *History of Monte Cassino*, II, 207.]

[Col. 1158C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons P., abbot, and the chapter of Monte Cassino: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The fervour of your devotion and the integrity of faith which you show toward us and the Roman Church more strongly admonish and induce us to attend diligently to the benefits and advancement of your monastery and to show our favour to you more abundantly. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, from the kindness of the Apostolic See we grant you by these present letters that, for goods which you at any time buy, or cause to be bought, at the city of Benevento for the use of that same monastery of yours, nothing shall at any time be demanded for passage-toll or market-toll; but that in that city you may purchase freely, and without any payment, those things which it is necessary for you or your monastery to buy, and depart thence with them. [Col. 1158D]

Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted to infringe this page of our concession or in any way oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Anagni, the seventh day before the Kalends of March.

IN THE YEAR 1178.

[Col. 1159A]

**MCCCXXXIV. To Gerald, abbot, and the brethren of the church of St Mary of Reno—Confirms their possessions and rights.** (Anagni, 23 January.)

[TROMBELLI, *Historical Memoirs of St Mary of Reno*, Bologna, 1752, quarto, p. 373.]

Since the care and solicitude for all Churches has been entrusted to us, though unworthy, etc. He enumerates their possessions as follows:

We confirm by apostolic authority to you the very place on which the aforesaid church is built, with all its appurtenances; the church of St Andrew at Turicella; the church of St Dominic [Col. 1159B] near Bagno; the church of St Saviour; and also the church of St Praxedes, as it was granted to you by our predecessor Pope Anastasius of pious memory—without prejudice to the right and due respect of the cardinal who shall at the time hold office in that church. We likewise hold ratified and firm, and decree that they shall remain inviolate for all time, the liberties and immunities reasonably granted by Gerard, bishop of Bologna of good memory, to your church and to the other churches named above: namely, that, with all their movable and immovable goods, they shall be wholly free and untroubled from every condition, service, and tribute of monks, clerics, or laymen holding from the bishop, and from the dominion of any person, great or small, save episcopal right. [Col. 1159C]

You may also receive clerics and laymen fleeing the world, free and absolved, for conversion, and retain them in your church without any contradiction. Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, to leave that house without his prior’s permission, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one may dare retain a person who leaves without letters of authorization from the community. But if he departs and, having been admonished by you, refuses to return, you, son prior, and your successors may, as the aforesaid bishop of Bologna decreed, bar him from the divine offices. No abbot or prelate within the bishopric of Bologna may dare, contrary to that bishop’s ordinance, receive one so interdicted within that bishopric. [Col. 1159D]

We also grant that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken being nevertheless preserved. Furthermore, we grant you free power to receive the ordinations of your clerics from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, as the aforesaid bishop is known to have granted you that power by an authentic written instrument. We also confirm to you the tithes of your produce arriving from any part of the bishopric of Bologna, [Col. 1160A] as those same tithes were granted to your church by the prudent foresight of that bishop.

We decree therefore, etc. I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, of Pammachius. I, Albert, priest-cardinal of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina. I, Boso, priest-cardinal of St Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of St Mark. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St Susanna. I, James, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in [Col. 1160B] Cosmedin. I, Cinthius, deacon-cardinal of St Adrian. I, Hugh, deacon-cardinal of St Angelo. I, Laborans, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Portico.

Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the tenth day before the Kalends of February [23 January], in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

**MCCCXXXV. Takes the monastery of St Mary of Eberbach under protection and confirms its goods, possessions, and privileges.** (Anagni, 26 January.)

[WENK, *History of the Land of Hesse*, III, 10.]

[Col. 1160C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ARNALD, abbot of the monastery of St Mary of Eberbach, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting that those who choose the religious life should have apostolic protection, etc. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-Virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service. First, indeed, we decree [Col. 1160D] that the monastic order known to have been established in that monastery according to God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the institution of the Cistercian brethren, shall be maintained and observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and whatever goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, etc.

(It enumerates their possessions.)

Certainly, no one at all may presume to exact tithes from you on the fruits of your labour, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. You may also receive clerics and laymen fleeing the world, free and absolved, for conversion, and retain them in your monastery without [Col. 1161A] any contradiction. Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, to leave that house without his abbot’s permission; and no one may dare retain one who leaves without letters of authorization from the community. Desiring also, with paternal solicitude, to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we forbid by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosures of your houses or granges to commit violence, robbery, or theft, to set fire, or to dare seize or kill a person.

We decree therefore, etc.

(The subscriptions follow as in the preceding bull.)

Given at Anagni by the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of February [26 January], [Col. 1161B] in the sixth indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

**MCCCXXXVI. Restores to the monastery of Monte Cassino a golden panel alienated from it, and forbids its future alienation under anathema.** (Anagni, 30 January.)

[MARGARINI, *Bullar. Casin.*, II, 185.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, abbot, and the chapter of Monte Cassino, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Vivian [alternatively, Malfred], formerly bishop of Palestrina, of good memory, recognizing, as a prudent, circumspect, and God-fearing man, from whom [Col. 1161C] and through whom, after God, he had what he had, left us in his last will a golden panel which he had acquired from your monastery. We, however, carefully observing the marvellous and delightful workmanship of that panel, and considering that, since it had belonged to your monastery, it was more fitting and beneficial that it should be given to that monastery rather than to others, donate your panel to your monastery for your honour, for our salvation and that of the aforesaid bishop, and out of reverence for blessed Benedict. Under pain of anathema, we forbid anyone to presume to take it from that monastery or alienate it by sale, gift, pledge, or any other means; rather, it shall be kept there permanently for the honour of yourselves [Col. 1161D] and of blessed Benedict, and for the adornment of that monastery. And so that the excommunication which we pronounce in this matter may become known to all, we will and command that these letters remain with that panel as long as they endure.

Given at Anagni, on the third day before the Kalends of February [30 January].

**MCCCXXXVII. To Hugh, bishop of Terracina—Confirms his statutes concerning the discipline of the canons.** (22 February.)

[CONTATORE, *History of Terracina*, book III, p. 371.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HUGH, bishop, and his beloved sons, the canons of Terracina, present and future, in perpetuity: greeting and apostolic blessing.

For the praise and glory of our Saviour Jesus [Col. 1162A] Christ, and also for the advancement of the churches themselves in spiritual as well as temporal matters, . . . it is fitting for us to confirm by apostolic authority those things established by useful and honourable provision, so that, when they have been . . . strengthened by apostolic . . . they may remain in their condition inviolate and unshaken, and may be increased in many ways in the service of the divine majesty. . . . From the rescript which you, brother bishop, sent us, and from the report of your canons Peter and Leo, we have fully understood this: that you, considering . . . it fitting that each cleric of that church, living in his own house as a layman, could obtain no or little profit . . . established and decreed that there should be neither more nor fewer than sixteen canons there, [Col. 1162B] to whom all the ancient possessions . . . vineyards, gardens, fisheries, common mills, and . . . the fishery called Strunzola . . .; by you and the whole chapter, another suitable person from that church or elsewhere shall be appointed, and the person who is to be substituted . . . shall be received as a subdeacon.

It was further established that you or your successors should have power concerning possessions acquired or to be acquired . . . except in certain cases described by the sacred canons, namely, small plots of land, little vineyards, and small houses, the price of which, for the benefit of the Church, . . . It was also ordained that you, sons, canons, eating with the bishop, should sleep together, so that you might serve the Lord more devotedly. . . . We decree [Col. 1162C] further that you, brother bishop, shall have only six servants, namely a cellarer, a baker, . . . who shall serve the canons faithfully. From episcopal right you shall have six riding-horses, and you, sons, canons, two, to be purchased from the revenue of the mills and assigned to the service of the canonry; and both those riding-horses and those of the bishop shall be maintained from the common fund. For administration . . . two shall be appointed from among you, sons, canons, of whom one shall manage the internal care and the other govern the external. Likewise, that the fisheries and mills . . . of the bishop and canons be distributed for the clothing and shoes of the labourers. Furthermore, . . . which . . . your predecessor retained in your hands, you bestowed upon that same canonry, in which, by one of the priests, the divine offices, or by [Col. 1162D] . . . they may serve the Lord continually. Moreover, each of you, sons, canons, owes one day’s labour in flax, with the church’s oxen, on the possessions of that church, for clothing . . .; he shall harvest and manage it at his own expense.

Therefore, that the matters stated may remain firm in their constitution and ordinance for all time . . . we confirm them by the authority of the apostolic see and fortify them with the protection of this present writing. We also will that you shall have free election of your bishop . . . without any impediment whatever, decreeing that no one there, by any artifice of fraud or violence, . . . whom you shall, by common consent or by the sounder part of the counsel, in the fear of God, provide as one to be elected.

Given . . . by the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 1163A] Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of March [22 February], in the second indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the nineteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

**MCCCXXXVIII. Takes the church of Linköping under protection and confirms its goods and possessions.** (Lateran, 17 March.)

[LILJEGREN, *Swedish Diplomatarium*, I, 98.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother COLON, bishop of Linköping, and to his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity: greeting and apostolic blessing.

By the duty of the apostolate laid upon us, we must love our brethren and fellow bishops, both near and far, with sincere charitable affection, [Col. 1163B] and ensure that the churches in which they are known to serve God are more abundantly sustained by the protection of the same, and heard in their reasonable petitions. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, bishop, we assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid church of Linköping, over which by God’s authority you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through the Lord’s provision, shall remain firm [Col. 1163C] and inviolate to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to name expressly:

The residence at Linköping with its appurtenances; Munkabodha with its appurtenances; Normalosa with its appurtenances; the residence near Skänninge with its appurtenances; Forsa with its appurtenances; the residence at Hesleby with its appurtenances; residences in Öland with their appurtenances; residences in Möre with their appurtenances; in Njudung, Kepstachd with its appurtenances, Wydesrydh with its appurtenances; in Finnveden, Lokarydh with its appurtenances, Skoparydh with its appurtenances, Kens with its appurtenances, Westruse with its appurtenances, Buddathorp with its appurtenances; in Tjust, Tyrkilsthorp with its appurtenances.

[Col. 1163D]

We decree therefore, etc.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April [17 March], in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1177 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the nineteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

**MCCCXXXIX. To Peter, cardinal of St Chrysogonus, legate of the apostolic see—That he is to convey to the pope the candlesticks and silver cup of the deceased bishop of Porto.** (Lateran, 27 March.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 970.]

Since W[illiam], formerly bishop of Porto, of good memory, deposited at the church of Limoges twenty-four candlesticks and a silver cup [Col. 1164A] weighing fourteen marks, gilded inside and out, we will and command that, through your prudent and discreet messenger, you cause these items, and any others of the goods of that bishop which are in their possession, to be requested as speedily as possible from our beloved sons the dean, archdeacon, and canons of that church, or also from the abbot of St Martial. If you are to return to us, bring to us the things you receive; but if you are not to return to us very soon, do not delay in placing them with our beloved son, the abbot of St German of Paris [perhaps: depositing them there]. For we have instructed them not to delay in handing over to you, or to your designated messenger, the aforesaid cup, the candlesticks, and any other goods of the aforesaid [Col. 1164B] bishop which they possess.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of April [27 March].

**MCCCXL. Takes the church of Reggio under protection and confirms the goods and rights of its canons.** (Lateran, 5 April.)

[MURATORI, *Italian Antiquities*, V, 251.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JAMES, archdeacon, and the canons of the church of Reggio, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized as suited to religion and honour, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and give fitting support to the petitioners’ wishes. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, [Col. 1164C] we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree, etc., and have thought fit to name expressly:

The court-estate of St Stephen with every right pertaining to it; its parish church, with the full integrity of its dignity; land at Civitate, situated in the parish of Quarantule; the land belonging to you at Trecentula; the tithes of four holdings at Fabrica; the tithes of Nuvellaria and its parish church, with everything wholly belonging to that parish; land belonging to you at Campagnola; everything you have in the court-estate of Canole; [Col. 1164D] whatever belongs to you in the court-estate of Corrigie; what John Burdonus holds at Curviatico by right of your canonry; the holding of Moronus at Nuvellaria; the holding of Bazoarius situated in the court-estate of Nova; the land of Fredulfinus of Gurgo; the holding situated at Bagnolo; and whatever the Ildebrandi hold at Massenzatico; two holdings at the place called Pinizo, and one at the place called Magnum Casale; the court-estate of Ripa Alta with its parish church and tithes; the land you hold at Cubiliolo and Mutilena; a holding at Albineto, a holding at Alliano, holdings at Querzola, a holding at Castelliunculo near the castle of Gipsi, and certain land near the fortress of Timbertus; the court-estate of Massa in its entirety; the court-estate of Campilia [Col. 1165A] with everything wholly belonging to it; likewise the small court-estate of Villa, the village called Visiliaco, whatever belongs to you at the place called Goa, the holding at Minotio, and what belongs to you at Castelli, Montebluto, and Gasulis; the tithes of Gavassa and the tithes at Runcori of the same Gavassa in Manipuli; and what you acquired there from Gerard Rangone.

Further, we confirm the tithes of your city and its dependencies, as you possess them by ancient custom and canonical right; likewise the offerings of the faithful, at masses for the living and the dead, whether the bishop is present or absent, both in the city and outside it; also the offerings from consecrations of churches in your bishopric, both within and outside the city, as you have reasonably been accustomed to have them and are known to have them now. [Col. 1165B] Further, everything pertaining to the office and benefice of the archpriesthood, archdeaconry, provostship, and master of schools of that church.

We decree therefore, etc.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of April [5 April], in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1178 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the nineteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

**MCCCXLI. Confirms various constitutions and privileges of the church and chapter of St Omer in Artois.** (16 April.)

[MIRAEUS, *Diplomatic Works*, IV, 28.]

[Col. 1165C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WILLIAM, dean of St Omer, and his brethren, present and future, professing the canonical life, in perpetuity.

. . . Following in the footsteps of Innocent and Adrian, Roman pontiffs of blessed memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid church of St Omer, in which you are devoted to divine service and where, namely, his venerable body is believed to rest. . . .

Concerning the revenues and small prebends belonging to the hospital of the poor, we decree that, when those who presently receive them die, [Col. 1165D] they shall be granted by neither provost, dean, chapter, nor anyone else to clerics or laymen, but, when vacant, shall be assigned solely to the table of the poor in the hospital, to serve that use perpetually. . . .

When the provost or dean of your church dies, no one may be appointed there through any fraudulent device or violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, in the fear of God, shall provide to be elected. . . .

We confirm by the present document the good and reasonable customs hitherto maintained in your church, and forbid anyone to impose new and improper customs upon you against your will. The subprovost, master of schools, baker, [Col. 1166A] cellarer, and cook—the ministers or officials of that church—shall be appointed by the dean, as is customary, after consultation with and with the assent of the canons residing in the same town. They are not to be as possessors, but interchangeable annually, as the canons judge expedient.

The custodian, called the minister, shall always remain subject to appointment by the provost, dean, and chapter, because the ornaments of the church are in his charge. If the aforesaid ministers commit any offence, they shall be corrected by the dean and chapter according to the custom of the Church.

Furthermore, we decree that, as was established by Milo, first bishop of Thérouanne, of good memory, the bishop of Thérouanne shall become a canon in the church of St Omer, and the provost of St Omer a canon in that of Thérouanne, on account of a prebend. [Col. 1166B] That is, at each death of the persons concerned, the new successor—whether a provost invested by the bishop or a bishop invested by the provost—shall without delay be invested with the prebend of the deceased, saving nevertheless the right to the anniversary; nor shall the bishop for that reason be admitted to the counsel of your chapter.

Given, etc., on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May [16 April], in the year 1178.

**MCCCXLII. Takes the monastery of Cluny under protection and confirms its possessions.** (Lateran, 17 April.)

[*Bibliotheca Cluniacensis*, 1436.]

[Col. 1166C]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, etc.

The more specially your Church is subject to us without intermediary, the more diligently we are bound to provide for its rights, lest in the course of time it be burdened by improper harassment concerning matters which it is known to possess lawfully. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, your church, in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future acquire by grant of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, [Col. 1166D] offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through the Lord’s aid, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. Moreover, we confirm by apostolic authority to you and that Church the priory of St Mary of Nazara with all its appurtenances, and the priory of the Holy Trinity of Lentona with all their appurtenances, as your Church canonically possesses those priories, and as is contained in an authentic written instrument concerning the donation of the aforesaid priory of St Mary.

We decree therefore, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, John, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. [Col. 1167A] I, Bozo, priest-cardinal of St Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St Susanna. I, Vivian, priest-cardinal of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, James, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ardicio, deacon-cardinal of St Theodoric. I, Cincius, deacon-cardinal of St Adrian. I, Laborans, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Portico. I, Rainerius, deacon-cardinal of St George at the Golden Veil.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 1167B] on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May [17 April], in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1178 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the nineteenth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

**MCCCXLIII. To Roger, bishop of Worcester—Concerning the elect of the church of St Augustine, Canterbury.** (Lateran, 17 April.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 920.]

Since we formerly instructed our venerable brother Richard, archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the apostolic see, not to delay in granting the blessing to our beloved son, the elect of St Augustine, in his monastery, which belongs directly to the jurisdiction of the Roman Church, [Col. 1167C] and since the archbishop refused to carry this out, we could rightly have conferred that blessing upon the elect ourselves, or through another who would not so readily oppose us. Yet, wishing still more fully to test in this matter the virtue of obedience, after the lengthy dispute which the same archbishop, through his messengers, had before us against that elect concerning the controversy over the blessing—and which was decided by a definitive sentence with the common counsel of our brethren, namely: that the archbishop of Canterbury should bless him and his successors in the monastery of St Augustine, without exaction and setting aside the objection of obedience—we have thought fit, out of the customary and abundant benignity of the apostolic see, to refer the same elect back to the aforesaid archbishop for the blessing. [Col. 1167D]

Considering, therefore, the labours and expenses which that monastery has already endured for a long time in this affair, we command and enjoin upon your brotherhood by apostolic letters and in virtue of obedience that, if the aforesaid archbishop delays to bless the same elect within the period fixed by our letters, as we have determined, you, relying on our authority and setting aside every excuse, objection, and appeal, shall, as soon as you are asked concerning this matter, not delay to carry it out. No decree of ours or another’s which enjoins deference to an appeal, and no letters obtained or to be obtained from us, may obstruct you; nor may any exception resist your fulfillment of our mandate, or cause you to fulfill it less fully or more slowly. [Col. 1168A]

Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May [17 April].

**MCCCXLIV. To Roger, elect of the monastery of St Augustine, Canterbury—Testifies that he has decreed that he and his successors shall be consecrated by the archbishops in that monastery.**

(TWISDEN and SELDEN, *Writers of English Affairs*, II, 1822.)

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ROGER, elect, and the brethren of St Augustine, Canterbury, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Having formerly received your complaint that [Col. 1168B] our venerable brother, the archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the apostolic see, was unwilling to confer upon you, son elect, the blessing in your monastery, which belongs directly to the jurisdiction of the Roman Church, we instructed the same archbishop by apostolic letters either to bless you, son elect, in the aforesaid monastery without requiring a profession, or to appear before us by himself or through a sufficient representative by the recently past feast of the Purification. And when both you, son elect, and our beloved sons Master Gerard Pucelle and Master Peter of Blois, procurators of that archbishop, came before us concerning this cause, [Col. 1168C] and held a long dispute with one another in our presence, they asserting that you ought to be blessed by the archbishop in the church of Canterbury and render him obedience, while you, on the other hand, maintained that he ought to confer the blessing in your monastery without requiring obedience: after examining the ancient privileges granted to your church, especially the privilege granted to your monastery by blessed Augustine, archbishop of Canterbury; after considering also the writings of our predecessors of pious memory, Anastasius and Adrian, Roman pontiffs, upon which that archbishop seemed to rely; and having learned that our father and predecessor of holy memory, Pope Eugenius, had enjoined upon Theobald, formerly archbishop [Col. 1168D] of Canterbury, that he should confer the blessing upon Sylvester, formerly elect of your monastery, in that monastery, without requiring from him a profession of obedience: with the counsel of our brethren, we absolve you from the claim of that archbishop. We decree that the archbishop of Canterbury shall bless you and your successors in your monastery without exaction, setting aside the objection of obedience. And so that this ruling of our decision may be observed inviolate for all time, we confirm it by apostolic authority and fortify it by the document of this present writing. Therefore no one at all, etc.

Given, etc.

**MCCCXLV. To Richard, archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the apostolic see—Notifies him concerning the foregoing letters.**

(Ibid., p. 1822.)

[Col. 1169A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the archbishop, legate of the apostolic see, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When our beloved sons, the elect of Blessed Augustine of Canterbury, Master G. Pucelle, and Master P. of Blois, your clerics, had come before us concerning the dispute between you and that elect over the blessing to be bestowed upon him, and many varied and diverse arguments had been advanced in our hearing both for you and for the other party, after examining the privileges granted by Roman pontiffs to the church [Col. 1169B] of Blessed Augustine, especially the privilege which blessed Augustine, archbishop of Canterbury, granted to that monastery; after also considering the writings of Anastasius and Adrian, Roman pontiffs of pious memory, on which you seemed to rely; and having learned that our father and predecessor of holy memory, Pope Eugenius, had enjoined upon Theobald, formerly archbishop of Canterbury, that he should confer the blessing upon Sylvester, formerly elect of the monastery of St Augustine, without requiring from him a profession: with the counsel of our brethren, we absolve that elect from the claim of you and your successors. We decree that the archbishop of Canterbury for the time being shall henceforth bless the elect in the church of Blessed Augustine [Col. 1169C] without requiring obedience.

Therefore, by apostolic letters, we command and enjoin upon your brotherhood in virtue of obedience that you shall bless the aforesaid elect in his monastery, requiring no obedience. But if, within thirty days after you have been requested concerning this matter, you perhaps refuse to bless him, we have instructed our venerable brother, the bishop of Worcester, that, relying on apostolic authority and notwithstanding any objection or appeal, he shall bless him.

**MCCCXLVI. Takes the church of Cefalù [Cephaloedium] under protection and confirms its possessions, privileges, and rights.** (Rome, at St Peter’s, 25 April.)

[PIRRI, *Sacred Sicily*, II, 803.]

[Col. 1169D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GUIDO, bishop of Cefalù, and to his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

By the duty of the apostolate laid upon us, etc. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, bishop, we graciously assent to your just requests, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the church of Cefalù, over which by God’s authority you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future acquire by grant of pontiffs, [Col. 1170A] bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through the Lord’s aid, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to name expressly:

The city of Cefalù itself, as granted by the illustrious kings of Sicily, with all its appurtenances; the hamlet of Pollina with all its appurtenances; whatever the noblewoman Adelasia, niece of Roger, formerly illustrious king of blessed memory, lawfully bestowed upon that church, as is contained in authentic instruments drawn up concerning it; the benefices of Collesano, Calatafimi, Polizzi, and Mistretta; the church of St Nicholas of Malvicino, as John of Bruccato held it, with all its possessions [Col. 1170B] and appurtenances; the church of St Nicholas of Camerata, situated at Polizzi, with all possessions called *Tertiariae*; the church of St Lucy of Syracuse with its hamlets and appurtenances; the church of St Mary of Camerata with all its possessions and appurtenances; the church of St Mary of Gibilmanna with all its possessions and appurtenances; the church of St Conus of Grattera with all its possessions and appurtenances; the church of St John of Roccella with all its possessions and appurtenances; and the church of St Saviour of Capiccio with all its possessions and appurtenances.

Likewise, we confirm by apostolic authority to that church the diocese with its tithes [Col. 1170C] and every episcopal right, as it was granted to the church entrusted to you: namely, the aforesaid city of Cefalù with all its appurtenances; Alcusa with its appurtenances; Gratteri with its appurtenances; Rocca d’Atini with its appurtenances; Tusa with its appurtenances; Pollina with its appurtenances; and [the territory] from where the river Tortae begins and descends to the sea as far as Cefalù.

Furthermore, we decree and establish by the page of this writing that the prior of St. Gregory of Grattera, and the churches situated in the diocese, may not dare, on account of the temporal service in respect of which they are known to answer to others, to withhold from you obedience in spiritual matters. Moreover, we hold ratified and firm the lawful grants made to the aforesaid church by Roger and William, kings of Sicily of illustrious memory, [Col. 1170D] and strengthen them by apostolic authority. We also confirm by this present privilege the reasonable immunities and liberties granted to you and your successors by the aforesaid illustrious kings of Sicily. We likewise decree that no archbishop or bishop may be permitted to harass you and the house entrusted to you by undue and unaccustomed vexations or burdens. We add and enjoin by apostolic authority that no one may receive into religious conversion the canons or lay brethren (*conversi*) of your church without the consent of you or your successors, unless one should wish to transfer to a stricter Rule. We further hold ratified and firm, and confirm by apostolic authority, the ordinance which, with the common counsel [Col. 1171A] and consent of your chapter, you are known to have made concerning the appointment of priests in the place of deceased canons, for the salvation of the departed. We prohibit anyone within your bishopric from daring to build anew a church or oratory without the consent of you or your successors, without prejudice to the privileges of the Roman pontiffs.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for absolutely no person to rashly disturb the aforesaid church, etc. Saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical reverence due to the archbishop of Messina. If anyone therefore in future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, of Pammachius. [Col. 1171B] I, Boso, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Theodore. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Susanna. I, James, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Adrian, deacon-cardinal of the title of St. Theodore. I, Sancius, deacon-cardinal of the title of St. Adrian. I, Liberius, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Portico. I, Dianerius [Rainerius], deacon-cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, 25 April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1178, and in the nineteenth year of the pontificate of lord [Col. 1171C] Pope Alexander III.

### MCCCXLVII. Confirms to the canons of St. Euphemia on the Island of Cuma certain tithes and all their possessions.  
(Rome, at St. Peter’s, 25 April.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 296.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of St. Euphemia on the Cuman Island: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have inspected an authentic document, through which it became known to us that L., bishop of Cuma, of blessed memory, ordained that at least during two seasons of the year—namely, from the Advent of the Lord until Christmas, and throughout the whole of Lent—you ought to assemble together and [Col. 1171D] apply yourselves more diligently to the service due to the Lord. So that you might be better able to fulfil this obligation, he granted you certain tithes in pious consideration, and decreed that as many brethren should be assembled in your church as those same tithes would suffice to support with food during the two Lents of the year, and, if possible, on Sundays and feast days; and that no one should at any time be admitted into your community without the election of the brethren. Therefore we prohibit this ordinance of his, made in this respect by the foresight of the aforesaid bishop, as is known, from being violated by anyone’s presumption; and we confirm to you and to your church by apostolic authority those tithes themselves, just as you canonically [Col. 1172A] possess them by grant of the said bishop.

Moreover, by this present writing we strictly forbid anyone, because the fortress in which you had been accustomed to reside has been destroyed, to dare to divide your unity and brotherhood under pretext of hostility, or to take away or diminish your goods or chapels. Rather, we decree that henceforth you shall possess everything just as you held it by right before the destruction of the fortress. We further add that, if it should happen that your church is transferred to some place belonging to your people, or rebuilt in the place where it stood, you shall nevertheless retain the privileges of the old church, the possessions granted to it, its ordinances, and the reasonable customs which you were entitled to have in the old church. Nor may anyone be set over you beyond the established and customary [Col. 1172B] number—namely, twelve brethren—unless the possessions increase so greatly that the number of brethren ought deservedly to be enlarged. We likewise confirm to you the regulations concerning your people, just as you have hitherto held them reasonably. Therefore let absolutely no person, etc.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, 25 April.

### MCCCXLVIII. Confirms the privilege established by Eugenius III for the canons of the Church of St. Peter at Rome.  
[Note: [Col. 1171] See *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXX, col. 1588, under Eugenius III.]  
(Rome, at St. Peter’s, 25 April.)

[*Bullarium Vaticanum*, collection of bulls of the most holy Vatican basilica. Rome, 1747, folio, vol. I, p. 64.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1172C] sons JOHN, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul and archpriest of the Church of Blessed Peter, and to the other canons of that church, both present and future, canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

The fellowship of the blessed Peter and Paul is so exalted, so glorious, that both are teachers of the nations, authors of martyrs, and princes of priests. And although they surpass all the apostles by a certain special prerogative, they do not experience in heaven any inequality of merits in their equality [variant reading: “being made equal”]. To Peter, by our very Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, were entrusted the keys of the kingdom of heaven; Paul was chosen by God to fill the kingdom of heaven with the multitude of the nations through [Col. 1172D] his preaching. Peter is the rock and foundation of faith, and supports us firmly in its solidity so that we may not fall. Paul, lest we be wounded by the perverse doctrine of heretics, arms us with moral uprightness and the invincible reasoning of faith. Peter, holding primacy, binds and looses by authority; Paul, a loving preacher, by wonderful exhortation fortifies us beforehand, lest anything blameworthy or deserving of binding appear in us. Peter is our support and the house of strength; planted and rooted in his faith, we stand. Paul, the vessel of election, called those predestined and chosen by God with the sounding of the heavenly trumpet; and, praying for us without ceasing, he protects us by interceding with God, lest we [Col. 1173A] depart from faith and truth.

Since, therefore, these two greatest lights, illuminating God’s Church with equal and friendly splendor and with brotherly love, shine forth, the principle of equity and justice persuades us that we—although unworthy, yet acting on earth in Christ’s place and seen to sit in the chair of the prince of the same Apostles—should love the household of Blessed Peter with a fatherly affection and assist it with pious provision in its needs. Moved, then, by the obligation of this consideration, beloved sons in the Lord, following the example of our fathers and predecessors of holy memory, Eugenius and Adrian, Roman pontiffs, we grant you, with the consent of our brother bishops and cardinals, by authority of the Apostolic See, and confirm by the page of this present document, a fourth part of all offerings which arise from the altar of the same blessed Apostle Peter, both from the Ark and from all [Col. 1173B] the ministries of that church, except for the ministry of Blessed Leo. That is, whenever you wish, you shall always have the free power to retain and keep the same offering in your own hands, or, with the consent of us and our successors, to sell it to any persons you wish; while in all other respects the free disposition and custody of that church remains reserved in the hands of us and our successors.

We have judged it fitting to do this so that you, laboring diligently day and night in the praises of God—in celebrating Masses, in singing Matins, and in rendering the other Hours with care and propriety for the salvation of the living [Col. 1173C] and the dead—may honor the aforesaid Church of Blessed Peter with the service owed to it, and that the faithful of God, visiting the thresholds of the Apostles with due devotion, may always hold that place in greater devotion and reverence.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly infringe the page of this our grant or disturb it in any manner. If anyone therefore in future, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, Boso, priest-cardinal of St. Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Mark. [Col. 1173D] I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Susanna. I, Vivianus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, James, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Cosmedin. Of St. Theodore. I, Ardicio, deacon-cardinal. I, Cinthius, deacon-cardinal of St. Adrian. I, Hugh, deacon-cardinal of St. Angel. I, Laborans, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Portico. [Col. 1174A] I, Rainerius, deacon-cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, 30 April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1777. [Note: [Col. 1173D] In place of 1177, one must read 1178: first, because Alexander III was absent from Rome in 1177, as may be seen in Pagi; and also because the nineteenth year of the pontificate of the same Alexander begins on 7 or 20 September 1177 and ends on 6 or 19 September 1178. Thus the last day of April in the nineteenth year of Alexander’s pontificate accords very well with [Col. 1174D] 1178, but can only with difficulty be reconciled with 1177. Furthermore, the eleventh indiction assigned to this diploma coincides with 1178.], and in the eighteenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCCXLIX. At the request of Bishop Berno, confirms the episcopal see of Schwerin and the possessions of its church.  
(Rome, at St. Peter’s.)

[*Origines Guelficae*, vol. III, preface, XLVII.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother BERNO, bishop of Magnopolis, [Note: [Col. 1174D] Magnopolis in Pontus, restored by Pompey the Great; first called Eupatoria after Mithridates, its founder; now Tchénikèh.] [Col. 1174B] and to his successors canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

Blessed is God in his gifts and holy in all his works: he continually makes his Church fruitful with new offspring, and, enlarging the Church’s bounds by the word of faithful preachers, does not cease in his mercy to draw even barbarian peoples into the net of faith. Thus, in accordance with the prophet’s word, “in the haunts where dragons and ostriches formerly dwelt,” when good preachers sow and you are watered by the grace of the Holy Spirit, “there shall spring up the verdure of reed and rush” (Isa. 35:7). Indeed, it is by the gift of him who wills all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of truth (1 Tim. 2:4) that you, venerable Berno in Christ, appointed bishop to preach to pagans and sow [Col. 1174C] the word of faith, have exposed yourself to labors and dangers. Considering that Christ died for us, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for us and rose again (2 Cor. 5:15), amid many distresses you scattered the seed of the divine word and put out at interest the talent entrusted to you; you enlightened with the light of truth many peoples who did not know the Lord, and brought them back to the worship of God, though before they had been held captive in the snares of the devil.

Now therefore, since you came to us with great labor and asked the Apostolic See that we should, by authority of the most holy Roman Church, which by God’s appointment we serve, [Col. 1174D] confirm the episcopal see in the place called Zuerin: concurring favorably with your petition, we decree that the pontifical chair shall remain forever in that place, and that the places written below shall henceforth be subject to it under diocesan law.

Namely: the cloister and churches built or to be built throughout the province of Duke Henry, which province extends from Zuerin on one side as far as Vepro; from Vepro it runs through Murz and Tolonze, reaching [Col. 1175A] Groswin and the river Ponem. Likewise, on the other side, from Zuerin it passes by the maritime districts, including the island of Bujani and half of the island of Rujan, and reaches the mouth of the aforesaid river Pene. By gift of the aforesaid duke: part of the island of Zuerin, according to the duke’s own division; one mill; and another island; in Sadelbande, one village; on the other side of the Albia, two villages; near Sturizche, another two villages; from the land of Pribeslai, the island called St. Mary’s and the village of Clive, with another ten villages in Ylo; the fortress of Butislo with the land of Altimenti, and four villages in the wilderness of Nohum, another five villages around Warin as far as Glambike, and beyond Nivele and Wolchza—all with the full consent of the aforesaid prince Pribeslai, together with every right and utility. The village of St. Godehard, [Col. 1175B] formerly called Goderach, by gift of Casemari, the most Christian prince; the land called Pitina and one noble village in Barth; two villages near Demin, and one in Circipene.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that church presently possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We decree, therefore, etc.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1177 [1178], and in the nineteenth year of the pontificate of lord [Col. 1175C] Pope Alexander III.

### MCCCL. Confirms a certain custom of the canons of the Church of Bremen.  
(Rome, at St. Peter’s, 1 May.)

[LAPPENBERG, *Hamburgische Urkunden*, I, 228.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Bremen: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to us that in your church it was established long ago by prudent deliberation that, when a canon dies, the revenues of his prebend should be collected for a year and spent either on his debts or for pious purposes [Col. 1175D] for his salvation. Therefore, because it is our duty to uphold pious and praiseworthy ordinances, holding the aforesaid constitution and custom ratified and confirming it as is fitting by apostolic authority, we command and enjoin your whole body by apostolic letters that whatever has been withheld from this custom by the senior provost or by any of your obedientiaries from the day on which Arduicus, formerly your archbishop, confirmed that custom to you by pontifical authority, you shall cause to be restored—without further occasion for or recourse to appeal—in order that it may be spent for the purposes which we have stated.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the Kalends of May [1 May].

### MCCCLI. Privilege for the monastery of St. Nicholas at Angers; given at the Lateran, 11 May.

(Abbey of St. Nicholas at Angers, according to Bréquigny, *Table chronologique*, III, 535.)

[Col. 1176A]

[Col. 1176A]

### MCCCLII. To Philip, archbishop of Cologne.—The rights and privileges of the Church of Cologne are confirmed.  
(Lateran, 19 June.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 909.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PHILIP, archbishop of Cologne, and to his successors canonically appointed: for canonical remembrance.

Although, by reason of the administration of the government entrusted to us, we are bound to extend apostolic protection to all our brethren and fellow bishops, [Col. 1176B] we are nevertheless especially obliged to assist those who stand out as much in virtue as in dignity; for it ought to be a matter of our care and circumspection that we appear to have regard for all persons according to their qualities and merits. Therefore, venerable brother archbishop in Christ, carefully considering your prudence and devotion, and readily assenting to your petitions, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the Church of Cologne, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever goods the same church presently possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings [Col. 1176C] of the faithful, or other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Moreover, considering your prudence and devotion, brother archbishop, we confirm to you those things contained in the privileges of our fathers and predecessors: namely, the cross and the pallium, to be borne at the proper time and place; likewise the insignia of the festal horse, called in the vernacular by some a *naccum*. We also grant and establish by apostolic authority that the high altar of your church, dedicated to the one true God in memory of the Blessed Virgin Mary, and the other altar dedicated in memory of Blessed Peter, prince of the Apostles, shall be served reverently by seven cardinal-priest canons, clad in dalmatics and adorned with mitres. We grant them also, together with an equal number of deacons and subdeacons prudently chosen for this ministry, permission to use sandals, as this was granted to the aforesaid church by authentic privileges of our fathers and predecessors and has hitherto been observed. Moreover, we confirm under the protection of apostolic favor the authority and honor which your church is known hitherto to have possessed: namely, that whenever a synod is convened within your diocese by the Roman pontiff or by a legate sent from his side, the archbishop of Cologne shall hold the first place in the synod after him and shall be first in pronouncing the authority of the sacred canons; provided, however, [Col. 1177A] that, as he is first, he may excel in uprightness of life and in the grace of merits, and may imitate in conduct the examples of him whose words he proclaims. We further ratify by authority of this document the consecration of kings to be performed within the boundaries of your diocese; and by the page of this writing we decree that the election of the archbishop shall be held, according to the statutes of the canons, by the sons [canons] of the aforesaid church.

Furthermore, we confirm by apostolic authority to you and your successors: the monasteries, churches situated in Cologne, and all holy places within and around the city of Cologne which belong to the jurisdiction of the Church of Cologne; the mint of the aforesaid city, its toll, market, and all civil jurisdiction, to be under the power of you and your successors; the abbeys in various places, villages, hamlets, and castles, with all their appurtenances—namely, male and female serfs, cultivated and uncultivated lands, waters, meadows, fields, woods, forests; likewise the assemblies in Westphalia popularly called *Gograrhophe*, and the allodial estates of Dulberg, Hachen, Marchan, and Wassemberg—as you reasonably possess all these things. We also decree that, just as none of your archbishops is subject to you, so you ought not to be subject to any primate; while preserving, however, the subjection owed to us in your case, as in that of the other archbishops, to apostolic authority.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, [Col. 1177C] or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the use and in every respect to the benefit of those for whose government and support they were granted, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See. If any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act contrary to this page of our constitution, and, after a second or third warning, does not make suitable satisfaction and correction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the wrong committed, be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer, and be subject at the last judgment to divine vengeance. But may all who preserve the rights of that church have the peace of our Lord [Col. 1177D] Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Place of the seal.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Boso, priest-cardinal of St. Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Susanna. I, Hubaldus, bishop of Ostia. I, Hyacinthus, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Arditio, deacon-cardinal of St. Theodore. [Col. 1178A] I, Cynthius, deacon-cardinal of St. Adrian. I, Hugh, deacon-cardinal of St. Angel.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, 19 June, in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1178, and in the nineteenth year of the pontificate of lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCCCLIII. Takes the monastery of St. Geremarus under protection, enumerates and confirms its goods and possessions.  
(Lateran, 20 June.)

[LOUVET, *History and Antiquities of Beauvaisis*, I, 453.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot of the monastery of St. Geremarus [Col. 1178B] of Flavacourt, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, so that we may love religious persons and strive in every way to advance the religious life pleasing to God. For no service is ever rendered acceptably to God unless it proceeds from the root of charity and is preserved in purity of religious observance. Therefore all lovers of the Christian faith ought to love the religious life and more attentively support venerable places together with the persons devoted to divine service, so that they may not be harassed by the molestations of wicked persons or oppressive exactions. [Col. 1178C]

Accordingly, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests. Following the example of our father and predecessor of holy memory, Pope Eugenius, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. First of all, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been established in that monastery according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery presently possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings [Col. 1178D] of the faithful, or other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to name expressly the following:

The place itself on which the aforesaid monastery is built, with all its appurtenances. At Calvimont: the church of St. Mary of Alteria with its dependencies; the church of Serandis with its dependencies; the church of Jambeville with its dependencies; the church of St. Peter of Guppillariis with its dependencies and the tithes of its fields in the Forest of Lyons; the church of the Sepulchre of Villers with its dependencies; the church of St. John of Viviers with its dependencies; the church of St. Remigius near Clermont, with [Col. 1179A] its dependencies; the church of St. Martin of Count Brevolio with its dependencies; the church of St. Martin of the other Bruolio with its dependencies; the village of Ruates with its dependencies; whatever right you have in the village of Fulcheriae, the village of Gres, the village of Spalburg, the village of Monasterol, and their churches; the church of St. Medard of Lord Medard, with its dependencies; the church of St. Peter of Goy with its dependencies; the church of St. Walaric of Allodium with its dependencies; the church of St. Peter of Gamaches with its dependencies; the church of St. Waleric of Breio with its dependencies; the church of St. Mary of Pisce with its dependencies; the church of St. Clement of Lomariis with its dependencies; the church of St. Peter of Fraxinomont with its dependencies; [Col. 1179B] the church of St. Mary of Constanillar with its dependencies; the church of Amoldimont, with two shares of the great and small tithe; and, before the tithes are divided, you first receive for your own use one *modius* from those same tithes, together with two tenants there.
