Parties are formed in different directions and cannot agree upon the same person. Therefore, pursuing with due favour your desire for a remedy in this matter, lest religious houses should more grievously collapse through lack of a pastor—which may the Lord avert—we grant you by these present letters that, whenever any monastery within your jurisdiction falls vacant, and the brethren or sisters of that place cannot, upon your admonition, agree within a suitable period, to be fixed by you, upon a suitable person, it shall be lawful for you by apostolic authority to confirm as abbot or abbess the suitable person upon whom you know the greater and sounder part of the chapter agrees [Col. 1207B].

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of March.

### MCCCXCIV. To the abbot and chapter of St. Bertin of Sithiu.—That there shall be two priests in the parish church of Broburg. (Lateran, February 19.)

[*Collection des Cartulaires*, III, 352.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved abbot of St. Bertin: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has been reported to us that, although your church of Broburg ought, by ancient custom, to have two priests in its service, and although [Col. 1207C] one priest is insufficient for its administration, certain persons are urgently demanding that you entrust it to a single priest. Unwilling, therefore, to permit the aforesaid church to be deprived of its customary service, we forbid you by apostolic authority to allow it to be content with the ministry of one man. Rather, in accordance with ancient and reasonable custom, you shall always assign two priests to its service; yet one must be subject to the other, in accordance with canonical ordinances.

Given at the Lateran, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of March.

### MCCCXCV. To the same.—Copy of the confirmation of two portions of the tithe of Lolinghem, belonging to a certain knight of Watinis. (Lateran, February 19.)

[Ibid., p. 353.]

[Col. 1207D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and chapter of St. Bertin: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever the Apostolic See is asked for something consistent with justice and consonant with propriety, it is fitting readily to grant consent to the honourable desires of petitioners and to bring their requests to fulfilment. Moved, therefore, by this consideration and acceding to your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority to you and to that monastery the two portions of the tithe of Lulinghem adjudged to your monastery, and the marsh given to you as alms by G., knight of Watenis, as you reasonably possess them; and [Col. 1208A] we strengthen them by the protection of this present document. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this document of our confirmation or rashly act against it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he shall incur the indignation of almighty God and of His apostles, the blessed Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of March.

### MCCCXCVI. To the same.—Copy of the confirmation concerning the tithes of Varancies. (Lateran, February 27.)

[Ibid., p. 351.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and brethren of St. Bertin: greeting [Col. 1208B] and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we should readily grant consent to the just desires of petitioners and, by bringing them to fulfilment, accomplish requests which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the tithes of Warancies, as you justly and peacefully possess them, and strengthen them by the protection of this present document. We decree that no one whatsoever may infringe this document of our confirmation or rashly act against it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he shall incur the indignation of almighty God and of His apostles, the blessed Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1208C] Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of March.

### MCCCXCVII. To the same.—That no archbishop, bishop, or any other person may pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict in churches subject to their jurisdiction. (Lateran, March 2.)

[Ibid., p. 352.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and brethren of St. Bertin: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The care of the government entrusted to us leads us effectively to hear the petitions of religious persons which accord with reason, so that they may rejoice that they have obtained from us what ought to be done in favour of religion. [Col. 1208D] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously acceding to your just petitions, we grant you by apostolic authority that no one may pronounce a sentence of interdict in churches subject to your jurisdiction, unless there is a manifest cause, or a cause proved by canonical judgment.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth Nones of March.

### MCCCXCVIII. To the same.—That they are not bound to confer prebends upon laymen. (Lateran, March 3.)

[Ibid., p. 351.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and brethren of St. Bertin: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1209A] We wish and ought readily to grant assent to the just petitions of religious men, so that they may devote themselves more vigorously to divine service and to the observance of their profession when they see that they are more promptly heard by the Apostolic See. Wishing, therefore, that provisions piously bestowed upon your house may be reserved for the use of those who, by the Lord’s inspiration, profess the regular life there, we grant you by apostolic authority that henceforth you shall not be obliged to confer a prebend in your monastery upon any layman or secular clerk.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth Nones of March.

### MCCCXCIX. He receives the monastery of St. Blaise of the Black Forest under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, March 6.)

[Gerbert, *History of the Black Forest*, III, 102.]

[Col. 1209B]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son THEODEBERT, abbot of the monastery of St. Blaise of the Black Forest, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

The care of the universal Church has been entrusted to us by God, the provider of all good things, in order that we may love religious persons and endeavour by every means to advance religion pleasing to God. For service is never rendered acceptably to God unless it proceeds from the root of charity and is preserved in the purity of religion. All lovers of the Christian faith ought therefore to cherish religion [Col. 1209C] and diligently support venerable places, together with the persons dedicated in them to divine service, so that they may not be troubled by the vexations of wicked men or wearied by oppressive exactions. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests; and, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Urban, Calixtus, Honorius, Innocent, and Adrian, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery of St. Blaise, built in the diocese of Constance in the place called the Black Forest.

First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order established in that monastery according to the Lord and the Rule of blessed Benedict [Col. 1209D] shall be inviolably observed there for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s provision, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is built, with all its appurtenances; the church of Bataimaringin, with the church subject to it; Steina; Brombach; Richoceim, with a portion of its [Col. 1210A] tithes and the rent of the lands in the cemetery of Wisentowa; Grishaeim; Sneisham; Chilctorf; Sthatlinchowin; Wilare; Omingin, with half the tithes; Imeindingin, with all tithes except those of sacred land; the right which you possess in the church of Frikingin, with a third part of the tithes both of the estates and of the fields; Sconowa, newly built on your newly cleared land, with all tithes acquired in the same district of Sconowa; Gundiswane; Blochingin; Burron; Brunnon; Nallingin, with a portion of the tithes; Luwingin, with portions of the summer tithes and of the estates; Entilibuoch; Nuvillacho; Walmundisrieth; Loppinhausun; Nunchilcha; Ronti; Tongingin; Hogenilo; Outenwilla; and the other churches which you reasonably possess with their appurtenances.

[Col. 1210B] Reinstetin, with tithes justly acquired from the brethren of Rote Carubitis and from laymen; Mittilhuoch; Tanhaeim; Orsinhusin; Wolpach; Wiurimos; and other churches with their appurtenances; the cell of Berowa, with the churches belonging to it—that is, Berowa, Swercin, Nuchilcha, and the other churches of that cell; the cell of Witinowa, with its churches of Wisilat and Etermiberch; the cell of Burgulum, with its churches of Eggenheim, Sicenchilcha, and Chaltinbach, together with every right and authority in tithes and in other matters which Hermann, formerly bishop of Constance of good memory, is known reasonably to have granted to the monks of Burgulum and confirmed by his charter; likewise the cell of Wizilinchovin with its appurtenances.

[Col. 1210C] Certainly, no one whatsoever may presume to demand tithes from you on lands newly brought under cultivation which you till by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals. You may also receive into conversion clerks or laymen fleeing from the world, free and unbound, and retain them in your monastery without anyone’s opposition. Furthermore, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, to leave that place without the permission of his abbot, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; nor may anyone dare retain a departing monk without letters of authorization from your community. We also decree that, in the parish churches which you hold, you shall choose suitable priests [Col. 1210D] and present them to the bishop. If they are suitable, the bishop shall entrust the care of souls to them without objection, so that they may render account to the bishop for the care of the people, while showing you due subjection in temporal matters belonging to that monastery.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars and churches, the ordinations of monks to be advanced to sacred orders, and other things belonging to the episcopal office from the bishop of Constance, in whose diocese you are, provided that he is Catholic, possesses the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to supply these freely and without any improper demand. Otherwise, you may approach whatever Catholic bishop you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration [Col. 1211A]; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested.

We also decree that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who desire to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

Moreover, we confirm to you the ordinance concerning the liberty and advocacy of your monastery established by Henry IV, emperor of good memory, by King Lothair, and by King Conrad, and ratified by our predecessors of happy memory, Calixtus, Honorius, Innocent, and Adrian, Roman pontiffs, with the deliberation of bishops and cardinals: namely, that in the election of an advocate the abbot shall have free power [Col. 1211B]—with the counsel of his brethren—to choose such a person as he recognizes to be good and useful for defending the liberty of the monastery, one who desires to hold and administer that advocacy properly not for earthly advantage but for love of God, remission of sins, and the reward of eternal blessedness. But if he proves to be a harasser rather than an advocate, seizes the monastery’s goods instead of defending them, and does not amend after being admonished once, twice, or three times, the abbot shall have authority, with the counsel of the brethren, to appoint another advocate who ought to defend the monastery more usefully and faithfully.

Furthermore, as has been determined by judgment, the liberty of your monastery shall in every respect remain independent of the jurisdiction of the [Col. 1211C] Church of Basel. When a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and those under interdict, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed in authority there by any deceitful device or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, of Pammachius. [Col. 1211D] I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Anastasia. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Mark. I, Theodinus, priest-cardinal of St. Vitalis, of the title of Vestina. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Susanna. I, Vivianus, priest-cardinal of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Arduinus, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, James, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of St. Theodore. I, Rainerius, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1212A] I, Gratianus, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second Nones of March, in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1178 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and the twentieth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCD. He receives the Church of St. Maurice of Agaune under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, March 14.)

[Plancher, *History of Burgundy*, I, 57.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WILLIAM, abbot of the church of St. Maurice of Agaune, and his brethren, present and future, to be regularly appointed, forever.

[Col. 1212B] Since, though unworthy, we have been assumed by the providence of the divine dispensation to the care and government of the universal Church, when requests are made to us concerning the protection of churches, it is fitting graciously to yield to the desires of petitioners and bring their requests to fulfilment. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions and strengthen by the privilege of the Apostolic See [Col. 1212C] the church of blessed Maurice—known to belong by right and ownership to St. Peter—in which you, living the apostolic life according to the Rule of blessed Augustine, devote yourselves to divine service, following the example of our father and predecessor, Pope Innocent of holy memory. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire by grants of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s provision, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid church is built, with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Sigismund; the church of St. Lawrence; the church of St. Mary; and the hospital of St. James, situated in the town belonging to the same church of St. Maurice, with all [Col. 1212D] appurtenances belonging to those churches and hospital; the church of Sine muro, with its appurtenances; the church of Annumglaris, with its appurtenances; the church of Cinimiaco, with its appurtenances; the church of Massiniaco, with its appurtenances; the church of Viole, with its appurtenances; the church of St. Michael of Tarentaise, with its appurtenances; the church of Latuelle, with its appurtenances; the church of Fessum, with its appurtenances; the house of Ponte-Alben, with its appurtenances; the church of Allio called St. Maurice, with its appurtenances; the church of Olous, with its appurtenances; the church of Ortonnes, with its appurtenances; the church of Vergis, with its appurtenances; the church of Conteis, with its appurtenances; the church of Vaignes [Col. 1213A], with its appurtenances; and the church of Vilugio, with its appurtenances.

Moreover, we, Alexander, likewise confirm by apostolic authority the due liberty granted to that church by our predecessors: namely, that the church itself, together with its dependent cells, shall be subject only to the Roman pontiff, and that no one whatsoever may exercise any lordship or exaction in those places. We also enact that no canon except one professing the regular life may ever be substituted or introduced among them by any device.

We therefore decree, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the second Ides of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1178 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1213B], and the twentieth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCDI. Privilege for the Church of Tropea. (Lateran, March 15.)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, IX, 452.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother CORIDON, bishop of Tropea, and to his successors canonically appointed, forever.

Although unworthy, we have been assumed to the administration of the supreme pontificate in order that we may grant apostolic protection to all, and especially to our brethren and fellow bishops, and strengthen their Churches against the assaults of evil men. Therefore, [Col. 1213C] venerable brother bishop in Christ, graciously granting your petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, the Church of Tropea, over which by God’s authority you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter be able to acquire by grants of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors.

We therefore decree, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Alberic, cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman [Col. 1213D] Church, on the Ides of March, in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1178 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and the twentieth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCDII. He receives the monastery of St. Martin at Muri under protection, grants it various privileges, and imposes upon the monks an annual payment of one gold piece. (Lateran, March 18.)

[Hergott, *Genealogy of the House of Habsburg*, II, 192.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ANSELM, abbot of the monastery of St. Martin of Muri, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

Those who, having set aside worldly desires, have vowed in the religious habit to render due service to the Lord [Col. 1214A] ought more especially to receive apostolic support, lest the attack of any rash person either turn them away from their purpose or—God forbid—impair the strength of holy religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document.

First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order established in that monastery according to the Lord and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be inviolably observed there for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions, etc.

(It enumerates the possessions of the monastery; then continues:)

[Col. 1214B] Moreover, by the authority of these present letters we grant you that, should your advocate, exceeding the rights of his advocacy, impose unlawful exactions upon you, your monastery, or the property belonging to that monastery, or otherwise prove burdensome and useless to you, then, unless he comes to his senses when admonished, you may choose another advocate, through whom the rights of the monastery may be more effectively preserved unimpaired and defended against the robberies and violence of evildoers.

We also grant that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. When a general interdict of the land is in force [Col. 1214C], you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, without ringing bells, excluding those under interdict and the excommunicated, and in a subdued voice. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed in authority there by any deceitful device or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of the Lord and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1178 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and the twentieth year of the pontificate of Lord Alexander [Col. 1214D] Pope III.

### MCDIII. He receives under protection the Jerusalem monastery of “the holy primitive Church of Mount Sion,” “built in honour of the Mother of God and of the Holy Spirit by Godfrey of illustrious memory,” and confirms its possessions situated in Sicily. He grants the abbot the use of mitre and ring. (Lateran, March 19.)

[Pirri, *Sicilia sacra*, II, 1326.]

### MCDIV. He confirms the rights and privileges of the monastery of St. Simplician at Milan. (Lateran, March 20.)

[Muratori, *Italian Antiquities*, II, 219.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1215A] sons OPRAND, abbot of the monastery of St. Simplician, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

Whenever we are asked for something known to accord with religion and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it gladly and give suitable consent to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, most beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions and, following in the footsteps of Pope Eugenius, our father and predecessor of happy memory, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document.

First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order established in your monastery according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict [Col. 1215B] shall be inviolably observed there for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions, etc.

(It enumerates their possessions.)

Certainly, no one may presume to demand or extort tithes from you on newly cleared land which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the sustenance of your animals. You may also receive into conversion clerks or laymen fleeing from the world, free and unbound, and retain them without any opposition. Upon your death, etc.

“SHOW ME THY WAYS, O LORD.” “SAINT PETER; SAINT PAUL.”

[Col. 1215C] I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, Philip, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul and Pammachius. I, John, priest-cardinal of St. Vitalis, of the title of Vestina. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Susanna. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Chrysogonus. I, Cinthius, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Hugh, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Clement. I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of the title of St. [Col. 1215D] Mary. I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of the title of St. Theodore in Cosmedin. I, Laborans, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, Rainerius, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1216A] I, Gratianus, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Matthew, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary the New.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1178 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and the twentieth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

### MCDV. Privilege for the monastery of St. George in the Black Forest. (Lateran, March 26.)

[Neugart, *Codex diplomaticus Alemannicus*, II, 105.]

[Col. 1216B] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MANEGOLD, abbot of the monastery of St. George, situated in the Black Forest beside the river Brigana [Note: [Col. 1215D] German: Dieg. Brig.], and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

By reason of the office entrusted to us, we are bound to love religious places and to provide with fatherly solicitude for their peace, so that persons there dedicated to divine service may devote themselves more freely to the observance of their profession in proportion as they are more securely fortified by apostolic protection against the assaults of wicked men. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions and, following in the footsteps of Pope Innocent [Note: [Col. 1215D] The Second. See the bull of this pontiff in *History of the Black Forest*, vol. III, p. 72 (*Patrologia*, vol. CLXXIX, col. 437).] of happy memory, receive under the protection and defence of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery [Col. 1216C], in which you are dedicated to divine service. This monastery was offered to blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, by the noblemen Hezelo and Hesso, founders of that place; and we strengthen it by the authority of this present document. We decree that whatsoever possessions and goods have been conferred upon that monastery by the aforesaid men or by other faithful persons, and whatever it may hereafter be able to acquire by grants of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names, which the same monastery holds by right [Col. 1216D] of ownership:

The cell in the diocese of Metz, Lukesheim. The cell of Saint John on the estate of Megenhelmeswilre.  
[Note: [Col. 1215D] In the Vosges, in Lower Alsace, diocese of Strasbourg. For the charter of foundation of this cell, dated 1127, see *Gallia Christiana*, vol. V, *Instrumenta*, col. 479.]

The cell of Saint Nicholas on the estate of Ripoldesowe.  
[Note: [Col. 1215D] Rippoldsau, among very high mountains near the Kinzig valley. It is still subject to the monastery of Saint [Col. 1216D] George.]

The cell on the estate of Fridemvilre, which was acquired by lawful exchange from the church of Reichenau.  
[Note: [Col. 1216D] Fridenweiler, near Neustadt in the Black Forest, principality of Fürstenberg. There is now there a Cistercian nunnery under the care of the abbot of Tennenbach.]  
[Note: [Col. 1216D] Reichenau is meant.]

The cell of Amitenhuisen.  
[Note: [Col. 1216D] Amtenhausen, in the Baar, principality of Fürstenberg. A Benedictine nunnery now flourishes there; the abbot of Saint George exercises its care.]

The cell of Urspringen. [Col. 1217A]  
[Note: [Col. 1217C] In Swabia; a Benedictine nunnery subject to Saint George.]

The village of Steten with its church.  
[Note: [Col. 1217C] A village in the district of Rottweil, on the Eschach.]

One third of the village of Fuezen, with its church.

The estate of Kembiz, with its church, and Blansingen and Nuifare.  
[Note: [Col. 1217C] Kleinkems on the Rhine in upper Breisgau, principality of Baden.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217C] There.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217C] Niffern, opposite the village of Blansingen across the Rhine in Alsace.]

The village of Walde, with the church of Egge; Degernowe; Ingeltingen, with its church; Esteten, with its church; the estate at Oewingen; Liderengen, with its church and half the tithes; Dagewingen; Magerbein; Baltrameshoue; Dindinhoue; Scophelo, with its church; Husen; Bickelspere; Turnewane, with its church and half the tithes; Cugenwalt; Betechove; Swenningen, with its church and half the tithes; Mulehusen, with its church; Sitingen; Gonningen; Gruningen; Aseheim; Cneigen; Uberach; Wilaresbach; Tuningen. [Col. 1217B]

[Note: [Col. 1217C] Walde was formerly the seat of Hezelo, the founder, between Villingen and Schramberg. The ruins of the old castle remain.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217C] Degernau and Ingoltingen in Swabia, on the Riss.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217C] Near Munderkingen, there.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217C] Oeffingen, in the bailiwick of Tuttlingen, principality of Württemberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Leidrengen, in the bailiwick of Rosenfeld in the same principality.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Dauchingen between Rottweil and Villingen.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] In the county of Oettingen.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] In Upper Alsace.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Dintenhofen near Ehingen on the Danube.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Schopfloch in the bailiwick of Kirchheim, principality of Württemberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Hausen, district of Rottweil.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Bickelsberg in the bailiwick of Rosenfeld.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Durrwangen in the bailiwick of Bahlingen, principality of Württemberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] In other Saint George documents, Guginwald is joined with Achara, or Acheren, in Ortenau.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Beckenhofen, several villages below Villingen.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] At the sources of the Neckar, principality of Württemberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Mühlhausen, district of Rottweil.]  
[Note: [Col. 1217D] Seitingen in the lordship of Gonzenberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] Guningen in the upper county of Hochinberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] Below Villingen.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] From which the county formerly took its name, on the stream Asch or Aesch. The villages of Obereschach and Niedereschach still exist; one is subject to the commandery of Villingen, the other to that of Rottweil.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] Klengen and Ueberauchen are subject to Villingen; Weilerspach and Tunengen to Rottweil.]

Walewis; Scanebrunne; Furtwangen, with its church; Tannebrunne, with its church; Engen; Slata; Einbach, with its church; Husen; Achare, with its church; Mulnheim, with its church; Buhele; Trudeim; Alteim; Scoppheim; Scaftolsheim; Eggeboldesheim; Buotenheim; Belhan; Edingen; the church of Sellebach; Fokkenhusen, with its church. The church of this village too we grant shall be held by you, your successors, and the brethren under pastoral right, and that its subjects shall be cared for in the capacity of a priest.

[Note: [Col. 1218C] Walwies in the county of Nellenburg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] Schemmbrunn near Schramberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] In the Black Forest and the bailiwick of Triberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] In the bailiwick of Hornberg, principality of Württemberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] In Hegau, principality of Fürstenberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C] Schlatt, there.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218C–D] Since it is certain that the church of the town of Hausen in the Kinzig valley was given to Saint George in 1148 by Frederick of Wolfrach, Einbach must likewise have been in that neighbourhood, where the valley called Ibacherthal lies open.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Achtkaren in Breisgau.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] There, principality of Baden.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Near Haguenau in Lower Alsace.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Schopfheim on the Wiese in the Black Forest, principality of Baden.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Both places are in Lower Alsace.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Perhaps Bietigheim, principality of Württemberg.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Bellen near the town of Hüfingen in the Baar.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] A town in Breisgau, Austrian principality.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Selbach in Ortenau and the county of Geroldseck.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Formerly a village between Villingen and Munchweiler, whose name now adheres to the surrounding fields.]

Moreover, we bind and confirm by apostolic authority, under the yoke of obedience by which they are bound to you, the other cells which are subject to you and your monastery not by right of ownership like those named above, but by obedience. [Col. 1217C] We entrust them to you and your successors canonically appointed, to be cared for and governed forever by you and your brethren in the fear of God according to the Rule of Saint Benedict: the cell at Wagawilla, the cell at Crouchdal, and the cell of Saint Mark. [Col. 1218A]

[Note: [Col. 1218D] Alternatively, Widersdorf in Lorraine.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] Alternatively, Krafthal in Lower Alsace.]  
[Note: [Col. 1218D] In Upper Alsace.]

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, promotion to orders, consecrations of altars or churches, and any other sacraments from the bishop of Constance, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these freely and without abuse. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration.

We decree that the burial places of the aforesaid monastery [Col. 1218B] and its cells, in which the order is observed, shall be wholly free, so that none may obstruct the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; provided always that the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken remain intact. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any crafty device or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall judge to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict.

Therefore no ecclesiastical or secular person shall have leave to claim for himself in the aforesaid monastery [Col. 1218C] any conditions of ownership, hereditary right, advocacy, or exercise of any authority [Col. 1219A] that harms the freedom of that place; nor to take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with unjust exactions. Rather, all shall be preserved whole and shall in every way benefit the use of those for whose governance they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and to the canonical right of diocesan bishops in the aforesaid churches. Furthermore, we grant you free power to appoint an advocate; if he proves useless to the monastery, you may remove him and appoint another suitable person in his place. As a token of the liberty received from the Holy Roman Church, you shall pay one bezant yearly to us and our successors. If anyone, therefore, etc.

[Col. 1219B] I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal priest of the Title of Saints John and Paul, of Pammachius. I, John, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Mark. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Susanna. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April, in the twelfth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1178, [Col. 1219C] in the twentieth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.  
[Note: [Col. 1219] Since the twelfth indiction and the twentieth year of Alexander III’s pontificate agree, the year of the Incarnation should be placed as 1179.]

## MCDVI. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Michael of Tonnerre. (Lateran, 29 March.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, new edition, *Instrumenta*, IV, 189.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons STEPHEN, abbot of the monastery of the church of Saint Michael of Tonnerre, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity, etc.

… Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive the aforesaid [Col. 1219D] monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this our present writing. First, we decree that the monastic order, known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions or goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. [Col. 1220A] Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

The church of Blessed Michael and its cemetery, with the lands and people dwelling in that borough; the church of Blessed Ambrose of Atheis, with its lands, tithes, and other appurtenances; the chapel and village of Tessiaco, with their appurtenances; the church of Ligniaco-villa, with its appurtenances, and one third of the tithe of the castle of Ligniac; the chapel of Mollemaco, with its appurtenances; the church of Vallepelletana, with lands and mills; the chapel of Florigniaco, with its village and mill, jurisdiction, lands, and appurtenances; the village called Carriacus, with mills, lands, and jurisdiction; the churches and village of Caniaco, with jurisdiction and their appurtenances; the church [Col. 1220B] of Espinolio, with two thirds of the tithe, and the tithe of the mill of Camelli; the church of Saint Columba, with its tithes and appurtenances; the chapel of Saint Vinemar, with its tithes and revenues; the church of Anciaco-servili, with one third of the tithe and one third of the mills, and the mill opposite the castle; the church of Pinella, with its appurtenances, the tithe of the *fruagium* of Parson, and one third of the same wood with lands and jurisdiction; the church of Crusiaco, with its tithes and revenues, and the church of Puteis; the church and village of Cursegradu, with jurisdiction and all its appurtenances; the church of Ebroilo and half the tithe, with one-third revenues and its appurtenances; the church of Turgeio, with one third of the tithe, lands, meadows, and woods; the church of Saint Lawrence of Con. and one third of the tithe; rights of use in the woods of Vaula, Turgeio, and Ebroilo for all uses of the church and its workshops; the church of Saint Michael and the mills of the borough of Tonnerre; and, for all uses of the house and oven of Cursegradu, the pasture of all animals of that village and pannage for sixty pigs. Two thirds of the tithe of the village called Viros; half the tithe and revenues of the church of Lentagio; the church of Protonolo, with one third of the tithe, its lands, and possessions; the church of the Holy Trinity at Bar-sur-Seine, with the thirds and mills belonging to that church, and the fairs of the feast of the Holy Trinity on the first Sunday, second and third weekday, [Col. 1220D] and one third of the mills of Villamorini, with lands and meadows. Lands and revenues at Valeriis, Chaale, and Estorniaco. Lands and revenues of the Holy Virtues; the chapel of Monasteriolo, with lands, meadows, woods, and one third of the jurisdiction; the chapel and half the village of Campaniaci, with jurisdiction, lands, waters, and woods belonging to that village.

In the diocese of Troyes: the church of Saint Peter in the village called Jassenna, with tithes, mills, lands, meadows, and all its appurtenances. In the same parish, in the village called Trena: the chapel of Saint Michael; the mills of the borough of Tonnerre and of the borough of Beraud; and the mills of Boenerii. [Col. 1221A] Also two thirds of the mill-seat called Camelli; the chapel of Cappa and the whole territory, with jurisdiction and vineyards; the land called Charron; the Field of Rainfred; and one third of the commons and jurisdiction of Vallis Plana.

Furthermore, we decree that whoever dies in the castle of Tonnerre or in the parish of Saint Anian shall be carried to no place but your monastery and buried there, unless, being of sound mind, they have chosen burial elsewhere. In the parish churches which you hold, you may choose priests and present the chosen men to the bishop. If they are found suitable, the bishop shall commit the care of souls to them, so that these priests shall answer to the bishop concerning the care of the people, but to you concerning temporal matters. Upon the death of you, the present [Col. 1221B] abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any crafty device or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall judge to be elected according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict.

We therefore decree, etc.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1179, in the twentieth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander.

## MCDVII. Privilege for the Church of Imola. (Lateran, 30 March.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, II, 630.]

Alexander … to his venerable brother Henry, [Col. 1221C] bishop of Imola, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

“From the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See,” etc., to the end of the bull, as in the diploma of Eugenius III granted to the same Church in 1151, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June. See *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXX, col. 1473.

## MCDVIII. He commands Desiderius, bishop of Thérouanne, to ensure that the “tithe of the allodial estate (alletium)” be assigned to the monastery of Saint-Bertin at Saint-Omer; likewise, he exhorts Philip, count of Flanders, to grant the “tithe of the allodial estate (alletium)” to the same monastery.

[*Collection des Cartulaires*, III, 349.]

## MCDIX. Bull confirming the monastery of Garsten. (Lateran, 5 April.)

[FROELICH, *Diplomatarium Garstense*, p. 51.]

[Col. 1221D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons CONRAD, abbot of the monastery of Garsten, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting that we readily grant a desire known to pertain to the purpose of religion and the salvation of souls, and give suitable support to the petitioners’ wishes. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive the aforesaid monastery, in which you are dedicated to divine service, under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it with the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions [Col. 1222A] or goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by concession of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify:

Namely, the estate at Behemperg, which Margrave Ottakar of Styria delivered into the hands of Altmann, bishop of Passau; the site where the church was established for the parish at Gersten, in which the monastery was founded, with all its appurtenances, all priestly right, free investiture of parish churches, every tithe, and its endowment. Its boundaries run from the river Rubinck to the course of the other river Freidenze, [Col. 1222B] to the source of the Gavelentz, and to the gate, with all parochial right. The wood given to the monastery by Conrad, a nobleman of Cakoz; in this wood a district has been established consisting of thirty holdings and one manor. Whatever has reasonably been granted to you by its bishops or by others, we command shall, as it has been observed until now, henceforth also be observed inviolate.

We also grant that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that none may obstruct the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, without prejudice to the rights of the parish churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations [Col. 1222C] of altars or churches, and the ordinations of monks to be promoted to holy orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic and enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these freely and without burden. When a general interdict has been imposed, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. You may receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, who are free and absolved, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, from leaving the cloister through frivolity without his abbot’s permission; and no one shall dare retain one who has departed without a common letter of authorization, except for the sake of a stricter religious life.

No one shall presume to exact tithes from you from your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the produce of your animals. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by crafty device or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall judge to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, or harass it [Col. 1223A] with any vexations. Rather, all shall be preserved whole and shall in every way benefit the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts hereafter to violate this page of our decree, and, having been warned a second and third time, does not make suitable amends, let that person lose the dignity of office and honour, recognize himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject to severe vengeance at the last judgment. But let all who preserve the rights of that place have the peace of our Lord [Col. 1223B] Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

SAINT PETER. SAINT PAUL. POPE ALEXANDER III.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul. I, John, cardinal priest of Saint Mark. I, Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Susanna. I, Cinthius, cardinal priest of Saint Cecilia.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of April, in the twelfth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1223C] 1179, in the twentieth year of the pontificate of Pope Alexander III.

## MCDX. He receives the monastery of Saint Nazarius of Lorsch under protection and confirms its goods and rights. (Lateran, 7 April.)

[*Codex Laureshamensis diplomaticus*, I, 276.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SIGEHARD, abbot of the monastery of Saint Nazarius of Lorsch, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever something is requested of us which is recognized to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it readily and give suitable assistance to the petitioners’ wishes. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions, receive the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been instituted in your monastery according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through the Lord’s favour, shall remain [Col. 1224A] secure and unimpaired to you and your successors, etc. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

The place itself on which the aforesaid monastery has been built, with all its appurtenances; the old monastery with its appurtenances; Albrinesberc with its appurtenances; Michelstat with its appurtenances; Capellam with its appurtenances; Nullenburc with its appurtenances. No one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes or first-fruits from you from your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or expense, or from the produce of your animals. You may also receive clerics and laymen fleeing the world, free and absolved, into conversion, and retain them in your monastery [Col. 1224B] without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, from leaving it without the permission of his abbot, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one shall dare retain one who has departed without a common letter of authorization from you. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, without ringing bells, excluding the interdicted and excommunicated, and in a subdued voice. We also decree that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that none may obstruct the devotion and final will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted, without prejudice to the rights of the churches from which [Col. 1224C] the bodies of the dead are taken.

Moreover, by the kindness of the Apostolic See we grant you permission, without injury to neighbouring churches and with the consent of the diocesan bishop, to build churches or oratories in your places. We further prohibit you, son abbot, or any other person, from presuming without the common consent of the brethren, or of the greater and sounder part of them, to grant in benefice, sell, lease, or alienate in any manner the possessions, tithes, offerings, or other goods of that monastery belonging to the abbot’s table, the brethren’s provisions, the rights of obediences, or provostships; if this is done, we decree that the alienator shall lose his rights. We decree that the provostships of your cells and the obediences of the monastery [Col. 1224D] are to be entrusted only to wise monks of your chapter, with their property safeguarded. Under threat of anathema we also prohibit the advocates of that monastery from allowing anyone to build castles or other fortifications on the monastery’s possessions, burden the household or tenant farmers of the church with new and unjust exactions, or rashly oppose the abbot in demanding or obtaining the church’s rights. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by crafty device or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall judge to be elected according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. We therefore decree, etc.

[Col. 1225A] I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Conrad, humble minister of the church of Salzburg and bishop of Sabina, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the Title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Mark. I, Theodore, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Vitalis, of the Title of Vestina. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Susanna. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Vivian, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. [Col. 1225B] I, Cinthius, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Cecilia. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Clement. I, Arduin, cardinal priest of the Title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Matthew, cardinal priest of the Title of Saint Marcellus. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Laborans, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. [Col. 1225C] I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor, on the seventh day before the Ides of April, in the twelfth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1178, in the twentieth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

## MCDXI. He receives the monastery of Tournus under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, 8 April.)

[JUENIN, *New History of Tournus*, 174.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GIRARD, abbot of the monastery of Tournus, [Col. 1225D] and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See entrusted to us exhorts us to give the protection of our aid to divine places and persons which duly seek it with devotion. For just as no effect should be granted to those who seek unjust things, so the petition of those who seek what is legitimate and just should not be delayed—especially of those who seem devoutly to embrace religious life and rejoice to serve the Lord under it, or who strive to serve almighty God by an honourable life and praiseworthy discipline of conduct. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. Following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Urban, Calixtus, [Col. 1226A] Innocent, Lucius, and Eugenius, we receive the monastery of Tournus, in which you are dedicated to divine service, under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it with the privilege of this present writing; decreeing that whatever possessions, etc. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names:

Namely, in the diocese of Clermont: the monastery of Saint-Pourçain, with the churches of Besson, Quintiniac, Salines, Celsiac, Tavallio, Fellinia, Monteaureo, Sustris, Charel, Liniac, Martiliac, Montfanc, Boiac, Barbariac, Vernei, Villena, Lupiac, Paredo, Briallis, Varinnis, Vorot, and Lupo; the churches of Begiac, Nuilliac, Copelz, [Col. 1226B] Branciac, Tresalliac, and Floriac, with the chapel of Cavarocha; the church of Salviliis; the church of Lebiac; the church of Saint Nicholas; the church of Vernolio.

In the diocese of Chalon: Pristiac, Aguliac, the church of Baldreriis, the church of Saint Andrew, Lambres, Manciac, the church of Giniac, of Ver, the church of Griviliac, and of Cuyseriac.

In the diocese of Lyon: the church of Saint Andrew of Balgiac; Vasliac; Brienna; Juvenciac; the church of Saint James of Gressiac; Saint Benignus; the church of Cabrosio; of Chanvennis; Bisiac; the church of Blessed Mary of Solliniac; of Moncelz; Saint Martin of Budella; the church of Saint Andrew commonly called Pannos; the church of Monte-Raculfo; of Saisiriac; of Paronniac; the cell of the castle of Corgeron; [Col. 1226C] the church of Saint Lydius, commonly called Olives; Lovincum; Montem aureum; Silvinicum.

In the diocese of Mâcon: Hulchisiac, Villare, Plotas, Belniac, the church of Li, Donziac, the cell of Saint Romanus, Saint Maurice, Saint Symphorian, Saint Mary of Capella-Riverias, Saint Peter of Romaniscas, the church of Aziac, of Fissiac, Saint Julian of Lanciac, and Saint Vitalis of Lenna.

In the diocese of Bourges: the church of Saciac. In the diocese of Autun: the church of Pariniac with its chapel, and the church of Petraficta with the chapel of Saint Justus. In the diocese of Nantes: the monastery of Saint Philibert; the church of Saint Vitalis of Raas; the church of Macecol; Saint Martin of Paciac; Saint Luminius; the church of Limosiver; Saint Columban; [Col. 1226D] the church of Colcoiac; the church of Mores; the residences of Legiac and Tolvei; the churches of the monasteries.

In the diocese of Poitiers: the island of Herum; the church of Bellovidere with its cemetery; the cell of Saint Mary of Lausdun; the church of Saint Nicholas; Saint Peter; the churches of Basilicis and of Holy Cross; the churches of Berniziac and Aziac; Manciac; Tatiac; the church of Madernas; the church of Bernazii; of Mont-Saint-Léger; and the church of Estivallibus.

In the diocese of Tours: Pontiac, Verniolum, Corcoiacum. In the diocese of Angers: the cell of Saint Mary of Cunault, with its appurtenances; the churches of Duadicastris, Saint Dionysius, Saint Peter, Saint John, and Saint Léger; the church of Logne; the church of Saint Lawrence; the village of Landrum; Terentiacum; the churches [Col. 1227A] of Varinnas; Saint Mary of Thanais, with its chapel.

In the diocese of Geneva: the church of Perrois and the church of Monte-castro. In the diocese of Lausanne: the church of Birola. In the diocese of Le Puy: the monastery of Saint Philibert; the church of Saint Peter of Saletas; Saint Felix of Landos; Saint Mary of Prastasias; Saint Martin of Corconensis; the chapel of Saint Philibert; Saint Cyricus; Saint Maurice of Vallamblanensis; Saint Vincent; the chapel in the castle of Senoil; Saint Mary of Baisam; the chapel in the castle of Rocol; Saint Julian of Chaspiniac; of the castle of Mercolio; and the church of Saint Quintin.

In the diocese of Die: the church in the castle of Gramnat; Saint Vincent; Saint Romanus; and the church of Torretes. In the diocese of Tricastin: the church of Valle-Nymphis; Saint Martin; Saint Mary; Saint Peter; Saint Romanus; the chapel of Saint Michael of [Col. 1227B] Garda; the church of the alms-house; Saint Mary of Graina. In the diocese of Orange: the churches of Dorsera, Saint Mary, Saint Benedict, Saint Christopher, and Saint Saturninus. In the diocese of Vaison: the church of Saint Germanus, Saint Peter of Falcon, and Saint Mary of Purpureres. In the diocese of Vienne: the cell of Saint Agnes of Mota; Saint Martin of Aziac, with its cemetery; Saint Veranus of Rivas; the church of Fay; Saint John of the castle of Mirol; the church of Villanova; the chapel of Saint Michael of Albon; the church of Saint Saturninus with its parish; the church of Saint Philibert of Miniac; the church of Saint Romanus; the church of Saint Andrew; and Saint Ferreolus. In the diocese of Besançon: the church of Saint Cornelius; Saint Desiderius; the church of Planesel; and the church of Dazzon.

In the parish churches which you hold, [Col. 1227C] you may choose priests and present the chosen men to the bishop. If they are found suitable, the bishop shall commit to them the care of souls; and these priests shall answer to the bishop concerning the care of the people, but to you concerning temporal matters. You may also receive into conversion clerics and laymen fleeing the world, free and absolved, and retain them in your community without any opposition. No one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you from your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the produce of your animals. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, [Col. 1227D] without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. We also decree that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that none may obstruct the devotion and final will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are under interdict or excommunicated, without prejudice to the rights of the churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any crafty device or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall judge to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict.

We therefore decree, etc. In the monogram: **“Show me your ways, O Lord.”**
[Col. 1228A] I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Conrad, humble minister of the Church of Gallipoli, bishop of Sabina. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Gorgonius. I, Vivian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Cynthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Arduin, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. [Col. 1228B] I, William, archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Rainerius, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. I, Matthew, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Ides of April, in the twelfth indiction, in the year 1179 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twentieth year of the pontificate of lord Alexander [Col. 1228C] Pope III.

MCDXII. To Richard, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He reports that he himself consecrated Roger, abbot of St Augustine’s. (Lateran, 9 April.)

[TWYSDEN, *Rerum Anglicarum Scriptores*, II, 1446.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RICHARD, Archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the Apostolic See: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When our beloved son R., now abbot but then elect of Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury, had for a second time come into our presence, not without [Col. 1228D] serious labours and expenses, because, as he said, you had refused to lay your hand of blessing upon him in his monastery in accordance with our command, the ordinance of our father and predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory, and the tenor of our letter, we blessed him as abbot, without prejudice to your right and dignity and that of your successors. Therefore, desiring to provide for you and your Church in the future, we decree by apostolic authority that what we did in blessing the aforesaid elect is incapable of causing any prejudice to your right or to your Church.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of April.

MCDXIII. To Roger, Abbot of Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury.—Concerning the blessing of his successors.

[Ibid., p. 1825.]

[Col. 1229A]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ROGER, Abbot of Saint Augustine’s: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since you had long ago come into our presence, after our venerable brother Richard, Archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, had refused to confer the office of blessing upon you in your monastery, and had asked the clemency of the Apostolic See to cause the office of blessing to be conferred upon you in your monastery, we, adhering to the footsteps of Pope Eugenius, our father and predecessor of holy memory, [Col. 1229B] commanded the aforesaid archbishop, by the common counsel of our brethren, and strictly ordered him in our letters, to confer upon you in your monastery the office of blessing without demanding any profession, within thirty days after receiving our letters. If he should refuse to do so within the prescribed period, we commanded our venerable brother, the Bishop of Worcester, in virtue of obedience, promptly to perform the same act.

But since they did not at all carry out our command, you returned to our presence, wishing to ensure that the monastery entrusted to you should not any longer lack pastoral provision. For this reason, we could justly have punished both the archbishop and the bishop more severely for contempt of our command, [Col. 1229C] and henceforth deprived that archbishop and his successors of the power of blessing your successors. Yet, moderating our indignation and tempering the rigour of justice by the customary clemency of the Apostolic See, we conferred upon you, though unworthy, the office of blessing, without prejudice to the right of that archbishop and his successors in blessing an abbot.

We decree that henceforth the Archbishop of Canterbury for the time being shall bless your successors in the monastery entrusted to you, without demanding a profession. If, within forty days after being requested, he should fail to bless them, unless he can allege a manifest and canonical excuse, they shall come to the Roman Church [Col. 1229D] to receive blessing, or shall obtain it through a bishop appointed by the Roman pontiff. And that this constitution of ours may be inviolably observed for all time, we strengthen it by apostolic authority and confirm it by the page of this present writing, etc.

MCDXIV. To Henry, King of the English.—He declares that Roger the abbot has been rashly accused.

(Ibid.)

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to HENRY, illustrious King of the English: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have heard that it has been falsely represented to your royal majesty that our beloved son R[oger], now Abbot [Col. 1230A] of Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury, has found no favour with you because he had made his monastery tributary to the Roman Church by an annual payment of ten marks of gold. This is wholly contrary to the truth; and we are astonished if the prudence of your serenity could in any manner have credited such a representation, since the establishment of any tribute from the aforesaid monastery never entered our mind, nor did any word concerning it proceed from the mouth, or even from the side, of the abbot himself.

We do not wish your highness to be unaware that it is not the custom of the Roman Church to establish such payments or burden any church in this manner. The reason we wrote as above to our venerable brother R[ichard], Archbishop of Canterbury, legate [Col. 1230B] of the Apostolic See, concerning the blessing of the abbot just mentioned, was that from long ago the abbots of Saint Augustine’s had been accustomed to endure many difficulties, very great labours, and losses in obtaining blessing, by travelling to Rome, returning to England, and travelling again to Rome. For in the time of Pope Eugenius, our father and predecessor of blessed memory, the then abbot-elect was wholly unable to obtain blessing from the Archbishop of Canterbury until he travelled to Rome at great expense, and returned to England.

The present abbot, unable to receive the grace of blessing from the archbishop, was compelled, as his predecessors had been, to come to Rome and return to England not without difficulty, carrying to the same archbishop letters of strict command that he should take care within thirty days to confer upon him in his monastery the office of blessing without demanding a profession. [Col. 1230C] If he should perhaps refuse to do so, we commanded our venerable brother, the Bishop of Worcester, under the same strict injunction, to perform the same act within another thirty days. Since neither carried out the command, the same abbot was compelled to trouble us, not without great personal danger and loss of resources.

Although we were moved and disturbed, and judged it highly injurious that the archbishop and bishop had not executed our command, and although by right we could have deprived the archbishop and his successors henceforth of the authority to bless the Abbot of Saint Augustine’s, nevertheless, moderating our indignation [Col. 1230D] and tempering the rigour of justice by the customary mercy of the Apostolic See, we conferred the office of blessing upon the aforesaid abbot, without prejudice to the right of the archbishop and his successors in blessing the abbot; namely, that they ought to bless the abbots of Saint Augustine’s in that monastery without demanding a profession.

Commending him, therefore, to your royal highness, we earnestly request and exhort you that, for love of God and reverence for blessed Peter and ourselves, you love, support, and defend the aforesaid abbot. Do not permit him to be further harassed for Jewish debts; nor act against him or his monastery because we state in our letters that the monastery itself belongs directly to us. For we understand this in relation to an ecclesiastical, not a secular, person; and in this no derogation from your honour is intended.

MCDXV. To Roger the abbot and the brethren of Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury.—That no one may be ordained in churches whose presentation belongs to them unless presented by them.

[Ibid., p. 1830.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to ROGER, Abbot of Saint Augustine’s, etc.

Since in our … And below: We therefore, considering that this monastery belongs in a special manner to the disposition of blessed Peter and ourselves, and that for this reason we are more especially bound to it, grant you and your successors, by the customary clemency of the Apostolic See, that if archbishops or bishops and other prelates of churches, after being humbly and devoutly requested by you three times, fail to render you full justice concerning your wrongdoers among their parishioners, you shall henceforth have free authority, by our authority and with all contradiction and appeal set aside, to excommunicate them; and no one shall dare to alter a sentence thus reasonably pronounced, unless appropriate satisfaction has first been rendered.

MCDXVI. To the same.—Concerning the excommunication of wrongdoers.

[Ibid.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ROGER, abbot, and the monks of Saint Augustine’s: [Col. 1231C] greeting and apostolic blessing.

Concerning the lesser [matter], we could … And below: By apostolic authority we prohibit anyone from being ordained in churches subject to your presentation unless he has been presented by you. If any persons should be ordained without your presentation, they shall be removed from those churches and their ordination shall be held wholly void—unless, which God forbid, it is established that you maliciously delay the presentation of clerics.

MCDXVII. He grants Roger the abbot and the brethren of Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury, “that when a general interdict of the land is in force, they may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice.”

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1231D]

MCDXVIII. He takes the Church of Reims under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, 13 April.)

[VARIN, *Archives administratives de Reims*, I, I, 381.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother WILLIAM, Archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina, legate of the Apostolic See, and to his successors canonically appointed for ever.

Since, by God’s grace, you are endowed with nobility of birth, uprightness of character, and learning, the requests which you reasonably make of us ought willingly and effectively to be granted, so that, just as [Col. 1232A] you are known to have obtained a fuller measure of the Apostolic See’s favour, so you may rejoice that it is secured to you in those things for which you justly ask. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Archbishop, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Reims, over which by God’s providence you are known to preside, and confirm it by the privilege of this present writing.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought it right to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 1232B] The bishoprics of Soissons, Laon, Cambrai, Beauvais, Châlons, Senlis, Noyon, Arras, Tournai, and Thérouanne; within your own diocese, the monasteries of Saint Remigius, Saint Nicasius, Saint Dionysius, and Saint Peter within the city of Reims; outside the city, the monasteries of Mouzon, Saint Thierry, Saint Peter of Hautvillers, Saint Basolus, and Saint Mary of Igny; and in all these monasteries spiritual rights and patronage, with every right of institution and their ordering. Moreover, the monasteries of Épernay and Avenay; likewise, within the bishopric of Soissons, the right of patronage in the monastery of Orbais; within the bishopric of Tournai, the right of patronage [Col. 1232C] in the monastery of Cysoing; within the bishoprics of Noyon and Amiens, the jurisdiction hitherto exercised over the burgesses of Saint-Quentin and Saint-Valery—namely, that those summoned shall come before the court of Reims; lordship of the city of Reims with all its appurtenances.

Also, the fief which the noble Count of Champagne is known to hold from your Church, for which, while preserving his fidelity to the king, he is bound to perform liege homage to you: namely, Vitry, Vertus, Regitestum, Châtillon, Épernay, Rociacum, Fismes, Braine, and the county of the castle in Porcien, with their castellanies, other possessions, and castles held by that count in his own person or by others from him.

Also, the fief of Bouillon, [Col. 1232D] which the Bishop of Liège is known to hold from the Archbishops of Reims, for which he is likewise bound personally, with his hand in the hand of the Archbishop of Reims, to promise that he will faithfully render and observe service and justice for him; and for which the same bishop is further bound to procure that the eight barons of that fief perform homage to the same archbishop. When summoned by the archbishop to suppress his wrongdoers, he must render aid and service with knights and armed men, as is known to be contained in authentic writings.

Also, the fief which the Count of Regitestum is known to hold from you, namely the county of Osmonte; the fief held from you by the Count of Grandpré; and that held from you by the Count of Soissons. Also, the castle of Mouzon, Attigny, Bétheniville, [Col. 1233A] Sept-Saulx, Cormicy, Courville, Chaumuzy, and Stanna, with their appurtenances.

Moreover, by apostolic authority we decree that no one except the Archbishop of Reims may anoint the King of France or place the first crown upon him, as had been established by ancient custom. We command that appeals made to you or your court by any persons subject to your jurisdiction be brought with due devotion. And whatever special right your Church has hitherto enjoyed in such appeals, even when the see is vacant, we confirm by apostolic authority to you and your successors. All these things, indeed, as your predecessors from of old, and you yourself until now, are known to have possessed them, we have judged fitting to confirm by apostolic authority to you and your successors.

We decree, therefore, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of April, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1179 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twentieth year of the pontificate of lord Alexander Pope III.

MCDXIX. To Sigehard, Abbot of the Monastery of Lorsch.—He grants him and his successors the use of the mitre.

(*Codex Laureshamensis*, I, 279.)

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son SIGEHARD, Abbot of Lorsch: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1233C] He deserves to be honoured by a special grace and the bestowal of a gift who is found more devoted toward blessed Peter and the most holy Roman Church. Therefore, moved both by the testimony we have received concerning you and by the requests of our beloved sons Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, and Otto, Count Palatine, we grant you and your successors, by the customary clemency of the Apostolic See, the use of the mitre for ever.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May.

MCDXX. To William, Archbishop of Reims, and his suffragans.—He declares that the religious of Dunes, of the Cistercian Order, are exempt from paying tithes on lands which they themselves cultivate. (Lateran, 17 April.)

[MIRAEUS, *Opera diplomatica*, III, 58.]

[Col. 1233D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers W[ILLIAM], Archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina, legate of the Apostolic See, and his suffragans; and to his beloved sons, the abbots, archdeacons, provosts, and priests established in their bishoprics: greeting and apostolic blessing.
