Now because, through certain provosts who had charge of the goods of your canonry, the aforesaid goods were dissipated to such an extent that you could scarcely be suitably maintained from them, in order to remove so great a disadvantage you jointly established with our venerable brother Conrad, your bishop, that each year one of you should be chosen to administer, in place of the provost, the goods of that canonry for your benefit. Assenting to your petitions, [Col. 1315B] we confirm that constitution by apostolic authority.

We therefore decree, etc.

I, Alexander, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, …, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Ard…, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary in Trastevere, of the title of Calixtus. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. I, Matthew, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New.

Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest [Col. 1315C] and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of August, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year 1181 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the twenty-second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Alexander III.

MDXX. To the archbishop and bishops established throughout Sweden. — That they should care for the souls of their subjects. (Viterbo, 26 July.)

[LILJEGREN, *Diplomata Suecana*, I, 74.]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren the archbishop and bishops established throughout Sweden, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The less instructed are those entrusted to your care in matters pertaining to salvation, the more you ought to watch over their reformation, lest, God forbid, if you are negligent, the good which they would have done had they not lacked necessary instruction be required of you. It is dangerous for you to forget that fearful declaration of fellowship in responsibility which says: “If you do not announce to the wicked [in another reading, “to the ungodly”] his wickedness, I will require his blood from your hand” (Ezekiel 3). Isaiah likewise, greatly distressed by his silence, says: “Woe is me, because I have kept silent” (Isaiah 5). Furthermore, you must not pass over with closed eyes the fact that the testimony of holy labour builds up more than the exercise of speech; for, as blessed Gregory testifies: “A sermon does not possess the sweetness which a corrupt life reproaches within the conscience.” Hence whoever speaks God’s word must first endeavour to discover how he ought to live; only after living thus may he teach with open countenance, according to [Col. 1316A] what we find written of our Saviour: “Jesus began to do and to teach” (Acts 1).

Therefore we admonish and earnestly exhort you all; under threat of divine judgment, we command that, considering the obligation of your office, you show yourselves in all things as ministers of God and give useful thought, with the help of heavenly grace, to the protection of the flock entrusted to you—not as hirelings who have no concern for the sheep, but as true shepherds. Thus, on the day of judgment, you may deserve to hear that joyful voice: “Well done, good and faithful servant” (Matthew XVV [probably XXV]). Moreover, henceforth know that, since everyone ought to receive a reward according to his labour, we relax by apostolic authority—trusting in the power of blessed Peter and Paul—one year for English persons who cross the sea to visit the thresholds of the apostles; two years for your people, because they are extremely remote [Col. 1316B] and have made themselves tributaries of the Apostolic See; and, because they come with greater labour, three years of the penance imposed for sins of which they are truly contrite and have confessed.

There is, however, no doubt that for those who do not come but pay the tribute, that payment itself avails for the remission of sins. Furthermore, since it is most burdensome for those who lay violent hands upon clerics to present themselves before the apostolic presence for absolution, by these present letters we grant you that, if any persons commit the aforesaid offence without mutilation, blinding, or death, you may absolve them by apostolic authority from the sentence of excommunication after receiving an oath that they will thereafter refrain from similar acts. [Col. 1316C] But those who publicly kill or mutilate priests, clerics, monks, or men of any religious order, you shall, notwithstanding any appeal, declare bound by the bond of excommunication, and cause them to be avoided by all as excommunicated persons, until they present themselves before the apostolic presence with letters from their bishop containing the truth of the matter.

Given at Viterbo, on the seventh day before the Kalends of August.

MDXXI. Privilege for the Cluniacs. — It forbids anyone to build a church, chapel, or oratory in the parishes of the Cluniacs, and especially in the parish of Moulins, without the consent of the abbot of Cluny. (Viterbo, 28 July.)

[Bullarium Cluniacense, 72.]

[Col. 1316D]

ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons THEOBALD, abbot, and the brethren of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although unworthy, we have been placed by the Lord in such a position and office that we are bound to honour and cherish the Churches of God, and especially religious houses, with special devotion, and to provide with pastoral care for their protection from harm and their advancement. Moved, therefore, by this consideration and likewise inclined by your prayers, we forbid by the authority of these presents anyone to presume to build anew a church, chapel, or oratory within your parishes, and especially in that of Moulins, without your consent and that of the diocesan bishop—while preserving, nevertheless, [Col. 1317A] the privileges of the Roman Church. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of [Col. 1318A] his apostles, blessed Peter and Paul.

Given at Viterbo, on the fifth day before the Kalends of August.

SPURIOUS DOCUMENTS.

[Col. 1317]

I. To Henry, king of England. — Concerning Thomas Becket. (Rome, 2 December.)

[Gilbert Foliot’s *Letters*, ed. GILES, II, 109.]

[Col. 1317A]

[Col. 1317B] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the most excellent prince and his most Christian son, the lord king; to the college of Canterbury; and to all archbishops and bishops belonging to that college: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Holy and Catholic mother Church, joined to her spouse, who is Christ, by the sweetness of ineffable love, received from him most abundant dowry-gifts, fruitful in the abundance of graces, and especially among them the benefit of liberty. For he willed that, through his beloved bride, she should rule the faithful by a free dominion, so that she might have power over each as over children in a mother’s manner, and that all might honour her with filial reverence as universal mother and lady. For she is his beloved ark, over which his heart watches untiringly by day [Col. 1317C] and by night. She is his fertile garden, in the fragrance of whose sweetness he especially delights. Who, therefore, will not fear to offend her or provoke her by injuries? Who can believe that the bridegroom is not gravely offended by an insult to his bride? What violator of the Church’s liberty can be protected, against God and man, by any defence so that he may not be crushed into dust and ashes by the hammer of heavenly power?

For mother Church has cause to grieve deeply and, full of complaints, to express her sorrow in cries: she has been assailed by grave injuries and struck by monstrous crimes and losses. She grieves, I say—and no wonder—for she sees that those who should have been dear to her have become her enemies. Those who sucked [Col. 1317D] her breasts, refreshed by the sweetness of maternal milk, compel her—alas!—to taste the cup of bitterness. Those made fruitful through her by the abundance of great goods do not hesitate to provoke her with hostile efforts and, so far as lies in them, to oppress her liberty. O damnable vice of ingratitude, a thing hateful to heaven and earth, a hostile thing! For every law of holy Church is thrown into confusion when sons thus despise their mother.

We have indeed seen this complaint concerning a certain Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury, in your letters sent to the Apostolic See; and in them we found that he had renounced his right without your counsel and had made himself a fool in the king’s court. Since he ought not to have renounced it without our special permission, because the laws provide [Col. 1318A] that this is one special case reserved to the supreme pontiff, although, as is said, he was elected through simony, we commend purity of conscience and rebuke scrupulous inquisitiveness. But lest the purity of religion succumb in confusion or the depravity of simony escape unpunished, [Col. 1318B] we depose him from every ecclesiastical order and from the archbishopric and declare him utterly foolish. Under pain of major excommunication, we command you to impose a fitting punishment upon him: namely, that he be confined in a strict monastery to perform perpetual penance there.

Therefore, dearest son, we command you to expel him from your court, because it is unbecoming that one who had been a metropolitan in so sacred a college and had lived among religious persons should be a jester or actor in your presence. Further, dearest son, if the bishops of your kingdom prove—God forbid—too negligent in carrying out our apostolic command and in the archbishopric, we wish you to extend helping hands to sustain the liberty of the Roman Church; and thus you will obtain the apostolic blessing. For after judgment has been rendered, if they remain incorrigible, holy Church can do no more than invoke the secular arm.

Further, most beloved son, it has reached our ears that another succeeded in the place of the aforesaid archbishop and publicly preached many monstrous and malicious things in the vernacular against your most illustrious person; likewise, without consulting apostolic counsel and before the pallium had been sent, he administered holy orders. We therefore judged that he had been duly elected neither by papal will nor even by royal power, but against the will alike of all rulers and interested persons. Thus, by this case, [Col. 1318D] we may properly invoke the title concerning a cleric promoted by a leap: he had not been elected from a sacred place, namely from a cloister, as was proper, nor from a bishopric to the dignity of archbishop, but—lamentably—from keeper of a prison to archbishop. Yet although due order was not preserved in the election, by apostolic authority we quash, invalidate, and annul that election; for his empty election we excommunicate him and now personally summon him to appear before us.

Furthermore, according to the counsel of our brethren, we graciously wish to dispense with him as follows: that for the time being he may have administration and fellowship with his table-companions and servants, until he can conveniently undertake the journey to the Apostolic See. We command that [Col. 1319A] he present himself before the apostolic presence as soon as possible. Let him know for certain that, unless the special affection which we have had and still have for his person restrained the just movement of our mind, he would learn by punishment how greatly he had offended in presuming, in contempt of canonical enactments and general custom, to usurp the office of archbishop.

Written at Rome, on the second day of December, in the first year of our apostolate.

II. Bull granting indulgences to the Church of Saint Mark at Venice. (Venice, at Saint Mark’s, 12 May.)

[VERCI, *History of the Trevisan March*, I, 22.]

[Col. 1319B] ALEXANDER, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all Christ’s faithful, present and future: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although we ought to extend the right hand of our munificence as a debt to all the faithful of the holy Roman Church, it is especially fitting that we raise to the prerogative of spiritual grace, and enlarge with the worthier favours of our beneficence, those who show themselves to us and to the holy Roman Church with more fervent devotion, steadfast in faith and faithfully effective in work.

[Col. 1319C] Therefore, desiring that the church of St. Mark at Venice, in the diocese of Castello, may frequently be distinguished by more eminent honors, [Col. 1320A] and that Christ’s faithful may the more willingly gather there out of devotion, and more readily extend helping hands for its preservation, inasmuch as they see themselves there more abundantly enriched by the gift of heavenly grace, relying on the mercy of almighty God and the authority of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, we grant full absolution from all their sins to all who are truly penitent, confessed, and contrite, who each year devoutly visit the said church of St. Mark on the day of the Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, from the evening of its vigil until the evening of that day, and extend helping hands for its preservation. Moreover, during the seven days following the said feast, on each of those days we mercifully remit in the Lord one seventh part of the penances imposed upon them. These presents are to endure for all time.

Therefore let absolutely no one violate this document of our grant and remission, or rashly oppose it. But should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and that at the Last Judgment he will be punished with such severity by the strict Judge.

Given at Venice, at St. Mark’s, on the sixth day before the Ides of May, [Col. 1320C] in the eighteenth year of our pontificate.

[Col. 1319]

# A SUMMARY EXPOSITION OF THE SERIES OF DECRETAL LETTERS OF ALEXANDER III, ROMAN PONTIFF

(According to the recension of Philipp Jaffé, *Regesta Romanorum pontificum*, p. 679 [Note: [Col. 1319D] We have judged it superfluous to print here in full the decretal letters of Alexander III which pertain to our collections of councils and canon law [Col. 1320D] shortly to be published. EDITORS OF THE *PATROLOGIA*].)

## YEAR 1165

[Col. 1319D]

I. He replies to W[illiam], bishop-elect of Chartres, that “in cases entrusted for decision within a fixed period, unless the day fixed by the Apostolic See is extended by the common consent of the parties, the mandate expires when that period has elapsed.” Mansi XXII. 300; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 266; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 49; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 29, chapter 4.—“Concerning cases which.”

## YEAR 1166?

II. He replies to the Archbishop of Bourges concerning “matrimonial cases.” Mansi XXII. 427.—“It has been reported,” etc.

[Col. 1320D]

III. He replies to the Archbishop of Esztergom, telling him not to regard the pallium as simoniacally procured because “when Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Damaso—then, however, cardinal deacon of St. Eustachius and legate of the Apostolic See—came into those regions to carry the pallium, Alan, his brother, sent that cardinal one horse.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 283; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 3, chapter 18; Mansi XXII. 426.—“Although your questions.”

## YEARS 1170–1171

IV. He replies to [William], Bishop of Agde, that penance must be imposed upon a woman who, “wishing to gain for herself her husband’s greater love, received Christ’s body and retained it in her mouth; she then offered her husband a kiss with it, and she was unable to swallow it, but afterward it was turned into flesh—and the flesh grew, and is still in her mouth,” etc. (From book XII of the register.) Baluzius, *Miscellanea*, III. 373; Mansi XXI. 1100–1101, XXII. 439; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 439; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 418, 199, 228; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 1, chapter 12.—“Concerning that woman”; “Concerning the woman who”; “Certainly concerning the matter that”; “Furthermore, concerning the woman.”

V. He answers the questions of [Theobald], Bishop of Amiens. (From book XII of the register.) Mansi XXII. 438; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 257, 59, 192, 196, 268, 332; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 30, chapter 15; title 31, chapter 10; book IV, title 15, chapter 2; title 19, chapter 3; book V, title 33, chapter 7.—“That the Apostolic See”; “Certainly concerning the canon”; “Furthermore, concerning Hugh”; “In addition, concerning the donation”; “Moreover, concerning the count”; “Moreover, since”; “Moreover, although.”

VI. He writes to [Raymond], Archbishop of Arles and cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, concerning the marriage of Ermengard and Blasius. (From book XII of the register.) Mansi XXII. 437; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 318; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 54; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 29, chapter 16.—“The matrimonial case”; “The matrimonial case.”

VII. He forbids the Patriarch of Jerusalem to have the names of absent clerics subscribed in privileges “as though they were present.” (From book XII of the register.) Mansi XXII. 434; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 157; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 10, chapter 5.—“With how much greater dignity.”

VIII. He writes to the procurator and canons of Sora concerning Mariota’s marriage. (From book XII of the register.) Mansi XXII. 439; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 314; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 229; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 1, chapter 13.—“Coming to the Apostolic…”

IX. He writes to the Abbot of St. Benedict of Vebia (otherwise Nebia) concerning the penance of a monk who killed thieves. [Col. 1321C] (From book XII of the register.) Mansi XXII. 437; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 224; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 307; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 12, chapter 10.—“We have received your letter.”

X. He commands the bishop and archdeacon of Vicenza to adjudge Heremann’s sons legitimate. (From book XII of the register.) Mansi XXII. 435; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 265; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 17, chapter 8.—“It has been brought to…”

XI. He replies to the Bishop of Worcester that “monks are to be heard when accusing their abbots.” (From book XII of the register.) Mansi XXII. 433; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 275; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 275, 135; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 30, chapter 2; book V, title 1, chapter 11.—“On your side, of this kind” (“Concerning confirmations”).

## YEARS 1172–1173

[Col. 1321D]

XII. He replies to [William], Bishop of Chartres, concerning a priest who “had repeatedly slept in a church with another man’s wife.” (From book XIV of the register.) Mansi XXII. 434; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 220; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 310; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 17, chapter 5.—“You informed us about a certain man.”

XIII. He answers the questions of the Bishop of Nidaros—printed *Vidrosiensis*, but read *Nidrosiensis*—legate of the Apostolic See. (From book XIV of the register.) Mansi XXII. 435; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 326; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 347; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 19, chapter 3; book V, title 40, chapter 14.—“He asked us.”

## YEARS 1163–1179

XIV. He writes to R[oger], Archbishop of York, and R[oger], Bishop of Worcester, concerning the case of the clerics R. and A. Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 242; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 67; Decretals of Gregory [Col. 1322A], book I, title 36, chapter 6.—“From the letters of your brotherhood”; “From your letters”; “From your letters.”

XV. He commands G[ilbert], Bishop of London, and R[oger], Bishop of Worcester, to judge between R., a priest, and T., a cleric. Mansi XXII. 301; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II. 268; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 51.—“It came to us from…”

XVI. He replies, through the messenger B., to Roger, Bishop of Worcester. He commends the poor. Letters of St. Thomas, ed. Giles, II. 108.—“The letters of your brotherhood.”

XVII. He replies on various matters to R[oger], Bishop of Worcester, who seeks advice. Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II. 99.—“We remember that we, from…”

XVIII. He commands R[oger], Bishop of Worcester, that the man who, having put away his wife, married another, should, “if the former woman and the second are related to one another in the first or second degree of consanguinity, be made to relinquish both and remain forever without hope of marriage; but if they are found to be related in the third degree, he is to compel the man to leave the second and receive the first as his wife.” Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II. 102; Mansi XXII. 290; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 318; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 252.—“It has come to our ears.”

XIX. He asks R[oger], Bishop of Worcester, not to take from the brethren of Oseney the church of Beibur. Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II. 103; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 156; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 10, chapter 3.—“Since we [have] to you”; “Since we long ago.”

XX. He commands R[oger], Bishop of Worcester, and the prior of Panteia to judge between the monks of Aera (otherwise Atra or Acra) and the monks of Caen (otherwise Gadon or Ganon). Mansi XXII. 277; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 201; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 280; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 3, chapter 15.—“The complaint of the monks.”

[Col. 1322C]

XXI. He commands R[oger], Bishop of Worcester (otherwise the Abbot of Evesham), to render judgment between the brethren of Durham monastery and the monks of St. Albans. Mansi XXII. 394–395; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 367, 44; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 23, chapter 5.—“The case which is being litigated”; “To the archdeacons of…”

## YEARS 1174–1179

XXII. He commands R[ichard], Archbishop of Canterbury, primate of all England and legate of the Apostolic See, and R[oger], Bishop of Worcester, to restore a certain benefice to the cleric G. Mansi XXII. 354; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 247; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 35; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 17, chapter 7.—“From the complaint sent to us.”

XXIII. He writes to R[ichard], Archbishop of Canterbury, and R[oger], Bishop of Worcester, that the canons of Pleinteim (otherwise Plutino or Plunnium) “are not to be excluded [Col. 1322D] from giving testimony in the matter concerning their own church.” Mansi XXII. 305; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 280; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 100; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 20, chapter 12.—“When the messenger of the canons…”

## YEAR 1180

XXIV. He commands [Richard], archbishop, and the Archdeacon of Canterbury that, when the Abbot of St. Augustine “brings suitable persons to be presented to his vacant churches, they are to receive them without obstruction.” (Fragment.) Chronicle of William Thorn, in Twysden, *Rerum Anglicarum Scriptores*, II. 1831.—“Very grave [matter] to…”

XXV. He commands [Robert], Bishop of Hereford, [Baldwin], Bishop of Worcester, and Master Peter of Melide that, “if [Richard], Archbishop of Canterbury, wishes to impugn as false the privileges by which the abbot and brethren of St. Augustine believe themselves defended against his claim, they are to cause them to be exhibited to him as soon as possible [Col. 1323A] and faithfully copied.” Chronicle of William Thorn, in Twysden, *Historiae Anglicanae Scriptores*, II. 1831.

## YEARS 1159–1181

XXVI. He replies to the King of England that the right of patronage over the church of Ligurgis (otherwise Bligurgis or Bligurd) could not have been granted to the knight R. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 212; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 304; Mansi XXI. 1091, XXII. 440.—“The letters of your magnificence.”

XXVII. He writes to the King of England concerning the patronage of churches. Mansi XXII. 414; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 78; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 1, chapter 3.—“How greatly the divine [power]”; “How greatly divine [power].”

XXVIII. He commands the abbots of St. Albans and Leicester to order the church of Aleton restored to the monastery of St. Evroul. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 377; Mansi XXI. 1095, XXII. 403.—“Our beloved sons.”

XXIX. He writes to the parish priest and clerics of St. Nazarius of Albareto [Col. 1323B] concerning the dispute “which they had in the church of Solaria.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 124; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 28, chapter 8.—“On the basis of reason”; “But after the appeal.”

XXX. He writes to the Bishop of Abaria (otherwise Amiens) concerning someone who “met his death in a tournament.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 415; Mansi XXI. 1100; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 13, chapter 2.—“It has come to our hearing.”

XXXI. He commands the Bishop of Albi to judge between the monks of La Sauve-Majeure and O. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 571; Mansi XXI. 1095.—“The prior and monks.”

XXXII. He writes to the Bishops of Albi and Beauvais concerning a certain knight’s marriage. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 370; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 13, chapter 8.—“From [the matter] sent to us.”

XXXIII. He writes to the Bishop of Alife concerning possessions granted to laymen. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 70, 161; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 41, chapter 1; [Col. 1323C] Mansi XXII. 381; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 236.—“But concerning possessions”; “Your [letter] asked.”

XXXIV. He commands the abbot and monks of St. Andrew to pay certain tithes to the canons of Plaicio. Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II. 105; Mansi XXII. 396; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 331; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 33, chapter 6.—“If concerning the land.”

XXXV. He replies to the Bishop of Andria concerning “clerics who claim as their own by hereditary right churches that they have built.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 210; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 302; Mansi XXII. 340; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 38, chapter 15.—“Your [letter] consulted us.”

XXXVI. He forbids archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of churches established throughout England to “pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against certain monks.” Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 212; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 182.—“Although all places…”

XXXVII. He writes to bishops, archdeacons, and other prelates [Col. 1323D] of churches established throughout England concerning the excommunication of those “who have laid violent hands upon monks or lay brethren of a certain order.” Mansi XXII. 335; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 214; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 345; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 39, chapter 9.—“Parishioners.”

XXXVIII. He commands [the archbishops and bishops established throughout England] that, “if any lay violent hands upon the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem, they are publicly to declare them excommunicated.” Mansi XXII. 334; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 212; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 344.—“Grievously [they offend] the eyes…”

XXXIX. He writes to archbishops and bishops established throughout Gaul (otherwise England) against those who “on the pretext of lay recognition or secular power claim for themselves, in a secular court and without the bishop’s permission having been sought, the patronage of churches and ecclesiastical benefices.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, [Col. 1324A] IV. 212; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 304; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 38, chapter 21; Mansi XXII. 440–441.—“It has been reported to [our] ears”; “It has come to our ears”; “Furthermore, because…”

XL. He writes to bishops, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches established throughout Gaul that they are not to place under interdict or excommunicate the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem or their churches. Mansi XXII. 408; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 230; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 331.—“Certainly, since from…”

XLI. He replies to the Bishop of Arras concerning his lawsuit with the cleric S. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 192; Mansi XX. 1089.—“It has become fully known to us.”

XLII. He writes to the Bishop of Arras (otherwise Arles) concerning a certain wood which the canons of Beauvais are to restore to the monks of Chaalis. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 165; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 266; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 17, chapter 3.—“When the beloved sons…”

[Col. 1324B]

XLIII. He writes to the Bishop of Ávila—printed *Abulen.*, but read *Avilensis*—concerning G., priest of the church of St. James, excommunicated by the Bishop of Zamora after an appeal to the Apostolic See had been made. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 379; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 28, chapter 34.—“It has come to our hearing.”

XLIV. He writes to the Archbishop of Bari concerning the marriage of P., a citizen of Bari. Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 327; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 228; Mansi XXI. 1091.—“P. came to us.”

XLV. He commands the Bishop of Bath to remove those to whom the King of Scotland, while he was holding the inheritance of Count S. under occupation, “granted churches.” Mansi XXII. 413; Mansi XXI. 1098; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 397.—“Our beloved son” (“Our beloved brother”).

XLVI. He replies to the Bishop of Bath concerning those “who are joined under the name of marriage before they are of marriageable age.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 235; Decretals of Gregory, [Col. 1324C] book IV, title 2, chapter 8.—“Your [letter] to us.”

XLVII. He commands the Bishop of Bath to admonish R. to restore the dowry to the woman E., “who was separated from him by ecclesiastical judgment.” Mansi XXII. 388; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 334; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 270.—“From E.’s complaint” (otherwise M.); “From M.’s question.”

XLVIII. He writes to the Bishop of Bath concerning those “who, being below the proper age, enter into betrothals for marriage.” Mansi XXII. 296; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 323; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 235; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 2, chapter 7.—“Concerning those who are under…”

XLIX. He writes to the Bishop of Bath that “women, and also other persons who are not legally independent, cannot be absolved by the diocesan bishop if they have laid violent hands upon a cleric.” Mansi XXII. 335; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 211; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 343; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 39, chapter 6.—“Women, or also”; “Women also, or.”

[Col. 1324D]

L. He writes to the Bishop of Bath concerning the ordination of deacons. Mansi XXII. 372; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 240; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 29; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 11, chapter 1.—“But subdeacons.”

LI. He replies to the Bishop of Bath that “both those who are drawn into litigation and their principal supporters are to be restrained by ecclesiastical censure if they manifestly obstruct justice.” Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 265; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 48; Mansi XXII. 299; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 28, chapter 1.—“Because it has been asked.”

LII. He writes these words to the Bishops of Bath and Exeter: “If anyone, unaware that he is a cleric, lays violent hands on a cleric who wears long hair, he should not for that reason be presented before the Apostolic See, nor should he be marked by excommunication.” Mansi XXII. 332; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 210; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 342.—“But if anyone [lays hands] upon…”

[Col. 1325A]

LIII. He replies to the Bishop of Beauvais concerning those who “come to confession concerning crimes and, though they wish to confess, nevertheless assert that they cannot abstain.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 418; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 38, chapter 5.—“That certain persons, as…”

LIV. He replies to the Bishop of Beauvais (otherwise Bavaria) that “a person may not contract marriage with a woman whom, while his own wife is alive, he has in fact joined to himself”; and that lepers “are free to enter into marriage.” Mansi XXII. 291, 395; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 319; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 247–248; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 7, chapter 3; title 8, chapter 2.—“Concerning the point that”; “But concerning the point that”; “But concerning the matter that”; “Since from many [things].”

LV. He replies to the Bishop of Beauvais concerning clandestine marriages. Mansi XXII. 433; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 237; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 3, chapter 2; title 17, chapter 9.—“That [which] to us from…”

[Col. 1325B]

LVI. He replies to the Bishop of Beauvais concerning false testimony. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 98; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 20, chapter 9.—“As has become known to us.”

LVII. He replies to the bishop and archpriest of Bologna concerning appeals. Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 292; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 130; Mansi XXII. 447; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 28, chapter 18.—“Your [letter] consulted us”; “Concerning the matter that.”

LVIII. He replies to the Bishop of Brixen concerning clerics “who, though they abound in many ecclesiastical benefices, are unwilling to be promoted to higher orders.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 359; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 14, chapter 6.—“You ask us.”

LIX. He commands the Bishop of Brescia to ensure the restoration of goods taken from the monastery of St. Quirinus at Tegernsee. Pez, *Thesaurus anecdotorum*, VI. I, 391.—“They informed us.”

LX. He writes to the Bishop of Brescia concerning the marriage of Matthew and the woman Agolechis. Mansi XXII. 284; [Col. 1325C] Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 312; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 198; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 32, chapter 7.—“From the public instrument.”

LXI. He replies to the Bishop of Brescia concerning tithes of newly cultivated land. Mansi XXII. 443; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 191; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 30, chapter 13.—“Since from us…”

LXII. He writes to the archdeacon and chapter of Brindisi that the wife of a certain V., received into a community of nuns, is to be restored to her husband. Theiner, *Disquisitiones criticae*, 431.—“Being present in…”

LXIII. He replies to the Archbishop of Bordeaux that a young man to whom a girl related by blood has been betrothed ought not to be compelled to marry her. Baluzius, *Miscellanea*, III. 376; Mansi XXI. 1103, XXII. 326; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 330; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 406; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 14, chapter 2.—“But concerning the matter”; “Concerning the matter that.”

LXIV. He writes to the Archbishop of Bordeaux that two archdeaconries may not be administered by the archdeacon G. Mansi XXII. 365, 384; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 229; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, [Col. 1325D] IV. 328; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 5, chapter 14.—“Furthermore, concerning the archdeacon”; “Furthermore, concerning G.”

LXV. He replies to the Archbishop of Bordeaux concerning a knight “who challenges his marriage, saying that he is related to his wife in the fourth degree of consanguinity.” Mansi XXII. 297; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 323; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 266.—“Your [letter] consulted us.”

LXVI. He replies to the Archbishop of Canterbury concerning the marriage of the young man R. and Mary, daughter of Gilbert of St. Léger. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 224; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 320; Mansi XXII. 292, 312, 401; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 1, chapter 7.—“From the letters which”; “But as to what you asked”; “But concerning this matter, that.”

LXVII. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury that “if there are men or women who contract the disease of leprosy, he is to compel wives to follow their husbands and husbands to follow their wives.” [Col. 1326A] Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 332; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 247; Mansi XXII. 394; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 8, chapter 1.—“It has come to us.”

LXVIII. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury to restore the church of Durefort to the cleric Renald. Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 13, chapter 7; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 369.—“Renald complained to us.”

LXIX. He replies to the Archbishop of Canterbury concerning delegated judges and remissions. Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 295; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 133; Mansi XXI. 1087.—“We, in our eminent [position]…”

LXX. He grants to the Archbishop of Canterbury that he need not “confirm the judgments of judges delegated by himself within the province” if “nothing concerning the cases themselves has been argued in his presence.” Baluzius, *Miscellanea*, III. 374 and 380; Mansi XXI. 1103 and 1108, XXII. 411, 482; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 362, 363; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 29, chapter 18.—“When you consulted”; “If concerning the case.”

[Col. 1326B]

LXXI. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury to order the Hospitallers not to “presume to give Christian burial to excommunicated persons.” Mansi XXII. 385.—“Since for this purpose…”

LXXII. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury concerning the right of patronage over the chapel of Stretton. Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 302; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 211; Mansi XXII. 341, 413; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 38, chapter 16.—“Concerning the right of patronage.”

LXXIII. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury concerning the litigation between the canons of St. Frideswide and the canons of Oseney. Mansi XXI. 1086, XXII. 321; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 294; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 132.—“They informed us.”

LXXIV. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury to grant a prebend to Master Ia., canonically instituted in his church. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 151; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 5, chapter 9.—“It has been reported to [our] ears.”

LXXV. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury concerning the case [Col. 1326C] of L., a priest. Mansi XXII. 445; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 99; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 20, chapter 10.—“Coming to us with…”

LXXVI. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury to “remove from churches the sons of clerics in which their fathers ministered, whether as incumbents or vicars, without any intermediate incumbent; but to tolerate those who obtained churches held by their fathers through the mediation of other incumbents.” Baluzius, *Miscellanea*, III. 374 and 379; Mansi XXI. 1102 and 1105, XXII. 449; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 360; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 17, chapter 11.—“For the extirpation [of]”; “To the holy ones of God.”

LXXVII. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury (otherwise Tours or London) concerning clerics under interdict or excommunication. Mansi XXII. 369; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 223; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 323; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 27, chapter 3.—“But clerics, if…”

LXXVIII. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury (otherwise Rouen) to absolve Peter of Ursiton (otherwise Neasclea) from excommunication. [Col. 1326D] Mansi XXII. 345; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 237; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 110; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 24, chapter 7.—“You should know concerning our…”

LXXIX. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury (otherwise the dean of For and the archdeacon of Bedefet) to order the canons of Lanstanet (otherwise Lamestanter) to relinquish a certain chapel unjustly occupied. Mansi XXII. 346; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II. 238; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 112.—“It has been made known to us.”

LXXX. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury to protect a certain archdeacon from the bishop’s wrongs. Mansi XXII. 365; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 229; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 327; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 31, chapter 2.—“Furthermore, because…”

LXXXI. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury to forbid monks “to presume to receive or hold villages or churches on lease.” Mansi XXII [Col. 1327A] 373; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 231; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 221.—“To your brotherhood, through…”

LXXXII. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury to “correct and punish” the Bishop of Coventry because “he granted churches to boys under ten years of age.” Mansi XXII. 365; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 241; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 31; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 14, chapter 2.—“On the ground of the charge entrusted [to you]”; “From [the matter] entrusted to you.”

LXXXIII. He replies to the Archbishop of Canterbury concerning “remissions granted at the dedications of churches.” Mansi XXII. 393; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 341; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 38, chapter 4.—“But what you asked.”

LXXXIV. He grants to the Archbishop of Canterbury that, “if the possession of those who appeal to his hearing has been disturbed, he may restore it, passing over the person against whom the appeal was lodged.” Mansi XXII. 318; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 291; Augustinus [Col. 1327B] Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 128; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 28, chapter 17.—“Since we are bound…”

LXXXV. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury concerning clerics who “are said to keep prostitutes in their houses.” Mansi XXII. 351; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 336; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 143.—“Since in Canterbury”; “Since in the province.”

LXXXVI. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans that they are not to permit clerics “to keep prostitutes in their houses.” Mansi XXII. 348; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 334; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 142, 144; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 2, chapter 4; title 3, chapter 1.—“As for extirpating”; “But if any…”

LXXXVII. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans not to permit, “when incumbents of churches die, their sons, relatives, or others to intrude themselves into the aforesaid churches.” Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II. 63; Mansi XXII. 379; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 209; Augustinus [Col. 1327C] Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 132.—“From frequent complaints”; “From the complaints of clerics.”

LXXXVIII. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans that, “if it is manifest and public that fathers held incumbencies in churches, they are to exclude their sons from those same churches.” Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 248; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 37; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 17, chapter 10.—“Since [it is provided] by the sacred canons”; “Since it is by sacred [canons].”

LXXXIX. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans to forbid clerics, upon the death of church incumbents, “to make an agreement to pay those churches revenues greater than customary.” Mansi XXII. 377; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 208; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 64, 282; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 35, chapter 6; book III, title 39, chapter 11.—“Since the clerics of your…”

XC. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans that they are not to permit clerics “to receive churches and ecclesiastical [Col. 1327D] benefices without the consent of the diocesan bishop.” Mansi XXII. 378; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 209; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 154; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 7, chapter 3.—“From frequent complaints.”

XCI. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans concerning the excommunication of those who “kill clerics, cause them to be killed, or otherwise lay violent hands upon them.” Mansi XXII. 333; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 211; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 344.—“Not without sorrow.”

XCII. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans to see that clerics do not take usury. Mansi XXII. 344; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 216; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 314; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 19, chapter 2.—“Since not only…”

XCIII. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans that they are not to grant the incumbency of any church to anyone “under fourteen years of age.” Mansi XXII. 366; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix [Col. 1328A] 241; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 32; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 14, chapter 3.—“It is unbecoming.”

XCIV. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans to compel their parishioners “to pay to the churches to which they are due tithes from the proceeds of mills and fisheries, from wool and hay.” Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II. 65; Mansi XXII. 282; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 248; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 183; Decretals of Gregory, book III, title 30, chapter 5.—“It has come to us that…”

XCV. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans concerning the appointment of stewards for vacant churches. Mansi XXII. 341; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II. 264; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 58; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 31, chapter 4.—“Since we often”; “Since you often.”

XCVI. He replies to the Archbishop of Canterbury and his suffragans concerning those “who, having left their wives, do not hesitate to cling to concubines and strive, through the obstacle of an appeal, to defend their error [Col. 1328B] and rashness.” Mansi XXII. 317; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 291; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 128.—“It has been reported to [our] ears.”

XCVII. He writes to the Archbishop of Canterbury and the Bishop of Chichester concerning the case of A., a priest. Mansi XXII. 309.—“A. reported to us.”

XCVIII. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury and the Bishop of Worcester to restore a certain church to N. Mansi XXII. 361.—“We command that N…”

XCIX. He commands the Archbishop of Canterbury and the Bishop of Worcester (otherwise the Abbot of Rievaulx and the Prior of Bridlington) to decide a certain controversy. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 92; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 278; Mansi XXII. 281; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 8, chapter 1.—“Our beloved sons.”

C. He commands all monks and regular canons established throughout the province of Canterbury, “when churches in which they hold the right of presentation become vacant, to present suitable clerics to the diocesan bishops, who are to answer to the bishops concerning spiritual matters and to them concerning temporal matters.” [Col. 1328C] Letters of Gilbert Foliot, ed. Giles, II. 68; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 203; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 304; Mansi XXII. 342.—“Since it is fitting for us.”

CI. He replies to the Bishop of Caprula—printed *Crapulanus*, but read *Caprulanus*—concerning “the withdrawal of an appeal.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 129; Mansi XXI. 1086.—“You asked from…”

CII. He commands the Bishop of Capua (otherwise *Capitulanus*, or *Caprarius*), the Abbot of St. Lucy, and the Prior of Holy Cross to judge between the monks N. and O. “concerning an election made by each side.” Mansi XXII. 305; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 279; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 99; Decretals of Gregory, book II, title 20, chapter 11.—“The case which [is] between N…”

CIII. He writes to the Bishop of Chartres concerning a settlement made before an extraordinary judge. Mansi XXII, [Col. 1328D] 378; XXI. 1091; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 208; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 66, 216; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 36, chapter 5.—“For the future, know” (*noveris* / *noveritis*, “you should know,” singular/plural).

CIV. He commands the Bishop of Chartres to decree that ecclesiastical persons of the bishopric are not to make wills concerning what comes to them from the goods of churches. Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 236; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 175.—“Care urges us.”

CV. He writes to the Bishop of Chartres (the Archbishop of Canterbury) concerning the case of the cleric G., the abbess of Helenstowe, and the cleric H. Mansi XXII. 317.—“From the letters of the venerable…”

CVI. He replies to the Bishop of Chartres (otherwise the Archbishop of Canterbury) concerning delegated judges. Mansi XXII. 303; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 270, 284, 293; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 52, 106, 131; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 29, chapter 11; book II, title 28, chapter 21.—“Certainly, because we”; (“Concerning witnesses not”; “The question which”).

[Col. 1329A]

CVII. He commands the Abbot of Monte Cassino to judge concerning the marriage of certain persons. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 254; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 324; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 14, chapter 1; Mansi XXII. 297.—“From your letters.”

CVIII. He again commands the Bishop of Castello—printed *Catelanus*, but read *Castellanus*, i.e. Venetian—to confer “the gift of blessing” upon Cassiota, abbess of St. Zacharias. Baluzius, *Miscellanea*, III. 380; Mansi XXI. 1108; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 409; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 1, chapter 13.—“We remember already…”

CIX. He writes to the Bishop of Le Mans concerning absolving laymen “bound by the bond of excommunication for violently laying hands upon a cleric.” Mansi XXII. 335; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, appendix 214; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 345; Decretals of Gregory, book V, title 39, chapter 11.—“For the future, know.”

CX. He writes to the Bishop of Le Mans concerning the subdeacon F., who took a wife. Mansi XXII. 449; Augustinus [Col. 1329B] Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 243; Decretals of Gregory, book IV, title 6, chapter 2.—“From your letters.”

CXI. To the Bishop of Le Mans, concerning “the presentation of a priest.” Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, appendix 227; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 54; Mansi XXII. 413; Decretals of Gregory, book I, title 29, chapter 15.—“Concerning the matter which you add”; “But concerning the matter.”

CXII. He replies to the Bishop of Le Mans that it has been enacted that clerics “ordained in remote regions must be supported, concerning their ordination, by the testimony of at least five bishops.” Mansi XXII. 371; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 227; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 42; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 22, c. 1. — “Your letter moved us.”

CXIII. He writes this to the Bishop of Le Mans: “Upon churches which a bishop has newly recovered from the hands of laymen, we see that no levy ought to be imposed beyond the cathedraticum and all the dues imposed upon other churches.” He adds that “clerics cannot by right make a testament concerning movables which they have acquired through churches.” [Col. 1329C] Mansi XXII. 275, 381; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 227; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 216, 174; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 26, c. 8; tit. 39, c. 9. — “But concerning the churches which”; “To these present matters”; “To this present matter.”

CXIV. He writes to the Bishop of Cesten. concerning a young man deprived of his genitals. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 40. — “Beloved in Christ.”

CXV. He writes to the Bishop of Chester concerning the removal of simoniacal clerics. Mansi XXII. 278; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 200; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 280; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 3, c. 13. — “It has been reported to our ears.”

CXVI. He writes to the Dean of Chichester concerning the controversy of the clerics W. and E. Mansi XXII. 308; (Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 281; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 110; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 23, c. 10). — “The letter of Exeter”; (“Because [it has] the appearance of truth”; “Because it is probable”).

[Col. 1329D] CXVII. He writes to the Dean of Chichester concerning his final controversy with the archdeacon. Mansi XXII. 395; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 95; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 19, c. 3. — “From your letter” [singular feminine]; “From your letter” [plural]; “From your letter” [singular].

CXVIII. He grants to the Abbot of Cîteaux and the brethren of Cuman. (otherwise, to the abbot and brethren of Rival.) “that, if letters have been obtained from the Apostolic See against them concerning tithes or other matters which that See has specially granted to their order, without mention having been made of the Cistercian Order, they shall by no means be bound to answer them.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 354; Mansi XXII. 402; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 3, c. 6. — “Since the order.”

CXIX. He rebukes the abbots of the Cistercian Order because “some of them, having utterly forgotten, or being ignorant of, their original institution, possess, contrary to the rule of the order, villages, mills, churches, and altars; receive fealties and homages; and maintain judicial officers and tax-collectors.” [Col. 1330A] Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 396; Mansi XXII. 424; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 35, c. 3. — “Recalling how these things.”

CXX. He grants to the abbots of the Cistercian Order established throughout England that “if anyone has purposed to visit the Lord’s Sepulchre or other shrines of saints, and, because of illness or some other reasonable cause arising, wishes to assume the religious habit among them, they may receive him freely.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 395; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 34, c. 4. — “Sacred Scripture.”

CXXI. He writes to bishops, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches throughout Gaul that they are not to “permit converts of the Cistercian Order to be received into their dioceses without the abbots’ permission.” Mansi XXII. 374; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 233; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 193; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 31, c. 7. — “It is not for you.”

CXXII. He exhorts all bishops not to compel Cistercian brethren [Col. 1330B] “to come to synod or council.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 396. — “Our beloved sons.”

CXXIII. He orders certain bishops to forbid archdeacons, deans, and priests to pronounce either a sentence of excommunication or interdict against the servants or hired labourers of Cistercian brethren because they work on certain days which others regard as solemn. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 368; Mansi XXI. 1094. — “Those informing us.”

CXXIV. He orders Master Fidaritio of Civitatis (otherwise, Fidantia, canon of Civit.) not to declare the boy T., if he lays aside the habit assumed before completion of his fourteenth year, wholly released from the claim of the hermits of Monte Foliano. Mansi XXII. 357; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 233; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 195; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 31, c. 8. — “Let it be known to us”; “To our hearing.”

CXXV. He orders the Bishop of Clermont to command that the father of I., bearer of the letter, who “while dying could not obtain ecclesiastical burial,” be buried in a cemetery. [Col. 1330C] Mansi XXII. 390; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 215; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 312; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 17, c. 5. — “In your letters, which”; “Your letters, which.”

CXXVI. He forbids the Bishop of Cosenza to permit a certain deacon “to ascend to a higher grade without the permission of the supreme pontiff.” Mansi XXII. 569; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 223; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 306; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 12, c. 8. — “It was contained in the letter.”

CXXVII. He orders the Bishop of Coventry and the Abbot of Chester to forbid R., Archdeacon of Chester, to fine with a monetary penalty “clerics or laymen who ought to be punished for their offences,” etc. Mansi XXII. 276; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 205; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 339; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 23, c. 6. — “We command that from…”

CXXVIII. He writes to the Bishop of Coventry and the Prior of Thevilla concerning the dispute of P., a cleric, and R., a priest. [Col. 1330D] Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 378; Mansi XXI. 1096. — “The case which is being contested.”

CXXIX. He forbids the Bishop of Coventry and his officials to exact from the brethren of Pipennella, “who belong to the Cistercian Order, tithes from the produce which they cultivate by their own hands or at their own expense.” Mansi XXII. 329; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 252; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 30, c. 12. — “To our hearing.”

CXXX. He commends B. to the Bishop of Cremona; B. has done penance for retaining a church’s chalice. Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 225; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 326; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 18, c. 5. — “From your letter.”

CXXXI. He writes to the Bishop of Cusano (otherwise Consano, Constantio), that he is to compel R. of Lantino to restore certain tithes. [Col. 1331A] Mansi XXII. 281; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 249; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 184. — “We have learned from…”

CXXXII. He orders the Abbot of Dalon. and the Prior of Artigia to judge between P. Gaufredi and the canons of St. Luviani. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 28; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 9, c. 2. — “Since between P…”

CXXXIII. He admonishes E., provost of Dietram’s Cell, to render account to the Abbot of Tegernsee in temporal matters “concerning the church founded upon his estate, according to ancient and reasonable custom.” Pez, *Thesaurus anecdotorum*, VI. I, 396. — “From one of happy memory.”

CXXXIV. He writes to the Abbot of St. Peter of Diva that, “if any one of his subjects, lest he be corrected for his offences, has recourse to the remedy of appeal, he is nevertheless to correct him.” Mansi XXII. 312; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 122; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 286; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 28, c. 3. — “Let it be known to us.”

[Col. 1331B] CXXXV. He commands Hugh, Bishop of Durham, to ensure that the church which Guy, nephew of Jocelin of Balliol, took away from William of Hecgesclivia is restored. *Letters of St Thomas*, ed. Giles, II. 92. — “It has been reported to us.”

CXXXVI. He writes to the Bishop of Durham that, “if an abbot or prior has letters from his chapter approving [a transaction], the chapter cannot revoke a transaction which he has made if it has been observed for some years.” Mansi XXII. 376; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 207; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 65; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 36, c. 5. — “It sometimes happens.”

CXXXVII. He replies to the Bishop of Durham that “sons of priests ought to be admitted to the diaconate or priesthood only if they are of approved life in a monastery or a house of regular canons.” Mansi XXII. 353; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 245; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 34. — “What [you ask] concerning these matters.”

[Col. 1331C] CXXVIII. He writes to the Bishop of Durham concerning appeals. Mansi XXII. 316; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 290; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 127; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 28, c. 15. — “It has been represented to our ears.”

CXXXIX. He writes to the Abbots of St Edmund and Ramesereia (otherwise Ramesia, Meseia) concerning the marriage of Emma and Andrew. Mansi XXII. 294; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 321; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 224; *Decretals of Gregory*, IV, tit. 1, c. 9. — “On Emma’s behalf”; “On behalf of N.”; “On behalf of C.”; “On behalf of Emina.”

CXL. He denies to R[oger], Archbishop of York, who requested it, permission “to compel white and black monks, regular and secular canons, to pay tithes from rented lands which they hold for a term or at farm.” Gilbert Foliot, *Letters*, ed. Giles, II. 72; Martène, *Thesaurus*, I. 600; Mansi XXII. 327; Boehmer, *Corpus* [Col. 1331D] *juris canonici*, II, app. 250; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 185. — “Your brotherhood.”

CXLI. He replies to R[oger], Archbishop of York, who consulted him concerning appeals and other matters. Gilbert Foliot, *Letters*, ed. Giles, II. 75. — “Just as the Roman Church.”

CXLII. He replies to the Archbishop of York concerning appeals. Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 295, 296; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 134; Mansi XXII. 394, 414, 423; XXI. 1087; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 28, c. 24; III, tit. 8, c. 3. — “He set before us”; “It has been reported to our ears”; “Set upon a lofty watchtower”; “When some case.”

CXLIII. He writes to the Archbishop of York “concerning a prior who, paying no regard to his protection and to an appeal made to the Apostolic See, caused one of his canons to be stripped of everything down to his shirt, and compelled him to renounce both accusation and appeal.” Mansi XXII. 319; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 379; [Col. 1332A] *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 28, c. 31. — “Concerning the prior who did not…”

CXLIV. He replies to [Roger], Archbishop of York, that neither he nor other judges may, “where the judgment of a case is committed [to them] without the remedy of appeal [to the Apostolic See], determine also incidental questions after setting appeal aside.” “But,” he says, “a suitable term must be fixed for the appellant to prosecute [the appeal]; if within it he has not prosecuted the appeal, then from that time he shall be compelled, both concerning incidental questions and concerning the principal cause, to abide by the judgment of the delegated judge, appeal being set aside.” Baluze, *Miscellanea*, III. 375; Mansi XXI. 1103; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 379; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 28, c. 33. — “To our ears.”

CXLV. He writes this to the Archbishop of York: “If we have ordered a judgment pronounced by us to be put into execution by someone, and fraud intervenes, the executor has no authority to take cognizance of the whole matter; rather, the questions must be referred to the Apostolic See.” Mansi XXII. 423; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 120; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 27, c. 5. — “Henceforth let it be known.”

CXLVI. He replies to the Archbishop of York concerning delegated judges. Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 271; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 53; Mansi XXII. 403; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 29, c. 13. — “It has been asked on your behalf”; “On behalf of your brotherhood.”

CXLVII. He replies to the Archbishop of York concerning cases “which are committed disjunctively.” Mansi XXII. 400; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 297; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 14; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 3, c. 4; II, tit. 27, c. 9. — “Among the other consultations.”

CXLVIII. He replies to the Archbishop of York that “if letters concerning some cause are obtained from him, and later other letters are obtained without mention of the earlier letters, the judges ought wholly to suspend execution of the letters until they consult the Roman pontiff.” Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 265; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 49; Mansi XXII. 299, 402; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 29, c. 2. — “But if [letters are obtained] from us.”

CXLIX. He grants to the Archbishop of York that “if clerics who have obtained a benefice in churches subject to his jurisdiction move to another diocese in order to reside there without his permission, he may deprive them of their benefices, unless perhaps they are devoted to scholarly studies.” [Col. 1332C] Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 384; Mansi XXII. 383; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 4, c. 5. — “We have thought fit for your brotherhood.”

CL. He writes to the Archbishop of York (otherwise, the Bishop of Durham) that “churches are not to be granted to clerics on terms such that, after their death, others are to succeed by name.” Mansi XXII. 376; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 207; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 64; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 35, c. 5. — “We have received [word] that certain…”

[Col. 1332D] CLI. He replies to the Archbishop of York concerning priests’ sons. Mansi XXII. 355; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 247; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 37; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 17, c. 9. — “From your [letter] to us”; “On your behalf to us.”

CLII. He writes to the Archbishop of York concerning certain churches granted to the church of Blessed Peter at York. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 211; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 304; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 38, c. 20; (Mansi XXII. 342). — “It has been represented to our ears.”

CLIII. He orders the Archbishop of York not to permit the nobleman W., son of Godric, to be harassed by R., cleric of Pontefract, over a certain church. Mansi XXII. 277; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 279; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 3, c. 12. — “When they were in…”

CLIV. He writes to the Archbishop of York concerning the construction of a church in the village of H. (otherwise, Nortona). Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 217; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 48, c. 3. — “To our hearing.”

[Col. 1333A] CLV. He orders the Archbishop of York to exhort Nicholas, Archdeacon of Bedford, not to claim the prebend of the church of Bevianensis. Mansi XXII. 382, (535); Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 243; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 150. — “It has been reported to our ears.”

CLVI. He writes to the Archbishop of York concerning “A., a priest keeping a concubine.” Mansi XXII. 350; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 336; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 143; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 2, c. 5. — “Concerning what you assert.”

CLVII. He writes to the Archbishop of York concerning William’s marriage. Mansi XXII. 287; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 314; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 233; *Decretals of Gregory*, IV, tit. 2, c. 5. — “There came into our presence.”

CLVIII. He orders the Archbishop of York to release the priest A. from a certain oath. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 366; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 43, c. 2. — “Not [Col. 1333B] without much…”

CLIX. He replies to the Archbishop of York that G., who “has entered the religious order of the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem,” may not lawfully be separated from their fellowship. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 392; Mansi XXI. 1098. — “To the hearing of the Apostolic See.”

CLX. He writes to the Archbishop of York and the Bishop of Coventry that the archdeaconry is to be restored to the chaplain N. Mansi XXII. 384; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 270; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 53; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 29, c. 12. — “On behalf of N.”

CLXI. He writes to the Archbishop of York, the Bishop of Exeter, and the Abbot of Herfort concerning the Prior of Prigileven., accused of incontinence. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 377; Mansi XXI. 1096. — “Since a certain person formerly…”

CLXII. He commands the regular canons and monks of the Diocese of York that “if, without the consent of [Roger], archbishop, they have diminished any portions or ancient revenues of clerics, or divided parishes, they are to restore them to their former entirety.” [Col. 1333C] Mansi XXII. 326; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 249; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 152; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 5, c. 10. — “Avarice, which…”

CLXIII. He commands the abbots, priors, and clerics established throughout the Archdiocese of York not to claim churches for themselves “by donation of laymen, unless the bishop’s authority is present.” He adds concerning the excommunication of those “who lay violent hands upon clerics, canons, or converts.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 208, 343; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 300; (Mansi XXII. 338; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 38, c. 11; V, tit. 39, c. 5). — “Because of pastoral”; “Pastoral care”; “With pastoral”; “There is no doubt.”

CLXIV. He informs the provost and canons of the church of Eburdinensis (Ebredunensis?) that he has annulled their excommunication pronounced by the archbishop. Mansi XXII. 306; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 280; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 101; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 20, c. 16. — “Since you, son…”

CLXV. He orders the Bishop of Ely to judge between P., rector of the church of Gestunens, and John of Fescam. Mansi XXII. 398, 399; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 47, 384; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 28, c. 2. — “P. coming to us”; “See to it more diligently”; “But if the aforesaid…”

CLXVI. He grants Richard, Archdeacon of Ely, that “if any church calls him to a benefice or any dignity, notwithstanding that he was not born of lawful marriage, he may freely be admitted to that benefice or dignity.” Ralph de Diceto, *Imagines Historiarum*, in Twysden, *Historiae Anglicanae Scriptores*, I. 651. — “Having heard the praiseworthy…”

CLXVII. He forbids the Archdeacon of Ely to entrust “the care of souls to anyone without the bishop’s permission and mandate.” Mansi XXII. 364; XXI. 1089; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 228; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 43, 155; [Col. 1334A] *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 23, c. 4. — “Since it is enough…”

CLXVIII. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter that “it is contrary to the ordinance of the holy fathers for a man, while his wife remains in the world, or a wife, while her husband does not assume the religious habit, to enter religious life,” etc. Mansi XXII. 283, 284; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 310, 311; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 197; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 32, c. 4. — “Since you are endowed”; “Since endowed you are”; “If anyone who…”

CLXIX. He orders the Bishop of Exeter to dissolve a certain marriage. Mansi XXII. 409. — “Of the bearer of the present [letter].”

CLXX. He orders the Bishop of Exeter to compel R., a knight, to marry the daughter of Edwin of Baseleher. Mansi XXII. 410. — “It came to us that…”

CLXXI. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning the marriage of V. [Col. 1334B] Mansi XXII. 409; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 401; *Decretals of Gregory*, IV, tit. 1, c. 15. — “V. (otherwise W.) coming to us.”

CLXXII. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning those “who, in contracting marriage, have given their pledged word”; they are to be warned to observe the pledge given. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 226; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 324; Mansi XXII. 298, 444. — “Moreover, those who…”

CLXXIII. He replies to the Bishop of Exeter that “a woman may marry during the period of mourning without disgrace.” Mansi XXII. 311; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 338; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 270. — “But concerning that [woman]”; “Concerning that question.”

CLXXIV. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning deacons who have contracted marriages. Mansi XXII. 351; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 337; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 243. — “It has been reported to us.”

CLXXV. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning “a certain learned and noble man, who gave a noble woman his pledge to contract marriage, but now desires to hasten to the fruit of a better life.” [Col. 1334C] Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 401; *Decretals of Gregory*, IV, tit. 1, c. 16. — “Committed”; “Your brotherhood informed us.”

CLXXVI. He replies to the Bishop of Exeter that one “who previously knew carnally the mother or sister of the woman whom he later took as wife” is to be warned to endeavour to induce his wife to observe continence: if she wishes to remain continent, they are to observe continence together; but if she cannot be induced to this, he is both to render the marital debt and to do penance for what he has committed. Mansi XXII. 326; XXI. 1099, 1106; Baluze, *Miscellanea*, III. 379; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 405; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 330. — “Concerning that which…”

CLXXVII. He writes this to the Bishop of Exeter: “No Templar monks can shield themselves by a privilege of the Apostolic See from the duty to avoid excommunicated persons, and, for violently laying hands upon clerics, to be avoided as excommunicated persons.” Mansi XXII. 333; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 211; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 344; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 39, c. 8. — “But no monks…”

CLXXVIII. He orders the Bishop of Exeter to compel archdeacons to relinquish churches which they occupy. Mansi XXII. 364; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 229; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 327; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 31, c. 3. — “To our ears.”

CLXXIX. He orders the Bishop of Exeter to compel G. to restore the church of Ferelegia (otherwise Ferleia) to Master W. Mansi XXII. 375; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 203; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 286; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 4, c. 4. — “The complaint of the master.”

CLXXX. He orders the Bishop of Exeter to admonish Walter to recover and restore to the church “a silver chalice and half of one breviary of the church of Offetolon (otherwise Ofecolon, Ossecoleo),” which Walter’s father, priest of that church, had pledged. [Col. 1335A] Mansi XXII. 380; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 235; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 167; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 21, c. 3. — “From the present [letter].”

CLXXXI. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning “a priest who has fallen into the crime of homicide.” Mansi XXII. 369. — “This priest also…”

CLXXXII. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning A., a cleric “born in the priesthood from incest.” Mansi XXII. 411. — “It has been represented to our ears.”

CLXXXIII. He urges the Bishop of Exeter to induce a certain priest to renounce a priesthood obtained simoniacally. Baluze, *Miscellanea*, III. 378; Mansi XXI. 1104; XXII. 392; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 410; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 3, c. 20. — “Of your brotherhood’s…”

CLXXXIV. He replies to the Bishop of Exeter concerning appeals. Mansi XXII. 303; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 270; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 59. — “Further, when someone…”

[Col. 1335B] CLXXXV. He replies to the Bishop of Exeter concerning the commutation of pilgrimage vows. Mansi XXII. 392, 425; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 258; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 200; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 34, c. 1. — “Concerning pilgrimage”; “Concerning the vow of pilgrimage.”

CLXXXVI. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning the repair of parish churches. Mansi XXII. 380; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 217; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 48, c. 4. — “Concerning those who [repair] parish churches”; “But concerning those who…”

CLXXXVII. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning the dispute between P. and R. Mansi XXII. 388; (Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 334; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 264; *Decretals of Gregory*, IV, tit. 17, c. 6). — “We remember that [we wrote] to your brotherhood”; (“So great is the force…”).

CLXXXVIII. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter concerning the controversy of W., cleric of Coelestin., and G. of Cal. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 366; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 43, c. 3. — “It came to us that…”

CLXXXIX. He replies to the Bishop of Exeter (otherwise, the Archbishop of Canterbury) concerning those “who, being excommunicated, visit the Apostolic See and, concealing the causes for which they are bound by the bond of excommunication, carry away letters of their absolution.” Mansi XXII. 384; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 264; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 58; [Col. 1335C] *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 31, c. 5. — “On your behalf to us…”

CXC. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter (otherwise, Durham or Verona) concerning appeals. Mansi XXII. 316; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 290; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 127. — “But as to an appeal…”

CXCI. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter (otherwise, Lisieux) that “if anyone obtains from the Apostolic See confirmation of a matter in litigation, the judge may nevertheless take cognizance of the case and bring it to its proper conclusion.” Mansi XXII. 409; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 297; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 138; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 30, c. 1. — “If anyone [obtains confirmation] of a litigated matter…”

[Col. 1335D] CXCII. He replies to the Bishop of Exeter (otherwise, the Bishop of Sens) that “if schoolboys or clerics under the age of puberty strike one another, or one strikes another, they are not to be sent to the Apostolic See.” He adds concerning monks, regular canons, doorkeepers, and officials. Mansi XXII. 334, 335; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 213; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 341, 342; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 39, cc. 1, 2, 3, 4. — “But concerning that which”; “But monks”; “But if anyone”; “But if [the case] of anyone”; “An official on behalf of…”

CXCIII. He orders the Bishop of Exonexant (Exeter?) to permit A., his parishioner, to divorce his adulterous and sorcerous wife. Baluze, *Miscellanea*, III. 380; Mansi XXI. 1017. — “Your letter.”

CXCIV. He writes to the Bishops of Exeter and Worcester concerning a cleric who “claims a church by a knight’s gift.” Mansi XXII. 416. — “If it has been established to you.”

CXCV. He orders the Bishops of Exeter and Worcester to “admonish the prior and monks of Acre to confer and assign to Peter, a cleric, and to his brother a decent and suitable benefice.” [Col. 1336A] Mansi XXII. 375; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 206; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 63; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 35, c. 4. — “Since Simon formerly”; “Since already long ago.”

CXCVI. He orders the Bishops of Exeter and Worcester to compel witnesses named by Radulf, a cleric, to give testimony. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 106; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 284; Mansi XXI. 1085; XXII. 309. — “The witnesses whom…”

CXCVII.
