He writes to the Bishops of Exeter and Worcester concerning the sending of suitable and discreet persons to [examine] witnesses “who are sick, worn out by old age or weakness, or reduced to poverty.” Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 283; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 104; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 20, c. 8. — “If any of the witnesses…”

CXCVIII. He writes to the Bishops of Exeter and Worcester concerning the case of certain clerics. Mansi XXII. 309; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II. 282; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 103. — “Further, because”; “To that [matter] which…”

CXCIX. He orders the Bishops of Exeter and Worcester (otherwise, Rouen and Winchester) to compel the people of Hortun (otherwise Ortana) to pay tithes. [Col. 1336B] Mansi XXII. 282; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 249; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 184; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 30, c. 7. — “Since the people of…”

CC. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter and the Abbot of St Albans concerning the dispute between R. and W. Mansi XXII. 308; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 281; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 101; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 20, c. 18. — “R. made known to us”; “R. informed us.”

CCI. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter and the Dean of Chichester concerning the dispute between R., priest of Curket, and W., cleric of Chichester. Mansi XXII. 319. — “To our hearing.”

CCII. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter and the Abbot of Forden. concerning the case of the noblemen F. and R. of Ardenna. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 262; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, [Col. 1336C] tit. 29, c. 17; II, tit. 14, c. 3; IV, tit. 17, c. 4. — “The case which is between…”

CCIII. He writes to the Bishop of Exeter and the Abbot of Reforden. concerning the case of the canons of Holy Trinity of Barlen. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 370; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 13, c. 9. — “When he had come to us…”

CCIV. He orders the Bishop of Exeter and the Dean of Lincoln to restore in full the Prior of Gisebuir., excommunicated by R[oger], Archbishop of York and legate of the Apostolic See. Mansi XXII. 312; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 121; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 286; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 1, c. 6; tit. 28, c. 1. — “Our beloved sons.”

CCV. He replies to the Bishop of Fermo concerning the marriage of a certain nobleman. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 373; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 20, c. 24. — “In the letter.”

CCVI. He orders the Bishop of Florence that “whenever Lan., parish priest of St Pancras of Lucrum, has reasonably pronounced a sentence of interdict or excommunication against clerics or laymen of his parish, [Col. 1336D] he is to ensure that it is observed.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 57; Mansi XX. 387; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 263; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 31, c. 3. — “Since by the churches’…”

CCVII. He writes to the Abbot of Fountains and M., vicar (otherwise Master Vacarius), concerning W., brother of O. of Anjou, a parishioner of the church of York, whom “W. de Romare, having seized him, kept so long in iron fetters and prison until he compelled him to swear that he would take H. as his wife.” Mansi XXII. 290; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 317; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 246; *Decretals of Gregory*, IV, tit. 7, c. 2. — “O. informed us.”

CCVIII. He rejoices that Albert, Bishop of Freising, will come to him. Meichelbeck, *Historia Frisingensis*, I. I. 362; Pez, *Thesaurus anecdotorum*, VI. I. 393. — “An ancient friendship.”

CCIX. He replies to the Abbot of St Geneviève concerning punishment of an acolyte who was present while his brother was rebaptized. [Col. 1337A] Mansi XXII. 367; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 218; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 300; *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 9, c. 2. — “From your letters”; “From your letters.”

CCX. He adjudges the church of Levintri to the Prior and canons of Giseleburn; it was claimed by G., provost of the church of Beverley. Mansi XXII. 280; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 278; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 93; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 15, c. 1. — “Those established in [our] presence.”

CCXI. He writes to certain persons concerning the suit of the canons of Giseleburn and Thurin. Mansi XXII. 280; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 279; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 94. — “The case which is between…”

CCXII. He writes to the Patriarch of Grado, that he is to exercise mercy toward V., a priest, who “went to a place of depravity” (*pravitatum*; alternatively *privatum*, “private place”), intending to invoke an unclean spirit. Mansi XXII. 428; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 220; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 318; [Col. 1337B] *Decretals of Gregory*, V, tit. 21, c. 2. — “From your letters”; “From the tenor of your [letter].”

CCXIII. He replies to the Bishop of Hereford concerning “a married layman who, with the leave and permission of his wife, entered a monastery while she remained in secular dress.” Mansi XXII. 283; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 311; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 196; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 32, c. 1. — “Further, whether a layman”; “Further, you inquire.”

CCXIV. He replies to the Bishop of Hereford concerning A., who “betrothed a certain girl in her cradle, but afterwards took the girl’s mother as his wife.” Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 232; Mansi XXII. 324; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 328; *Decretals of Gregory*, IV, tit. 2, c. 4. — “The letter of your brotherhood”; “Your brotherhood’s letter”; “Your letter.”

CCXV. He writes to the Bishop of Hereford that “clerics in minor orders who, being married, hold ecclesiastical benefices by grant of his predecessors, ought to be tolerated by way of non-enforcement, since the nation, the barbarous people, and the multitude are factors in the case.” Mansi XXII. 349; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 145; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 335; [Col. 1337C] *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 3, c. 2. — “But concerning the clerics…”

CCXVI. He writes to the Bishop of Hereford that, “at church dedications, clerics are not to be promoted to sacred orders outside the fasts of the Four Seasons.” He adds that “it is lawful on Sundays and other feast days to promote one or two persons to minor orders.” Mansi XXII. 372; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 240; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 29; *Decretals of Gregory*, I, tit. 11, cc. 2 and 3. — “But concerning that”; “But concerning this which”; “But concerning that which.”

CCXVII. He writes to the Bishop of Hereford that “rigour and strictness of law are not to be required in ecclesiastical persons and affairs.” Mansi XXII. 279; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 277; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 91; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 14, c. 1. — “Further, when it happens…”

[Col. 1337D] CCXVIII. He replies to the Bishop of Hereford that, “if letters addressed to him contain an express form, and he learns that they were obtained in that form through suggestion or suppression of the truth, he should proceed not according to the form expressed in them, but according to the strict requirement of justice.” Mansi XXII. 301; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II. 268; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 51. — “We have learned from…”

CCXIX. He commends Wal. to the Bishop of Hereford, that the latter may grant him a church. Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 260; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 24; (Mansi XXI. 1083). — “It is fitting and…”

CCXX. He replies to the Bishop of Hereford (otherwise, Ely) concerning priests who, before profession, “have returned to their former state.” Mansi XXII. 358; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 234; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 195; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 31, c. 9. — “Concerning that which was asked…”

CCXXI. He replies to the Bishop of Hereford (otherwise, Worcester) that those “who have assumed the religious habit, if they later take wives, must be compelled to put them away and return to the church.” [Col. 1338A] Mansi XXII. 288, 358; Boehmer, *Corpus juris canonici*, II, app. 235; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 244; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 28, c. 9; IV, tit. 6, c. 3. — “We remember from…”; “We remember on behalf of…”

CCXXII. He orders the Bishop of Hereford and the Abbot of Evesham to command that the church of Blessed Mary before the gates of Gloucester be restored to G., a cleric. Mansi XXII. 416; (Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 386). — “To our ears.”

CCXXIII. He orders the Bishop of Hereford and the Abbot of Forde to adjudge a certain church to William of Leicester. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 206; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 299; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 38, c. 7; (Mansi XXII. 337). — “From the letters.”

CCXXIV. He orders the Bishop of Hereford and the Abbot of Forde to judge between Adam, a cleric, and [Col. 1338B] H., a knight. Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 103; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 282; Mansi XXII. 310; *Decretals of Gregory*, II, tit. 20, c. 7. — “On Adam’s behalf.”

CCXXV. He writes to the Bishop of Hereford and the Abbot of Forde (otherwise, the Bishop of Exeter) concerning rights of presentation to churches. Mansi XXII. 336; Boehmer, *Corpus*, II, app. 299; Augustinus Tarraconensis, *Opera*, IV. 206; *Decretals of Gregory*, III, tit. 38, c. 6. — “Because certain clerics…”

CCXXVI. He forbids the Archdeacon of Hereford to exact money from clerics “for performing ecclesiastical ministry, for appointing vicars, or for chrism.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 410; Mansi XXI, 1099; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 3, ch. 21. — “You are to know concerning our…”

CCXXVII. He writes to the bishop of Hermonien. (?) concerning Aide’s ten-year-old son, who, while shooting with other boys, “struck a certain nephew of the same Aide with an arrow, and he died.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 320; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 23, ch. 2. — “Aide having brought to us…” [Col. 1338C]; “Having reported to us II.”

CCXXVIII. He writes to the bishops of Hippo and Salerno (alternatively, to the bishop of Spalato) concerning clerics who have contracted marriages. Mansi XXII, 349; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 338; *Augustini Tarr. Op.* IV, 244. — “Concerning what you assert”; “But concerning that which…”

CCXXIX. He forbids the Hospitallers and Templars, “when they have acquired the right of patronage in parish churches, to institute priests in them except through the bishop.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 209; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 301; (Mansi XXII, 339; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 38, ch. 13). — “Since the world…”

CCXXX. He exhorts archbishops and bishops to observe the privileges of the Hospitallers. Mansi XXII, 408; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 229; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 330; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 33, ch. 4. — “Our beloved sons.”

CCXXXI. He exhorts the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem not to transfer their privileges in the diocese of Hereford. Mansi XXII, 408; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 230; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 331. — “There has come to us from…” [Col. 1338D]

CCXXXII. He orders the Archbishop of Genoa to ensure that those “who buy pepper, cinnamon, or other goods worth no more than five pounds do not promise by public instrument that they will pay six pounds at a fixed time to those from whom they received these goods.” Mansi XXII, 343; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 217; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 315; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 19, ch. 6. — “In your city…”

CCXXXIII. He writes to the Bishop of Genoa that he should not “grant a place in more than one church to one person, nor introduce into his diocese the custom of the Gallican Church, which admits one person to several benefices.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 384; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 5, ch. 15. — “Since you are not unaware…”

CCXXXIV. He replies to the Bishop of Genoa concerning B., a canon of St Mary of the Vineyards, who “laid violent hands upon a certain subdeacon.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 345; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 39, ch. 10. — “From the tenor of the letters…” [Col. 1339A]

CCXXXV. He replies to the Bishop of Genoa concerning appeals. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 379; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 28, ch. 30. — “To these matters, just as…”

CCXXXVI. He replies to the Bishop of Genoa concerning “those who betroth women and, before marrying or knowing them carnally, take other women as wives,” etc. Mansi XXII, 443, 444; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, 326; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 240, 227, 236; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 23, ch. 11; bk. IV, tit. 2, ch. 9, tit. 4, ch. 4. — “Your brotherhood…”; “Likewise, moreover…”; “But concerning those who…”

CCXXXVII. He replies to the Bishop of Genoa concerning “parishioners to be compelled to purgation.” Mansi XXII, 320; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 57, 77, 335; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 264, 292; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 34, ch. 6. — “Since among others…”; “We among others…” [Col. 1339B]; “Therefore among others…”; “On your side, to us…”; “Whether indeed…”; (“We, in the exalted…”).

CCXXXVIII. He writes to the Bishop of Genoa that a layman sued by a cleric “concerning his own property or that of the church ought to be brought before a secular court on this matter.” Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 277; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 83; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 2, ch. 5. — “If a priest or…”; “But if a priest…”

CCXXXIX. He replies to the Bishop of Genoa (alternatively, Bologna) concerning the extortion of testimony. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 106; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 284; Mansi XXII, 306; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 21, ch. 3. — “But concerning that which…”; “Concerning that which is to be made certain…”

CCXL. He orders a certain person to compel the prior of the Island to restore to the canons of York their parishioner, whom he had buried in his own church. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 389; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 28, ch. 5. — “On behalf of the canons…”

CCXLI. He writes to G., prior, and the brethren of St John, living according to the discipline of the late Elect, that “no married man is to be received among them without his own wife’s permission.” Mansi XXII, 285; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 313; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 199; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 32, ch. 8. — “A married man…” [Col. 1339C]

CCXLII. He establishes a rule for G., prior, and the brethren living according to the discipline of the late [lacuna] cleric (alternatively, of the Crusaders). Mansi XXII, 374; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 232; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 193. — “At your request…”

CCXLIII. He grants the Jews “the shield of his protection.” He decrees:

1. “That no Christian shall compel them, unwilling and refusing, to come to baptism”;
2. “That no Christian shall presume, without judgment of the secular authority, either to wound or kill any of them, or to take away their money, or to alter the good customs which they have hitherto had in the region in which they previously lived; and especially that no one shall in any way disturb them with clubs or stones during the celebration of their festivals” [Col. 1339D], etc.;
3. “That no one shall dare to mutilate or invade a Jewish cemetery.”

(This decree is also ascribed to Clement III.) Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 305; Mansi XXII, 355; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 412. — “Just as for the Jews…”

CCXLIV. He exhorts certain persons:

1. That, “if a case should arise between them and any Christians whatsoever, they should not presume, at the latter’s summons, to have recourse to a secular court or judge alone; and that in any case against Christians, especially clerics, they should admit only the testimony of two or three men of approved life and faithful conduct”;
2. That they “forbid all Christians to place themselves continually in the service of Jews for any wage; and that they take care to prohibit their midwives and women from presuming to nurse Jewish infants in their houses”;
3. That they “prohibit their parishioners by every means from taking usury.”

Baluzius, *Misc.* III, 379; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 367, 412, 316; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 306; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 20, ch. 23; bk. V, tit. 6, ch. 8, tit. 19, ch. 7; Mansi XXI, 1105; XXII, 356. — “Although to all…” [Col. 1340A]; “For this purpose, by these presents…”; “Moreover, to parishioners…”

CCXLV. He writes to a certain bishop that he should decree “that Jews are not to keep doors or windows open on the day of Preparation, but are to close them throughout the whole day; nor is he to permit any Christian servants to live with them.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 290; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 6, ch. 4. — “Because concerning these matters…”

CCXLVI. He orders a certain bishop more strictly to compel Jews who hold parishes of churches under a title of purchase, lease, or even pledge to relinquish them, after first seeking and obtaining the consent of Henry, illustrious king of the English; and he forbids all the faithful, under threat of anathema, to dare to do homage or swear fealty to Jews, or for any Christian to become the servant of a Jew. Mansi XXII, 357; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 306, 307. — “Not without much…”; “Moreover, together with the sacred…” [Col. 1340B]

CCXLVII. He orders the monks of St Mary of Laurentius to pay tithes to the church of Collingham. Gilbert Foliot, *Letters*, ed. Giles II, 108; (Mansi XXII, 331; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 254; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 190). — “We have heard that the tithes…”; “As the rights belonging to you…”

CCXLVIII. He orders the abbot and brethren of St Laurence to restore a certain piece of land to G., a cleric. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 316; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 19, ch. 8. — “A complaint has been made to us…”

CCXLIX. He writes to a certain person concerning I., prior of St Laurence, accused both of simony and adultery. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 375; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 21, ch. 4. — “It has come to our hearing…”

CCL. He replies to the Bishop of Lisieux (alternatively, Brescia) concerning delegated judges and “violent ejectment.” Mansi XXII, 302, 361; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 269, 277 [Col. 1340C]; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 51, 89; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 29, ch. 9; bk. II, tit. 13, chs. 5 and 6. — “In the letters which…”; “in your letters…”; “Concerning that question…”; “Likewise, when someone…”; “Likewise, when anyone…”; “When anyone says…”

CCLI. He writes to the Bishop of Lisieux (alternatively, Exeter) concerning those who are to be admitted to the personate of a parish church. Mansi XXII, 366; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 242; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 32; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 14, ch. 5. — “Moreover, although to…”

CCLII. He writes to the Bishop of Lincoln concerning “rectors of churches infected with the stain of leprosy.” Mansi XXII, 395; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 154. — “But concerning that which…”; “Concerning rectors…”

CCLIII. He orders G., Archdeacon of Lincoln, to remove R., a priest “begotten by a priest, whose father had ministered in the same church of Bileberi.” Gilbert Foliot, *Letters*, ed. Giles II, 85; (Mansi XXII, 353; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 245 [Col. 1340D]; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 33; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 17, ch. 2). — “To our presence…”

CCLIV. He writes to the dean and canons of Lincoln (alternatively, Limoges) that he had granted the subdeacon Herbert permission to take a wife. Mansi XXII, 352; XXI, 1092; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 337; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 244. — “When he had pressed…”; “When he had stood by…”

CCLV. He orders the Dean of Lincoln and the Abbot of Rievaulx that, if “P., a cleric, renounced the church not through fear or compulsion, but voluntarily, they are to impose perpetual silence upon him regarding this matter.” Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 275; Mansi XXII, 359, 404; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 87; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 13, ch. 3. — “Having received the complaint…”

CCLVI. He writes to a certain bishop concerning the right of patronage of certain churches situated in the dioceses of Lincoln and Salisbury. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 209; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 302; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 38, ch. 14 [Col. 1341A]; (Mansi XXII, 340). — “From the representation…”

CCLVII. He writes to the Bishop of Langres concerning the dispute of R., a priest, and G. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 384; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 4, ch. 6. — “R. having complained to us…”

CCLVIII. He writes to G., Bishop of Livonia (alternatively F., Bishop of Le Noyon, Linconen.: perhaps Lincoln?), concerning P., who “had secretly received the order of deacon.” Mansi XXII, 368; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 223; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 324; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 30, ch. 1. — “P. having come to us…”; “The bearer of the present letters having come…”; “The bearer of these present letters to us…”

CCLIX. He grants the Bishop of London that, “if through infirmity or some grave necessity he cannot attend to the hearing of cases committed to him by the apostolic see, he may entrust his functions to prudent and suitable persons.” Mansi XXII, 299; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 265; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 49 [Col. 1341B]; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 29, ch. 3. — “If because of infirmity…”

CCLX. He replies to the Bishop of London concerning an appeal to the Apostolic See. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 48; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 265; (Mansi XXII, 298). — “Since it belongs to you concerning…”

CCLXI. He grants the Bishop of London authority to rescind institutions made by archdeacons without his consultation. Mansi XXII, 364; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 228; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 155. — “There has come to our ears…”

CCLXII. He writes to the Bishop of London concerning clerics “who keep concubines.” Mansi XXII, 350; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 336; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 143; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 2, ch. 6. — “But if clerics…”

CCLXIII. He orders the Bishop of London that, if Stephen “has acted contrary to a settlement confirmed by the giving of faith,” he should not delay depriving him of the church. Mansi XXII, 348; XXI, 1085; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 239 [Col. 1341C]; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 113. — “If Stephen…”

CCLXIV. He writes to the Bishop of London that he should not confer several ecclesiastical benefices upon one person. Mansi XXII, 382; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, 243; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 150; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 5, ch. 6. — “Since we are bound by…”

CCLXV. He orders the Bishop of London to restore the church of Newburgh to W., a priest. Mansi XXII, 353; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 246; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 34; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 17, ch. 5. — “Coming into our presence…”

CCLXVI. He grants the Bishop of London that, “if the appointment to any church belongs to his institution and is delayed because of laymen’s disputes over the right of patronage, he may appoint a suitable person in that church.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 209; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 301; (Mansi XXII, 339; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 38, ch. 12). — “But if at any time…” [Col. 1341D]; “But if the appointment…”

CCLXVII. He orders the Bishop of London to correct the discipline of the monks of Nestun. Mansi XXII, 375; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 222; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 50, ch. 7. — “It has been reported to our ears…”

CCLXVIII. He orders the Bishop of London to compel the monks of Wardone (alternatively, Warsinia) to restore a certain piece of land to T. Eschaler and his mother. Mansi XXII, 346; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 217; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 315. — “From the transmitted complaint…”

CCLXIX. He orders the Bishops of London and Worcester to induce the Hospitallers of A. to pay certain tithes to the church of Master N. (alternatively, Henry). *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 190; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 255. — “Master … having brought the matter to us”; “Master … having reported it.”

CCLXX. He orders the Bishops of London and Worcester to judge between R., canon of Lincoln, and W. Salvage. Mansi XXII, 347; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 239; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 113; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 24, ch. 10. — “The complaint of R…” [Col. 1342A]

CCLXXI. He orders the Bishops of London and Worcester to hear the case of R. and F., “leaving judgment concerning the possessions to H(enry), King of the English.” Mansi XXII, 389; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 264; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 17, ch. 7. — “The case which is between…”

CCLXXII. He grants the prior and brethren of Holy Trinity, London (alternatively Lundon., alternatively Lorido), “that they may give testimony in cases involving their church.” Mansi XXII, 309; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 103; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 282; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 20, ch. 16. — “Furthermore, also by authority…”

CCLXXIII. He advises the abbot and brethren of Lorengio (alternatively Dolon.) to reach a peaceful agreement with the abbot and brethren of Ursitum (alternatively Nisyon) “concerning the tithes over which there is a dispute between them.” Mansi XXII, 328; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 251; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 185; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 30, ch. 9. — “It has been represented to us…” [Col. 1342B]

CCLXXIV. He replies to the Bishop of Lucca that the relatives of one whom he has bound by the bond of excommunication for manifest crimes—namely homicide, arson, violently laying hands upon clerics, violation of churches, and incest—are to be admonished to make satisfaction; if they do so, he may be buried in a cemetery. Mansi XXII, 391, 447; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 215; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 313; Aguirre, *Conc.* V, 96. — “But concerning the second…”

CCLXXV. He replies to the Bishop of Lucca concerning a widow who, “after taking the veil, subsequently, when a year had elapsed, married a certain nobleman,” etc. Mansi XXII, 410; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 325; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 245, 307; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 6, ch. 4; bk. V, tit. 12, ch. 11. — “Indeed, [he] consulted…”; “Your [letter] consulted us…” [Col. 1342C]; “The affection [for us] consulted…”; “Henceforth you are to know…”

CCLXXVI. He writes to the Bishop of Lucca concerning the penance of a cleric who “asserts that he was in a certain conflict.” Mansi XXII, 369; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 223; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 321; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 25, ch. 3. — “The bearer of these letters, in…”

CCLXXVII. He informs the Archbishop of Lyons (alternatively Lund) that he has ordered the Archbishop of Sens, legate of the Apostolic See, and the Bishop of Paris to compel a certain person to restore money taken from him. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 163; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 305; (Mansi XXII, 441; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 16, ch. 1). — “That grave and…”

CCLXXVIII. He dissuades the Archbishop of Lund from his plan of resigning the episcopate. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 28; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, 259; (*Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 9, ch. 1). — “Your letter recently…”

CCLXXIX. He informs Anno and the brethren of the monastery of Marmuloso that he has granted the castle of Tiberias to John, Peter, and Leo, sons of the late Cencius Frangipani. Borgia, *Istoria di Velletri*, p. 241. — “Since, from the duty entrusted…”

CCLXXX. He informs the abbot and brethren of the monastery of St Michael of Marturi what he has ordered the archpriest of Volterra and the abbot of Spongia to do concerning their dispute with the parish priest and clerics of St Mary. He adds that Julius, Bishop of Florence, “had notified him that certain chapters had been inserted into the privilege recently granted to them which appeared contrary to reason”; he therefore orders the bull to be returned. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 102; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 282; Mansi XXII, 308; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 20, ch. 19. — “The case which is being conducted…”

CCLXXXI. He replies to the Bishop of Marseille that he should compel Jews “either to pay tithes from the lands which they cultivate, or to renounce their possession entirely.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 192; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 30, ch. 16. — “But concerning lands…” [Col. 1343A]

CCLXXXII. He replies to the Bishop of Marseille concerning “men of the parish of one church who cultivate lands in another parish.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 391; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 30, ch. 18. — “Since they are men…”

CCLXXXIII. He orders the dean and chapter of Maurienne that, “if it should happen that their bishop departs this life before payment of the debts which he contracted for the church’s benefit, they are to pay those debts from the revenues belonging to his table.” Mansi XXII, 381; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 23, ch. 1. — “For this purpose, in…”

CCLXXXIV. He replies to the Bishop of Mauritania (perhaps Maurienne) that “the position of the possessor is better than a prescription of forty years.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 118; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 285; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 26, ch. 6. — “There has come to our ears concerning you…” [Col. 1343B]

CCLXXXV. He orders the Archbishop of Milan not to permit certain tithes to be taken from the Bishop of Vercelli. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 183. — “The complaint of the venerable…”

CCLXXXVI. He undertakes the protection of the Church of Meaux and confirms the possessions of its canons (fragment). Du Plessis, *Hist. de Meaux* II, 66. — “Since it belongs to us…”

CCLXXXVII. He informs the Bishop of Meaux that the prioress and convent of Celonantia had asked whether “a certain young man, their convert, deprived of his genitals, could be ordained priest.” He orders him to ascertain whether “he was cut by enemies,” or by physicians, or whether “he laid hands upon himself”; “for,” he says, “the canons admit the first cases, but decree that the third be punished as a homicide.” Baluzius, *Misc.* III, 374; Mansi XXI, 1102. — “Beloved [daughters], in…” [Col. 1343C]

CCLXXXVIII. He orders the prior and provost of Mortara to judge between certain spouses. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 249; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 9, ch. 2. — “A woman proposed to us…”

CCLXXXIX. He replies to the canons of Modena that “a child born of a second marriage cannot by law be joined, in the fourth degree, to the kinship of the former husband.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 255; Mansi XXI, 1092. — “Our beloved son…”

CCXC. He exhorts the abbot and brethren of Neubothe to pay tithes from certain estates to the brethren of Holy Cross. Gilbert Foliot, *Letters*, ed. Giles II, 109; Mansi, *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 30, ch. 8. — “Our beloved sons…”

CCXCI. He writes to the Abbot of Neuss concerning the absolution of certain persons from excommunication. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 344; Mansi XXI, 1094. — “If perhaps after…”

CCXCII. He forbids the Abbot of Nexibus (alternatively, the Archbishop of York) to absolve those who “have assumed the habit of religion in his monastery and subsequently confess that they committed such an offence as incurred a sentence of excommunication by the act itself.” Mansi XXII, 333; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 211; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 343. — “Your [letter] consulted us…” [Col. 1343D]

CCXCIII. He informs “the bishop of Nomenensis, mer…” that his companion has been released by him from a vow to make the journey to Jerusalem. Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, 258. — “We have heard well…”

CCXCIV. He writes to the Bishop of Norwich that he is not to permit “clerics established in the priesthood or in other lower orders to substitute others in the vicariates of churches.” Mansi XXII, 318; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 244; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 48; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 28, ch. 4. — “But clerics, or…”; “Clerics in the priesthood…”

CCXCV. He writes to the Bishop of Norwich against collusion by clerics concerning benefices. Mansi XXII, 378; Boehmer, *Corp. can.* II, app. 209 [Col. 1344A]; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 319; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 22, ch. 3. — “We have heard, in the diocese…”

CCXCVI. He replies to the Bishop of Norwich that clerics who have sworn that they will “pay a greater pension in the name of a benefice, beyond the customary pension” are to be removed. Mansi XXII, 347; (*Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 375; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 24, ch. 11). — “Your brotherhood has informed us…”; “Because your [letter] has informed us…”

CCXCVII. He writes this to the Bishop of Norwich: “If a priest knows that someone is guilty of some crime, or if he has confessed it and refuses to amend, he ought not to rebuke him by name unless someone can prove it by due judicial procedure,” etc. Mansi XXII, 447; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 264; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 58; (*Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 31, ch. 2). — “If a priest knows…”

CCXCVIII. He replies to the Bishop of Norwich concerning clerics presented by an advocate. Mansi XXII, 338; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 213 [Col. 1344B]. — “When an advocate…”; “But when an advocate…”

CCXCIX. He writes to the Bishop of Norwich concerning presentations of persons. Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 303; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 211; (Mansi XXII, 341). — “But if bishops…”

CCC. He replies to the Bishop of Norwich concerning delegated cases. Mansi XXII, 300; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, 268; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 50; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 29, chs. 7–8; bk. III, tit. 38, ch. 18. — “You have informed us through…”; “But whenever…”; “Whenever clerics…”; “But if any…”

CCCI. He replies to the Bishop of Norwich concerning a girl “given as wife to a certain man below marriageable age.” Mansi XXII, 288; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 316; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 234; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 2, ch. 6. — “It was contained in the letters…”; “But it was contained…”

CCCII. He writes to the Bishop of Norwich concerning the dispute of Hubert and Master N. Mansi XXII, 414; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 156 [Col. 1344C]; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 10, ch. 2. — “It was contained in the letters…”

CCCIII. He orders the Bishop of Norwich to direct Hugh, a priest, to relinquish the vicarage of the church of Buruvelle. Mansi XXII, 383; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 244; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 47; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 28, ch. 1. — “It has come to our hearing…”

CCCIV. He writes to the Bishop of Norwich and the Abbot of Evesham concerning the dispute between H., a cleric, and R. Mansi XXII, 293; (*Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 120; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 27, ch. 6). — “We have written to you…”; “With certain persons…”

CCCV. He writes to the Bishop of Norwich and to T. and Wi., archdeacons, concerning the marriage of W. and A., a widow. Mansi XXII, 289; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 317; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 128; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 27, ch. 7. — “The bearer of these letters, W…”

CCCVI. He writes to I., legate of the Apostolic See, “concerning the tributary churches of the bishopric of Novacen. (alternatively Novara).” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 417; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 33, ch. 8. — “We have received letters…”; “We have received letters…” [Col. 1344D]

CCCVII. He writes to the Bishop of Huesca and the prior of St Mary of Zaragoza concerning M., the wife of the nobleman Ateorelia, who became a nun. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 68; Mansi XXII, 431; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 40, ch. 1. — “It has been reported to…”; “It has been reported to our ears…”; “It has been conveyed to…”

CCCVIII. He replies to the Archbishop of Palermo that no dispensation can be granted for receiving money at usury so that poor persons held captive by Saracens may be freed by that money. Mansi XXII, 343; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 215; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 314; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 19, ch. 4. — “But concerning that which…”; “Concerning that which, from…”

CCCIX. He replies to the Archbishop of Palermo concerning those “who, after swearing an oath, promise that they will marry certain women and afterwards, without having known them, leave the country.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 223; Mansi XXII, 289; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 317; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 1, ch. 5, tit. 5, ch. 3. — “But concerning those…” [Col. 1345A]

CCCX. He replies to the Archbishop of Palermo concerning punishment of Saracens who abduct boys and presume to abuse them. He adds concerning one who “had intercourse with his brother’s wife.” Mansi XXII, 445, 446; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 331; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 311, 405; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 12, ch. 3; bk. V, tit. 17, ch. 4. — “In the archbishopric…”; “But concerning that man who…”

CCCXI. He writes to the Archbishop of Palermo that he must not allow churches to be “resigned by clerics into the hands of advocates without his authority and knowledge.” Mansi XXII, 342. — “It has been represented to our ears…”

CCCXII. He replies to the Archbishop of Palermo (alternatively, the Bishop of Vigilio) that “secular clerics can make no testament concerning movable or immovable property which they have received in consideration of the church.” Mansi XXII, 380; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 236; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 174; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 26, ch. 9. — “Because your [letter] has led us…” [Col. 1345B]

CCCXIII. He forbids the consuls of Pavia to “intervene in tithes or ecclesiastical business.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 77; Mansi XXII, 1084. — “It has been reported to our ears…”

CCCXIV. He writes to the Bishop of Paris that “husbands are permitted to accuse their wives even on suspicion alone.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 309. — “To husbands also…”

CCCXV. He orders the Bishop of Paris, the Abbot of St Remigius, and the Dean of Meaux to direct that the church of Alde be restored to R. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 370. — “A complaint has been made to us…”

CCCXVI. He orders the Bishop of Paris, the Abbot of St Remigius, and the Dean of Meaux to judge between the brethren of Arcemar and their abbot. Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 275; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 87 [Col. 1345C]; Mansi XXII, 359. — “The brethren of Arcemar…”

CCCXVII. He forbids Simon, Archdeacon of Paris, to exact money from the brethren of the church of St Victor “for the enthronement of an abbot.” Duchesne, *H. Fr. Scr.* IV, 569; Martène, *Coll.* VI, 248; Bouquet, *Rec.* XV, 913; Mansi XXI, 973. — “Since you are a man…”

CCCXVIII. He replies to the Bishop of Parma concerning a certain marriage. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 266; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 18, ch. 1. — “It has been reported to us…”

CCCXIX. He replies to the Bishop of Padua concerning the marriage of a certain excommunicated person. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 79; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 1, ch. 7. — “We have understood from…”

CCCXX. He replies to the Bishop of Padua concerning a woman who “allowed herself to be betrothed by her husband’s own brother.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 259; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 325 [Col. 1345D]; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 16, ch. 1. — “The letters which…”

CCCXXI. He replies to the Bishop of Poitiers concerning P.’s marriage. Mansi XXII, 325; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 329; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 253; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 13, ch. 2. — “P. having come to us…”

CCCXXII. He orders the Bishop of Poitiers to compel G. to marry a certain girl in accordance with the oath which he had given. Mansi XXII, 294; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 321; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 225; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 1, ch. 10. — “From the letters of the venerable…”

CCCXXIII. He replies to the Archbishop of Pisa concerning one who entered a monastery against his wife’s will. Mansi XXII, 283; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 310; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 197; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 32, ch. 3. — “A certain man entered…”

CCCXXIV. He dissuades Richard Gentile, a nobleman, from harassing the monastery of Pescara. *Chron. Casaur.*, in Muratori, *B. Ital. sacr.* II.II, 905. — “Concerning prudence…” [Col. 1346A]

CCCXXV. He replies to the Bishop of Piacenza concerning “the sons of usurers who succeed them when they die in the sin of usury.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 316; *Decr. Greg.* bk. V, tit. 19, ch. 9. — “Your [letter] has led us…”

CCCXXVI. He replies to the Bishop of Piacenza concerning “new witnesses in a matter already adjudicated.” Mansi XXII, 307; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 281; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 101; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 20, ch. 17. — “But in order that these…”; “Your brotherhood [has informed] us…”

CCCXXVII. He orders the priests Pontius and Asilius to come to him on the Wednesday of the following week, in order to give testimony in the case of the Bishop of Palestrina and the Abbot of Subiaco. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 105; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 283; Mansi XXII, 305; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 21, ch. 2. — “Since concerning the case…”

CCCXXVIII. He orders the brethren of the church of Rames that they “must in no way presume to appropriate tithes from lands in the tithe-district of the treasurer of Sens (alternatively Sées) which they do not cultivate with their own hands.” Mansi XXII, 328; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 251; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 186; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 30, ch. 11. — “Although, out of kindness…” [Col. 1346B]

CCCXXIX. He orders the Abbot of Ramsey and the Archdeacon of Ely to judge between the monks of Crowland and the canons of Lincoln. Mansi XXII, 402; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 277; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 91; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 14, ch. 2. — “From your letters…”

CCCXXX. He orders the Archbishop of Ravenna to settle the dissension among the nuns of St Margaret. Mansi XXII, 400; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 260; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 23; (*Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 6, ch. 8). — “The case which is between…”

CCCXXXI. He replies to the Archbishop of Ravenna concerning recusations and the case of H. and Baldwin’s nephew. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 127; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 290; Mansi XXII, 316. — “Your brotherhood consulted us…”; “Yours consulted us…” [Col. 1346C]

CCCXXXII. He replies to the Archbishop of Ravenna (alternatively, Reims) concerning the appeal of the Abbot of St Apollinaris. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 130, 122; (Mansi XXII, 312; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 292, 286; *Decr. Greg.* bk. II, tit. 28, ch. 2). — “Among other matters, that…”; (“Concerning that which the abbot…”).

CCCXXXIII. He exhorts G., Archbishop of Ravenna, “not henceforth to be troubled or disturbed if he writes to him anything harsh or severe.” Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 288; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 14; *Decr. Greg.* bk. I, tit. 3, ch. 5. — “Whenever your…”; “Whenever any…”

CCCXXXIV. He replies to the Archbishop of Reims (alternatively, the Bishop of Andria) concerning one “who has never rendered, or been able to render, the marital debt to his wife.” Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 321; Mansi XXII, 293; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 257. — “But concerning that which…” [Col. 1346D]

CCCXXXV. He replies to the Archbishop of Reims (alternatively, the Bishop of Andria) concerning a deacon “who, on Holy Saturday, wounded another deacon and took a woman as his wife,” etc. Mansi XXII, 351, 371; Boehmer, *Corp. jur. can.* II, app. 226, 337; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 243, 191; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 30, ch. 14; bk. IV, tit. 6, ch. 1. — “Concerning the deacon…”; “But [concerning] the parishioners…”

CCCXXXVI. He orders the Archbishop of Reims to compel the Count of Clermont to fulfil the vow which he had undertaken to go to Jerusalem. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 395; Mansi XXI, 1098. — “It has come to our hearing…”

CCCXXXVII. He orders the Archbishop of Reims to compel the Count of Dampierre to restore the tithes he had taken from I., a priest. Mansi XXII, 377. — “The complaint of I., a priest…”

CCCXXXVIII. He informs the Archbishop of Reims how he has decided the controversy between the churches of Macularensis (alternatively Martinensis or Marciensis) and Formolensis (alternatively Formosolensis). *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 118; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, 285; Mansi XXII, 396. — “The controversy which is between…” [Col. 1347A]

CCCXXXIX. He orders F., dean, and Master M., of Reims, to compel the monks of St Vincent of Lyons “to restore to the brethren of St Martin all the property of a certain woman and of the son of Randulf Canis, together with the benefices which they received on the occasion of their burial.” *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 389; *Decr. Greg.* bk. III, tit. 28, ch. 6. — “Since it is free…”

CCCXL. He orders Fulk, dean, and Master R., canon of Reims, to judge between P., a citizen of Reims, and A., a priest released from excommunication. Baluzius, *Misc.* III, 382; Mansi XXI, 1095, 1108; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 375. — “Since the case which…”

CCCXLI. He orders the Abbot of Remestre and the Archdeacon of Exeter to judge between V. and R., clerics disputing over a certain church. Mansi XXII, 415; (*Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 385). — “Coming to the Apostolic…” [Col. 1347B]

CCCXLII. He writes to the Abbot of Rivesham and the Dean and Archdeacon of Lincoln concerning the dispute between the canons of Guisborough and R., a cleric. *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 211; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 303; (Mansi XXII, 342). — “Our beloved sons…”

CCCXLIII. He replies to the Archbishop of Rouen concerning a young man maintained by Nicholas Sagantinus. Mansi XXII, 307; Boehmer, *Corp.* II, app. 333; *Augustini Tarr. Opp.* IV, 262; *Decr. Greg.* bk. IV, tit. 17, ch. 3. — “Sent to us…”

CCCXLIV. He writes to the Archbishop of Rouen and the abbot of Geomar (otherwise, the bishop of Dol) concerning vexatious appeals. Mansi XXII. 421, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 209, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 70 [Col. 1347C] and 126, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 42, chapter 1.—“From the definite [information] of certain persons.”

CCCXLV. He replies to the Archbishop of Salerno, who asks “whether, if a lawful present consent has intervened between a man and a woman, though carnal intercourse has not followed, the woman may marry another.” Mansi XXI. 288, 283, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 315, 310, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 238, 197, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 4, chapter 3; Book III, title 32, chapter 2.—“Although contrary to the usual practice”; “But after consent.”

CCCXLVI. He writes to the Archbishop of Salerno that, if any clerics resolve voluntarily and without payment to serve the brethren of the Hospital for one year or three, with their prelate’s permission, they are not to be hindered in any way. Mansi XXII. 384.—“We command that, if.”

CCCXLVII. He writes to the Archbishop of Salerno (otherwise, of Salona) that, concerning a fourth share of tithes and offerings for the dead, a cleric can protect himself against a bishop’s claim by the prescription of forty years’ time. [Col. 1347D] Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 117, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 284, Mansi XXII. 395, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 26, chapter 4.—“But concerning the fourth share.”

CCCXLVIII. He writes to the Archbishop of Salerno (otherwise, the archpriest of Salona) concerning the punishment of usurers. Mansi XXII. 344, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 216, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 314, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 19, chapter 5.—“Since you, as.”

CCCXLIX. He writes to the Archbishop of Salerno (otherwise, of Salona) that “laymen are not to be admitted to make accusations or give testimony against a cleric in criminal cases,” etc. Mansi XXII. 306, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 280, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 100, 274, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 20, chapters 14 and 15.—“Henceforth, laymen”; “in ecclesiastical cases.”

CCCL. He replies to the Archbishop of Salerno concerning “clerics convicted of a crime before a secular judge”; concerning a duel voluntarily offered by a cleric; concerning a priest of Campania who “lost part of a finger in a duel”; [Col. 1348A] and concerning a priest who killed a boy. Mansi XXII. 367, 368, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 221, 222, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 40, 78, 308, 305, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 20, chapter 1; Book II, title 1, chapter 4; Book V, title 12, chapter 7, title 14, chapter 1.—“But if clerics”; “And if clerics”; “Further, if a cleric”; “Concerning the priest”; “But the priest.”

CCCLI. He writes to the Archbishop of Salerno concerning clerics “who publicly keep concubines in their houses.” Mansi XXII. 348, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 334, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 142, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 2, chapter 3.—“But clerics in.”

CCCLII. He writes to the Archbishop of Salerno concerning spiritual kinship. Mansi XXII. 387, 388, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 332, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 250, 251, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 11, chapters 1 and 2.—“But whether”; “If a man or woman.”

CCCLIII. He commands the Archbishop of Salzburg to compel H. and C. and their children to restore to the monastery of St. Quirinus (at Tegernsee) an estate situated in the place called Salinae. Pez, *Thesaurus anecdotorum* VI. I. 396.—“From the complaint.”

CCCLIV. He commands the bishops of Saintes and Chalon to compel R., formerly abbot of Trier (otherwise, Tremes), and certain monks, to fulfil the oath which they have sworn. Mansi XXII. 347, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 239, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 112, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 24, chapter 9.—“From the rescript”; “From the writing.”

CCCLV. He commands the canons, brethren, and monks possessing churches in the diocese of Salisbury not, “when incumbents die, to seize the churches on their own authority, or to install clerics in them.” Mansi XXII. 414.—“From the communication sent to us.”

CCCLVI. He writes to the bishops of Salisbury and Exeter concerning the removal of I., a priest’s son. Mansi XXII. 354.—“It has been represented to us.”

CCCLVII. [Col. 1348C] He writes to the dean and chapter of Salisbury concerning the prebend of Britford bestowed by Bishop Jocelin upon Hugh Buvet. Theiner, *Disquisitiones criticae* 430 (Mansi XXII. 366).—“Since Hugh.”

CCCLVIII. He commands the Archbishop of Sens to absolve certain knights excommunicated by the Bishop of Troyes. Mansi XXII. 412, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 367, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 2, chapter 6.—“From the communication sent to us.”

CCCLIX. He replies to the Archbishop of Sens (otherwise, York) concerning appeals. Mansi XXII. 314, 315, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 288, 289, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 11, 125, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 3, chapter 1.—“As the Roman Church”; “But concerning the point that”; “Concerning the point that.”

CCCLX. He replies to the Archbishop of Sens concerning a delegated judge. Mansi XXII. 300, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II. 266, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 49, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 29, chapter 5.—“Furthermore, concerning.”

CCCLXI. [Col. 1348D] He replies to the Archbishop of Sens (otherwise, Exeter) that “it is not safe for anyone to act against his oath, unless the oath is such that its observance would tend to the destruction of eternal salvation.” Mansi XXII. 346, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II. 237, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 111, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 24, chapter 8.—“But if anyone.”

CCCLXII. He writes to the Archbishop of Sens that, “if a man and woman have contracted marriage by mutual consent, and the man, after knowing her carnally, has married another, he must be compelled to dismiss the second woman and return to the first.” Mansi XXII. 291, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 320, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 240.—“Further, if any.”

CCCLXIII. He replies to the Archbishop of Split (otherwise, Spoleto) concerning bigamists and other matters. Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 225, Mansi XXI. 1092, (Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 41, 254, where these fragments [Col. 1349A] are attributed to Lucius III).—“Concerning the matter that from”; “But concerning the matter”; “Concerning simoniacally.”

CCCLXIV. He replies to the Bishop of Split concerning those “who, whether in health or sickness, have transferred themselves with their possessions to religious places.” Mansi XXII. 421 (where this letter is attributed to Lucius III), Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 255, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 28, chapter 4.—“Concerning those who in.”

CCCLXV. He replies to the Bishop of Split concerning one “who had known a certain woman in unlawful intercourse and afterwards joined her sister to himself in marriage.” Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 330.—“It was contained in the letter.”

CCCLXVI. He commands the abbot of Stamford and the prior of Eshib[e?] to give judgment between the monks of the greater monastery and the church of St. Mary of Martinon. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 364, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 36, chapter 8.—“Coming to the apostolic [see].”

CCCLXVII. He commands the abbot of Stratford (otherwise, Stafford, Castleford) [Col. 1349B] and the prior of Cesebi (otherwise, Helesby, Esebi) to judge between the clerics W. and A. Mansi XXII. 376, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 207, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 66, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 36, chapter 4.—“Being present”; “Being in our presence.”

CCCLXVIII. He writes to the Archbishops of Esztergom and Kalocsa that “a married man wishing to enter a monastery is not to be received unless his wife likewise enters religious life,” etc. Mansi XXII. 284, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 312, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 198, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 32, chapters 5 and 6.—“A married man”; “Certainly, if married persons.”

CCCLXIX. He writes to the Bishop of Syracuse concerning a dispute between the abbot of the Caesarean monastery of St. Peter and Urban, abbot of the monastery of St. Lucy. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 377.—“Because, as the abbot states.”

CCCLXX. He replies to the Archbishop of Tarragona concerning witnesses “against whom crimes are alleged by the opposing party.” Mansi XXII. 305, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, [Col. 1349C] appendix 280, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 100, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 20, chapter 13.—“Concerning the matter that.”

CCCLXXI. He writes to the Archbishop of Tarragona that, when the canons of Pamplona complained “that the duke (king?) of Navarre had despoiled them of their goods,” he had entrusted the case to him for decision. “But,” he says, “because they concealed from us that an appeal had been made to the Apostolic See, we forbid you to proceed in any way with the execution of the matter.” Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 354, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 28, chapter 35.—“Upon receiving the complaint.”

CCCLXXII. He replies to the Archbishop of Terdon[?] concerning what is to be done on feast days. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 369, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 9, chapter 2.—“Because in part.”

CCCLXXIII. He commands the Archbishop of Toledo to remove an archdeacon and a cleric who had received simoniacal payments from Bernard, formerly Bishop of Ceromo (otherwise, Exeter; perhaps Segovia?); [Col. 1349D] and to exhort the king and princes to restore to the church money received from that same bishop. Mansi XXII. 277, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 199, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 279, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 3, chapter 11, Aguirre, *Concilia* V. 96.—“Concerning the fact that the king.”

CCCLXXIV. He commands the Archbishop of Toledo that those who have celebrated sacred rites while under interdict and excommunication, if they are “only forty or fewer,” are to be deprived of the priestly office forever; “but if he learns that a great multitude have sinned in this matter, he is to condemn to perpetual deposition those found to have been more responsible for the offence, suspend the others from office for a time, and impose penance on all.” Mansi XXII. 446, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 323, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 27, chapter 4, Aguirre, *Concilia* V. 96.—“The bearers of the present letter.”

CCCLXXV. He replies to the Archbishop of Toledo concerning appeals. Mansi XXII. 315, Boehmeri *Corpus* [Col. 1350A] II, appendix 289, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 127, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 28, chapter 14.—“Your [letter] consulted us”; “Your brotherhood consulted us.”

CCCLXXVI. He commands the Archbishop of Toledo and his suffragans to exhort “the laypeople of the smaller villages, called *aldeae*, to pay tithes in full to the churches in which they hear Mass and more frequently receive baptism and the other ecclesiastical sacraments.” Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 191.—“The vows which to.”

CCCLXXVII. He replies to the Bishop of Toulouse (otherwise, Toledo) concerning clerics who “received orders after a resignation made by his predecessor.” Mansi XXII. 370, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 226, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 30, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 13, chapter 1.—“He asked of us.”

CCCLXXVIII. He commands the Bishop of Tournai to forbid anyone “to dare, without his consent, to enter churches of his diocese, to hold them, or to resign them without consulting him.” Decr. Greg. Book I, title 9, chapter 4.—“He admonishes”; “To all persons.”

CCCLXXIX. He replies to the Bishop of Troyes (otherwise, Tarragona) concerning tithes. Mansi XXII. 328, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 251, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 186, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 30, chapter 10.—“On behalf of your brotherhood”; “On behalf of your”; “On behalf of you.”

CCCLXXX. He replies to the Bishop of Crete (Troyes) concerning the divorce of a certain knight. Mansi XXII. 290, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 318, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 268, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 19, chapter 4.—“You have informed us that.”

CCCLXXXI. He writes to the Archbishop of Tribur[?] and his suffragans that, since “their region does not abound greatly in crops, and the sea, from which the people have customarily had their greater sustenance, has become more barren than usual,” their parishioners may, on Sundays and other feast days, except for the greater [Col. 1350C] solemnities of the year, if the herrings come close to land, suitably devote themselves to catching them. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 369, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 9, chapter 3; Book V, title 38, chapter 6.—“Although of so ancient.”

CCCLXXXII. He replies to the abbot and brethren of Trois-Fontaines concerning a monk “who, while he was in the world, gave five solidi for ordination.” Mansi XXII. 367, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 219.—“Your [or your plural] [letter] consulted us.”

CCCLXXXIII. He replies to the Bishop of Toul concerning P., who “defiled his father’s betrothed by carnal intercourse.” Mansi XXII. 324, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 329.—“The bearer of this letter, P.”

CCCLXXXIV. He replies to the Archbishop of Tours that “neither illegitimate persons nor slaves ought to be ordained.” Mansi XXII. 371, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 246, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 39, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 18, chapter 5.—“Your [letter] consulted us.”

CCCLXXXV. [Col. 1350D] He writes to the Bishop of Veroli not to compel the abbot of St. Nicholas of Ceperano to receive P. Rubeus. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 29, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 9, chapter 3.—“From the report sent to us.”

CCCLXXXVI. He writes to the Bishop of Veroli concerning the prohibition of certain marriages. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 256.—“Because it has been reported to us.”

CCCLXXXVII. He replies to the Bishop of Vigevano, who asks “whether enclosed women, incapable of intercourse with men, may contract marriage and, if they have contracted it, whether it ought to be dissolved.” “The Roman Church has customarily judged in comparable cases that women who cannot be had as wives should be treated as sisters.” Baluzii *Miscellanea* III. 376, Mansi XXI. 1104, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 339 (Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 15, chapter 4).—“To your inquiry.”

CCCLXXXVIII. He replies to the Bishop of Vigevano that he “can and ought to demand nothing for the consecration of churches beyond procuration.” Mansi [Col. 1351A] XXII. 275, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* III, appendix p. 199, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 278, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 3, chapter 10.—“Since holy”; “Since the Roman [Church].”

CCCLXXXIX. He writes to the Bishop of Vigevano that “a man or woman entering a second marriage ought not to be blessed by a priest, because the blessing must not be repeated.” Mansi XXII. 311, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 338, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 270 (Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 21, chapter 3).—“But a man.”

CCCXC. He writes to the Bishop of Vigevano concerning “a girl betrothed before the age of twelve,” etc. Mansi XXII. 286, 293, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 314, 320, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 236, 224, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 1, chapter 8.—“But if [he has betrothed] a girl”; “If a girl under”; “But the betrothed woman”; “The betrothed of another.”

CCCXCI. He writes to the Bishop of Vigevano that “debtors ought not to be compelled to pay interest unless they are bound by oath to pay it.” Mansi XXII. 344, Boehmeri [Col. 1351B] *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 237, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 110, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 24, chapter 6.—“But debtors.”

CCCXCII. He writes to the archpriest of Volterra and the abbot of Spongia concerning the controversy between the brethren of the monastery of Maturia and the parish priest and clerics. Mansi XXII. 323, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 271, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 84, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 4, chapter 1.—“From your letters.”

CCCXCIII. He writes to the parish priest and clerics of Maturia concerning their dispute with the monks. Mansi XXII. 323, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 271, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 85.—“We greatly wonder.”

CCCXCIV. He writes to the dean, precentor, and chapter of Wells concerning a prebend to be bestowed upon Master E. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 205, Mansi XXI. 1090.—“From the careful report.”

CCCXCV. He writes to the Bishop of Worcester that “ordinary priests or clerics cannot, by their own authority, after their death make liable to rent the churches [Col. 1351C] over which they preside.” Mansi XXII. 377, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 208, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 216, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 39, chapter 8.—“Furthermore, those who.”

CCCXCVI. He writes to the Bishop of Worcester concerning those “who have carnally known the mother, sister, or daughter of their wife.” Mansi XXII. 324, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 328, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 269.—“If any of the parishioners”; “If any parishioner.”

CCCXCVII. He praises the Bishop of Worcester because “he postponed proceeding in a certain case, since the thread from which his seal hung had been broken.” Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 107, Mansi XXII. 401, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 297.—“Carefully”; “As [we know] from the letters.”

CCCXCVIII. He commands the Bishop of Worcester to restore what the abbot of St. Edmund’s had taken from R., the bearer of the letter. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 19, Mansi XXII. [Col. 1351D] 361, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 46, chapter 2.—“The abbot of St. Edmund’s.”

CCCXCIX. He permits the Bishop of Worcester to grant “by hereditary right lands which have been cleared from woodland and made arable, to those by whose labour, whether their own or their parents’, they are known to have been cleared.” Mansi XXII. 380, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 161, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 13, chapter 7.—“But those lands.”

CD. He replies to the Bishop of Worcester concerning “the sons, born after the establishment of spiritual kinship, of two godfathers.” Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 251, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 11, chapter 3.—“Concerning the matter that.”

CDI. He writes to the Bishop of Worcester concerning the case of the cleric R. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 386, Mansi XXII. 394.—“From the complaint sent to us.”

CDII. He commands the Bishop of Worcester to remove the priest C., who “publicly keeps a concubine and is not ashamed, like a layman, to frequent taverns.” [Col. 1352A] Mansi XXI. 1088, XXII. 352, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 338, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 144.—“On the complaint of the prior.”

CDIII. He replies to the Bishop of Worcester concerning William, “who, although he had pledged his faith that he would take a certain woman as wife, nevertheless presumed to join another woman to himself.” Mansi XXII. 286, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 314, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 223.—“Your [letter] consulted us.”

CDIV. He writes to the Bishop of Worcester concerning the case of Master V. of Flamevil. Mansi XXII. 417.—“Coming to the apostolic [see].”

CDV. He replies to the Bishop of Worcester concerning gifts made by abbots. Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 235, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 16, 171, 242, Mansi XXII. 380, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 24, chapter 3; Book IV, title 5, chapter 3.—“Moreover, if [it concerns] an abbot”; “But when to someone.”

CDVI. He commands the Bishop of Worcester to compel R., [Col. 1352B] a priest, to grant the church of St. Mary of Wicun to the cleric Milo. Mansi XXII. 352, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 245, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 33, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 17, chapter 4.—“A complaint having been made to us.”

CDVII. He prescribes to the Bishop of Worcester that he must not “allow priests’ sons to minister in their fathers’ churches.” Mansi XXII. 353, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 245, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 33, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 17, chapter 3.—“By this present [letter] to you”; “Also by this present [letter]”; “By the authority of this present [letter].”

CDVIII. He replies to the Bishop of Worcester concerning an appeal made after citation; concerning “a sentence to be suspended after an appeal”; and concerning “appeals made in very small cases.” Mansi XXII. 314, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 288, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 124, 125, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 28, chapters 9, 10, 11.—“We remember”; “But when any”; “Concerning the matter that”; “Concerning appeals.”

CDIX. [Col. 1352C] He replies to the Bishop of Worcester “concerning monks who burden the vicars of parish churches.” Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 255, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 153, Mansi XXII. 297, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 5, chapter 12.—“But concerning monks.”

CDX. He writes to the Bishop of Worcester that, if H., having been despoiled, renounces the church, he is not to admit against him witnesses of the opposing party concerning the oath and the voluntary renunciation. Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 274, Mansi XXII. 359, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 86, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 13, chapter 2.—“Take care diligently, and.”

CDXI. He replies to the Bishop of Worcester that “authentic documents, if the subscribing witnesses have died, do not appear to him to possess any strength of validity unless perhaps they were made by a public hand or bear an authentic seal.” Mansi XXII. 305, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 280, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 106, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 22, chapter 2.—“But authentic documents.”

CDXII. [Col. 1352D] He writes to the Bishop of Worcester and the abbot of St. Alban’s concerning W., “who forcibly entered the church of N. and died.” Mansi XXII. 361 (Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 367, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 1, chapter 11).—“Because W., who”; “Because V., who.”

CDXIII. He commands the Bishop of Worcester (otherwise, Winchester) to protect the prior and brethren of Lauch (otherwise, Lauth). Mansi XXII. 337, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 297, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 207, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 38, chapter 9.—“The complaint of the prior.”

CDXIV. He replies to the Bishops of Worcester and Coventry concerning the dispute between Master A. of Hyde and R. of Alta Ripa, and concerning certain letters not to be charged with forgery. Baluzii *Miscellanea* III. 373, Mansi XXII. 1101.—“From the letters which.”

CDXV. He writes to the Bishop of Worcester and R., Archdeacon of Ely, concerning the dispute between T., clerk of the king of Scots, and H., parson of the church of Sandeta [Col. 1353A] (otherwise, Sandala, Sandeia). Mansi XXII. 360, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 276, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 87, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 13, chapter 4.—“The complaint having been heard.”

CDXVI. He commands the Bishops of Worcester and Hereford to judge between W., priest of Tritona (otherwise, Certonia, Cretona), and the monks of Bueria (otherwise, Bineria, Breveria). Mansi XXII. 330, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 253, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 188, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 30, chapter 3.—“From the manifold [evidence].”

CDXVII. He writes to the Bishop of Worcester and the prior of Luciwreden concerning the restoration to the cleric G. of the chapel of Streiton. Mansi XXII. 355, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 247, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 36, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 17, chapter 8.—“Being present.”

CDXVIII. He commands the Bishops of Worcester and Norwich concerning the punishment of a priest “who has forged [Col. 1353B] his letters.” Mansi XXII. 367, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 220, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 318.—“But concerning the priest”; “Concerning the priest who”; “Moreover, concerning the priest.”

CDXIX. He commands Gregory (?), Bishop of Trent, to compel the abbot and monks of St. R. to restore money exacted from the priest Fr. “for becoming a monk”; and to suspend the abbot “together with the senior persons of the monastery, from the priestly office for the excess of so great wickedness.” Baluzii *Miscellanea* III. 378, Mansi XXI. 1104, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 410, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 3, chapter 19.—“Coming to us.”

CDXX. He dispenses Master M., abbot of Vad[?] Forden[?], from a certain vow. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 395, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 34, chapter 3.—“Your learning [or letter].”

CDXXI. He replies to the Bishop of Winchester that “no Christian is to be compelled to pay interest, [Col. 1353C] unless he is bound to pay it by oath or pledge.” Mansi XXII. 344.—“Concerning the matter that we.”

CDXXII. He writes to the Bishop of Winchester concerning appeals. Mansi XXI. 1086, XXII. 447, 321, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 293, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 131, 132, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 28, chapter 22.—“Furthermore, those who to”; “But concerning the point that”; “Concerning the point that from.”

CDXXIII. He writes to the Bishop of Winchester that, when a betrothed woman has died untouched, her sister may freely be taken as wife by the bridegroom. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 223, Mansi XXII. 410.—“They are not one.”

CDXXIV. He writes thus to the Bishop of Winchester: “If, without consulting the bishop, a layman grants a church which is not vacant to a religious house, and afterwards, when it has become vacant, a cleric is instituted there by the bishop upon the presentation of that same layman, the prior grant cannot impede the later institution.” [Col. 1353D] Mansi XXII. 337, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 299, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 207, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 38, chapter 8.—“This point ought not to be passed over.”

CDXXV. He commands the Bishop of Winchester to compel those “who have received their principal from the fruits of pledges, or otherwise from deductions for expenses, to restore the pledges.” Mansi XXII. 345, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 216, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 315.—“Nevertheless.”

CDXXVI. He writes to the Bishop of Winchester concerning the portion granted by the holder of a church to a vicar. Mansi XXII. 398, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 244, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 48, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 28, chapter 3.—“Moreover, if”; “If the holder.”

CDXXVII. He replies to the Bishop of Winchester concerning delegated judges. Mansi XXII. 300, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 266, 267, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 50, 13, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 3, chapter 3, title 29, chapter 6.—“Although we are [burdened] by a multiplicity”; “But if”; “A sentence from.”

CDXXVIII. [Col. 1354A] He replies to the Bishop of Winchester concerning a witness accused of a crime. Mansi XXII. 306, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 280, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 100, 105.—“Further, if anyone”; “But any person to.”

CDXXIX. He commands the Bishop of Winchester (otherwise, London) to “forbid most strictly that anything be demanded or even promised from anyone in his parish for permission to teach.” Mansi XXII. 279, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 203, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 287, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 5, chapter 2.—“You are to forbid most strictly.”

CDXXX. He commands the Bishop of Winchester (otherwise, Worcester) to compel “counts as well as barons, and also knights and all others of his parish” to pay tithes. Mansi XXII. 282, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 248, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 183, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 30, chapter 6.—“Messengers and letters.”

CDXXXI. He commands the Bishop of Vomicum (Worms?) [Col. 1354B] that W., betrothed to two women, if “after having pledged faith he has known the first woman,” must remain with her. Baluzii *Miscellanea* III. 380, Mansi XXI. 1107.—“Returning to us.”

CDXXXII. He exhorts the Bishop of Zamora—who, summoned to a council by Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of (St. Mary) in Cosmedin, formerly legate of the Apostolic See, did not come, and who received consecration while excommunicated—to come himself to clear himself, or to send envoys. Mansi XXII. 320, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 293, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 130, Aguirre, *Concilia* V. 97, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 28, chapter 19.—“When we were prepared.”

CDXXXIII. He answers certain questions of Cardinal Mark. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 373, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 20, chapter 22.—“Concerning the point that from.”

CDXXXIV. [Col. 1354C] He writes to a certain bishop concerning appeals. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 379, Mansi XXI. 1097.—“Concerning the point that from.”

CDXXXV. He commands a certain bishop to grant one of his parishioners, whose wife committed fornication with that man’s cousin both before and after marriage, permission to enter a second marriage, “unless it is proved that, after he learned that the aforesaid woman had sinned with his cousin, he committed incest with her.” Baluzii *Miscellanea* III. 376, Mansi XXI. 1099, 1104, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 408.—“It has come to our ears.”

CDXXXVI. He commands a certain bishop to give the woman I. permission “to marry whom she wishes.” Mansi XXII. 285, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 313, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 245, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 6, chapter 5.—“Coming before us”; “Coming into [our] presence.”

CDXXXVII. He replies to a certain bishop concerning the marriage of his parishioner Peter. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 375, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 23, chapter 12.—“The letters of your brotherhood.”

CDXXXVIII. He commands a certain bishop to forbid R. to trouble his niece “concerning an inheritance.” Mansi XXII. 389, Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 332, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 261, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 17, chapter 1.—“He complained to us.”

CDXXXIX. He commands a certain bishop to give judgment between I. and W., who are disputing concerning a church. Mansi XXII. 382, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 244, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 150, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 5, chapter 7.—“Reporting”; “Reporting to us.”

CDXL. He writes to a certain bishop concerning the dispute between Master Alan of Cardeia and R. of Alta Ripa. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 374.—“From the letters which.”

CDXLI. He grants all abbots that, “if bishops demand anything contrary to the liberty of the order, they may refuse what is requested.” [Col. 1355A] Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 416, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 31, chapter 5.—“Certainly, if bishops.”

CDXLII. He writes to a certain abbot concerning those who have laid violent hands upon his brethren, to exhort them to go to Rome. Mansi XXII. 333, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 211, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 343, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 39, chapter 7.—“Further, if any.”

CDXLIII. He commands archdeacons and deans not henceforth to burden “the incumbents of churches with unlawful exactions and procurations.” Mansi XXII. 276, Boehmeri *Corpus juris canonici* II, appendix 205.—“You are to know concerning our.”

CDXLIV. He writes to certain archdeacons concerning the avoidance of simony. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 281 (Mansi XXII. 275, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 39, chapter 12).—“Those things which concerning”; “But when collections”; “Nevertheless also.”

CDXLV. [Col. 1355B] He confirms to “the abbot and convent of the monastery of the greater church, and H., their cleric,” the chapel of Herdelei. Mansi XXII. 412 (Boehmeri *Corpus* II, appendix 271, Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 53).—“Long ago, as”; “(Because the abbot).”

CDXLVI. He releases Richard Breare from homage and fealty owed to G., Archdeacon of Canterbury. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 282, Decr. Greg. Book V, title 3, chapter 17.—“From your careful [report].”

CDXLVII. He replies to someone concerning the right of patronage. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 398 (Decr. Greg. Book III, title 38, chapter 25).—“It was [reported] to us.”

CDXLVIII. He replies to someone concerning settlements. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 364, Decr. Greg. Book I, title 36, chapter 7.—“Concerning what you asked.”

CDXLIX. He replies to someone concerning “those who, because for some reason they cannot receive the nuptial blessing in their own diocese, secretly remove themselves to other dioceses and there contract clandestine marriages.” Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 403, Mansi XXI. 1099.—“Your [letter] consulted us.”

CDL. He replies to someone concerning “a certain person aged fifteen years or more who has taken as wife a girl of thirteen years.” [Col. 1355C] Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 406, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 15, chapter 3.—“We have learned from your letters.”

CDLI. He writes to someone concerning a chaplain “who has celebrated the blessing with a second wife,” to be sent to the Apostolic See. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 409, Decr. Greg. Book IV, title 21, chapter 1.—“Nevertheless, the chaplain.”

CDLII. He forbids someone to permit a sentence of excommunication or interdict to be pronounced without judicial process “against those who hold lands or other possessions from him in fief, even though they are prepared to submit to justice before him regarding those fiefs.” Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 78, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 1, chapter 5.—“But because sometimes.”

CDLIII. He grants someone that nothing be taken from his clerics “as long as they remain [Col. 1355D] in his service.” Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 149, Decr. Greg. Book III, title 4, chapter 7.—“Henceforth, because.”

CDLIV. He writes to someone that “the Roman Church does not admit a prescription against churches of less than forty years.” Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 376, Decr. Greg. Book II, title 26, chapter 8.—“But this point, you.”

CDLV. He commands someone to order the restoration to certain clerics of revenue taken away from them. Augustini Tarr. *Opera* IV. 389, Mansi XXI. 1097.—“To the hearing of the Apostolic See.”

CDLVI. He appoints a certain judge between Master R. and Master Husdric, under whom he “has directed the schools at Blois.” Mansi XXII. 278.—“Our beloved son.”
