CCI.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the bishop-elect of Châlons. 261  
CCII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—Concerning the reform of the monastery of St Maximin. 261  
CCIII.—To Hugh, bishop of Soissons.—He commends his devotion and promises him every favor. 262  
CCIV.—To Gilbert, bishop of London.—He orders him to urge Henry, king of England, to attend to the liberty of the Churches. 263  
CCV.—To the archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the son of the nobleman Frajapanis. 265  
CCVI.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—The summoning of the archbishop to a conference between pope and king. 265  
CCVII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the church of St John of Condé. 266  
CCVIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the brethren of the church of St Remigius. 266  
CCIX.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the church of St Remigius. 266  
CCX.—Privilege for the monastery of St Mary of Mont-Ramey. 267  
CCXI.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That he persuade the king of Sicily to fortify himself against his enemies, and commend to him the bishop of Tropea. 269  
CCXII.—To the same.—He gives thanks because the king has conceived no small joy over the honor and reverence shown to the Roman Church by the envoys of the emperor of Constantinople. 269  
CCXIII.—To the same.—That he order Geoffrey, knight of Molinons, captured by the citizens of Sens, to be released. 270  
CCXIV.—To Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury.—He strengthens him against the king’s begun persecution, and at the same time warns him not to concede to the king anything contrary to ecclesiastical liberty. 271  
CCXV.—To Gilbert, bishop of London.—That he restore King Henry’s mind to a state of peace and concord. 272  
CCXVI.—To the master of the Hospital of Jerusalem.—He commends Peter, prior of the Hospital of St John at Constantinople. 272  
CCXVII.—To W., prior, and the chapter of Canterbury.—He praises them because they share in the tribulations of Archbishop Thomas. 273  

## Year 1163–1164

CCXVIII.—To the abbot of St Remigius of Rheims.—Concerning the case of T., a clerk. 274  
CCXIX.—To Hugh, bishop of Soissons.—That justice be done to the bishop of Senlis concerning vineyards taken from him. 275  
CCXX.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That he cause property taken from the brethren of St Mary of Porte-Lion to be restored. 275  
CCXXI.—To the same.—On behalf of the church of Brioude. 275  
CCXXII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the illness of Lord Henry, archbishop of Rheims, and that God may restore him to health. 276  
CCXXIII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He in turn commends to the king the prior of St Medard, who had been commended to him by the king. 277  
CCXXIV.—To the same.—That he establish a fair at La Ferrière on the anniversary day of the abbot’s consecration. 277  
CCXXV.—To the same.—That the prior of [uncertain: Cerel]’s journey to England be delayed no longer. [Col. 1474] 278  
CCXXVI.—To the same.—That he order the dispute between the brothers Adam and Gregory to be judged by an impartial judge. 278  
CCXXVII.—To the abbots of St Remigius and of La Charité, and to the dean of Rheims.—On behalf of the church of St Maurice at Tours and of Cluny. 278  
CCXXVIII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He announces that the prior of Châteaufort and his associates have been excommunicated by Joscelin, archbishop of Tours, Geoffrey, bishop of Angers, and the abbot of Marmoutier, because of the disgrace inflicted on the abbot of Bourgueil. 279  
CCXXIX.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the case between the abbot of Cluny and the canons of Blessed Maurice. 280  
CCXXX.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of B., a clerk. 280  
CCXXXI.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That he defend the Parisian church of St Geneviève against the wrongs of G., his butler. 281  
CCXXXII.—He confirms the agreement concerning two prebends made between Hugh, bishop of Soissons, and his chapter. 281  
CCXXXIII.—To the abbots of St Remigius and St Nicasius.—Concerning the case of the clerk Odo and his mother, and of Hugh the Smith. 282  

## Year 1164

CCXXXIV.—To Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury.—He recalls for examination the concession made to Roger, archbishop of York, to have the cross borne before him throughout all England. 282  
CCXXXV.—To Roger, archbishop of York.—That he not make use of the concession to have the cross carried before him throughout all England until the dispute has been decided. 283  
CCXXXVI.—To the archbishop and canons of York.—That the archbishop not presume to have the cross borne before him in the province of Canterbury. 283  
CCXXXVII.—He confirms the privileges of the priory of St Mary of Campo in the district of Roussillon. 284  
CCXXXVIII.—To Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the office of apostolic legation, customarily granted to Canterbury but granted to York at the king’s request. 285  
CCXXXIX.—To the same and to the bishops of England.—That they concede to King Henry nothing contrary to ecclesiastical liberty. 287  
CCXL.—To the same.—That he not take offense at the legation granted to Roger of York. 287  
CCXLI.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims, and Henry, cardinal.—Concerning the pope’s affair. 288  
CCXLII.—To Eberhard, archbishop of Salzburg.—That he persuade and require Gerhoh, provost of Reichersberg, to keep silence concerning certain doctrinal disputations. 288  
CCXLIII.—To Gerhoh, provost of Reichersberg.—He imposes silence upon him concerning the same doctrinal disputations. 289  
CCXLIV.—To Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury.—He consoles him in his grief and absolves him from his oath. 290  
CCXLV.—He subjects the monastery of Rebais to Stephen, bishop of Meaux. 290  
CCXLVI.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning thanksgiving for Ar., cardinal-deacon of St Theodore, and concerning reports from Italy conveyed through Master Odo. 291  
CCXLVII.—Privilege for the monastery of St Mary of [uncertain: Strata]. 292  
CCXLVIII.—Privilege for the Carthusian Order. 293  
CCXLIX.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of a certain Gil., that money lent to him be repaid. 294  
CCL–CCLI.—Privilege for the monastery of St Peter at Chartres. 294  
CCLII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the church of St Remigius. 294  
CCLIII.—He takes the monastery of Val-Richer under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 295  
CCLIV.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of R., the chancellor. 297  
CCLV.—To the same.—For the absolution of William, a monk. 298  
CCLVI.—To the same.—Concerning the case of Milesendis and R. de Courti. 298  
CCLVII.—He commends to Hugh, bishop of Soissons, Rain., archdeacon of Salisbury, who is to devote himself to studies in Paris. 299  
CCLVIII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—Concerning the chancellor of Emperor Frederick, at whose command workmen had already begun work on the frontier of France. 299  
CCLIX.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That the king not determine otherwise in a case judged by apostolic authority by the bishop of Le Mans. [Col. 1475] 300  
CCLX.—He establishes the city of Uppsala as the metropolitan see of the bishoprics of Skara, Linköping, Strängnäs, and Västerås, etc. 301  
CCLXI.—Bull concerning the establishment of the metropolitan see of Uppsala. 303  
CCLXII.—To Abbot Henry and the brethren of St Mary of Vitsœl. 304  
CCLXIII.—Concerning the distribution of the monks of [uncertain: Trenorciensis] among various monasteries, with five or four left there, so that meanwhile the debts may be paid. 304  
CCLXIV.—To Hugh, bishop of Soissons.—That a certain hospital at Compiègne be held by the monastery. 305  
CCLXV.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—Concerning a certain Nicholas who had complained to the pope about the canons of Tours. 306  
CCLXVI.—To the same.—Concerning the monastery of [uncertain: Trenorciensis]. 307  
CCLXVII.—To the abbots of St Germanus and St Victor, the prior and subprior of St Victor, and Odo, formerly abbot of St Geneviève.—That they inquire into the penalties imposed upon William, canon of St Geneviève. 307  
CCLXVIII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—What sort of diet he ought to follow on every Friday. 307  
CCLXIX.—He secures for the brethren of St Mary of Valcrose the place called Fons Calidus, “Hot Spring.” 308  
CCLXX.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the case between the abbot of St Remigius and the abbot of Der. 309  
CCLXXI.—To William, count of Nevers, and Ida his mother.—That they abstain from harassing the monastery of Vézelay. 309  
CCLXXII.—He informs Louis, king of the Franks, that he has received his letters and will carry out his commands. 310  
CCLXXIII.—At the request of Master García and the brethren of Calatrava, he takes Calatrava under protection and confirms the brethren’s rules, possessions, and privileges. 310  
CCLXXIV.—He takes the monastery of St Mary of Hortense under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 312  
CCLXXV.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—Concerning certain changes in France which the welfare both of the Church and of the kingdom then requires. 313  
CCLXXVI.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—Concerning the election in the church of Chartres. 313  
CCLXXVII.—To the same.—Concerning the hospital of Compiègne. 314  
CCLXXVIII.—To the same.—He assigns the hospital of Compiègne to the abbey of that city. 314  
CCLXXIX.—He takes the church of St Mary of Liskeard under protection and confirms its possessions. 315  
CCLXXX.—Privilege for the monastery of St John at Moutiers-Saint-Jean. 316  
CCLXXXI.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He commends the monastery of St Maximin to him. 318  
CCLXXXII.—He assigns to Theobald, prior, and the brethren of the church of St Martin-des-Champs the church of St Martin at Tours, adjudged to them. 318  
CCLXXXIII.—He commends Brother F., his envoy, to Louis, king of the Franks. 320  

## About the Year 1164

CCLXXXIV.—He commends to Louis, king of the Franks, the monastery of Compiègne, to which he wishes the hospital house to be secured. 320  

## Years 1163–1165

CCLXXXV.—To Cono, abbot of St Vitonus.—He praises him for his zeal for the Apostolic See and exhorts him always to adhere to it in devotion. 321  
CCLXXXVI.—To Martin, abbot, and the monks of St Vaast.—He confirms the agreement made between them and the abbess of [uncertain: Strumensis]. 322  
CCLXXXVII.—Order concerning the arrangement of the property of the canons of Paris. 323  

## Years 1164–1165

CCLXXXVIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Robert, a knight. 323  
CCLXXXIX.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of A., bishop of Arras. 324  
CCXC.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the case of the abbess of Bertolocors and the nuns of St Ignatius. 325  
CCXCI.—To the monks of St Vaast.—That in electing an abbot they elect a person from their own community, not an outsider. 326  
CCXCII.—To Master F. and Master R., canon of Rheims.—On behalf of Theobald Bigot. 326  
CCXCIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the church of St Remigius. [Col. 1476] 327  
CCXCIV.—To P. of Narbonne and the bishops of Nîmes, Uzès, Mende, and Maguelone.—He praises their care in abolishing tolls and customs duties; but he punishes Bernard, count of Melgueil, who refuses to comply, with a sentence of interdict. 327  
CCXCV.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the Eastern Church. 328  
CCXCVI.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—Concerning the case of the bishop of Cambrai, to whom he still grants a truce. 328  
CCXCVII.—He promises Louis, king of the Franks, that he will not fail Peter, archbishop of Bourges. 329  
CCXCVIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the church of St Remigius. 329  
CCXCIX.—To the abbot of St Remigius, the abbot of Château-Thierry, and L., dean of Rheims.—Concerning the case between the abbot of Orbais and the abbot of Igny. 330  
CCC.—To the abbot of St Remigius of Rheims.—Concerning the case between the abbot of St Remigius and Odd. 330  
CCCI.—He directs the dean and treasurer of Rheims to commend Guy, bishop-elect of Châlons, to Archbishop Henry. 331  
CCCII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the abbot of St Remigius. 331  
CCCIII.—He asks Louis, king of the Franks, to urge William, king of Sicily, to receive into favor Florio of Camebotta, whom he has sent into exile. He wishes the same Florio to be commended to the emperor of Constantinople. 332  
CCCIV.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—That G., count of Roceio, be compelled to return money which he took from the envoy of the archbishop of Lyons. 333  
CCCV.—To Maurice, bishop of Paris.—Concerning the remission of the annual census of one ounce of gold for the church of Latiniacum. 333  
CCCVI.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That he labor to bring about peace between certain persons. 334  
CCCVII.—Privilege for the abbey of Fontevraud. 334  
CCCVIII.—To Walter, bishop, and Robert, archdeacon of Langres.—Concerning the church of Sarrinia. 335  
CCCIX.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the church of St Memmius. 335  
CCCX.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That R., a priest, have his possessions restored to him by their unjust possessor. 336  
CCCXI.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the Cistercian brethren. 336  
CCCXII.—He commends Erm. of Narbonne to Louis, king of the Franks. 337  

## Year 1165

CCCXIII.—He grants to the abbot of St Bertin at Saint-Omer “that, in cases concerning churches situated in different dioceses, he shall not be bound to attend the synods of those bishops, even when summoned.” 337  
CCCXIV.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He desires a meeting and consultation with the king. 337  
CCCXV.—Privilege for the monastery of Foigny. 338  
CCCXVI.—A bull by which he confirms all the possessions of St Peter already confirmed by his predecessors, and moreover, in the diocese of Chartres, two holdings—namely Soretiacum and Niglebold; in the diocese of Séez, the church of St Anianus; and in the diocese of Coutances, the church of Ham and the church of Goetberti Villa. 339  
CCCXVII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He sends him letters from the emperor of Constantinople. 339  
CCCXVIII.—He takes the monastery of Cîteaux under protection and confirms its privileges. 340  
CCCXIX.—Bull for Holy Cross at Bordeaux. 341  
CCCXX.—He takes under protection the monastery of the Dunes, formerly on the seashore and now at Bruges, and confirms its possessions and privileges. 343  
CCCXXI.—Privilege for the monastery of Ruisseau. 345  
CCCXXII.—Confirmation of the agreement made between Stephen, former bishop of Paris, and Theobald, archdeacon. 346  
CCCXXIII.—He takes the monastery of St Martin at Autun under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 346  
CCCXXIV.—To the abbot of Cîteaux.—Concerning the affair of the church of Clairvaux and its abbot. 348  
CCCXXV.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the matter or affair entrusted to the archbishop of Auxerre for action at Clairvaux, and how those of Sens are to be recalled. 350  
CCCXXVI.—Bull for the monastery of St Serenus at Cantumerula. 351  
CCCXXVII.—He confirms the exemption and temporal goods of the monastery of St Valery. [Col. 1477] 352  
CCCXXVIII.—He confirms the possessions and privileges of the church of Paris. 353  
CCCXXIX.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the church of Blessed Glodesindis at Metz. 354  
CCCXXX.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That the archdeaconry of Chartres be granted to one of his clerks. 354  
CCCXXXI.—To the monks of St Peter at Chartres. 355  
CCCXXXII.—To Theobald, a nobleman.—He commends to him the church of Bonneval and Walter, its new abbot. 355  
CCCXXXIII.—He exhorts the abbot of St Remigius of Rheims to restore a certain possession to the prior of St Maurice. 355  
CCCXXXIV.—Privilege for the monastery of Rigny. 356  
CCCXXXV.—Privilege for the monastery of Bonmont in the diocese of Geneva. 359  
CCCXXXVI.—He confirms the possessions of the church of St Mark at Venice. 362  
CCCXXXVII.—He exhorts the Templars residing in the dioceses of Lyons and Chalon to reach an agreement with the brethren of [uncertain: Trenorciensis] concerning certain tithes withheld from the monastery. 363  
CCCXXXVIII.—Bull for the monastery of L. Satyri. 364  
CCCXXXIX.—He praises the abbot and brethren of Pontigny for treating Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury, honorably, and commends Thomas himself to them. 368  
CCCXL.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the affair of the church of Clairvaux. 368  
CCCXLI.—To the brethren of the church of St Peter at Chartres. 369  
CCCXLII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Everen., a priest. 369  
CCCXLIII.—He asks Louis, king of the Franks, to deter the count of Nevers and his mother from harassing the monastery of Vézelay. 369  
CCCXLIV.—He directs Hugh, archbishop of Sens, to urge the count of Nevers and his mother to repair the injuries inflicted upon the monastery of Vézelay; unless they do so within twenty days, he orders him to bind them with excommunication. 370  
CCCXLV.—He orders Henry of Autun, Walter of Langres, Alan of Auxerre, and Bernard of Nevers, bishops, to observe the sentence of excommunication which the archbishop of Sens has pronounced against the count of Nevers and his mother. 371  
CCCXLVI.—He informs Abbot William and the brethren of Vézelay of the foregoing letters. 372  
CCCXLVII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of a certain woman named Hersende. 372  
CCCXLVIII.—To the same.—On behalf of C., nephew of the pope. 373  
CCCXLIX.—To Gilbert, bishop of London.—Concerning the church of Canterbury. 373  
CCCL.—To Henry, king of England.—Concerning the inviolability of ecclesiastical immunity and the prohibition against bringing clerics before a secular tribunal. 375  
CCCLI.—To Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury.—He consoles him, oppressed by hardships. 377  
CCCLII.—To the same.—He announces that he has annulled the sentence pronounced against him by the bishops and barons of England. 377  
CCCLIII.—To the abbot of the monastery.—On behalf of the complaint at issue between E. and A., a priest. 377  
CCCLIV.—Bull for the monastery of Manziacum, which is taken under the protection of the Apostolic See. 378  
CCCLV.—A bull by which the monastery of St Illidius and all its possessions are taken under the protection of the Roman Church. 380  
CCCLVI.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That B., cantor of St Anianus, was rightly deprived by the Apostolic See of his benefice and office. 381  
CCCLVII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He commends to him the archdeacon of Bourges; he bids him hope well concerning German affairs. 382  
CCCLVIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Ralph, a priest, that his church be restored to him. 383  
CCCLIX.—To Clerembald, bishop-elect and monk of St Augustine.—That, all appeal ceasing, he make his profession to the church of Canterbury. 383  
CCCLX.—To princes, counts, barons, and all the faithful of God.—Concerning sending aid to the East against the Saracens. 384  
CCCLXI.—Bull addressed to Peter, abbot of Bonfont. 386  
CCCLXII.—He receives the monastery of St Daniel at Venice under the protection of Blessed Peter, confirms its possessions, and bestows other privileges upon it. [Col. 1478] 388  
CCCLXIII.—He directs the bishops of Rodez and Cahors to decide the dispute between Bishop William and the canons of Albi on one side, and the monks of Aurillac on the other. 389  
CCCLXIV.—He informs the monks of Aurillac of the foregoing letter. 390  
CCCLXV.—To Gislebert of Cîteaux and the rest of that order.—He confirms their institutions and adorns them with privileges. 390  
CCCLXVI.—He directs Pontius, archbishop of Narbonne, and William, bishop of Béziers, not to allow Fons Calidus, “Hot Spring,” to be taken from the church of Valcrose. 394  
CCCLXVII.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—That he give Thomas, in exile, a bishopric or abbey if one becomes vacant. 394  
CCCLXVIII.—To John, bishop, and the canons of Maguelone.—That they cause the altar and offerings of the church of St Saviour, formerly granted by Adrian IV, to be restored to the prior of St Mary.—To Lord William and the people of Montpellier, for the support of the church. 395  
CCCLXIX.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He commends William, bishop-elect of Chartres, to the king; he exhorts him to be steadfast in defending the cause of the Church against Emperor Frederick. 396  
CCCLXX.—He confirms the patrimony of Guinand, count of Roussillon. 396  
CCCLXXI.—He directs Pontius of Narbonne and Hugh, bishop of Tarragona, together with Artaldus, bishop of Elne, and the bishop of Girona, not to allow the patrimony of Guinand, count of Roussillon, to be invaded by his known brothers. 397  
CCCLXXII.—To Gilbert, bishop of London.—He orders him to continue exhorting Henry, king of England, to show devotion to the Roman Church and defend its rights, and to receive Thomas of Canterbury into favor and grace. 397  
CCCLXXIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the pope: how he escaped by sea from the hands of those lying in wait, who intended to seize his possessions, him, and his companions. 398  
CCCLXXIV.—He confirms to Roger, archbishop of Reggio, and his successors the use of the pallium, already granted by Gregory VII and Eugenius III, and the right of consecrating his suffragan bishops, both Greek and Latin. He confirms the privileges granted to the church of Reggio by emperors and kings, and decrees that the churches of Gerace, Suma, Tropea, Nicastro, Bova, Oppido, and Crotone shall henceforth be suffragans of the church of Reggio and subject to the Apostolic See. 400  
CCCLXXV.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the pope’s reception in the City and concerning a certain woman, C.  
CCCLXXVI.—To the clergy established in the diocese of Bangor.—That they elect a bishop whom Thomas of Canterbury may confirm. 401  
CCCLXXVII.—To the prior and brethren of Canterbury.—That they relieve the need of Thomas in exile. 402  
CCCLXXVIII.—To Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury.—He confirms the sentence issued by him against certain perverse persons. 402  
CCCLXXIX.—To Henry, bishop of Troyes.—He commends Master Herbert, who remained attached as a companion to Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury, in exile. 402  

## Year 1165?

CCCLXXX.—To Robert, bishop of Hereford.—He reproves him because he supported Archbishop Thomas less than he ought in defending the liberty of the Church. 403  
CCCLXXXI.—He reproves them because in many matters they have proved lukewarm and negligent. 404  

## Years 1165–1166

CCCLXXXII.—To Henry, archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the case between the church of [uncertain OCR: “Erapous smanil”] and the church of Roye. 405  

## Year 1166
CCCLXXXIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—He asks him to procure for him one hundred marks of silver and to assist his needs from the churches of his diocese. 405

CCCLXXXIV.—To all the bishops of England.—That, in matters concerning the Church of Canterbury, they should support Archbishop Thomas. 406

CCCLXXXV.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He orders him to exhort the clergy of the Church of Bangor to elect a bishop; if they do not do so, he himself is to do it within three months. 407

[Col. 1479]

CCCLXXXVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—He commends the exiled Thomas. 407

CCCLXXXVII.—To the clergy and people of Bangor.—That they should elect a bishop. 408

CCCLXXXVIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the chaplains of Laon. 408

CCCLXXXIX.—He takes the monastery of Saint John of Pissare under his protection and confirms its property and rights. 409

CCCXC.—To Roger of York and all the bishops of England.—That none of them should presume to take part in crowning a new king, should such a contingency arise, without the concurrence of Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury. 411

CCCXCI.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He grants him the legation over all England, excepting the diocese of York. 411

CCCXCII.—To the bishops, abbots, and other prelates of churches established throughout England outside the diocese of York.—That they should obey Thomas of Canterbury, appointed legate of the Apostolic See. 412

CCCXCIII.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—That, if he sees an opportunity, he should not delay in exercising ecclesiastical justice against invaders of the possessions of the Church of Canterbury. 413

CCCXCIV.—To all the bishops of the province of Canterbury.—He informs them of the preceding letter. 413

CCCXCV.—To the abbots and brethren of Cîteaux and Pontigny.—That they should not allow Thomas of Canterbury to be removed from the monastery of Pontigny. 414

CCCXCVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Robert the priest. 415

CCCXCVII.—To Gilbert of London and all the bishops of the province of Canterbury.—That, under threat of anathema, they should more strictly compel those who have invaded the benefices of the clerics of Archbishop Thomas of Canterbury to make full restitution. 415

CCCXCVIII.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He confirms the sentence of interdict pronounced by him against Jocelin, Bishop of Salisbury. 416

CCCXCIX.—To the same.—He orders that he has annulled the grant made by Jocelin, Bishop of Salisbury, to John of Oxford. 416

CD.—To the Archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the election of the abbess of Dodon. 416

CDI.—He exhorts Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, to deal more mildly with Jocelin of Salisbury. 417

CDII.—To Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen, and his suffragans.—Concerning the evils inflicted upon the Church by Henry, King of England. 417

CDIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning a subdeacon of Laon who had taken a wife, and the lawsuit of the Bishop of Laon against the chaplains of Laon. 418

CDIV.—To the same.—Concerning the case pending between G. and Hersend. 419

CDV.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, and his suffragans.—He announces that Counts H. and W. of Vals have been excommunicated. 420

CDVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of a certain man, concerning a pledge at Molendini. 420

CDVII.—To the Bishop of Le Mans.—Concerning the affair of Philip, nephew of Henry, Archbishop of Rheims. 421

CDVIII.—To Philip, Count of Flanders.—He confirms his marriage to Elizabeth, daughter of the Count of Péronne. 422

CDIX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Baldwin the monk, that he may be received. 422

CDX.—To the same.—On behalf of L., Prior of Saint Remigius of Rheims. 422

CDXI.—Privilege for the monastery of Pontigny. 423

CDXII.—To the bishops of England.—He states that, in the case of Thomas of Canterbury, he has sent two legates *a latere* into England with plenary authority. 425

CDXIII.—To Henry, King of England.—That the authority of the Archbishop of Canterbury should be suspended until he has obtained peace from the king. 426

CDXIV.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He exhorts him to patience. 427

CDXV.—To Waldemar, King of the Danes.—Concerning the transfer of the cloister of Weng and the recall of Archbishop Eskil. 428

CDXVI.—To the bishops of Denmark.—On the same subject. 429

## In the year 1166?

CDXVII.—To Gilbert, Bishop of London.—That he should not fail to transmit Saint Peter’s Pence, “which was due to him from England.” 430

## In the years 1166–1167

CDXVIII.—To John, Bishop of Maguelonne. 431

CDXIX.—To John, Bishop of Maguelonne. 431

CDXX.—He praises Bertrand, Archbishop of Bordeaux and legate of the Apostolic See, because he approved the sentence pronounced by Bertrand, Abbot of Holy Cross, against the monks of Saint Macarius. 432

CDXXI.—To the abbot and brethren of Saint Remigius.—That they should receive William, a fugitive monk. 433

CDXXII.—To John, Bishop of Maguelonne.—Concerning the canons of the Church of Maguelonne. 433

CDXXIII.—To Stephen, Bishop of Meaux.—That, if any convent is not agreed in the election of an abbot, it belongs to the bishop to confirm as abbot the person to whom the greater and sounder part has consented. 434

CDXXIV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Robert the priest. 434

CDXXV.—To the same.—On behalf of the same person. 435

CDXXVI.—To the abbot and brethren of Cluny, concerning the election, made through necessity and without their counsel and authority, of the abbot of Saint Benedict of Padilirone; that this should not be drawn into precedent. 435

CDXXVII.—To the Abbot of Saint Remigius of Rheims.—On behalf of Dejectus, priest. 436

CDXXVIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and his suffragans.—That they should excommunicate Drogo the schismatic. 437

CDXXIX.—To the same.—Concerning the absolution of certain excommunicated persons. 438

CDXXX.—To the same Henry.—On behalf of Hugh, a cleric. 438

CDXXXI.—To the same.—On behalf of John, a cleric, that he may be invested with a prebend. 439

CDXXXII.—To the same.—On behalf of the cantor of Douai, that he may be restored. 440

CDXXXIII.—To the dean and chapter of Châlons.—That they should not demand money for schools. 440

CDXXXIV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the admonition of ecclesiastical prelates that they should assist him. A commendation of perseverance in affection for the Roman Church, and an exhortation to the same. 441

CDXXXV.—To the same.—On behalf of Walter, a cleric. 442

CDXXXVI.—To the same.—On behalf of a certain G., that his inheritance may be restored to him. 442

CDXXXVII.—To the same.—Concerning the affair of the Bishop of Grenoble. 442

CDXXXVIII.—To the same.—Concerning the ordination and consecration of the Bishop of Tournai. 443

CDXXXIX.—To the same.—Concerning the case of the Church of Brague. 444

CDXL.—He orders the canons of Pisa to avoid B., formerly a canon and an excommunicated defender of schism; nevertheless, they are to receive him if he returns to virtue. 445

CDXLI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of a certain Job, that what was taken from him may be restored. 445

CDXLII.—To the same.—On behalf of a certain burgess G. of Rheims. 446

CDXLIII.—He orders the Bishop-elect of Cahors to render judgment concerning Peter Mancovela, priest. 446

CDXLIV.—He informs the Bishop of Norwich that he has released the cleric R. from his vow of a journey to Jerusalem. 446

## In the year 1167

CDXLV.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the legation sent to England. 446

CDXLVI.—To Henry, King of England.—On the same subject. 447

CDXLVII.—To Louis VII, King of the Franks.—Concerning the legation entrusted, through France, to Archbishop Thomas of Canterbury. 448

CDXLVIII.—He takes the Church of Saint Saviour at Venice under his protection. 449

CDXLIX.—He confirms the possessions of the monastery of Saint Savin of Tarbes. 451

CDL.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the absolution of Count Hugh if he restores what he has taken. 452

CDL *bis*.—He confirms the immunities and privileges of the Church of Modena. 453

CDLI.—To William and Otto, cardinal legates.—He states that none of the rights of Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, have been taken away. 455

CDLII.—He confirms for Raymond, Bishop of Brivio, and his successors the right of sitting at the right hand of the Archbishop of Milan in synods. 456

[Col. 1481]

CDLIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the case of the Abbot of Saint Remigius and the woman Si. 456

CDLIV.—To Galdinus, Archbishop of Milan.—That he should revoke certain privileges granted by Robald, formerly archbishop, to the canons of Monza, to the injury of the convent of Cremella. 456

CDLV.—To Roger, Archbishop of York.—He orders that, when requested by Henry, King of England, he should place the crown upon Henry, the king’s eldest son. 457

CDLVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of a certain woman of Hersend. 457

CDLVII.—To the same.—Concerning the suspicion of stolen letters entertained against Milo. 458

CDLVIII.—To the same.—A recommendation and exhortation that he should assist him and induce the king to do likewise; and concerning the affair of Master G., priest, regarding a prebend at Soissons. 459

CDLIX.—To William and Otto, legates of the Apostolic See.—That, for the good of the Church, the kings of France and England should be reconciled, and that in England they should do nothing concerning the condition of the realm and Church without the knowledge of Thomas of Canterbury. 460

CDLX.—To the same.—That they should compel those excommunicated by the Archbishop of Canterbury for invading Church property to render due satisfaction; if they refuse, they should excommunicate them again. 460

CDLXI.—To Albert, legate of the Apostolic See.—He forbids him to accept the archbishopric of Split offered to him. 461

CDLXII.—He orders Henry, Abbot of Biburg, to accept the abbey of Saint Peter at Salzburg, offered by Archbishop Conrad and the monks. 461

CDLXIII.—He orders the monks of Biburg to release Abbot Henry for the monastery of Saint Peter at Salzburg. 462

CDLXIV.—Privilege for the Church of Ragusa. 462

CDLXV.—He orders the Bishops of Pula, Suacia, and Drivast to obey Tribunus, Archbishop of Ragusa. 462

CDLXVI.—He orders the clergy of the dioceses of Dulcigno and Antivari not to obey bishops excommunicated by Tribunus, Archbishop of Ragusa. 463

CDLXVII.—To Henry, King of England.—He states that letters of the king, delivered by Clarambald, Reginald, Simon de Carcere, and Henry of Northampton, have been received by him. 464

CDLXVIII.—He rebukes Hugh, Archbishop of Sens, because “without the knowledge and mandate of [Alan], Bishop of Auxerre, he received his resignation.” He nevertheless permits him to consecrate [William], elected in his place. 466

CDLXIX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he should cease harassing the canons of Rheims. 466

CDLXX.—To Louis, King of the Franks.—That he should restore to the canons of the Church of Rheims both his favour and their seized possessions. 467

## In the year 1168

CDLXXI.—He commends Tribunus, Archbishop of Ragusa, to abbots and other Latins, both clerics and laypeople. 468

CDLXXII.—Privilege for the Church of Jerusalem. 469

CDLXXIII.—He writes to P[eter], prior, and the brethren of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, that A[malric], the patriarch, has been admonished by letter from him not to presume, on any pretext, “to interfere in their affairs or obediences unless requested by them”; and “that, when they wished to admit anyone as a fellow canon, he should grant them his favour in this matter and should impose no one upon their fellowship”; nor should he, against their will, assign prebends in their church to different persons according to his own pleasure. 471

CDLXXIV.—He informs P[eter], prior, and the brethren of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem that he has directed Patriarch A[malric] “to require from them only a third part of the wax brought to their church”; that, “if he entered any city and, both in going out and in returning from an expedition, stayed there, he should allow them to retain all offerings made to it after the second day”; and that he should not forbid either “the bodies of the dead to be brought before their altars” or “crosses to be held before them on the day of Preparation [Good Friday].” He also reports that the Hospitallers have been admonished not to attempt, whenever they have a complaint against them, to withhold tithes from them. 472

CDLXXV.—He informs P[eter], prior, and the brethren of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem that he has sent letters to the Hospitallers ordering them not to deny them tithes; not “to presume to build a new church in the city of Joppa without the consent of the patriarch and of themselves”; and, when Joppa has been placed under interdict, not to ring bells in their church, which stands within the body of the city, or admit excommunicated or specifically interdicted persons to divine offices. 473

CDLXXVI.—He forbids the Patriarch of Jerusalem “to presume to institute or depose abbots, abbesses, or other ecclesiastical persons without the assent and counsel of the prior and canons of the Holy Sepulchre.” 474

CDLXXVII.—Privilege for the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem. 474

CDLXXVIII.—He confirms for the monastery of Saint Valery the parochial right of the castle of Saint Valery, adjudged against the Bishop of Amiens. 477

CDLXXIX.—He takes the convent of Saint Victorinus at Benevento under his patronage and confirms its property, liberty, and privileges. 479

CDLXXX.—To Henry, King of England.—He exhorts him to receive Archbishop Thomas of Canterbury back into favour. 480

CDLXXXI.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning Jocelin, Archbishop of Salisbury. 481

CDLXXXII.—To the same.—He revokes the suspension of his apostolic commission. 483

CDLXXXIII.—To the bishops of England.—Against investitures usurped by laymen. 484

CDLXXXIV.—To John Cumin.—That he should restore to Roger, Bishop of Worcester, the archdeaconry of Bath which he had seized. 485

CDLXXXV.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—That he should absolve Gerard Puella from the sentence by which he is bound. 485

CDLXXXVI.—To Louis, King of the Franks.—On behalf of Gerard Puella. 486

CDLXXXVII.—To Henry, King of England.—He grieves that he has not yet been reconciled with Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury. 486

CDLXXXVIII.—To Simon, Prior of Mont-Dieu, and Bernard of Corilo.—On behalf of Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury. 487

CDLXXXIX.—To Roger, Bishop of Worcester.—That he should return to his church. Concerning the envoys sent to King Henry. 488

CDXC.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—That he should deal with King Henry in a fatherly and kindly manner. 489

CDXCI.—To Louis, King of the Franks.—On the same subject. 490

CDXCII.—Privilege for the monastery of Saint Sylvester of Nonantola. 491

CDXCIII.—He confirms the liberty of the monastery of Nonantola. 493

CDXCIV.—To the monks of Saint Prosper at Reggio.—That they should remove from office Abbot Guido, held guilty of dilapidating the monastery. 495

CDXCV.—Privilege for John, Bishop of Catania. 495

CDXCVI.—To the Bishops of Soissons, Amiens, and Laon.—On behalf of Countess Constance of Saint-Gilles, against the Count of Boulogne, concerning her dower. 497

CDXCVII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—He excuses himself for not having satisfied his requests concerning the Bishop of Arras. He exhorts him to treat his suffragans kindly. He states that he has written to the Bishops of Soissons, Amiens, and Laon concerning his sister Constance, wife of the Count of Toulouse. He commends Master Paganus. 498

CDXCVIII.—He confirms the property and privileges of the monastery of Saints Felix and Fortunatus at Vicenza. 499

CDXCIX.—Privilege for the monastery of Saint Reparata at Marradino. 501

D.—He takes under his protection the Church of Saints Hippolytus and Cassian, and Saint John the Baptist of Fosciano, and confirms its possessions and privileges. 502

DI.—He takes the Church of Saint Peter at Bologna under his protection and confirms its property and rights. 504

## In the year 1168?

DII.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He advises him to overcome the king by humility. 505

## In the years 1165–1169

DIII.—To the King of Scotland.—He commends the exiled Thomas to him. 506

DIV.—To Philip, Count of Flanders.—On the same subject. 507

DV.—To Count Henry.—On the same subject. 507

DVI.—To the Abbot of Clairmarais.—He commends the sister of Archbishop Thomas of Canterbury and her children. 508

[Col. 1483]

DVII.—To Stephen of Meaux and the Abbot of Saint Crispin.—He orders them to exhort King Henry to restore, and cause to be restored without delay, the revenues, honours, and possessions of the Church of Canterbury. 508

DVIII.—To the Abbot of Cîteaux and Pontigny and all brethren of the Cistercian Order.—On behalf of Brother R. 509

DIX.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—That the resignation of Henry, Bishop of Winchester, harassed by King Henry, is void. 509

## In the years 1167–1169

DX.—He orders the abbot and monks of Vallis Laurea not to obey the Archbishop of Tarragona or the Bishop of Barcelona until their dispute over boundaries has been adjudicated. 509

DXI.—Concerning the case pending between Ric. and the Abbot of Saint Peter. 510

DXII.—To Henry, King of England.—He threatens him with ecclesiastical censure unless he abstains from sacrileges. 510

DXIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of B., a cleric, and that his prebend may be restored to him. 541

DXIV.—He confirms for Roger, abbot, and the brethren of the monastery of Ibreio the tithes of Dochinq, adjudged to them by Henry, Bishop of Winchester, and Gilbert of London. 512

DXV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he should keep Giderus of Sarnay, who is invading the possessions of the Church of Montfaucon, within the bounds of his duty. 513

DXVI.—To the same.—On behalf of Huldred, priest, concerning the church of Ponit. 513

DXVII.—To the same.—That he should compel Mainerius, priest, to restore to Henry the parish taken from him. 514

DXVIII.—To the same.—On behalf of Priest P. 515

DXIX.—To the same.—On behalf of the lepers of Cambrai. 515

DXX.—He informs the abbots of Saint Andrew of the Castle and of the Holy Sepulchre, and the canons of Saint Gaugeric, concerning the preceding letter. 516

DXXI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the Church of Saint Martin at Laon. 517

DXXII.—To the same.—On behalf of R., a cleric, that the lord of Rheims may show him favour. 517

DXXIII.—He confirms for the convent of Fontevraud the gift of fifty pounds of annual revenue charged upon the castle of Dijon, granted by Odo, Duke of Burgundy. 518

DXXIV.—To all archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates of Spain.—On behalf of the monastery of Ripoll. 518

DXXV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Amelius, concerning a certain estate. 519

DXXVI.—To the same.—Likewise on behalf of Amelius, concerning certain possessions. 519

DXXVII.—To the same and the Bishop of Laon.—That they should compel Rainald of Roset to restore to Giles of Cimai his wife’s dower. 520

DXXVIII.—To the same.—On behalf of Roland and Ebruin. 520

DXXIX.—To John, Bishop of Maguelonne.—He grants various privileges. 521

DXXX.—To the same.—He adds another privilege. 522

DXXXI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That the monastery of Saint Denis should be commended to him. 522

DXXXII.—To the same.—On behalf of John, priest, concerning the church of Poegni. 523

DXXXIII.—To Gerard, Archbishop of Split.—That he should order property taken from a certain person to be restored. 524

DXXXIV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he should cause the alms taken from the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem by the Duke of Louvain to be restored. 524

DXXXV.—To all ecclesiastics established in the land of Duke Welf. 525

## In the years 1168–1169

DXXXVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Amelius of Albiniac. 525

DXXXVII.—To the same.—On behalf of Peter, formerly a Jew. 526

DXXXVIII.—To Gerald, Bishop of Toulouse.—At the entreaty of King Louis VII, he releases Toulouse from interdict. 526

DXXXIX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Hugh, a servant. 527

DXL.—To the same.—On behalf of Drogo, canon of Ham. 528

DXLI.—To the same.—On behalf of G., a priest. 528

DXLII.—To the same.—On behalf of John, canon of Laon. 529

DXLIII.—To the same.—On behalf of Ha., a priest. 529

DXLIV.—He orders the Bishop of Thérouanne and the Abbot of Saint Quentin of Mont to hear the case between the Abbot of Humolaires and the Abbot of Ribemont, the abbess of Monasteriolum, and the knight of Brenoth. 530

DXLV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the Abbot of Saint Martin at Laon. 531

DXLVI.—To the same.—On behalf of William, Dean of Soissons. 531

DXLVII.—He informs Hugh, Bishop of Soissons, concerning the preceding letter. 532

DLXVIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Albert, a priest. 532

DXLIX.—He confirms for Albert, priest, the Church of Saint Remigius of Augeio and the chapel of Cersolio. 533

DL.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of B., a priest. 533

DLI.—To the same.—On behalf of the Church of Saint John at Soissons. 534

DLII.—To the same.—On behalf of Her., that what was taken from him may be restored. 534

DLIII.—To the same.—On behalf of the dean and canons of the Church of Soissons. 535

DLIV.—To the same.—On behalf of R., precentor of Soissons. 535

DLV.—To the same.—On behalf of Ralph of Cuphies, against Josbert of Mont and against Peter of Nantolium. 536

DLVI.—To the abbess and sisters of Bruburg.—How he imposes silence upon Manasses, priest, concerning their chaplaincy. 537

DLVII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he should compel the Premonstratensians to restore A. of Vilers to his land. 537

DLVIII.—To the same.—On behalf of a canon of Laon. 537

DLIX.—He decrees that those admitted as canons in the Church of Chartres who are not residentiaries shall receive only forty solidi each year. 538

DLX.—He permits the canons of Split to restore to his former position a certain canon who was deprived of his own church because, owing to a headache, he had once not read in church. 538

DLXI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the clerics of the Church of Brague. 538

DLXII.—To the Abbot of Saint Remigius of Rheims.—On behalf of Walando, a cleric. 539

DLXIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the Abbess of Bruburg. 539

DLXIV.—To the same.—That he should compel the dean of Saint Lawrence of Roset to reside there. 540

DLXV.—To Peter, abbot, and the monks of Vallis Laurea. 540

DLXVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Galterus, a cleric. 541

DLXVII.—To the same.—On behalf of G., a cleric, and Hugh, a burgess, and his wife M. 541

DLXVIII.—To the same.—Concerning the case of G., canon of Siclini, and Walter. 542

DLXIX.—He orders the Bishops of Amiens and Meaux to examine and settle the dispute concerning the chancellorship of Noyon between Henry, son of Count Robert, and Bald. 542

DLXX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Garinus of Blanciis, whose wife was killed. 543

DLXXI.—To the chapter of Holy Trinity, Canterbury.—That they should accept as prior the person whom Archbishop Thomas has set over them. 543

DLXXII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he should compel the canons of Arras to restore the head of Saint James. 544

DLXXIII.—He orders O., Abbot of Ourscamp, and F., Dean of Rheims, not to separate Alermus of Beauvais from his wife unless his brother B. is separated from his own wife. 544

DLXXIV.—To Chajalis, Count of Pharos.—He commands Count Chajalis and the other nobles of the island of Pharos, under penalty of excommunication, to treat Bishop Martin with due honour. 545

DLXXV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That satisfaction should be made to L., marked with the cross, for the killing of one of his men. 546

DLXXVI.—To the same.—On behalf of Aprilis of Manso. 546

DLXXVII.—To the same.—On behalf of Geoffrey, a cleric of Amiens. 547

DLXXVIII.—To the same.—On behalf of Berengar, a cleric. 547

DLXXIX.—He informs the canons of Pisa that the priests V. and M., who had left “Malincasa” (that is, Benincasa), have been absolved from excommunication, but that communion has not been restored to Villanus. 548

DLXXX.—He writes to Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, concerning the wife of the knight Hugh, who, having been repudiated on false grounds, is to be restored to her husband. 548

DLXXXI.—He orders Robert, Archdeacon of Châlons, and the Abbot of Saint Memmius to hear the case between Herbert Medonarius and Milo, a cleric. 549

DLXXXII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the Church of Sylva Major. 550

DLXXXIII.—To Dominic and Heimard.—He confirms the agreement made between them and Theodoric. 551

DLXXXIV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the canons of the Church of Ham. 552

DLXXXV.—To the same.—That he should cause the relics of Saint James, violently taken by the Count of Flanders, to be restored to the monastery of Saint Vedast. 553

DLXXXVI.—To the dean and chapter of Paris.—That they should invest Philip, nephew of the Bishop of Meaux. 553

DLXXXVII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Milo of Thèbes against his adversaries, because the authority of law decrees that a matter already adjudged must stand. 554

DLXXXVIII.—He writes to P[eter], prior, and the entire convent of the Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre at Jerusalem, that Patriarch A[malric] and King A[malric] ought not to be prevented from restoring to the Church of Joppa “cathedral dignity and the other things which it had long since lost through the violence and occupation of the pagans, now that an opportunity has arisen.” Nevertheless, the patriarch has been admonished by him to “find for them a worthy and honourable compensation.” 554

DLXXXIX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Falcon of the village of Aleran. 555

DXC.—To the same.—On behalf of the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem concerning the village of Bechehem. 556

DXCI.—He praises the canons of Pisa for combating schism. 556

DXCII.—He confirms for Ugo, Archbishop of Genoa, the monastery on the island of Gallinaria. 557

DXCIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That a cemetery should be granted to the sick people of Dampetra. 558

DXCIV.—He ratifies the sentence of interdict pronounced by Leonatus, Abbot of Pissare, against clerics from the land of Sansonesca, and confirmed by I., Bishop of Segni. 558

DXCV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of a pagan knight. 558

DXCVI.—To the same.—On behalf of the Church of Saint Remigius concerning certain rents. 559

DXCVII.—To the same.—On behalf of the Church of Saint Remigius against Stephen and certain others who violently hold lands of the church. 560

DXCVIII.—To . . . . . .—On behalf of the Prior of Vallis Sancti Petri. 560

DXCIX.—He orders the canons of Pisa, after pronouncing excommunication, to forbid anyone to receive benefices from the intruded and schismatic abbot of the monastery of Sesto. 561

DC.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—Concerning the complaint of Marbelinus and his mother Belot. 562

DCI.—He orders the Bishop of Furcone and the canons of Penne, Valva, and Chieti to observe, and to make Richard, brother of Leonatus, observe, the sentence of excommunication or interdict pronounced against certain clerics by Leonatus, Abbot of Pissare. 562

DCII.—He praises the parishioners of Saint Saviour at Venice because they have paid tithes, and urges them to persevere in that payment. 562

## In the year 1169

DCIII.—He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Saint Saviour and the sentence pronounced in its favour by apostolic delegates. 563

DCIV.—He takes the monastery of Cava under the protection of Saint Peter and the Apostolic See and confirms the privileges of preceding popes. 565

DCV.—He confirms the property and privileges of the monastery of Saint Nicasius of Rheims. 567

DCVI.—He orders Peter, Abbot of Saint Remigius, and the Dean of Rheims to adjudicate disputes between J., Abbot of Saint Mary of Vertus, and various persons. 568

DCVII.—He confirms the possessions and rights of the monastery of Vallombrosa. 569

DCVIII.—To Henry, King of England.—He states that he has sent Gratian and Vivian to him to request that he should not violate the rights of the Church and should be reconciled with Thomas. 571

DCIX.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—On the same subject. 572

DCX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Dominic and Haimard, companions. 573

DCX *bis*.—Privilege for the Church of Saint Nicholas of Nugarol. 574

DCXI.—He confirms the boundaries of the diocese of Modena and the property of its church. 576

DCXII.—Privilege for the Church of Saint John at Monza. 576

DCXV.—Privilege for the monastery of Cormeli. 580

DCXVI.—Privilege for the Church of Syracuse. 583

DCXVII.—To Henry, King of England.—That he should receive Thomas of Canterbury into favour. 586

DCXVIII.—Privilege for the Church of Saint Mary of Reno. 588

DCIX.—To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.—He rebukes him because, before the return of the envoys of the Apostolic See, he had “burdened certain persons in England with a sentence.” He exhorts him to suspend the sentence. 590

DCXX.—At the request of William, King of Sicily, he permits the bishops, suffragans of the Church of Palermo, to consecrate W[alter], archbishop-elect, in the presence of John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen, bearing the pallium. 591

DCXXI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Nicholas, concerning a prebend at Amiens. 592

DCXXII.—He confirms certain privileges for the abbots of the Cistercian Order. 592

DCXXIV.—He orders the clergy, judges, and all the people of Benevento not to continue the custom by which “merchants, travellers, and pilgrims received as guests by someone in that city, if it happens that they are afflicted there by some illness, are not permitted either to leave the house, to make a testament concerning their property, or, if they die, to choose where they wish to be buried; but their property is divided, partly among the Apostolic Curia, partly among the church, and partly among their hosts.” 595

DCXXV.—He takes the Church of Asti under his protection and confirms the possessions and rights of its canons. 597

DCXXVII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—Likewise on behalf of the Eastern Church. 601

DCLXIII.---To . . .---On behalf of P., a young man. 628  
DCLXIV.---Confirms to the Parisian abbey of Saint-Denis the church of Saint-Medard at Tremblay. 629  
DCLXV.---To . . .---On behalf of the abbot of Saint Mary of Vertus. 629  
DCLXVI.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---Concerning the annual payment due to the Roman Church. 630  
DCLXVII.---To the same and to Hugh, Bishop of Soissons.---For peace between Louis, King of France, and Henry, King of England. 630  
DCLXVIII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of the Count of Soissons, concerning measures of wine. 631  
DCLXIX.---To Girard, Archbishop of Split. 632  
DCLXX.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of Robert, a cleric. 632  
DCLXXI.---To the Archbishop of Split. 633  
DCLXXII.---To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.---That he punish with ecclesiastical severity Owen, prince of Wales, who had not received his letters concerning his cousin, “whom he is said to keep as though she were his wife,” and the archdeacon of Bangor, who had despised his written commands. 633  
DCLXXIII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of Richard, a priest. 634  
DCLXXIV.---Forbids churches and oratories to be built in the parish of the church of Prémontré without the provost’s consent. 634  

ANNO 1170.

DCLXXV.---Privilege for the monastery of Saint Peter at Modena. 635  
DCLXXVI.---To Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen, and Bernard, Bishop of Nevers.---They are to approach King Henry and urge him not only to restore Thomas of Canterbury fully, as he had promised through envoys, but also to “receive him with the kiss of peace.” If the king does not restore Thomas’s seized possessions within forty days, they are to place his lands on this side of the sea under sentence of interdict. They are to excommunicate those who have injured Peter, Archdeacon of Pavia. 637  
DCLXXVII.---To Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen.---That he vigorously carry out his embassy to Henry, King of the English. 639  
DCLXXVIII.---To Bernard, Bishop of Nevers.---Concerning the embassy entrusted to him and to the Archbishop of Rouen by apostolic letters. [Col. 1488] 640  
DCLXXIX.---To Henry, King of the English.---Commends to him, on behalf of Thomas of Canterbury, Rotrou and Bernard, his envoys. 641  
DCLXXX.---To Gilbert, Bishop of London.---Reports that he has ordered the Archbishop of Rouen and the Bishop of Exeter [or Nevers?] to absolve him from the sentence of excommunication pronounced against him by Thomas of Canterbury. 643  
DCLXXXI.---To Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen, and Bernard, Bishop of Nevers.---That they absolve Gilbert, Bishop of London. 644  
DCLXXXII.---To the bishops of Kent.---That they ensure observance of a sentence of interdict, should the envoys Rotrou and Bernard pronounce it “upon all the land of King Henry situated on this side of the sea.” 645  
DCLXXXIII.---To Roger, Archbishop of York, legate of the Apostolic See, Hugh, Bishop of Durham, etc.---On the same subject. 645  
DCLXXXIV.---To Joscius, Archbishop of Tours, and his suffragans.---On the same subject. 646  
DCLXXXV–DCLXXXVIII.---In the same terms to the Archbishop of Bourges and his suffragans, and likewise to other prelates of churches; in the same terms to the Archbishop of Bordeaux, legate of the Apostolic See, and his suffragans; in the same terms to the Archbishop of Auch and his suffragans; and in the same terms to all bishops and other prelates of churches established throughout the province of Rouen. 646  
DCLXXXIX.---To Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen, and Bernard, Bishop of Nevers.---Reports that it has been brought to his attention that King Henry has crossed into England. Orders them to hasten to him within twenty days and to carry out the commands issued in the previous letters. 647  
DCXC.---To the same.---Prescribes to whom they are to restore communion, and to whom deny it, among those excommunicated by Thomas of Canterbury. 648  
DCXCI.---To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.---That he avail himself of the counsel of Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen, William, Archbishop of Sens, legates of the Apostolic See, and Bernard, Bishop of Nevers. 649  
DCXCII.---Privilege for the church of Saint Mary at Viborg. 649  
DCXCIII.---To Waldemar, King of the Danes.---On behalf of the brethren of Calv. 651  
DCXCIV.---To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.---What is to be demanded from King Henry before his son’s coronation. 652  
DCXCV.---To Roger of York, Hugh of Durham, and all the bishops of England.---They are not to presume to crown the king’s son, since that office belongs to Canterbury. 653  
DCXCVI.---To the same.---They are not to presume to infringe the rights of the Church of Canterbury. 653  
DCXCVII.---To . . . .---On behalf of Haideric, whose nephew had been struck by an arrow. 653  
DCXCVIII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of Baldwin, a priest. 654  
DCXCIX.---To the same.---That he cause A., the bearer of the present letters, to have his church, occupied by others, restored to him. 654  
DCC.---To B., dean, and to the chapter of Saint Martin at Tours. 655  
DCCI.---Orders certain persons to judge between Gerard and Ar . . . , who are litigating concerning an inheritance. 655  
DCCII.---To the same.---That he cease from harassing his suffragans, especially Bartholomew, Bishop of Beauvais. 655  
DCCIII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of the brother of Walter, a priest, and on behalf of Walter himself, that he may show them kindness. 656  
DCCIV.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he again excommunicate Arwin, who had been absolved from excommunication by the abbot of Saint-Remigius, unless he restores Roland’s alb within fifteen days. 657  
DCCV.---To the bishops established in the March.---On behalf of the property of the monastery of Saint Clement. 657  
DCCVI.---To the chapter of Soissons.---That they restore to P., cleric of King Louis, the prebend withheld from him for two years. 658  
DCCVII.---To the provost, dean, archdeacon, and entire chapter of Auxerre.---On behalf of Master P. 658  
DCCVIII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of the church of Compiègne. 659  
DCCIX.---To . . . . .---On behalf of Nicholas, citizen of Châlons. 659  
DCCX.---Orders the Bishops of Rheims and Rouen and their [Col. 1489] suffragans to protect the church of Saint Peter of Silincourt from the injuries of its opponents. 660  
DCCXI.---Privilege for the church of Saint Mammes at Langres. 661  
DCCXII.---Privilege for the canons of Pisa. 663  
DCCXIII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he compel John, canon of Laon, and the woman He., litigating concerning an inheritance, to appear before Theobald, Bishop of Amiens. 663  
DCCXIV.---To the same.---On behalf of Stephen, canon of Rheims. 664  
DCCXV.---To the same.---On behalf of the same man. 664  
DCCXVI.---Confirms to John, Bishop of Bologna, and his successors the estates given in emphyteusis by Anastasius IV to Bishop Gerard for one hundred pounds, on condition that the bishops pay two pounds of pure silver annually to the Roman See. 665  
DCCXVII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and his suffragans.---In favour of the church of Vicogne. 665  
DCCXVIII.---To the chapter of Soissons.---On behalf of Peter, a canon. 665  
DCCXIX.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and the Count of Flanders.---On behalf of the church of Vicogne, that it may be relieved from usury. 666  
DCCXX.---To the people of Nonantola.---That the privilege granted to the Bishop of Modena was not bestowed to their injury. 667  
DCCXXI.---Confirms the judgment pronounced by Odo, legate of the Apostolic See, concerning the church of Saint Benedict, between the monks of Nonantola and Offredus, Bishop of Cremona. 668  
DCCXXII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of Peter, canon of Soissons. 669  
DCCXXIII.---Thanks the canons of Pisa for electing G., his notary, canon of the Church of Pisa. Their controversy with the monks of San Savino has been entrusted to the archbishop’s arbitration. 669  
DCCXXIV.---Forbids the whole chapter of abbots of the Premonstratensian Order to permit a palfrey to be given to archdeacons for the installation of an abbot. 670  
DCCXXV.---To Po., dean, and the chapter of Soissons.---On behalf of Peter, a canon. 670  
DCCXXVI.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of Baldwin, chancellor of Noyon. 671  
DCCXXVII.---To the same.---That he absolve certain persons excommunicated by the Bishop of Châlons. 671  
DCCXXVIII.---Privilege for the monastery of Casamari. 671  
DCCXXIX.---To F., dean, and the chapter of Rheims.---Against Jo., chancellor, and Giles, dean, of Villers-Dommange, on behalf of Robert, priest of Sacy. 674  
DCCXXX.---Urges Robert, prior, and the chapter of Saint Victor at Paris to obey Abbot Ervisius. 675  
DCCXXXI.---Confirms the peace established by Hugh, Bishop of Rodez, and his brother Hugh, Count of Rodez. 675  
DCCXXXII.---To Walter, Bishop of Tournai.---On establishing forty canons in the church of Tournai. 677  
DCCXXXIII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of P., a priest, that he may be kindly received by the lord of Rheims. 678  
DCCXXXIV.---To the same.---That he settle the dispute between U. and his brothers Nicholas and the monks of Anchin, and the dispute between the brethren of Saint Foillan and the canons of Saint Vincent. 678  
DCCXXXV.---To the same.---On behalf of the church of Carcamp, that the vicedean of Pincheri cease harassing it. 679  
DCCXXXVI.---To the same.---On behalf of the church of Carcamp. 679  
DCCXXXVII.---On behalf of Her., that he be absolved from the interdict. 680  
DCCXXXVIII.---To F., dean, and the chapter of Rheims.---On behalf of Vivian, a priest, against the Bishop of Châlons: what he did in good faith is not to be turned to his loss or disgrace. 681  
DCCXXXIX.---To the same.---Against Thomas and John, on behalf of Theobald, a cleric. 681  
DCCXL.---Grants remission of sins to those who visit the church of the monastery of Piscary on the feast of the translation of the body of Saint Clement. 682  
DCCXLI.---To a certain bishop.---That Herbert, a citizen of Châlons, be released from the excommunication pronounced after he had appealed. 683  
DCCXLII.---To William, Bishop of Sens, legate of the Apostolic See.---Clears up the accusation that it was by his command that the Bishop of London had been absolved. 683  
DCCXLIII.---Orders the Archbishops of Bourges, Rheims, Tours, and Rouen to ensure the complete abolition of the erroneous teaching that Christ, namely, insofar as he is man, is not something. [Col. 1490] 684  
DCCXLIV.---Renews the order formerly issued at Paris to William, Archbishop of Sens: having summoned his suffragans to Paris, he is to ensure that the proposition of Peter, former Bishop of Paris, “that Christ, insofar as he is man, is not something,” is suppressed; and he is to order the masters to teach that “Christ is, as perfect God, so also perfect man, and true man, consisting of soul and body.” 685  
DCCXLV.---Bull for the hospital of Saint Blaise at Monza. 685  
DCCXLVI.---To the dean and chapter of the Church of Chartres.---That they restore his prebend to Philip, son of Count Robert. 686  
DCCXLVII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he has written, on behalf of his nephew Philip, to the Archbishop of Sens and the chapter of Chartres. 687  
DCCXLVIII.---To the same.---Gives thanks for the ten marks of gold given to him and “assigned at Paris to Eustace, master of the Knights Templar.” Commends the brethren of the Knights Templar. 687  
DCCXLIX.---At the request of Gerard, Archbishop of Split, confirms the rule that the journeys of the archbishops to the emperor at Constantinople and to the King of Hungary are not to impose expense upon the clerics of Split. 688  
DCCL.---Bull for the monastery of Saint Stephen of the Valleys, in Saintonge. 688  
DCCLI.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he not permit the goods of the brethren of the Knights Templar to be violated. 690  
DCCLII.---To the same.---That he declare excommunicated Ralph of Couches, because he broke down a chapel of the Knights Templar. 690  
DCCLIII.---To the same.---On behalf of a certain knight who had been disinterred. 690  
DCCLIV.---To the same.---That Guy, canon of Saint John at Soissons, a repentant apostate, be received by his abbot. 691  
DCCLV.---Entrusts Peter, Abbot of Saint-Remigius, and Fulk, dean of Rheims, with settling the controversy of N., a cleric, and certain laymen. 691  
DCCLVI.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he restrain the exactions of Thomas, burgess of Saint-Remigius. 692  
DCCLVII.---To the same.---Entrusts him with determining the case pending between the abbess of Saint Peter and the Abbot of Saint-Remigius. 692  
DCCLVIII.---To the same.---On behalf of Hubald, burgess, concerning the castle of Saint-Remigius and the breach of peace. 693  
DCCLIX.---Privilege for the church of Saint Andrew at Muciane. 693  
DCCLX.---Appoints Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and P., Abbot of Saint-Lucian, as judges between Adelelm and his wife. 695  
DCCLXI.---Privilege for the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem. 695  
DCCLXII.---To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.---If he seems to have acted too leniently in Thomas’s cause, it was because he believed patience ought to be exercised. He suspends Roger of York from episcopal rank; he anathematizes Jocelin of Salisbury and Gilbert of London, who had attended the coronation of the new king. 699  
DCCLXIII.---To most of the bishops of England.---Because they attended the coronation of the king’s son contrary to the rights of Canterbury, he suspends them from every rank; furthermore, he anathematizes the Bishops of London and Salisbury. 700  
DCCLXIV.---To Roger, Archbishop of York, and Hugh, Bishop of Durham.---On the same subject. 703  
DCCLXV.---To Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen.---That he arrange for his foregoing letters to the Archbishop of York and the bishops of England to be conveyed, and that he inquire more carefully whether Henry, Bishop of Bayeux, and Frogerius, Bishop of Sées, attended the coronation. 705  
DCCLXVI.---To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, and Gilbert, Bishop of London.---That they grant Master W. of Lega the archdeaconry of Deyberia. 706  
DCCLXVII.---To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, and the other bishops of England.---That divine offices not be celebrated in the lands of excommunicated persons. 706  
DCCLXVIII.---To Louis, King of the French.---That he not communicate with excommunicated persons. 707  
DCCLXIX.---To William, Archbishop of Sens, and Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen.---That, under pain of censures, they secure fulfillment of the peace which the King of England promised in words. 708  
DCCLXX.---To Thomas of Canterbury.---Concerning those excommunicated persons who, though absolved by the Archbishop of Rouen and the Bishop of Nevers, have not restored the possessions taken from the Church of Canterbury, and who are to be excommunicated again. 708  
DCCLXXI.---To Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen, and Bernard, Bishop of Nevers.---On the same subject. [Col. 1491] 709  
DCCLXXII.---To Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.---On the coronation of the son of Henry, King of the English. 710  
DCCLXXIII.---To the same.---Concerning censure to be pronounced against the king unless he grants full peace together with restoration of possessions. 711  
DCCLXXIV.---To all prelates throughout the lands on this side of the sea belonging to the King of England.---That they observe the sentence pronounced upon the king’s lands on this side of the sea by William, Archbishop of Sens, and Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen. 711  
DCCLXXV.---Privilege for the church of Saint Mary at Gubbio. 712  
DCCLXXVI.---To Gilbert of London and Jocelin of Salisbury.---Reports that they have been removed from the administration of their offices and anathematized until they make satisfaction to Thomas of Canterbury. 713  
DCCLXXVII.---To Richard of Chester, Walter of Rochester, Godfrey of Saint Asaph, Nicholas of Llandaff, and Hugh, Bishop of Durham.---On the same subject. 713  
DCCLXXVIII.---To Henry, King of the English.---Congratulates him for restoring his favour and affection to Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury. Urges him to restore what was taken from the archbishop, etc. 715  
DCCLXXIX.---To the clergy and people in the realm of the King of England.---That they not disturb the concord and peace concluded between King Henry and Thomas. 716  

ANNO 1162–1171.

DCCLXXX.---Grants Stephen, Bishop of Meaux, authority, if the chapter is divided among itself, to hear the case himself. 716  

ANNO 1171.

DCCLXXXI.---Commands Lando, the elect, the archpriest, and the canons of the church of Lucca not to inflict injuries upon the brethren of Saint Frigidianus. 716  
DCCLXXXII.---Privilege for the church of Saint Mary at Seckau. 717  
DCCLXXXIII.---Orders all estates and privileges of the monastery of Admont, which he enumerates individually, to remain secure. 718  
DCCLXXXIV.---Privilege for the church of Saint Peter at Treviso. 722  
DCCLXXXV.---There survives for the nuns of Blasiliensis (diocese of Saint-Flour) a bull of Pope Alexander III, in which he refers to privileges granted them by the supreme pontiffs Sergius and Calixtus; and he enumerates the monastery’s principal possessions: the village in which the monastery is situated with all its appurtenances, the churches of Saint Saturninus and Saint Stephen with everything pertaining to them, and, in addition, the tithe of their newly cleared lands. Given at Tusculum through the hand of Gratian, subdeacon and notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1170, in the eleventh year of the pontificate of Pope Alexander III. 723  
DCCLXXXVI.---To Peter, Abbot of Saint-Remigius, and Fulk, dean of Rheims.---That they decide the case of two abbots. 723  
DCCLXXXVII.---Raises the church of Cefalù to an episcopal see and confirms its property and rights. 723  
DCCLXXXVIII.---To Stephen, Archbishop of Bourges, and Bernard, Bishop of Nevers.---That they absolve the Bishops of London and Salisbury, excommunicated by Thomas. 725  
DCCLXXXIX.---To Jocelin, Bishop of Salisbury.---Grants him exemption from the trouble of coming to him. 726  
DCCXC.---To Joscius, Archbishop of Tours, and his suffragans.---Confirms the sentence of interdict pronounced upon the lands of the King of England on this side of the sea because of violence done to Saint Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury. 727  
DCCXCI.---Bull for Mainard, Abbot of Acquasparta. 727  
DCCXCII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he report what was done at the meeting held between Emperor Frederick and his brother Louis. 729  
DCCXCIII.---To the suffragans of the Church of Tarragona.---Mourns the murder of Hugh, Archbishop of Tarragona, and admonishes and urges them to elect another as soon as possible. 730  
DCCXCIV.---To Herbert of Bosham, in exile after the martyrdom of his lord Saint Thomas.---A letter of consolation. 730  
DCCXCV.---To the archdeacon, dean, and other clerics of Nottinghamshire.---That they preserve the rights of the church of Saint Mary of Southwell. [Col. 1492] 731  
DCCXCVI.---Grants the church of Southwell various immunities and privileges, and confirms its property and possessions. 732  
DCCXCVII.---Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Morimond. 734  
DCCXCVIII.---To [Rotrou], Archbishop of Rouen, and [Theobald], Bishop of Amiens.---That they restore Roger of York fully if he clears himself on oath of the accusations made against him. 735  
DCCXCIX.---To the same.---He does not wish the Archbishop of York, although he has requested that a different course ought to be taken, to demonstrate his innocence in any other way than by being permitted, if he does so, to exercise his office in the regions on this side of the sea. 737  
DCCC.---To Henry, King of the English.---Commends Master D., English by birth. 737  
DCCCI.---To the same.---Commends R., Archdeacon of Salisbury, Richard Bar, and Master D.; not only before the arrival of another embassy, but even when they brought news of a new envoy, more welcome than the former, they had served the king’s interest with the utmost zeal. 738  
DCCCII.---Annuls gifts sealed with the seal of the monastery without authorization of the monks of Saint Augustine of Canterbury, and decrees “that their seal shall be kept in such a way that no person, except by the common consent and will of the brethren, or of the sounder part of the convent, may dare to authenticate with the said seal any charter containing a contract of gift or an obligation concerning the possessions of the monastery.” 738  
DCCCIII.---To A., provost of Reichersberg.---Congratulates him because, amid the persecutions of heretics, he has steadfastly adhered to him. 738  

ANNO 1170–1172.

DCCCIV.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That provision be made with some benefice for Walter, a priest, and his brother, who had moved from the diocese of Toul to that of Rheims because of the schismatics. 739  
DCCCV.---To the same.---Against John, a priest, who was harassing the brethren of Mari. 740  
DCCCVI.---To the same.---That he order a certain vineyard to be restored to the brethren of Mari. 740  
DCCCVII.---To the bishops established throughout the kingdom of the Franks.---Concerning the governance of schools. 741  
DCCCVIII.---To Peter, Abbot of Saint-Remigius, and B., Archdeacon of Rheims.---Entrusts them with judging a lawsuit. 742

DCCCXI.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---For correcting abuses in the bishopric of Tournai. 743  
DCCCXII.---To the same.---That he restrain the Bishop of Amiens, who was demanding obedience from the Abbot of Saint-Riquier. 744  
DCCCXIII.---To the same.---Concerning a case between Roger and his mother-in-law Guiard. 744

DCCCXV.---To Peter, Abbot of Saint-Remigius, and Fulk, dean of Rheims.---Concerning scholars of Rheims and a priest unjustly excommunicated and subjected to other injuries. 746

DCCCXVII.---To the same.---Entrusts them with judging a case. 747  
DCCCXVIII.---To the Abbot of Saint-Remigius at Rheims and the prior of Saint Martin-des-Champs.---Entrusts them with judging the case of two abbots. 748  
DCCCXIX.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he absolve the brothers Rainer and Walter from excommunication incurred for violently laying hands upon a priest. 749  
DCCCXX.---To the same.---That he protect G. Pauper, a cleric, from the harassment of Richard, a canon. 750

DCCCXXII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of G., a deacon, concerning the church of Undecosta. 751  
DCCCXXIII.---To the same.---On behalf of the brethren of the church of Maurimont. 752  
DCCCXXIV.---To the same.---That he restrain certain persons who were demanding tithes of newly cleared lands from the sick persons of Cambrai. [Col. 1493] 752  
DCCCXXV.---To [Henry], Bishop of Senlis, and [Peter], Abbot of Saint-Remigius.---That they restore to the brethren of Saint Mary of Brana the tithe taken away by the brethren of Corbie; likewise, that the tithe once sold by the abbot be restored to the same monastery. 753  
DCCCXXVI.---To the same.---That the monks of Saint-Remigius of Brana not trouble the brethren of Saint Mary of Brana. 754  
DCCCXXVII.---To the abbot and brethren of Corbie.---That they restore to the monastery of Brana the tithe they took away. 755  
DCCCXXVIII.---To the Bishops of Amiens and Tournai, and the Abbot of Saint-Remigius.---That they judge the disputes between the Abbot of Brana and a certain knight. 755  
DCCCXXIX.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---On behalf of the monastery of Saint-Medard concerning a case of usury. 756  
DCCCXXX.---To the same.---On behalf of the monastery of Maurimont concerning grain provisions. 757  
DCCCXXXI.---To all the faithful established throughout the kingdom of France.---That they assist the church of Nazareth. 757  
DCCCXXXII.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---Entrusts him with examining and deciding a case. 758  
DCCCXXXIII.---To the same.---That he receive the monastery of Corbie under his protection. 758  
DCCCXXXIV.---To the same.---That he restrain Guy, Archbishop of Châlons, from harassing the widow M. 759  
DCCCXXXV.---To Peter, Abbot of Saint-Remigius.---That he not forbid the men of his monastery to marry wives from another lordship. 759  
DCCCXXXVI.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---Entrusts him with deciding the case between the priests Lambert and Bartholomew. 760  
DCCCXXXVII.---To the dean and chapter of the church of Paris.---On the residence obligation of non-resident canons. 760  
DCCCXXXVIII.---To Peter, Abbot of Saint-Remigius, and Fulk, dean of Rheims.---That an abbot who had received another abbot’s man together with his property be compelled to restore both. 761  
DCCCXXXIX.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he prevent the usurious interest which Bernard the leper was demanding from Gerard of Joecourt. 761  
DCCCXL.---To the same.---That he absolve Albert, who had been excommunicated, and preserve for him the churches of Augey and Cersolium. 762  
DCCCXLI.---To the same.---Against Peter, Bishop-elect of Cambrai, and Drogo, chancellor of Noyon. 763
