DCCCXLIII.---To the Abbot of Ham.---That he recall to his monastery Drogo, his wandering canon. 764  
DCCCXLIV.---To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.---That he compel Odo, a butcher, to pay Richer the seventeen pounds owed to him. 765  
DCCCXLV.---To Peter, Abbot of Saint-Remigius, and Fulk, canon of the church of Rheims.---That they investigate the case of a usurer. 765  
DCCCXLVI.---To Peter, Abbot of Saint-Remigius.---That he investigate the case of certain wards. 766  

ANNO 1171–1172.

DCCCXLVII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he suspend from the priestly office Willard, a priest widely defamed, if the facts are established. 766

DCCCXLVIII.—To the same.—He entrusts to him the settlement of a certain case. 767

DCCCLXIX.—He directs Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, [Guy], Bishop of Châlons, and [Arnulf], Elect of Verdun, to restrain the castellan of Vitry from harassing Caladia. 768

DCCCL.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the monks of Noyon against the canons of Bragny. 769

DCCCLI.—He admonishes C[onrad], Archbishop of Mainz and legate of the Apostolic See, not to reopen the controversy between the monastery of St. Zeno of Verona and the citizens of Ferrara concerning the castle of Ostiglia, which had been adjudicated by Oberto ab Orto. For it is his duty, he says, “to establish peace and concord between the cities of Lombardy and their citizens, especially at this time, and to strive for their unity.” 770

[Col. 1494]

DCCCLII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the Templars of Jerusalem. 771

DCCCLIII.—To William, Archbishop of Sens, Apostolic See legate, S[tephen], Bishop of Meaux, and the Abbot of the Secret Valley.—That they restore the discipline which had collapsed in the monastery of St. Victor. 771

DCCCLIV.—He informs the abbot and canons of St. Victor of Paris of the foregoing letters. 772

DCCCLV.—He informs Louis, King of the French, what commands he has issued concerning the reform of discipline in the monastery of St. Victor of Paris. 773

DCCCLVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—He commends to him the Knights of the Temple. 774

DCCCLVII.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and B., Archdeacon of Rheims.—That they admonish the Bishop of Soissons no longer to refuse to invest with the church of St. Medard the subdeacon presented to him; otherwise, they themselves are to make the investiture. 775

DCCCLVIII.—To the priests and clerics of the parishes belonging to the monastery of St. Peter of the Mountains.—That they not bury their parishioners in their own churches, but that they be buried in the monastery of St. Peter of the Mountains. 775

DCCCLIX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he cause his church to be restored to the priest Araldus. 776

DCCCLX.—To the same.—He commends to him the brethren of the monastery of Vertus. 776

DCCCLXI.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and Fulk, Dean of Rheims.—He entrusts a case to them for judgment. 777

DCCCLXII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—He commends to him F., Archdeacon of Ostrevent. 777

DCCCLXIII.—To the same.—On behalf of Stephen, a cleric, against the canons of Châlons. 778

DCCCLXIV.—To Guy, Abbot of St. Nicasius, and M. Ralph, Canon of Rheims.—That they compel certain persons who had inflicted losses upon the monastery of St. Remigius to make restitution. 778

DCCCLXV.—To Peter, Abbot, and the brethren of St. Remigius.—He ratifies the remission of *frescengiae* granted to their monastery by the Archbishop of Rheims. 779

DCCCLXVI.—To the same.—He entrusts to him for settlement the case between the abbots of St. Urban and of Dervent. 780

DCCCLXVII.—To the same.—He entrusts to him for settlement the case between the canons of St. Nicholas of Châlons and the Abbot of Dervent. 780

DCCCLXVIII.—He entrusts the Bishops of Bourges and Amiens with the matrimonial case of S. and R. of Guise. 781

DCCCLXIX.—To Galdinus, Archbishop of Milan.—On behalf of Oberto, a subdeacon. 782

DCCCLXX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he gave no letters against him to the Abbot of Cheminon. 782

DCCCLXXI.—To the same.—In favor of Leo, elected Abbot of St. Ghislain, whom the schismatics had expelled. 783

DCCCLXXII.—To the same.—That he prevent the marriage between the daughter of King Louis and the son of Emperor Frederick. 783

DCCCLXXIII.—He commands the Bishop of Tournai to restore to Daniel, a priest, what had been taken from him. 784

DCCCLXXIV.—To the Bishops of Meaux and Amiens.—He entrusts to them the examination of the matrimonial case between Count Robert and the daughter of Hugh de Broyes. 784

DCCCLXXV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he receive humanely the Bishop of Beauvais, whom he had ordered to render him every due obedience, once he has made satisfaction. 785

DCCCLXXVI.—He directs Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and P., Abbot of St. Remigius, to have Richard, a cleric, restored to his prebend in the church of St. Pharaïldis. 786

DCCCLXXVIII.—To the same and Walter, Bishop of Tournai.—That they abolish an evil custom in the parish of Dudassel. 787

DCCCLXXIX.—He entrusts Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and G., Bishop of Laon, with the settlement of the dispute concerning certain offerings between the canons of Bruges and R., priest of Dudassel. 788

DCCCLXXX.—He entrusts the Archbishop of Rheims with the settlement of a case between a man and a woman. 789

DCCCLXXXI.—To the same.—That he cause what had been taken from the priests P. and T. by Count Rainald and Henry de Grand-Pré to be restored. 790

DCCCLXXXII.—To the same.—That he exhort the Bishop of Soissons, content with the bishopric alone, to relinquish the chancellorship. 790

[Col. 1495]

DCCCLXXXIII.—To the same.—Concerning the case between Jac., a priest, and the Abbot of St. Saviour of Vertus. 791

DCCCLXXXIV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and G., Bishop of Laon.—Concerning the case between the canons of Bruges and R., a priest. 791

DCCCLXXXV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he declare Roger Tokellus and Guy, who had laid violent hands upon clerics, to be excommunicated. 792

DCCCLXXXVI.—To the Bishop of Châlons.—That he cause the son of a priest, who had been ignorantly ordained a priest, to enjoy his church. 792

DCCCLXXXVII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—He deprives the Bishop of Senlis, who had divided a prebend, of the power of conferring prebends. 793

DCCCLXXXVIII.—To the same.—Concerning the absolution of Master Gerard from excommunication. 794

DCCCLXXXIX.—To the same.—He writes in favor of D., a deacon, to whom the brethren of St. Eugenius had given the church of Masdey. 795

DCCCXC.—To the Abbots of St. Remigius and St. Dionysius of Rheims.—He entrusts a case to them for judgment. 795

DCCCXCI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he suspend from his office the Bishop of Châlons, who had demanded money for absolving an excommunicated woman. 796

DCCCXCII.—To the same.—That he declare excommunicated two canons of his church who had laid violent hands upon a deacon. 796

DCCCXCIII.—To the same.—That the canons of Laon make satisfaction to the nuns of St. Peter of Rheims for the injuries inflicted. 797

DCCCXIV.—To the same.—He entrusts to him the case of Elisendis, a widow. 797

DCCCXCV.—To the same.—That he defend the men of St. Remigius from the harassments of the canons of Soissons. 798

DCCCXCVI.—To the Archbishop of Tours and the Bishop of Autun.—That they examine the sentence of excommunication pronounced by the Archbishop of Rheims against Count Henry. 798

DCCCXCVII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he not burden the Bishop of Beauvais and his other suffragans, and that he settle his disputes with Count Henry. 800

DCCCXCVIII.—To the same.—He replies to various matters concerning which he had consulted him. 802

DCCCXCIX.—To the illustrious King of the French.—That he settle the dispute between the Archbishop of Rheims and Count Henry. 803

CM.—To Bartholomew, Bishop of Beauvais.—That he has not granted him letters exempting him from the jurisdiction of the Archbishop of Rheims, and that he render that archbishop due obedience. 804

CMI.—To William, Archbishop of Sens.—That he grant the archdeaconry in his church to the nephew of the Archbishop of Rheims. 804

CMII.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and Fulk, Dean of Rheims.—That they take cognizance of the case of certain persons who had appealed from the Bishop of Amiens, appointed judge by the pope. 805

CMIII.—To the same.—He entrusts to them the judgment of the case of two women. 805

CMIV.—He reproves the Bishop of Arras because he had not yet granted R., a cleric, a prebend in his church. 806

CMV.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius.—That one who had seized the land of a man gone to Jerusalem be compelled to restore it. 807

CMVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of the Abbot of St. John of the Vines against R., a priest who had seized the church of Bonnis. 807

CMVII.—To the same.—Against Aalis, a female usurer. 807

CMVIII.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and Fulk, Dean of Rheims.—That they be judges in the case of the Abbot of Dervent and the clerics of St. Nicholas of Châlons. 808

CMIX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—He commends to him D. and G., who had left the diocese of Toul because of the schismatics. 809

CMX.—To the same.—Concerning the Elect of Cambrai, who had ordered the Abbot of Mareuil to be thrown from a horse. 809

CMXI.—He confirms certain statutes of the church of Chartres, written by William, legate of the Apostolic See. 810

CMXII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—In favor of G., a poor priest who, while ill and not in possession of his senses, had been clothed in the monastic habit. 811

[Col. 1496]

CMXIII.—To the same.—That he cause the vicarage of Suast to be restored to B., a priest. 812

CMXIV.—To the same.—That he compel Robert de Bove to restore what he had taken from A., a canon of St. Peter of Laon. 812

CMXV.—To the same.—That he restrain the harassment inflicted by Hugh of Junceriac upon the land of St. Medard. 813

CMXVI.—To the same.—That he settle the case between the Abbot of St. Medard and the Abbot of St. John of the Vines concerning the tithes of Espiers. 813

CMXVII.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and Fulk, Dean of Rheims.—Concerning money left by testament to churches and the poor. 814

CMXIX.—To the same.—That Adam de Corbie return his money to John, a cleric. 815

CMXX.—To the same.—On behalf of Mary, a citizen of Châlons. 815

CMXXI.—To the same.—Concerning the case between the canons of St. Peter of Laon and the canons of the cathedral church. 816

CMXXII.—To the same.—That the clerics of the Holy Trinity may have a cemetery. 816

CMXXIII.—To the canons of the church of Laon.—That he entrusted only those matters in their church requiring correction to be corrected by their dean. 817

CMXXIV.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and B., Archdeacon of Rheims.—That money owed to a cleric be restored. 817

CMXXV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—In favor of B., a regular canon, to whom two altars at Troisly had been granted for life. 818

CMXXVI.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and Fulk, Dean of Rheims.—That they hear the case between the Abbot of All Saints and the canons of the Holy Trinity. 819

CMXXIX.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and Fulk, Dean of Rheims.—He entrusts a case to them for judgment. 821

CDXXX.—To the same.—He entrusts a case to them for judgment. 821

CMXXXI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—He entrusts for examination the case of Hilary, a priest, whom he had absolved from the censures of the Bishop of Amiens. 822

CMXXXII.—To the same.—That his church be restored to Wiband, a cleric. 822

CMXXXIV.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius.—That he grant a prebend to a certain Hubert. 824

CMXXXV.—To the Bishop of Senlis and the Abbot of St. Medard.—That losses inflicted upon the monastery of St. Remigius be repaired. 824

CMXXXVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—Against the nuns of Malbod, who had rebelled against their abbess. 825

CMXXXVII.—To Peter, Abbot of St. Remigius, and Fulk, Dean of Rheims.—That they take cognizance of the case of a certain William, who complained that he was oppressed by usury. 826

CMXXXIX.—To the same.—On behalf of Jordan, a citizen of Laon. 827

CMXL.—To the Abbots of St. Remigius and St. Nicasius.—He entrusts a case to them for judgment. 827

CMXLI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he may promote to sacred orders, after penance, Robert, a cleric who had unwillingly been present at a homicide. 828

CMXLV.—To the same.—On behalf of the sick people of Épernay. 830

[Col. 1497]

CMLV.—To the same.—On behalf of the church of St. John of the Vines at Cervenniac. 837

CMLVIII.—On behalf of Sebert, a citizen of Rheims, concerning a certain house. 839

CMLIX.—To the same.—On behalf of John Multon. 839

CMLXI.—To the same.—That he protect T., a cleric, from the burdens imposed by the Bishop of Châlons, and subject A. de Possessa to excommunication. 840

CMLXV.—To the same.—That he persuade the king to have his son crowned. 843

CMLVI.—To the same.—Concerning satisfaction to be made to a canon of St. John of the Borough of Laon for injuries inflicted. 844

CMLXVII.—To [lacuna].—He entrusts a case for judgment. 844

CMLXXXVI.—To the same.—Of similar subject matter. 864

CMLXXXVII.—To the same.—Of similar subject matter. 865

CMLXXXIX.—To Leonas, Abbot of Pescara.—He informs him that he has exhorted Berard the Gentile and his brothers, and Roger, son of Riccardus, and his brothers, to repair within fifteen days the losses inflicted upon him; should they fail to do so, he is to excommunicate them. 866

CMXC.—To the people of Nonantola.—Concerning relief from their debt and the reform of discipline in the monastery. 867

CMXCI.—He grants Ubaldo, Bishop of Ostia, and the archpriest and canons of Velletri that wills “which their parishioners have made in their last wishes before their priest and three or two other suitable persons shall remain valid.” 867

## In the Year 1172

CMXCII.—He receives the church of Saragossa into protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 867

CMXCIII.—To Ildefonsus, King of Aragon.—He thanks him for expelling Robert from the kingdom; he exhorts him to exclude all Robert’s descendants from that kingdom and to add their goods to the royal treasury. 870

CMXCIV.—Privilege for the church of Tarentaise. 870

CMXCV.—To [Rotrou], Archbishop of Rouen, and [Theobald], Bishop of Amiens.—That they restore the fullness of his office to Gilbert, Bishop of London, if, with six compurgators, he swears that neither by writing, word, nor deed did he knowingly incite the king to the death of St. Thomas. 872

CMXCVI.—To Galdinus, Archbishop of Milan.—Concerning the election of a primicerius. 874

CMXCVII.—To the canons of St. Victor.—He confirms the resignation of Abbot Ervisius and the promotion of Guarin. 876

M.—He confirms all the rights and goods of the monastery of St. Mary of Tremiti. 880

MI.—He confirms the agreement made between Dominic, Abbot of Monte Cassino, and John, Bishop of Fondi. 882

## In the Years 1170–1173

MX.—To Theobald and the clerics of the church of St. Anastasia [otherwise, St. Lucy] of Verona, he informs them that the sentence pronounced against him by Hildebrand of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles and Raymond, Bishop of Brescia, “according to the custom of the city of Verona,” has been annulled by himself. 891

## In the Years 1171–1173

MXI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That Agatha be restored to R. de Adversa, her husband. 891

MXII.—To the same.—On behalf of the Abbot of Maroilles against C., a knight of Taisnières. 892

## In the Year 1173

MXV.—To the same.—Against the dean of St. Quentin and his subjects, who demanded money for blessing marriages. 896

MXVIII.—On behalf of the monastery of St. Saviour and St. Rotrudis of Andres. 898

MXX.—To the same.—Concerning the case between the canons of St. Martin and of Blessed Mary at Laon. 899

MXL.—Privilege for the church of Chartres. 915

## In the Years 1160–1174
