MLX.—To the same.—That the lepers of Épernay be exempt from tithes on newly cultivated lands, etc. 936

MLXI.—He commends to him Milo, an apostolic messenger. 937

MLXII.—To the same.—That he excommunicate An. de Loos, who had put R., a subdeacon, in chains. 937

MLXIII.—To the same.—That the parish of Nizy be restored to A., a priest. 938

MLXIV.—To the same.—On behalf of Evrard, a priest. 938

MLXV.—To the same.—He writes that he has given Count Philip of Flanders no privilege contrary to the rights of the church of Rheims. 938

MLXVI.—To the same.—He entrusts to him for examination the case between the Abbot of Humblari and F. de Noyelles. 939

MLXVII.—To the same.—On behalf of certain merchants of Flanders against the Abbot of Dervent. 939

MLXVIII.—To the same.—Against the canons of Compiègne, who were troublesome to the monks. 940

MLXIX.—To the same.—He thanks him for supporting by his protection the brethren of Compiègne, whom he commends to him. 940

MLXX.—To the same.—That he take care that the agreement made between the brethren of Compiègne and Tenoly be observed inviolate. 941

[Col. 1501]

MLXXI.—To the same.—Concerning the case between the canons of St. Lawrence of Beauvais and the Bishop of Beauvais. 941

MLXXII.—To the same.—He entrusts to him for settlement the case of H., a woman of Suune. 942

MLXXIII.—To the same.—On behalf of the monks of La Sauve-Majeure against Wiscard and Ralph de Coudicac. 942

MLXXIV.—He orders Rotrou, Archbishop of Rouen, “grieving over the various outcomes of wars and over the scandal of kings and of the land,” to be of strong spirit. He commands him “to apply himself diligently to the restoration of peace between the kings, and to correct with customary pontifical severity the transgressions of bishops, deans, archdeacons, clerics, and laymen.” He adds other commands. He forbids him “to lend his pallium to another metropolitan if it happens that he comes without a pallium to the church of Rouen on some principal feast: since,” he says, “the pallium does not pass beyond your person, but each person ought to be buried with it.” 943

MLXXV.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims, and all bishops and abbots established throughout the archbishopric of Rheims.—He commends to them the brethren of St. Remigius of Rheims. 946

MLXXVI.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—On behalf of Alagrin, a citizen of Anagni. 946

MLXXVII.—To the same.—That he cause Rainald’s land to be restored to him. 947

MLXXVIII.—To the same.—Against the canons of Compiègne, who had installed a chaplain in the church of St. Clement against the abbot’s will. 947

MLXXIX.—To the same.—That he ensure that the church of St. Medard of Barleux be given to W., a priest. 948

MLXXX.—To the same.—On behalf of G., a poor cleric, against R. de Thory, a canon of Beauvais. 948

MLXXXI.—To the same.—On behalf of the lepers of Tours-sur-Marne against the monks of that place and the priest Evirvinus. 949

MLXXXII.—He informs the Carthusian brethren that he has received under protection the monastery of Gyrie, founded by Henry, Bishop of Gurk. 949

MLXXXIII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he take care that losses inflicted upon the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem be repaired. 950

MLXXXIV.—To the same.—That he grant some benefice to G., a deacon. 950

MLXXXV.—To the same.—That he restore the church of Vieille-Senior to J., a priest. 951

MLXXXVI.—To William, Archbishop of Tarragona, and his suffragans.—That they admonish the King of Aragon not to permit Robert, who had conspired in the murder of Hugh, Archbishop of Tarragona, to reside in his kingdom. 952

MLXXXVII.—To Ildefonsus, King of Aragon.—Concerning the same matter. 952

MLXXXVIII.—To Fulk, dean, and the canons of the church of Rheims.—He exhorts them to resume the common life which they had abandoned. 953

MLXXXIX.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he recall his canons to the common life and cause the customary alms to be given. 954

MXC.—To the same.—On behalf of the monastery of St. Medard against the canons of St. Gervasius. 955

MXCI.—To the same.—Against the Count of Rétel, who was harassing the brethren of Juneriac. 936

MXCII.—To the same.—That he cause pledged land to be restored to Phy. de Pierrefonds. 956

MXCIII.—To the same.—That he declare excommunicated Ernald, who had laid violent hands upon B., a canon of Laon. 957

MXCIV.—To the same.—On behalf of John, a cleric, and Ralph his brother, against Lambert, their brother. 957

MXCV.—To the same.—On behalf of John, a cleric, and Radulf his brother, whom the Bishop of Châlons had unjustly excommunicated. 958

MXCVI.—To the same.—Concerning the dispute between the people of Lessines and of Malbod over the church of the village of Anor. 958

MXCVII.—To the same.—On behalf of G., a canon of Laon. 959

MXCVIII.—To the same.—On behalf of the brethren of St. Nicasius against the monks of Elanty. 960

MXCIX.—To the same.—Concerning the case between the viscount of Pinconio and the Abbot of Anchin. 960

MC.—To the same.—That he cause a cemetery to be blessed for the sick people of Mellent. 961

MCI.—He receives into protection the house of sick brethren dwelling near the city of Rheims and confirms “the fairs which Archbishop Henry granted to be held annually near that house.” 961

[Col. 1502]

MCII.—To Henry, Archbishop of Rheims.—That he strive to make peace between Louis, King of the French, and Henry, King of England. 962

MCIII.—To the same.—He entrusts to him a certain case for settlement. 963

MCIV.—To the same.—That with all his strength he strive to prevent the marriage between the son of the King of France and the daughter of Emperor Frederick. 964

MCV.—To the same.—That G., Bishop of Châlons, admit Horricus to the church of St. Julian of Helissia. 964

MCVI.—To the same.—On behalf of H., treasurer of Auxerre. 965

MCVII.—To the priests and clerics established throughout England and in the lands beyond the sea of the King of England.—That the King of England restore their wives to his sons. 965

## In the Year 1174
MCVIII.—To Gerard, abbot, and the whole convent of Clairvaux.—He announces that Abbot Bernard has been enrolled among the saints. 966  
MCIX.—To all abbots of the Cistercian order.—On the same subject. 967  
MCX.—To the archbishops, abbots, and other prelates of the Church established in the realm of the Franks.—Of similar purport. 967  
MCXI.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—On the same subject. 967  
MCXII.—To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—On behalf of the monastery of Cluny. 967  
MCXIII.—To the same.—That the schools of Regitest [reading uncertain] be preserved for the monks of St. Remigius. 967  
MCXIV.—To the same.—On behalf of the abbot of St. Remigius against men subject to him. 968  
MCXV.—To the same.—Against several persons who were harassing the monastery of St. Remigius. 968  
MCXVI.—He takes under protection the church of St. Mary of Mont-desiderius, of the Cluniac order, and confirms all its goods and rights. 969  
MCXVII.—He confirms all the goods of the monastery of St. Mary of Lisch. 971  
MCXVIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—That, if the count receives Countess C. of Toulouse honourably, he should persuade her to return to the husband whom she had left. 972  
MCXIX.—To the same.—He declares that F., his parishioner, never disparaged him in the curia. 973  
MCXX.—A bull concerning the church of St. Peter at Auxerre, recently designated by the name of an abbey. 973  
MCXXI.—To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—That satisfaction be made to the monastery of Gorze for injuries inflicted by G. of Aspermont. 974  
MCXXII.—A privilege for the church of Capua. 974  
MCXXIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—He commends to him the brethren of the monastery of Morimond. 976  
MCXXIV.—To the same.—On behalf of the abbot of Morimond against the harassments of several nobles. 977  
MCXXV.—To the same.—Against several persons who were harassing the monastery of St. Remigius. 977  
MXXVI.—To the same.—He exhorts him to gentleness toward A., a citizen of Laon. 978  
MCXXVII.—To the same.—Concerning the assignment of a priest to the lepers of Épernay. 978  
MCXXVIII.—To Henry, archbishop of Reims, and Desiderius, bishop of Thérouanne.—That tithes not be exacted from Cistercians on lands which they cultivate by their own labour.  
MCXXIX.—To the same.—On behalf of the brethren of St. Martin of Laon. 980  
MCXXX.—To Guigo, count of Forez.—He recites the settlement and exchange of rights made between him and the church of Lyons, and confirms it by his authority. 980  
MCXXXI.—He takes the monastery of St. Mary of Novy under protection, enumerates and confirms its goods. 985  
MCXXXII.—To Lupus, king of Valencia. 985  
MCXXXIII.—To Richard, archbishop of Canterbury.—He asserts for him and his successors the primacy of England. 985  
MCXXXIV.—He informs John, bishop-elect of Chichester, that he has instructed Richard, archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, “not to delay proceeding with his promotion on account of his being said to be a canon’s son.” 986  
MCXXXV.—To all the faithful established throughout France.—He commends Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus. 986  
MCXXXVI.—To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—That he exhort the king to make himself arbiter of peace between the Church and the Empire, and also strive to induce the kings of France and England to concord. 987  

[Col. 1503]

MCXXXVII.—To the suffragans of the church of Canterbury.—Concerning appeals. 987  
MCXXXVIII.—He takes the monastery of St. Andrew under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 988  
MCXXXIX.—He takes the church of St. Mary of Luffeld under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 989  
MCXL.—He takes the church of Stokes under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 990  
MCXLI.—A privilege for the abbey of St. Martin of Chora. 992  
MCXLII.—A privilege for the church of St. Martin of Tours. 994  
MCXLIII.—He writes to Conrad, archbishop of Mainz and legate of the Apostolic See, that the bishop of Gurk, together with Richer—whom he had unlawfully consecrated bishop of Brixen at Regensburg—had transferred the archbishopric of Salzburg, taken from Adalbert, to [Henry], provost of Berchtesgaden. He is to declare this crime void. He commands him to recall both bishops and the provost, together with the clergy and people of Salzburg, to obedience to Adalbert. 994  
MCXLIV.—To Siboto, provost, and the choir of the church of Salzburg.—That they return to obedience to Adalbert. 996  
MCXLV.—To Adalbert, archbishop of Salzburg.—He informs him about the preceding letters. 997  
MCXLVI.—To the dean and chapter of Paris.—He confirms the possessions of the church of Paris; likewise, concerning the prebend of St. Geneviève in the church of Paris. 998  
MCXLVII.—To Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—Concerning payment for the direction of schools. 998  
MCXLVIII.—To the dean and chapter of Paris.—Concerning the stipend of the canons. 999  
MCXLIX.—He confirms the regular discipline, possessions, and privileges of the canons of Pistoia. 999  
MCL.—He takes the monastery of St. Mary of Montreale under protection and confirms all its possessions and privileges. 1000  
MCLI.—To Abbot Marsilius and the brethren of Caro Insula, who “had transferred the monastery from two less suitable places to a very spacious place called Om,” he confirms their title to those same two places. 1004  

## In the year 1161–1175

MCLII.—To the abbots and brethren of the Cistercian order established in England.—He forbids them to seek rights of patronage in churches or churches themselves. 1004  
MCLIII.—On behalf of the prioress of Broburg concerning ten pounds. 1005  
MCLIV.—To the bishop of Beauvais.—On behalf of A., dean of Château-Raoul. 1005  
MCLV.—To G., bishop of Châlons.—On behalf of the cleric Milo, that he may show him favour. 1005  
MCLVI.—To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—Concerning the absolution of a certain citizen of Châlons, Ma. 1006  
MCLVII.—To the same.—That he compel the canons of St. Ursmar and of Antoing to dismiss all concubines. Those below the rank of subdeacon who have wives are to remain with their wives; but those who are in that rank or above are to remain attached to their churches and dismiss their wives. 1006  
MCLVIII.—To the same.—On behalf of Matthew, a citizen of Châlons. 1007  
MCLIX.—To the same.—That he hear and determine the case between M. and A., if this is permitted by the custom of the land; otherwise, that he refer it to the secular judge. 1008  
MCLX.—To the same.—On behalf of the abbot and brethren of Sarnai. 1008  
MCLXI.—To the same.—That at Valenciennes permission be granted to the hospital for the poor to build a church, and that ecclesiastical persons not be judged by secular persons. 1008  
MCLXII.—To the same and the abbot of Jauiac.—On behalf of J., a poor man and priest who had formerly been a novice in the monastery of Jauiac. 1009  
MCLXIII.—To [lacuna].—On behalf of F., a cleric, that his prebend be restored to him. 1010  
MCLXIV.—To the abbot of Corbie.—Concerning the right of the archbishop of Reims in the borough of Corbie adjoining the monastery. 1010  

## In the year 1164–1175

MCLXV.—To the bishop of Châlons.—That his priests not exact money for the baptism of infants or for the burial of the dead. 1011  
MCLXVI.—To Theobald, bishop of Amiens.—On behalf of John Aculeus, against his stepmother: that he hear and determine the case between them. 1011  
MCLXVII.—To Henry, archbishop of Reims.—On behalf of Theobald against Guy of Appy. 1012  

## In the year 1175

MCLXVIII.—He confirms for the convent of St. Mary at Palermo certain tithes granted by Tustin, bishop of Mazara. 1013  
MCLXIX.—He takes the monastery of Vallis Christiana under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1013  
MCLXX.—To Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—That those who killed the bishop-elect of Cambrai be publicly declared excommunicated. 1014  
MCLXXI.—He confirms the privileges and rights of the monastery of St. Stephen of Bagnoles. 1015  
MCLXXII.—To Conrad, archbishop of Mainz.—On behalf of the convent of Lunelec. 1016  
MCLXXIII.—To R[ichard], archbishop of Canterbury.—He commands that, under pain of excommunication, the Hospitallers and Templars be admonished that, if they have buried in church cemeteries any persons who died under excommunication, they must remove them. 1017  
MCLXXIV.—To W., bishop-elect of Lucca.—That a certain church usurped by him be restored to the canons of Lucca. 1017  
MCLXXV.—He commands R., provost, and all the monks of St. George to relinquish the church of St. Matthew of Fossa Natalis within forty days. He gives notice of the preceding letter to the bishop-elect of Lucca. 1018  
MCLXXVI.—He takes the abbey of Majella under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1019  
MCLXXVII.—To the bishops of Penne and Valva.—That they declare excommunicated the clerics of Castiglione. 1021  
MCLXXVIII.—To the archbishops of Lyons and Bourges.—That they recognize Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus, as legate. 1022  
MCLXXIX.—He takes Otto, provost of Raitenbuch, under protection. He commands him to receive into the unity of the Church clerics in the German kingdom who renounce the schism. 1022  
MCLXXX.—He confirms the bishopric of Ciudad [Civitas], established by Ferdinand, king of Spain. He pardons Bishop Peter for having received consecration from the archbishop of Compostela without authority from the Apostolic See. 1023  
MCLXXXI.—To the archbishop of Vienne and the bishop of Clermont.—That, under pain of excommunication, they compel Guigo, count of Forez, to observe the settlement confirmed by the pope between him and the church of Lyons. 1023  
MCLXXXII.—He commands archbishops and bishops that “they compel all who are bound to give vows or other revenues to the church of Compostela to pay the vows and revenues.” 1024  
MCLXXXIII.—To the master of the militia of St. James in Spain and his brethren.—He approves their institution. 1024  
MCLXXXIV.—He takes the monastery of Wariville under protection and confirms its goods. 1030  
MCLXXXV.—He confirms for the alms-house of St. Gervasius at Paris a gift situated beside the court of St. Gervasius, and an annual rent of four denarii. 1031  
MCLXXXVI.—To Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—That the abbot of Quintiac restore to the prior of Lanariac the tithes which he had taken from him. 1032  
MCLXXXVII.—He confirms the privileges granted to the canons of the church of Blessed Mary at Brixen. 1032  
MCLXXXVIII.—To Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—That he cease holding the church of Meaux. 1033  
MCLXXXIX.—To Onuphrius, abbot of St. Saviour of Messina, of the order of St. Basil.—He approves his institution. 1033  
MCXC.—He confirms the goods of the church of St. Mary of Cagia at Meaux. 1035  
MCXCI.—To the archbishop of Lyons, S. A. L., and suffragans, etc.—He commends Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus, his legate. 1036  
MCXCII.—He takes the monastery of St. Mary of Novy under protection and confirms its goods and immunities. 1036  

## About the year 1175

MCXCIII.—To Robert, bishop of Exeter, and Roger, bishop of Worcester.—That they remove Clarembald, abbot of St. Augustine’s, Canterbury. 1037  
MCXCIV.—To Roger, archbishop of York.—That, in accordance with the privilege formerly granted him, he carry the cross before himself throughout all England. 1038  
MCXCV.—He takes the monastery of St. Thomas of the Paraclete (of Ebleholt) under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1039  

## In the year 1160–1176

MCXCVI.—To the archbishop of Narbonne and the bishop of Elne.—He confirms, by authority of the Apostolic See, the sentence of interdict pronounced against the abbot of Canigou. 1041  
MCXCVII.—A privilege for the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu. 1041  
MCXCVIII.—To the rulers of Lombardy.—That they dissuade the citizens of Modena from harassing the monastery of Nonantola, and release twenty of the forty hostages taken from the monastery. 1042  
MCXCIX.—To all bishops of the province of Rouen.—That they not absolve those whom the chapter of the church of Rouen has bound. 1042  
MCC.—To the bishop of Soissons.—That A., who had left the monastery after a journey to Jerusalem, be received back into it. 1043  
MCCI.—A privilege for the church of St. Mary of Corbeil. 1043  
MCCII.—To the dean and chapter of Blessed Martin of Tours.—Concerning the bestowal, within a specified term, of modiationes [allowances measured in modii] upon one who brings more. 1044  
MCCIII.—He confirms an exchange made by the canons of St. Anianus at Orléans with Adela, queen of the Franks. 1044  
MCCIV.—He forbids laymen to interfere in the elections of Camaldolese abbots or priors. 1045  
MCCV.—He grants to the canons of St. Quentin that the bishop of Noyon may not dare to bring more than thirty mounted attendants to their church. 1046  
MCCVI.—He confirms a certain statute made by the chapter of St. Quentin. 1047  
MCCVII.—He commands all bishops not to introduce secular clerics into places where Premonstratensian brethren or sisters reside. 1048  
MCCVIII.—To the archbishop of Tarragona, legate of the Apostolic See.—He decrees that the churches of Tortosa and Lleida, recently freed from Moorish servitude, be subject to Tarragona as their metropolitan. 1048  
MCCIX.—To V., prior, and the canons of the church of St. Frigidianus at Lucca. 1048  
MCCX.—To the prior and brethren of the monastery of St. Sabinus.—That they be obedient to their abbot and resign to him their private property. 1049  
MCCXI.—To the bishop of Vic and his chapter.—He admonishes them to restore to the monastery of Ripoll the church of Granoylers, which they were holding unjustly. 1049  
MCCXII.—To the dean, treasurer, and chapter of the church of Blessed Martin of Tours.—He grants that they may lawfully recover churches held in fief from them and possessions pertaining to their own property. 1050  
MCCXIII.—To the clerics and laypeople of Bagnacavallo.—That they return to obedience to the canons of Faenza. 1050  
MCCXIV.—To the bishop of Vic.—He orders that the church of St. Stephen, violently occupied and retained, be restored to the monks of Ripoll within forty days. 1051  
MCCXV.—To the bishops of Huesca and Barcelona.—He orders them to admonish and induce the bishop of Vic to restore the church of St. Stephen, which he had violently occupied. 1051  
MCCXVI.—To the clergy of Pisa.—That they induce the people to pay the canons their tithes. 1052  
MCCXVII.—He grants to the abbot and brethren of the Premonstratensian order “that they may impose penance upon servants living from their table and administer the Lord’s body to them at stated times.” 1052  
MCCXVIII.—He confirms for the monastery of St. Germanus of the Meadows at Paris the chapel of St. John. 1052  
MCCXIX.—He writes as follows to the archbishop of Milan: “The nobleman P. has informed us that, when Frederick, called emperor, was formerly returning from Rome, he denied him the castle of Ferruca, otherwise Verruca; whence it happened that, after four castles had been destroyed, more than two thousand houses were destroyed and many people killed.” He commands that penance be imposed upon him. 1053  
MCCXX.—He commands Henry, patriarch of Grado, and Theodinus, cardinal-priest of St. Vitalis, to judge between C. and Leonard, bishops-elect of Torcello. 1053  

## In the year 1166–1176

MCCXXI.—To Hildebrand, cardinal-priest of the Twelve Apostles and legate of the Apostolic See, he replies that “he should cause the bishop-elect who has recently returned to the unity of the Church after abjuring the schism to be consecrated by the Catholic suffragan bishops of the church of Aquileia.” 1053  

[Col. 1506]

## In the year 1173–1176

MCCXXII.—To Simon, abbot of St. Albans.—He answers his questions. 1053  
MCCXXIII.—To Theobald, bishop of Piacenza.—That he restore to the monks of St. Sabinus the tithe of the enclosure situated beside St. Ambrose. 1054  
MCCXXIV.—He commands the archbishop of Vienne and his suffragans to restrain those harassing the Carthusians in their boundaries or pastures, and to prevent any other religious from building near them. 1055  
MCCXXV.—To Peter, archbishop of Salona.—He praises his faith and consoles him amid his afflictions. He denies that he will decree anything concerning the church of Zadar to his injury. 1056  
MCCXXVI.—To the bishop and consuls of Bologna.—That they desist from injuries against the church of Nonantola. 1057  
MCCXXVII.—He confirms the peace concluded between Hugh, bishop of Terracina, and Peter de Roberto. 1058  
MCCXXVII *bis*.—To the chapter of St. Peter at Weßobrunn.—That they not receive again the expelled schismatic abbot. 1059  
MCCXXVII *ter*.—To the same.—That they receive the brothers Henry and Charles. 1059  

## In the year 1174–1176

MCCXXVIII.—At the request of Abbot Rudolph and the monks of Cluny, he forbids the treasury, honours, obediences, and possessions of the church of Cluny to be alienated by abbots against the will of the chapter. 1060  
MCCXXIX.—He confirms for Rudolph and the brethren of Cluny the church of St. John built by them. 1060  
MCCXXX.—He confirms the goods of the convent of Gudhem, granted by King Canute and his brother. 1060  

## In the year 1175–1176

MCCXXXI.—To Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—He complains of the bishop of Paris, because he conferred an archdeaconry contrary to the pope’s command and to an appeal which had been made. 1061  

## In the year 1176

MCCXXXII.—He takes the convent of St. Justina at Lucca under protection and confirms its discipline, possessions, and rights. 1062  
MCCXXXIII.—To Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—That he exhort the king of the Franks and princes and others to take up the cross. 1063  
MCCXXXIV.—To the clerics of the church of Alessandria.—Concerning a new bishop granted to them or transferred from elsewhere. 1064  
MCCXXXV.—He confirms the settlement made by William, archbishop of Reims and legate of the Apostolic See, between the brethren of St. Peter and the chaplains of the churches of St. John, St. Nicholas, and St. James at Ghent. 1064  
MCCXXXVI.—He confirms the goods and privileges of the Camaldolese monastery. 1064  
MCCXXXVII.—He asserts for Ubaldo, archbishop of Pisa, the primacy of Sardinia. 1066  
MCCXXXVIII.—To the monks of St. George at Lucca.—That they resign the church which they had acquired by money. 1066  
MCCXXXIX.—A privilege for the monastery of Vallombrosa. 1067  
MCCXL.—He confirms the goods, rights, and privileges of the monastery of St. Mary of Florence. 1069  
MCCXLI.—He sends Roger, archbishop of York, a copy of the letters of William, king of Scotland, who, after making peace with the king of England, had asked him that the Scottish Church be subjected to the church of York. 1071  
MCCXLII.—To Peter, priest of St. Chrysogonus, and Hugh, deacon of St. Angelo, cardinals.—That the daughter of the king of the Franks either be married to the son of the king of England or be restored to her father. 1072  
MCCXLIII.—A privilege for the monastery of St. John in Venus. 1073  
MCCXLIV.—He confirms for Gunteram, bishop-elect of Sens, the church at Mont-Bonizi. 1075  
MCCXLV.—A privilege for the monastery of Bois-Audun. 1077  
MCCXLVI.—A privilege for the church of Aquileia. 1077  
MCCXLVII.—He grants the sisters of the convent of St. Mary at Soissons “that, until the number of nuns has been reduced to eighty, they ought to receive no woman as a sister except at the point of death, nor, once they have been reduced to that number, exceed it.” 1079  
MCCXLVIII.—He praises Robert, bishop of Exeter, Roger, bishop of Worcester, and Clarembald, abbot of Faversham, because they deposed Clarembald, abbot of St. Augustine’s, Canterbury. 1079  
MCCXLIX.—He exhorts the monks of St. Augustine’s at Canterbury, after Clarembald’s deposition, to choose another abbot for themselves. 1080  
MCCL.—He annuls whatever Clarembald did with the goods of the church of St. Augustine without the chapter’s consent. 1080  
MCCLI.—To the prior of the Charterhouse of Guidon and his brethren.—He approves their institution. 1080  
MCCLII.—To the cardinals sent as legates into Lombardy.—What hope he has hitherto given to Emperor Frederick’s envoys, who are to negotiate peace with the Church. He commands them to strengthen the Lombards in their league, etc. 1081  
MCCLIII.—He confirms the sentence pronounced by the bishop of Brescia in the dispute between the bishops of Piacenza and Parma concerning the church of Castrum Speculi and the church of St. Christina, which are adjudged to Piacenza. 1082  
MCCLIV.—He takes the monastery of St. Germanus of the Meadows under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1083  
MCCLV.—He takes the church of St. Lawrence at Florence under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1084  
MCCLVI.—To the rulers of the March.—Concerning peace with Emperor Frederick, which must never be confirmed unless their interests are likewise considered. 1086  
MCCLVII.—He takes the house of St. Julian of Perego under protection and confirms all its goods. 1086  
MCCLVIII.—He commands Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See, to protect the Parisian monastery of St. Magloire, commended to him by Louis, king of the Franks. 1087  
MCCLIX.—He grants the monastery of Laëtus a bull concerning altars and complete liberty of the church. 1088  
MCCLX.—He takes the monastery of St. Ghislain under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1088  
MCCLXI.—He orders that the archbishops of York and Canterbury be held in the same place and rank, provided that the one ordained first be regarded as prior. 1090  

## About the year 1176

MCCLXII.—He commands the bishop of Exeter [or Worcester] to forbid Geoffrey, bishop-elect of Lincoln, “since his election has not been confirmed, to grant an archdeaconry or prebend to anyone.” 1090  

## Within the years 1159–1177

MCCLXIII.—To the rulers of Lombardy.—That they recall the people of Modena from oppressing the monastery of Nonantola. 1090  
MCCLXIV.—At the request of A., bishop of Laon, he confirms a sentence pronounced by Aribert, formerly cardinal-priest of St. Anastasia, by which the office of vicedominus of the church of Laon had been taken from Lanfranc of Trissino, knight of Laon. 1091  
MCCLXV.—He writes to John, bishop of Caserta, concerning the dissolution of marriages of certain persons related in the third degree. 1092  

## Within the years 1167–1177

MCCLXVI.—To the regular canons of St. Satyrus.—He exhorts them diligently to observe regular discipline and forbids them to eat meat even outside the monastery. 1092  

## Within the years 1173–1177

MCCLXVII.—To the bishops of Paris and Senlis.—That they cause the wood called Sagitta, taken from the Cluniacs by Hu., butler of the king of the Franks, to be restored to them. 1093  
MCCLXVIII.—To R., bishop of St. Andrews, and to the other bishops of Scotland.—He confirms their privileges. 1093  

## In the year 1177

MCCLXIX.—A privilege for the Scottish monastery of St. James at Regensburg. 1094  
MCCLXX.—To Martin, abbot of St. Vaast.—He takes the monastery of St. Vaast under his protection, grants it various privileges, and especially permits the abbot to use the dalmatic. 1095  
MCCLXXI.—He takes the church of St. Mary at Pulsano under protection and confirms its goods and possessions. 1097  
MCCLXXII.—At the request of Bishop Stephen, he takes the church of Monopoli under protection and confirms its goods. 1098  
MCCLXXIII.—He commands William, archbishop of Reims and legate of the Apostolic See, that, “having summoned the masters of the schools of Paris and Reims and of other neighbouring cities, he forbid anyone to dare say that Christ is not something insofar as he is man; for,” he says, “as he is true God, so he is true man, subsisting from a rational soul and human flesh.” 1098  
MCCLXXIV.—He takes the monastery of Marmoutier under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1099  
MCCLXXV.—To the brethren of the Charterhouse of Seitz, whom he exhorts to live a holy life according to the norm of their order. 1100  

[Col. 1508]

MCCLXXVI.—A privilege for the church of Poreč. 1101  
MCCLXXVII.—He confirms the goods, possessions, and privileges of the monastery of St. Benignus at Dijon. 1102  
MCCLXXVIII.—He takes the Premonstratensian church under protection and confirms its privileges. 1105  
MCCLXXIX.—To Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus and legate of the Apostolic See.—He declares that he has not yet made peace with Emperor Frederick; he orders him to exhort the king of the Franks to observe the agreements made with Henry, king of England. 1108  
MCCLXXX.—A privilege for the church of Verona. 1110  
MCCLXXXI.—To the archpriest and canons of the parish church of St. Michael of Nonantola.—That the number of twelve canons not be increased. 1111  
MCCLXXXII.—To Albert, archpriest, and the canons of the church of Bologna.—He confirms their privileges. 1112  
MCCLXXXIII.—He takes the monastery of St. Mary of Vangadicia under protection and confirms its goods and rights. 1112  
MCCLXXXIV.—To Guy, provost, and the chapter of the church of Modena.—Concerning the number of fourteen canons, neither to be increased nor diminished. 1114  
MCCLXXXV.—He praises and confirms the devotion of Provost Balderan and the canons of St. Mary at Magdeburg toward the Roman Church. 1115  
MCCLXXXVI.—To Hugh, abbot, and the brethren of St. Germanus at Paris.—He grants them that they are not bound to pay procurations to the archbishop of Sens except for at most forty mounted attendants and forty-four men. 1115  
MCCLXXXVII.—He informs Duke Welf that he has undertaken the defence of the church of Steingaden against the bishop of Augsburg. 1116  
MCCLXXXVIII.—To visitors to the church of St. Mary of Charity at Venice, he grants an indulgence of twenty days. 1116  
MCCLXXXIX.—To the provost and chapter of Modena.—He decrees that benefices not be conferred upon canons residing outside. 1117  
MCCXC.—To the same.—He forbids churches to be built within the parishes of Modena without authorization from the bishop and chapter of Modena. 1118  
MCCXCI.—He confirms the sentence pronounced by the bishops of Equilio and Torcello that the monks of St. Nicholas receive Vitalis, bishop of Castello (Venice), on the feast of the Ascension of the Lord “for the procession and for the provision of a meal.” 1118  
MCCXCII.—To the abbot and brethren of St. Ouen.—He confirms their right in the church of St. Leufredus of the Cross. 1119  
MCCXCIII.—He writes to the men of Steingaden that, moved by the prayers of Duke Welf, he has undertaken to protect their church. 1119  
MCCXCIV.—To the provosts of Salzburg and Gurk.—Concerning the impeded arrival of Cardinal Henry. That it is false that he intended the deposition of Adalbert, archbishop of Salzburg, etc. 1120  
MCCXCV.—To Adalbert, archbishop of Salzburg.—That the rumour reporting that he has turned his favour away from him is false. Nevertheless, he is to come to him in Lombardy, to hear a just judgment. 1121  
MCCXCVI.—He grants Robert, abbot of the church of St. Quirinus at Tegernsee, the use of the mitre. 1122  
MCCXCVII.—He confirms the new city of Lodi, endowed with the possessions of the old town. 1122  
MCCXCVIII.—A privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Porto Nuovo. 1123  
MCCXCIX.—He takes the convent of St. Andrew at Ravenna under protection and confirms its goods and rights. 1125  
MCCC.—He takes the monastery of St. Mary in Organo at Verona under protection and confirms its goods, possessions, and privileges. 1126  
MCCCI.—He confirms the constitutions made and to be made by the Carthusian general chapter, with authority to appoint and remove priors and correct members of the order, from whom no appeal is permitted. 1128  
MCCCII.—He confirms for the convent of Blessed Mary at Soissons the guarantee of the prebends of the church of Blessed Peter. 1128  
MCCCIII.—He commands the archbishop of Split, apostolic legate, and Michael, bishop of Trogir, under pain of excommunication to admonish the pirates of Šibenik—who despoiled Raymond of Capella, his subdeacon, while returning to him from William, king of Sicily, both of royal letters and other objects of great value—to restore these things. 1129  
MCCCIV.—He informs Roger, archbishop of York and legate of the Apostolic See, and Hugh, bishop of Durham, that on 21 July the son of Albert, margrave of Brandenburg, chamberlain of Emperor Frederick, gave an oath: “that, after the same emperor came to Venice, he would cause, under oath, the peace of the Church, peace with William, king of Sicily, for fifteen years, and a truce with the Lombards for six years, to be ratified.” He reports that the emperor arrived at the church of St. Nicholas on 24 July, “and there both he himself and the archbishops, bishops, and other princes of the German kingdom, renouncing the schism, received through bishops and cardinals the benefit of absolution.” He further reports that at Venice, both on that day and on the following day, 25 July, the honours owed to him were rendered by the emperor in the church of St. Mark. 1130  
MCCCV.—To Peter, abbot of Monte Cassino, and the archbishop, he communicates in a letter the same matters which he communicated in the preceding letter to Roger, archbishop of York. 1131  
MCCCVI.—He announces to William, archbishop of Reims, and his suffragans that Emperor Frederick has returned to obedience to the Church. 1132  
MCCCVII.—To Guy, archbishop of Sens, and his suffragans, he writes the same things in the same words as in the preceding letter to William of Reims. 1132  
MCCCVIII.—To the general chapter of the Cistercian order.—Concerning the reconciliation of Emperor Frederick. 1132  
MCCCIX.—A privilege for the church of Bonn. 1133  
MCCCX.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He writes that Emperor Frederick has returned to his duty. 1135  
MCCCXI.—To the archbishop of York and the bishop of Lincoln.—On behalf of the nuns of Swineshead and Coton. 1136  
MCCCXII.—He confirms the privileges of the church of Blessed Peter at Osnabrück and the possessions of its clerics. 1137  
MCCCXIII.—He takes the monastery of St. Ulrich under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1137  
MCCCXIV.—To Richard, archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, and his suffragans.—Concerning peace restored with Emperor Frederick. 1140  
MCCCXV.—He informs the choir of the church of Salzburg, the prelates of its churches, and the ministerials of the said church that Conrad of Mainz has been elected in the place of Adalbert, who had voluntarily resigned his archbishopric, by [Roman], bishop of Gurk, [Theobald], bishop of Passau, and the prelates of Salzburg. 1141  
MCCCXVI.—He confirms the Premonstratensian discipline of the monastery of St. James at Mainz. 1142  
MCCCXVII.—He informs the archbishop of Split, apostolic legate, that he has committed to the arbitration of Raymond of Capella, his subdeacon, who is undertaking an apostolic legation to Slavonia, the dispute between him and the archbishop of Zadar concerning the bishopric of Hvar. 1143  
MCCCXVIII.—He forbids Everard, bishop of Tournai, in the division of prebends to proceed except according to the tenor of his written decree. 1144  
MCCCXIX.—He takes the church of St. Donatian at Bruges under protection and confirms its goods and possessions. 1144  
MCCCXX.—He permits Dominic, abbot of St. Justina at Padua, “in services for the dead, when the bishop is absent or unwilling to sing Mass, to sing a special Mass in the monastery.” 1146  
MCCCXXI.—He confirms the settlement made between a certain Bishop Baldwin and Gerard of Chérisy. 1146  
MCCCXXII.—He writes to John the priest, king of the Indians, that he had indeed long heard that he followed the Christian law; but that only then had the physician Philip reported that he wished “to be instructed in Catholic doctrine and to have in Rome a church and at Jerusalem some altar.” He therefore sends the same physician Philip, through whom he may be brought to the Catholic faith. 1148  
MCCCXXIII.—He takes the monastery of St. Mary Magdalene of Lake Jura under protection and confirms its goods and possessions. 1150  
MCCCXXIV.—A privilege for the church of Ferrara. 1152  
MCCCXXV.—He thanks Master Hugh Eterianus because he sent him, through Master Cacciaredus, a book composed “for God and for devotion to the Church.” He admonishes him “to urge the emperor of Constantinople more diligently to show devotion and reverence to the Roman Church and to its unity.” 1154  

## Within the years 1160–1178

MCCCXXVI.—He grants the lepers of Abbéville immunity from tithes and confirms their title to the land of Cantastra, granted by the count of Ponthieu. 1154  
MCCCXXVII.—He forbids parish priests, chaplains, and other clerics in the vicinity of the monastery of Puteoli “to prevent any of their parishioners in any way from freely being able to assume the monastic habit at the monastery or to be buried there.” 1155  
MCCCXXVIII.—To Rainald, bishop of Jesi.—He grants certain privileges. 1155  
MCCCXXIX.—A privilege for the church of St. Margaret of Elenfordesmere. 1156  
MCCCXXX.—He confirms for Robert of Chedeleswurd four hides of land in Chedeleswurd granted to him by the monks of Abingdon. 1156  

## In the year 1174–1178

MCCCXXXI.—He commands the bishop of Terracina to induce the people of Terracina to restore whatever possessions of the church of St. Stephen of Montanis they have acquired. 1157  

## Between the years 1176–1178

MCCCXXXII.—To Master Gerard Puella.—Concerning the revenues of the schools. 1157  
MCCCXXXIII.—He grants Peter, abbot, and the chapter of Monte Cassino “that for things which they may at any time purchase for the use of the monastery in the city of Benevento, nothing shall at any time be required for passage-toll or market-toll.” 1158  

## In the year 1178
MCCCXXXIV.—To Gerald, abbot, and the brethren of the church of St. Mary of the Rhine.—Confirms their possessions and rights. 1159  
MCCCXXXV.—Takes the monastery of St. Mary of Eberbach under protection and confirms its goods, possessions, and privileges. 1160  
MCCCXXXVI.—Restores to the Cassinese monastery a golden tablet which had been alienated from it, and forbids its future alienation under anathema. 1161  
MCCCXXXVII.—To Hugh, bishop of Terracina.—Confirms his statutes concerning the discipline of the canons. 1161  
MCCCXXXVIII.—Takes the church of Linköping under protection and confirms its goods and possessions. 1163  
MCCCXXXIX.—To Peter, cardinal of St. Chrysogonus, legate of the Apostolic See.—That he bring to him the candlesticks and silver cup of the deceased bishop of Porto. 1163  
MCCCXL.—Takes the church of Regina under protection and confirms the goods and rights of its canons. 1164  
MCCCXLI.—Confirms various constitutions and privileges of the church and chapter of Saint-Omer in Artois. 1165  
MCCCXLII.—Takes the monastery of Cluny under protection and confirms its possessions. 1166  
MCCCXLIII.—To Roger, bishop of Worcester.—Concerning the elect of the church of St. Augustine of Canterbury. 1167  
MCCCXLIV.—To Roger, elect of the monastery of St. Augustine of Canterbury.—Testifies that he has decreed that Roger and his successors are to be consecrated by the archbishops in that monastery itself.  
MCCCXLV.—Informs Richard, archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, concerning the foregoing letters. 1169  
MCCCXLVI.—Takes the church of Cefalù under protection and confirms its possessions, privileges, and rights. 1169  
MCCCXLVII.—Confirms for the canons of St. Euphemia on the Island of Cumarum certain tithes and all their possessions. 1171  
MCCCXLVIII.—Confirms the privilege established by Eugenius III for the canons of the Roman church of St. Peter. 1172  
MCCCXLIX.—At the request of Berno, bishop, confirms the episcopal see of Schwerin and the possessions of the church. 1174  
MCCCL.—Confirms a certain custom of the canons of the church of Bremen. 1175  
MCCCLI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Nicholas at Angers. 1176  
MCCCLII.—To Philip, archbishop of Cologne.—The rights and privileges of the church of Cologne are confirmed. 1176  
MCCCLIII.—Takes the monastery of St. Geremarus under protection, enumerates and confirms its goods and possessions. 1178  
MCCCLIV.—To the clergy of Salamanca.—That they obey Peter, the bishop consecrated by him. 1183  
MCCCLV.—To Alfonso, king of Castile.—Commends Peter, bishop of Salamanca. 1183  
MCCCLVI.—To Ubald, archbishop of Pisa, and all bishops and abbots established throughout Tuscany.—Invites them to a council to be held at Rome. 1184  
MCCCLVII.—To the archbishops, bishops, and abbots of Hungary.—Of the same subject. 1185  
MCCCLVIII.—To Guarin, archbishop of Bourges, his suffragans, and the abbots established throughout their dioceses.—Of the same subject. 1185  

[Col. 1511]

MCCCLIX.—Takes the Parisian church of St. Opportuna under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1185  
MCCCLX.—To the bishops of London and Winchester: observing that judgment concerning possessions belongs to the king, not to the Church, he directs them to leave the judgment concerning possessions to Henry, king of the English. 1185  
MCCCLXI.—Takes the monastery of St. Thomas of the Paraclete at Ébleholte under protection and confirms its goods and rights. 1186  

## Between the Years 1159 and 1179

MCCCLXII.—To the bishops of Parma and Reggio.—That they ensure the restoration of certain goods to the monks of Nonantola. 1187  
MCCCLXIII.—To the people of Nonantola.—That P., who has given his entire life to God, is to be judged free from his vow. 1188  
MCCCLXIV.—Takes the convent of St. Mary of Cale under protection and confirms its goods. 1189  
MCCCLXV.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the collegiate church of SS. Michael and Gudula. 1189  

## Between the Years 1160 and 1179

MCCCLXVI.—To the chapter of Blessed Martin of Tours.—That no one of servile condition, or born outside lawful marriage, be admitted as a canon. 1191  
MCCCLXVII.—To Hugh, bishop of Genoa.—On behalf of William, lord of Montpellier. He forbids the Genoese to harm the port of Maguelone. 1191  
MCCCLXVIII.—To the consuls and people of Genoa.—He dissuades them from acts of injury against William, lord of Montpellier. 1192  
MCCCLXIX.—To the abbot and brethren of the monastery of Possignano.—Asserts their right of patronage over certain churches. 1193  

## Between the Years 1166 and 1179

MCCCLXX.—To the provost, chapter, and [church of] Viborg.—Announces that he has taken the convent of St. Margaret of Asmild under protection. 1193  
MCCCLXXI.—To the clergy of the archdeaconry of Berkshire.—Grants them various privileges. 1194  
MCCCLXXII.—To the bishop of Chalon and the abbot of La Ferté.—That they compel certain knights to restore what they have taken from the monastery of Tournus. 1194  
MCCCLXXIII.—To the archbishops of Bourges and Besançon, etc.—Exhorts them to protect the goods of the monastery of Tournus. 1195  
MCCCLXXIV.—Grants to Nicholas, prior, and the brethren of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem the church of St. Giles, situated at Rome near the Golden Gate. 1196  
MCCCLXXV.—To the abbot and brethren of the monastery of St. Denis. 1196  
MCCCLXXVI.—To Simon, bishop of Meaux.—That no parish church be granted to anyone who does not reside there. 1197  
MCCCLXXVII.—Informs certain archbishops that he has taken the monastery of St. Nicholas at Angers under protection. 1197  
MCCCLXXVIII.—To the archbishop of Bourges and the bishops of Clermont and Le Puy.—That they ensure observance of the judgment pronounced for the monastery of Tournus. 1197  
MCCCLXXIX.—Gives the same command to the archbishop of Vienne. 1197  
MCCCLXXX.—To the consuls and people of Siena.—Confirms the peace concerning the boundaries between the Sienese and the Florentines. 1198  
MCCCLXXXI.—Confirms the possessions of the canons of the church of Cesena. 1198  

## In the Years 1173–1179

MCCCLXXXII.—To the abbot and canons of Lucerne.—Asserts for them a certain tract of land. 1199  

## In the Years 1175–1179

MCCCLXXXIII.—To Richard, archbishop of Canterbury.—Concerning the coronation of the kings of England. 1199  

## In the Years 1178–1179

MCCCLXXXIV.—To Master Gerard Puella.—Restores revenues voluntarily remitted during the time of the schism. 1200  
MCCCLXXXV.—Grants William, abbot of St. Denis, and his successors the use of the mitre, ring, and sandals. 1200  
MCCCLXXXVI.—Assures Simon, formerly abbot of St. Mary of Blois, of benefices conferred upon him by John, bishop of Chartres, after his resignation of office. 1201  
MCCCLXXXVII.—To Simon, bishop of Meaux. 1201  

## In the Year 1179

MCCCLXXXVIII.—Takes the monastery of SS. Flora and Lucilla at Aeti under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1201  
MCCCLXXXIX.—To John, bishop, and the chapter of Chartres.—That ecclesiastical offices be granted only to those who have promised residence. 1203  
MCCCXC.—To Matthew, bishop of Troyes.—Concerning the number of canons, priests, and deacons in the church of Troyes. 1203  
MCCCXCI.—To Lupus, king of Valencia.—Gives him thanks because he protects and honours Christians. 1205  
MCCCXCII.—Bull for the church of Béziers. 1205  
MCCCXCIII.—To Simon, bishop of Meaux.—Concerning the election of abbots in monasteries of his diocese. 1206  
MCCCXCIV.—To the abbot and chapter of St. Bertin at Sithiu.—That there be two priests in the parish church of Broekburg. 1207  
MCCCXCV.—To the same.—A copy of the confirmation of two parts of the tithe of Lulinghem, belonging to a certain knight of Watten. 1207  
MCCCXCVI.—To the same.—A copy of the confirmation concerning the tithes of Varancies. 1208  
MCCCXCVII.—To the same.—That no archbishop, bishop, or any other person pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict in churches subject to their jurisdiction. 1208  
MCCCXCVIII.—To the same.—That they are not bound to confer prebends upon laymen. 1208  
MCCCXCIX.—Takes the monastery of St. Blaise in the Black Forest under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1209  
MCD.—Takes the church of St. Maurice of Agaunum under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1212  
MCDI.—Privilege for the church of Tropea. 1213  
MCDII.—Takes the monastery of St. Martin in Mure under protection, grants it various privileges, and imposes upon the monks an annual payment of one gold piece. 1213  
MCDIII.—Takes the Jerusalem monastery of the Primitive Church of Mount Sion under protection and confirms its possessions situated in Sicily.—Grants the abbot the use of the mitre and ring. 1214  
MCDIV.—Confirms the rights and privileges of the monastery of St. Simplician at Milan. 1214  
MCDV.—Privilege for the monastery of St. George in the Black Forest. 1216  
MCDVI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Michael of Tornodorum (Tonnerre). 1219  
MCDVII.—Privilege for the church of Imola. 1221  
MCDVIII.—Commands Desiderius, bishop of Thérouanne, to ensure that the tithe due to the monastery of St. Bertin at Sithiu is rendered; likewise, he exhorts Philip, count of Flanders, to grant the tithe to that same monastery. 1221  
MCDIX.—Bull confirming the monastery of Garsten. 1221  
MCDX.—Takes the monastery of St. Nazarius of Lorsch under protection and confirms its goods and rights. 1223  
MCDXI.—Takes the monastery of Tournus under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1225  
MCDXII.—To Richard, archbishop of Canterbury.—Announces that he has consecrated Roger as abbot of St. Augustine’s. 1228  
MCDXIII.—To Roger, abbot of St. Augustine of Canterbury.—Concerning the blessing of his successors. 1229  
MCDXIV.—To Henry, king of the English.—Affirms that Roger, abbot, is being rashly accused. 1229  
MCDXV.—To Roger, abbot, and the brethren of St. Augustine of Canterbury.—That no one be ordained in churches subject to their presentation unless he has been presented by them. 1231  
MCDXVI.—To the same.—Concerning the excommunication of wrongdoers. 1231  
MCDXVII.—Grants to Roger, abbot, and the brethren of St. Augustine of Canterbury “that, when there is a general interdict upon the land, they may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, with the excommunicated and interdicted excluded, without ringing bells, and in a subdued voice.” 1231  
MCDXVIII.—Takes the church of Reims under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1231  
MCDXIX.—To Sigehard, abbot of the monastery of Lorsch.—Grants him and his successors the use of the mitre. 1233  
MCDXX.—Declares to William, archbishop of Reims, and his suffragans that the religious of the Cistercian order at Dunes are exempt from paying tithes on lands which they cultivate themselves. 1233  
MCDXXI.—To Henry, patriarch of Grado, and Dominic, bishop of Caorle.—That they cause the judgment rendered for the monastery of St. Saviour to be observed by all. 1234  

[Col. 1513]

MCDXXII.—Requests Christian, archbishop of Mainz, to assist Leonatus, abbot of Pescara, in recovering the monastery’s possessions. 1235  
MCDXXIII.—Commands [Gentilis], bishop of Osimo, [Peter] of Fermo, [Acceptabilis], bishop of Camerino, and [James], bishop of Senigallia, to order restoration to the monastery of Pescara of possessions seized during the schism. 1236  
MCDXXIV.—To Alfonso, king of the Portuguese.—Takes the kingdom of Portugal under protection. 1237  
MCDXXV.—Privilege for the church of SS. Stephen and Willehad at Bremen. 1238  
MCDXXVI.—Privilege for the church of St. Mary at the End. 1241  
MCDXXVII.—Grants an indulgence of twenty days to the church of St. Saviour on the anniversary of its dedication. 1242  
MCDXXVIII.—Assures Lombard, former archbishop of Benevento, at the canons’ wish, of certain revenues. 1242  
MCDXXIX.—Confirms the peace concluded between the brethren of the military order of the Temple and the brethren of the Hospital. 1243  
MCDXXX.—To the dean and chapter of Laon. 1245  
MCDXXXI.—To the abbot and convent of St. Vaast.—Confirms the settlement made by them with the count of Hainaut, and their rights in the town of Haspre. 1245  
MCDXXXII.—Privilege for the church of Acerenza. 1246  
MCDXXXIII.—To the dean and canons of St. Aignan of Orléans. 1246  
MCDXXXIV.—Confirms the privileges of the church of Cambrai. 1246  
MCDXXXV.—Takes the church of Lausanne under protection and confirms its rights. 1247  
MCDXXXVI.—Takes the monastery of Holy Cross of Bosonville under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1248  
MCDXXXVII.—Privilege for the church of Ascoli. 1251  
MCDXXXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Aper at Toul. 1252  
MCDXXXIX.—To the monks of St. Germain of Paris. 1255  
MCDXL–MCDXLI.—To Bartholomew, archbishop of Tours.—Reproves him for failing to appear by the appointed date, and grants him a further delay. 1255  
MCDXLII.—To the king of France.—That he endeavour to settle the controversy between the churches of Dol and Tours. 1256  
MCDXLIII.—To William, archbishop of Reims. 1256  

## In the Years 1170–1180

MCDXLIV.—Grants the prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre at Jerusalem and his successors that “after archbishops and bishops, they shall hold the first place among the abbots and priors of the patriarchate of Jerusalem in assemblies and offices of the Church.” 1257  
MCDXLV.—Commands the abbots of the Temple of the Lord, Mount Sion, and the Valley of Jehoshaphat, and the prior of the Mount of Olives, that “at the principal solemnities of the churches, if the patriarch of Jerusalem happens to be absent or ill, or if the church of Jerusalem is vacant, they are to receive the prior of that church with the brethren into the solemn procession, and permit them to sing the solemn Mass in the churches in place of the patriarch.” 1257  
MCDXLVI.—Assures the abbot of St. Denis and his successors of the right of distributing the prebends of the church of St. Paul. 1258  
MCDXLVII.—To the abbot and monks of St. Denis. 1258  

## In the Years 1171–1180

MCDXLVII *bis*.—Exhorts K[nut], illustrious king of the Swedes and Goths, the bishops and noble duke, and all clergy and people established throughout Gothia, to observe marriage laws, honour priests, and pay tithes. He warns them neither to “leave all their goods to churches after disinheriting their legitimate sons,” nor to “venerate as saints, in the manner of unbelievers, persons killed in drinking and drunkenness.” He remits for them “the forty-day fast before the feast of St. Michael, excepting Friday.” He gives thanks because they “visited him in many of his necessities through Richard the priest.” 1259  
MCDXLVIII.—To the monks of St. Savin.—That they obey their abbot. 1262  
MCDXLIX.—Confirms the rule of the canons of St. Regulus. 1262  
MCDL.—To the archbishop of Auch and the abbot of Marseille.—That they impose suitable penance upon disobedient monks. 1262  
MCDLI.—To Rotrou, archbishop of Rouen. 1263  
MCDLII.—Privilege for the monks of St. Benedict at Subiaco. 1263  

[Col. 1514]

## In the Years 1175–1180

MCDLIII.—To Raynerius, archbishop of Salerno. 1264  
MCDLIV.—Confirms to Fulbert the hermit the place called “God’s Mercy.” 1264  

## In the Year 1180

MCDLV.—Confirms the establishment of canons of the Order of St. Augustine in the abbey of Chinon and all their goods. 1265  
MCDLVI.—Takes the monastery of St. Victor under protection and confirms its privileges. 1267  
MCDLVII.—To the archbishop and bishop of Sardinia.—On behalf of the monastery of Monte Cassino. 1267  
MCDLVIII.—Privilege for the metropolitan church. 1268  
MCDLIX.—To the abbot and chapter of Cîteaux. 1269  
MCDLX.—To Omnibon, bishop of Verona, and the bishop of Mantua.—That they compel T. to restore the estate of Nogara to the monks of Nonantola. 1270  
MCDLXI.—He writes to B[artholomew], archbishop of Tours and legate of the Apostolic See, that, having been persuaded that he would come to him on the next Sunday on which is sung “Rejoice, Jerusalem” (*Laetare, Jerusalem*; 30 March), or “I am the good shepherd” (*Ego sum pastor bonus*; 4 May), his messenger has arrived. He adds that, induced by the prayers of Louis, king of the French, and King Philip, he has “extended until the next feast of Blessed Martin [11 November], though not without a heavy and grievous burden, the term for R., elect of Dol, who has been awaiting him for a year and more,” and orders him to appear by then. 1270  
MCDLXII.—To the chapter of the church of Bremen.—That laymen are not to be admitted to the election of an archbishop. 1270  
MCDLXIII.—Privilege for the church of Chalon. 1271  
MCDLXIV.—He writes to the bishops of Padua, Vicenza, and Treviso that, after so much labour expended upon the peace with the emperor and the Lombards’ truce, the Bolognese have destroyed the castle and church of Montebello; and that, although the truce has been violated by men of the imperial party, the emperor’s legates have nevertheless already demanded “magnificently” that the damage be made good according to the laws of the truce. He asks them to prevent such deeds and, if they have been committed, to order the injuries inflicted to be repaired. 1272  
MCDLXV.—Writes the same to the archbishop of Ravenna and his suffragans. 1272  
MCDLXVI.—To the canons of the church of Alexandria.—Confirms their status and possessions. 1272  
MCDLXVII.—To the archbishops and bishops, etc., established throughout Dalmatia.—Commends to them Theobald, his subdeacon and apostolic legate. 1273  
MCDLXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Laët. 1274  
MCDLXIX.—To the bishops of Scotland.—Confirms the judgment of the apostolic legate, by which he confirmed John, lawfully elected, and deposed Hugh, whom the king had intruded into the bishopric of St. Andrews. 1274  
MCDLXX.—To William, king of Scotland.—Commands him to permit John, lawfully elected and confirmed bishop of St. Andrews, peaceably to exercise his office; otherwise the kingdom is to be punished by interdict and the king by excommunication. 1275  
MCDLXXI.—To the bishops of Scotland.—Confirms the excommunication of Hugh, intruded into the bishopric of St. Andrews. 1275  

## In the Years 1159–1181

MCDLXXII.—To Henry, king of the English.—That he release William, a chaplain imprisoned by his officials, and restore to him the benefices taken away. 1276  
MCDLXXIII.—To Henry, king of the English.—Commends R., son of the king of Canterbury. 1277  
MCDLXXIV.—Takes the monastery of St. Ouen at Rouen under protection and confirms its goods and possessions. 1277  
MCDLXXV.—A decree for the monastery of St. John of the Vines. 1278  
MCDLXXVI.—A rescript to Hugh, abbot of St. John of the Vines. 1279  

## In the Years 1160–1181

MCDLXXVII.—To Manasses, bishop of Orléans. 1280  

## In the Years 1163–1181

MCDLXXVIII.—To Gilbert of London and R., archdeacon.—That they compel clergy and laity to desist from unlawful marriages and cohabitations. 1280  
MCDLXXIX.—To Gilbert, bishop of London.—He is not to permit sons of priests, or persons born while their fathers were priests, to succeed in churches in which their fathers had formerly ministered. 1281  

[Col. 1515]

## In the Years 1166–1181

MCDLXXX.—To Sueno, bishop of Aarhus. 1281  
MCDLXXXI.—To Bartholomew, bishop of Exeter, and Simon, abbot of St. Albans.—Concerning the dispute between Robert de Ber and William the clerk. 1282  

## In the Years 1168–1181

MCDLXXXII.—To the consuls of Piacenza.—That they ensure restoration of what has been taken from Hugh, his subdeacon. 1282  
MCDLXXXII *bis*.—A privilege granted to Ulrich, patriarch of Aquileia. 1283  

## In the Years 1171–1181

MCDLXXXIII.—To the doge of Venice.—Commends to him Henry, patriarch of Venice, and exhorts him favourably to assent to the transfer of the patriarchate of Grado to the city of Venice. 1284  
MCDLXXXIV.—To Gilbert, bishop of London.—That he compel Count Alberic to receive his wife with due honour. 1285  
MCDLXXXV.—To the bishops of Valva, Abruzzo, and Marsica, etc.—That they compel Gentilis of Raiano to pay the due rent to the monastery of Pescara. 1286  
MCDLXXXVI.—Entrusts to the bishops of Abruzzo and Penne the task of defending the churches of the monastery of Pescara from injuries. 1287  
MCDLXXXVII.—Makes a concession to the Cistercian abbots. 1287  
MCDLXXXVIII.—To all who observe the Rule of Grandmont, he “enjoins the labour which they endure in that observance in place of penance and for the remission of sins,” and confirms the Rule itself. 1287  
MCDLXXXIX.—To the abbot of Prémontré.—The abbot of Prémontré may absolve the members of his institute from sins and excommunication, and may give tonsure to his clerical novices. 1288  
MCDXC.—To the archbishops.—That they protect the rights of the monastery of St. Denis. 1288  
MCDXCI.—To Henry, patriarch of Grado.—Commands him to cause the judgment rendered for the monastery of St. Saviour to be observed. 1289  
MCDXCII.—To the archbishop of Tours and all bishops.—On behalf of the church of St. Martin of Tours. 1289  
MCDXCIII.—Forbids the dean and chapter of Troyes “that any one of them, when elected or consecrated bishop, retain for his own use the prebend he formerly held, or other revenues of the church, save those shown to belong to episcopal right.” 1290  
MCDXCIV.—Grants Peter, abbot of the Neapolitan monastery of SS. Severinus and Sosius, and his successors the use of the mitre. 1290  
MCDXCV.—To the bishops of Parma and Reggio.—On behalf of the monastery of Nonantola. 1291  
MCDXCVI.—To Richard, archbishop of Canterbury.—That he suspend from offices and benefices the clerics of Count Hugh who have procured sacred rites contrary to the interdict. 1291  
MCDXCVII.—To Wichmann, archbishop of Magdeburg, and … bishop of Brandenburg. 1292  
MCDXCVIII–MD.—To Guy, archbishop of Sens. 1292  

## In the Years 1179–1181

MDI.—To the abbess of Eremburg and the sisters of Gif. 1292  
MDII.—Confirms the settlement between Henry, bishop, and the canons of the church of Modena. 1293  

## In the Year 1181

MDIII.—Privilege for the church of Genoa. 1293  
MDIV.—To all princes.—Exhorts them to aid the Holy Land. 1294  
MDV.—Commends to archbishops, bishops, and abbots the knights of the Temple sent to seek aid for the Eastern land. 1296  
MDVI.—To Theobald, abbot of Cluny.—Confirms his settlements with William, count of Chalon, and Gerard, count of Mâcon, secured by the written instrument of Philip, king of France. 1297  
MDVII.—Informs Theobald, abbot, and the chapter of Cluny that he has commanded the bishop of Autun to consecrate the chapel of Beaune. If he refuses to carry out the command, he permits them to invite the bishop of Belley to perform the consecration. 1298  
MDVIII.—Commands Guy, archbishop of Sens; Henry, bishop of Bayeux; S., abbot of St. Geneviève; and the dean of the church of Bayeux, in the dispute between Roland, elect of Dol, and Bartholomew, archbishop of Tours and legate of the Apostolic See, to commit the testimony of witnesses to writing. 1298  
MDIX.—Takes the church of St. Mary of Flottin under protection and confirms its rights and privileges. 1298  
MDX.—Privilege for the monastery of Monte Cassino. 1303  
MDXI.—To Peter, abbot of Monte Cassino. 1304  
MDXII.—To Casimir, duke of Poland.—Confirms certain constitutions issued concerning the goods of the Church. 1304  
MDXIII.—Takes the church of St. Laud of Bourg-Achard under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1305  
MDXIV.—Takes the monastery of St. Ruffillus under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. 1308  
MDXV.—To the dean and chapter of Chalon.—That their bishop may not excommunicate or suspend clerics of Chalon unless he has first notified the chapter. 1310  
MDXVI.—To the dean and chapter of Chalon.—That they may present to the bishop of Autun persons fit to govern churches whom the bishop of Chalon has rejected. 1311  
MDXVII.—To Béla, king of Hungary.—That he cease delaying the free election of the archbishop of Split. 1311  
MDXVIII.—Takes the church of Holy Cross at Metz under protection and confirms its goods and possessions. 1312  
MDXIX.—Privilege for the church of Treviso. 1314  
MDXX.—To the archbishop and bishops established throughout Sweden.—That they provide for the souls of those subject to them. 1315  
MDXXI.—Privilege for the Cluniacs.—Forbids anyone to build a church, chapel, or oratory in Cluniac parishes, especially in the parish of Moulins, without the assent of the abbot of Cluny. 1316  

## Spurious

I.—To Henry, king of the English.—Concerning Thomas Becket. 1317  
II.—Bull granting indulgences to the church of St. Mark at Venice. 1319  

**A Series of Decretal Letters Summarily Set Forth.** 1319  

# Letters of Various Persons to Alexander III

I.—Of Philip, abbot of La Charité.—Congratulates Alexander upon his elevation to the highest dignity; reports that the kings of France and England have embraced the pope’s cause. 1359  
II.—Of Eleanor, queen of England, wife of Henry II.—Gives thanks for letters sent by the supreme pontiff and asks his favour for the abbot of St. Maxentius. 1362  
III.—Of Amalric, minister of the church of the Holy Resurrection at Jerusalem.—Reports that, by unanimous consent of the Eastern clergy and people, after Octavian, John, and Guy had been rejected, he himself was elected as temporal lord and spiritual father. 1362  
IV.—Of Fastred, third abbot of Clairvaux, to Omnibon, bishop of Verona.—Concerning the Council of Toulouse, at which Alexander, Victor having been rejected, was acknowledged as pope; and concerning the conventicle of Pavia. 1363  
V.—Of Peter of Pisa, dean of the church of St. Aignan of Orléans.—Against contumacious bishops. 1365  
VI.—Of Henry, archbishop of Reims.—On behalf of St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1366  
VII.—Of the same.—On behalf of Drogo, chancellor of the church of Noyon. 1366  
VIII.—Of the same.—That he should not ratify the election of the bishop of Cambrai. 1367  
VIII *bis*.—Concerning the rebellion of the monks of St. Macarius against the church of Holy Cross at Bordeaux. 1368  
IX.—Privilege granted by Ferdinand, king of the Spains, to the Roman Church concerning the donation and grant of the castle of Thoraph. 1369  
X.—Of Ferdinand, king of the Spains.—Places himself and his entire kingdom under the lordship of the pope. 1370  
XI.—Of Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Chrysogonus.—Enumerates men then in Gaul distinguished for learning and virtues. 1370  
XII.—Instrument by which Adinulf and Landulf, sons of Gregory, renounced every right which they had in the castle of Falbateria, and received it as a fief from Pope Alexander III. 1371  

## In the Years 1159–1181
XIII.—Of Guarinus of St. Victor.—That he is unable to send the brethren requested by Cardinal John, and that others too can scarcely be sent. 1373  
XIV.—Of Eberhard, bishop of Salzburg.—He commends the bishop-elect of Aquileia. 1374  
XV.—Of Hugh, abbot of the church of Blessed Mary of Adrianople, and Peter, prior of the hospital of St. John at Constantinople: what and how great things they accomplished among the Easterners for the stability and dignity of the Roman Church [Col. 1517] during the expedition of the Emperor Frederick Augustus. 1375  
XVI.—Of Louis, king of the Franks.—Against heretics, commonly called Populicans, wandering through the regions of Flanders. 1376  
XVII.—Of the same.—In the case of St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1376  
XVIII.—Of the same.—He commends St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1377  
XIX.—Of the same.—He states that St. Thomas, while in exile, was honourably received by him. 1377  
XX.—Of the same.—On the murder of St. Thomas. 1378  
XXI.—Of the same.—He exhorts the pope to cut away vices by his authority. 1378  
XXII.—Of A . . ., queen of the Franks.—On the perjury of John of Oxford; she commends Thomas of Canterbury. 1380  
XXIII.—Of Blessed Peter, surnamed Monoculus, eighth abbot of Clairvaux.—He complains that the Cistercian Order is harassed by secular persons through lawsuits, plundering of goods, and so forth, and implores the pope’s aid against these evils. 1381  
XXIV.—Of the same.—He gives thanks to the pope for the benefits bestowed, especially upon the monastery of Balerne, and desires that its suit, begun against unjust persons, may swiftly be concluded. 1382  
XXV.—Of the community of Clairvaux.—The community asks the pope not to deprive it of its abbot Henry, who was being sought for the bishopric of Toulouse. 1383  
XXVI.—Of Henry, king of England.—He congratulates the pope upon his election, and asks him to receive the king as his own and spiritual son. 1383  
XXVII.—Of the same.—He asks that the sentence of excommunication pronounced by the archbishop of Canterbury against certain persons be relaxed. 1384  
XXVIII.—Of the same.—On the free election granted by him to the English Church. He commends the bishop-elect of Bath. 1385  
XXIX.—Of the same.—Out of regard for the pope, he offers peace and affection to the archbishop of Canterbury; he complains that Vivian and Gratian, legates of the Apostolic See, did not abide by their promises to lift the excommunication. 1385  
XXX.—Of the same.—He complains that the bishops of London and Salisbury, after an appeal had been made to the pope, were again bound by a sentence of excommunication by the archbishop of Canterbury. 1387  
XXXI.—Of the same.—He reports the death of St. Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury. 1388  
XXXII.—Of the same.—He complains of the rebellion of Henry and his other sons against him, and implores the pope’s help. 1389  
XXXIII.—Of R., count of Leicester, to the supreme pontiff.—He requests his protection for the monastery of Lyre. 1390  
XXXIV.—Of William, cardinal-priest of St. Peter in Chains, to Emperor Manuel.—He urges him to enter into an alliance with King Louis of France for the defence of the Roman Church. 1391  
XXXV.—Of Otto, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.—For Gilbert, bishop of London. 1392  
XXXVI.—Of Philip, count of Flanders.—For Thomas of Canterbury. 1392  
XXXVII.—Of William, bishop of Pavia.—On the same subject. 1393  
XXXVIII.—Of William, bishop of Pavia, and Cardinal Otto.—On the dispute between Henry, king of England, and Thomas. 1394  
XXXIX.—Of the prior and community of Canterbury.—For R., bishop-elect of Winchester. 1396  
XL.—Of Odo, prior, and the community of Canterbury.—That, after elections had been held at the king’s command and R., a monk of the same community, had been elected abbot by unanimous consent, the younger king annulled the election. 1396  
XLI.—Of Roger, archbishop of York.—He gives thanks for benefits shown him by Alexander. He commends Gilbert, bishop of London. 1398  
XLII.—Of the canons of Rheims.—For Thomas of Canterbury. 1399  
XLIII.—Of Rotrou, archbishop of Rouen.—He humbly asks that the pope deal more mildly with the king in the cause of St. Thomas. 1400  
XLIV.—Of the same.—For Gilbert, bishop of London. 1401  
XLV.—Of the suffragan bishops of the Church of Canterbury.—Taking the king’s side against their metropolitan, they appeal to the Apostolic See and ask that Ascension Day be assigned them as the term of their appeal. 1401  
XLVI.—Of the same.—They complain that, contrary to the authority of the canons, after their appeal they were bound by a sentence of excommunication by the archbishop of Canterbury [Col. 1518]. Nevertheless, they request that the day of the passing of Blessed Martin be established as the term for their appeal. 1404  
XLVII.—Of the clergy of Normandy.—They ask that the pope show some indulgence to the king of England in the cause of St. Thomas. 1405  
XLVIII.—Of William, bishop of Auxerre.—Against Gilbert, bishop of London. 1406  
XLIX.—Of William, bishop-elect of Chartres.—For Thomas of Canterbury. 1407  
L.—Of the same.—For the same. 1408  
LI.—Of Giles, bishop of Évreux.—He humbly asks that the pope deal more mildly with the king of England. 1409  
LII–LIII.—Of Giles, bishop of Évreux. 1411  
LIV.—Of Henry, dean, and the chapter of St. Paul’s, London.—They commend Bishop Gilbert as he travels to Rome. 1412  
LV.—Of Stephen, bishop of Meaux.—For St. Thomas in exile. 1414  
LVI.—Of the same.—For the same. 1414  
LVII.—Of the same.—On the lamentable murder of St. Thomas. 1415  
LVIII.—Of Milo, bishop of the Morini.—Against Gilbert, bishop of London. 1446  
LIX.—Of Bernard, bishop of Nevers.—He asks that some indulgence be shown to the king of England in the cause of St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1417  
LX.—Of Baldwin, bishop of Noyon.—Against Gilbert, bishop of London. 1418  
LXI.—Of the same and Maurice, bishop of Paris.—That, after a conference had been appointed with the archbishop of Canterbury at Pontoise, the king of England, disregarding in contempt of the lord of Canterbury the conference that he had appointed, hastily returned to England. 1419  
LXII.—Of Maurice, bishop of Paris.—For St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1420  
LXIII.—Of the same.—Against Gilbert, bishop of London. 1421  
LXIV.—Of Matthew, bishop of Troyes.—For St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1422  
LXV.—Of A. Certesiensis.—For Gilbert, bishop of London. 1423  
LXVI.—Of Rotrou, archbishop of Rouen.—On the same subject as Letter LXI. 1424  
LXVII.—Of William, archbishop of Sens.—He asks that the sentence of excommunication pronounced by the archbishop of Canterbury against the bishops of London and Salisbury be ratified. 1425  
LXVIII.—Of the same.—Against Gilbert, bishop of London. 1425  
LXIX.—Of the same.—In the cause of St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1426  
LXX.—Of the same.—He grieves that Gilbert, bishop of London, has been absolved. On the coronation of King Henry’s son. 1428  
LXXI.—Of the same.—On the lamentable murder of St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1428  
LXXII.—Of the same.—On a similar subject. 1430  
LXXIII.—Of William, bishop of Sens, legate of the Apostolic See.—He commends Hugh of Campo Florido, bishop of Soissons and chancellor of France. 1432  
LXXIV.—Of an anonymous writer.—On the murder of St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1432  
LXXV.—Of Matthew, treasurer of Sens.—In favour of Thomas of Canterbury, against King Henry. He advises that the threats of the king of England be lightly regarded, “because the magnates of Poitou and Brittany, allied with the lord king of France, have woven for him an inextricable labyrinth.” 1434  
LXXVI.—Of C., priest of Lantony.—For Gilbert of London. 1435  
LXXVII.—Of Simon, prior of Mont-Dieu, and Engelbert, prior of the Valley of St. Peter.—What they did in carrying out the apostolic mandate for restoring concord between the king and the archbishop of Canterbury. 1436  
LXXVIII.—Of the same.—That, having achieved nothing in the matter entrusted to them, they presented the pope’s threatening letters to the king. 1437  
LXXIX–LXXX.—Of A., minister of St. Osyth.—For Gilbert, bishop of London. 1438  
LXXXI.—Of the abbot of Ramsey.—On the same subject. 1439  
LXXXII.—Of William of Ramsey.—On the same subject. 1440  
LXXXIII.—Of Henry, abbot of Stratford.—For Gilbert, bishop of London. 1441  
LXXXIV.—Of the Church of the Holy Trinity, London.—On the same subject. 1442  
LXXXV.—Of William, abbot of the Church of the Holy Trinity, London.—On the same subject. 1443  
LXXXVI.—Of R., prior of St. Victor at Paris, and Ervisius, abbot of St. Augustine’s.—For St. Thomas of Canterbury. 1443  
LXXXVII.—Of William, abbot of Reading.—For Gilbert, bishop of London. 1444  
LXXXVIII.—Of Lambard to Alexander.—How John of Oxford, returning from Rome, boasted that he had obtained many things from the pope; on hearing this, the king of France was so greatly disturbed that he said at once that he wished to send envoys to forbid the apostolic legates entry into his kingdom. 1445  
LXXXIX.—Of Theobald, count of Blois.—On the martyrdom of St. Thomas. 1447  
XC.—Of Master Vivian.—What he did in carrying out the apostolic mandate entrusted to him. 1448  
XCI.—Of the same.—On a similar subject. 1451  
XCII.—Of Laurence, abbot of Westminster.—For Gilbert, bishop of London. 1452  
XCIII.—Of anonymous writers.—Against Thomas of Canterbury. 1453  
XCIV.—Of an anonymous writer.—He relates what was done at the court which Emperor Frederick had summoned for his people on Pentecost, to negotiate peace between himself and the Roman pontiff [Col. 1520]. 1454  
XCV.—Of Richard, archbishop of Canterbury.—He accuses the abbot of Malmesbury of withdrawing himself from obedience to his bishop. He then laments at length the great evils resulting from exemptions granted by Roman pontiffs to abbots because of the tyranny of certain bishops. 1456  
XCVI.—Of the same.—He defends the reputation of bishops residing at the royal court against calumnies, and shows, from the example of the ancients, how greatly their presence there benefits the kingdom. 1459  
XCVII.—Of Bartholomew, bishop of Exeter.—For Richard, formerly archdeacon of Poitiers, bishop-elect of Winchester. 1461  
XCVIII.—Of the same.—For R., bishop-elect of Hereford. 1462  
XCIX.—Of the same.—For Richard, bishop-elect of Canterbury. 1462  
C.—Of the prior and community of the Church of Canterbury.—For R., bishop-elect of Winchester. 1464  
CI.—Of Odo, prior, and the community of the Church of Canterbury.—For R., bishop-elect of Canterbury. 1464
